cluster: Dashboard shell, navigation and global styles

surfaces.name: Global styles, tokens and fonts (index.html inline styles, global.css, house-tokens.css, site.css, cockpit.css)
surfaces.audience: Everyone signed in: venue staff, venue admin, hallkeeper, executive and platform admin. The rules apply on every route except the public homepage.
surfaces.dailyUse: Always on, for the whole working day. Every button hover, focus ring, cursor and scrollbar on every staff screen comes from these rules.
surfaces.currentLook: There are two registers at once. The page body is near-black (global.css:10-22, --vv-ink #0B0A09) and the only tokens are dark back-of-house ones: the House tokens say the ivory tokens are 'deliberately absent' (house-tokens.css:22). Cockpit-era globals from index.html apply to every non-homepage route: a gold SVG arrow cursor (index.html:77-79); a springy scale(1.06) plus brightness(1.15) hover and scale(0.93) press on every button and [role=button], with a 150 ms overshoot curve (index.html:95-113); and a 10 px gold-gradient scrollbar on a dark rgba(20,20,20,.6) track (index.html:138-168). The focus ring is 3 px cyan #87e7f0 with a 6 px cyan halo (global.css:42-54). Six families are loaded: Newsreader, Fraunces, Geist and Geist Mono (site.css), and Inter and Playfair Display (cockpit.css, which the Clerk routes pull in via cockpitImport, router.tsx:35-65). Georgia appears as a literal serif in 55 source files. Each ivory surface declares its own tokens. I counted 18 prefixes (--enq, --diary, --hk, --event, --workspace, --onboarding and so on) and 12 different 'paper' hexes, #f2edda through #fffef9. Across the dashboard and shared components there are 250 distinct 6-digit hex colours, about 11 border radii (0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12 and 14 px, 50% and 999 px) and about 10 focus-outline treatments (grep counts).
slogFactors: All-day hover wobble: every button on a staff route grows 6% and brightens with an overshooting spring (index.html:98-106), and the header does this on the Enquiries route too, because only the desk root carries [data-calm-controls] (EnquiriesView.tsx:514). Large targets swell as well: FileUploader's full-width drop zone is role=button (FileUploader.tsx:108), and ClientProfile's enquiry cards are <button>s (ClientProfile.tsx:129).

Controls in one row behave differently. The global rule's `transition … !important` replaces the header nav's 140 ms colour/background transition (DashboardLayout.css:37) on <button> items (Inventory, More) but not on <a> items (Plan, Diary, Hallkeeper). One nav bar therefore has two hover behaviours, one springy and one calm.

The focus ring is invisible on the chosen palette. The cyan #87e7f0 measured 1.22:1 on the desk sheet #f2eddd and on the header paper #f2edda (I computed the WCAG ratios from the hex values). The desk and the header each patch around it (EnquiriesDesk.css:84-89, DashboardLayout.css:41-42), and the header still inherits the cyan 6 px box-shadow halo from global.css:53, so it shows a forest ring inside a cyan glow.

Inference from CSS inheritance, not yet tested in a browser: the gold arrow cursor is set on body and inherits everywhere. The I-beam that normally appears over selectable text therefore never shows, which gets in the way of copying client emails and phone numbers.

Inference, not yet tested in a browser: styling ::-webkit-scrollbar forces an always-visible 10 px dark scrollbar with a gold thumb beside ivory pages. That is the strongest dark/gold object on an ivory/forest screen, and the thumb measures 2.33:1 against its own track.

Opening a staff route starts on dark screens. The first paint is the dark #171715 boot with system-ui text (Activity.css:3-11). Inferred from source: html/body stay #0B0A09, so overscroll or rubber-band scrolling and any unpainted gap show black above the ivory header.

The type has no single voice. The brand wordmark and state panels use Georgia (DashboardLayout.css:21, global.css:97), the desk headings use Newsreader (EnquiriesDesk.css:45), the planner uses Playfair Display, and Activity's panel capsule uses Geist Mono (Activity.css:54). All of these can sit on one screen.

`:root { color-scheme: light dark }` (global.css:6). Only the desk declares `color-scheme: light` (EnquiriesDesk.css:65). Inference, not yet tested: with the OS in dark mode, native selects, checkboxes and date pickers in other ivory views may render as dark UA widgets.
workflowGaps: There is no shared ivory token set, so every new surface re-picks near-identical values. The shell's paper is #f2edda and the desk's #f2eddd; the shell's ink is #122b25 and the desk's #14302a; the Inventory ground is #7f9182 and the Enquiries ground #819087 (DashboardLayout.css:2-4, 94, 98; EnquiriesDesk.css:10-24). The drift is invisible to one reviewer and obvious in aggregate.
Calm motion is opt-out rather than opt-in. Every future surface inherits the spring unless its author knows about [data-calm-controls].
`.vv-status-chip` (global.css:145-169) has 0 consumers. It is a dead dark/cyan chip grammar that invites reuse.
strengths: The reduced-motion kill switch is fixed at its source, with a clear warning against specificity arms races (index.html:80-94, 115-132). Reduced motion also removes all transforms in global.css:182-209.
The desk's opt-out uses :where(), so the global selectors keep their specificity (index.html:96-107).
Fonts are self-hosted with provenance and loaded per route family, so the front door is not blocked (index.html:8-15, router.tsx:32-65).
The House tokens have a contrast test for the dark register (house-tokens.css:20-21, src/__tests__/house-tokens.test.ts).

recommendations.change: Invert the spring. Delete the global scale(1.06)/brightness hover and scale(0.93) press from index.html:95-113 for all staff surfaces. If the planner cockpit still wants it, gate it on a [data-spring-controls] attribute on .venviewer-planner-shell. Put the desk's calm feedback in its place as the global default: 120 ms colour hover for fine pointers only, scale(0.97) press for buttons, none under reduced motion (EnquiriesDesk.css pattern). No test depends on the 1.06 hover (grep of e2e and src).
recommendations.why: This is the most-felt slog factor on every staff screen. It makes the header, drop zones and card-buttons wobble all day, and it splits one nav bar into two behaviours.

recommendations.change: Replace the cyan focus token with two focus tokens: --focus-on-light (desk ink #14302a, 12.07:1 on the sheet) and --focus-on-dark (cream #efe7cf, 8.76:1 on forest). Use a 2 px ring with 2 px offset and remove the cyan box-shadow halo at global.css:53. Retire the per-surface patches (DashboardLayout.css:41-42, EnquiriesDesk.css:84-89) once they are redundant.
recommendations.why: The current ring measured 1.22:1 on ivory, far below the 3:1 a focus indicator needs, and the halo leaks into the header's own ring.

recommendations.change: Scope the gold cursor and the gold/dark scrollbar to .venviewer-planner-shell, or delete them. Staff routes should use the system cursor and either the native scrollbar or a thin ivory-tuned one (thumb near --desk-rule-strong #bfc0ac on a transparent track).
recommendations.why: These are cockpit-era ornaments on an ivory/forest desk. They cost text-selection affordance, and on Windows they cost a permanent dark bar at the edge of every page.

recommendations.change: Create the missing ivory 'desk' token layer in styles/house-tokens.css by promoting the --enq-* set to shared names: ground sage, sheet, sheet-hover/selected, copper plane, ink 1-3, rules, forest, forest ink 1-3, cream, and tone washes for copper/amber/sage/brick/slate. Add --desk-serif (Newsreader), --desk-sans (Inter), --desk-ease-out and a radius scale of 3 px for controls and sheets, 999 px for chips and 50% for avatars. Extend house-tokens.test.ts to assert AA for every desk text pair, as the desk's session table did. Migrate DashboardLayout.css first, then each view.
recommendations.why: One source of truth stops the drift across 12 paper hexes and 18 surface prefixes, and makes every later view migration a token swap rather than a re-design.

recommendations.change: Set the staff-route canvas to the desk register. Give html/body the sage ground on staff routes, or put `color-scheme: light` plus an explicit ground on the shell. Make the index.html boot route-aware: the inline script already branches on location.pathname at lines 22-30, so give /dashboard, /diary and /hallkeeper an ivory boot capsule instead of #171715.
recommendations.why: This removes the dark→ivory flash on every staff arrival and the black overscroll band, and pins native form controls to the light scheme.

recommendations.change: Settle on one serif and one sans for staff surfaces: Newsreader for headings, numerals and the wordmark, Inter for UI text. Replace the literal Georgia in the shell and shared states (DashboardLayout.css:21, global.css:97, NotificationCenter.tsx:146, RouteArrival.css:86) with var(--desk-serif). Keep Geist Mono only where the content is genuinely tabular or code-like.
recommendations.why: Veterans read a single typographic voice as 'designed'. Two serifs next to each other (a Georgia wordmark and Newsreader 'Enquiries') read as assembled from parts.

recommendations.change: Delete the unused .vv-status-chip (global.css:145-169). Mark the dark .vv-state-panel/.vv-button grammar as legacy, to be replaced by the desk-register state panel (see the Routing surface).
recommendations.why: This removes the dark grammar that new work could copy by accident.

Is Newsreader, the desk's serif, the house serif for every staff surface, including the VENVIEWER wordmark that is currently set in Georgia caps?

surfaces.name: Dashboard shell: header, top navigation, More menu, account menu, skip link and workspace ground (DashboardLayout)
surfaces.audience: Venue staff (sales and bookings), venue admin, hallkeeper, executive and platform admin
surfaces.dailyUse: Constant. It frames /dashboard, /diary, /hallkeeper/*, /ops/*, /event-architect and /dev/capture-intake, and every change of section goes through it.
surfaces.currentLook: This is already the selected style's header. It sits on an 80 px ivory #f2edda bar (DashboardLayout.css:12-15), with 'VENVIEWER' in Georgia caps, a hairline, then the venue name. The Inter nav has a 2 px ink underline on the current item, and an outlined-initials avatar sits beside the name and role. The More and account popovers are ivory #f7f3e6, 4 px radius, with a soft shadow (DashboardLayout.css:59-65). Below the header, the ground depends on the view. It is dark forest #132b25 with 24 px padding by default (DashboardLayout.css:92-93). Inventory gets sage #7f9182, the Diary paper #f6f4eb and Enquiries sage #819087 (DashboardLayout.css:94-99). Every view except those three therefore sits on the old dark forest, as the committed baselines show for Reviews, Analytics, Loadouts and Admin.
slogFactors: The desk people use all day is hidden. Enquiries is not in the top nav: the top level is Plan, Diary, Hallkeeper and (for admins) Inventory, then 'More' (DashboardLayout.tsx:199-214). Pipeline, Proposals and Client Search are also behind More. A test asserts that Enquiries stays out of the top level (DashboardLayout.test.tsx:82). On the desk itself the underline sits under 'More', so the header never says 'Enquiries' (desk-overview.webp, desk-phone.webp).

On a More view the header does not say where you are. The underline sits on 'More' for eleven different views (DashboardLayout.tsx:179-180), and the main landmark is labelled 'Dashboard workspace' for all of them (DashboardLayout.tsx:247).

The More menu is one flat, unordered list of up to 12 destinations mixing sales, operations, admin and platform tools, with Notifications appended underneath (DashboardLayout.tsx:215-227). For an executive the top nav is only 'More', which contains the one page they are already on (desktop-executive-analytics-success baseline).

Labels are in mixed case: 'Pending Reviews', 'Executive Analytics', 'Client Search', 'Reference Loadouts', 'Venue Settings', 'Sign Out' against 'Clients & access' (DashboardLayout.tsx:38-53, 77); the Analytics page heading reads 'Executive analytics'.

The header's own colours drift from the desk. It uses four rule colours in one component (#c9cdbd, #bfc4b2, #b8c1ae, #d3d8c7), and the nav hover #e7e5d5 is 1.08:1 against the paper, which barely registers (DashboardLayout.css:14, 4, 63, 81, 39).
The ground under most views is dark forest #132b25 (DashboardLayout.css:92). This is the before image Blake judged a slog: ivory header, dark body, boxed cards.

Inferred from code: each page wraps its own DashboardLayout, and getVenue is not cached (api/spaces.ts:81-83). Every Diary↔Dashboard↔Hallkeeper move therefore remounts the header, resets the venue name to 'Dashboard' then 'Your venue', and shows an 'Opening venue…' particle status before the real name returns (DashboardLayout.tsx:151-167).
workflowGaps: A failed venue fetch leaves 'Your venue' in the header permanently, with no signal (DashboardLayout.tsx:160-164). The mobile baseline mobile-event-day-acknowledgement-error shows 'Your venue'.

Focus is lost after choosing a destination from More. Inferred from code: the effect on activeView closes the popover (DashboardLayout.tsx:103), which hides the focused menu button, and nothing moves focus to the new view's heading or main. Keyboard users restart from the top of the document.

'Home' is inconsistent. The wordmark always links to /dashboard (DashboardLayout.tsx:192), but a hallkeeper's home is /hallkeeper/today and a platform admin's is /dashboard?view=onboarding (role-routing.ts:8-9).
There is no global search in the header, although the selected reference has one ('Search inventory' field). Finding a client means More → Client Search → type.

The account menu holds only the email and Sign Out (DashboardLayout.tsx:238-243). There are no preferences (landing view, notifications), no keyboard legend, no help or contact, and no venue switcher.
There are no shell-level shortcuts. The desk's ↑ ↓ j k Enter Esc exist only inside the desk; no other key reaches Enquiries, Diary or search.
The browser tab title is never set for staff views. See the Routing surface.
strengths: The header visually matches the selected reference: ivory bar, serif wordmark, venue name after a hairline, underline for the current item, initials avatar with role.
Navigation is role-aware and mirrors the API (canShowNavItem, DashboardLayout.tsx:55-66), so staff are never offered a 403.

The skip link 'Skip to workspace' (DashboardLayout.tsx:189) has a visible ivory focus style (DashboardLayout.css:100-104). Escape closes a menu and returns focus to its trigger, and outside focus dismisses it (DashboardLayout.tsx:104-124). Menu items are 44 px targets.

Sign-out is protected while an inventory correction is dirty (InventoryExitBoundary, DashboardLayout.tsx:68-89, 257-259), and stale venue responses are discarded (request.current guard, lines 159-166).
The desk opts into a full-bleed sage surface through a single `surface` prop (DashboardLayout.tsx:32-34, 246).

recommendations.change: Make the daily desks first-class. Suggested top level for staff: Enquiries · Diary · Plan · Hallkeeper, plus Inventory for venue admins. Group the rest of More under small-caps headings: Sales (Pipeline, Proposals, Clients), Operations (Pending reviews, Reference loadouts, Event Architect), Venue (Settings, Clients & access), Platform (Admin, Capture Factory). When a More view is open, show its name in the nav slot (for example 'Pipeline ⌄' underlined) so the header always names the current place. Executives get 'Analytics' directly and no More. The test at DashboardLayout.test.tsx:82 has to change, so this needs Blake's call.
recommendations.why: The desk Blake judged best is buried two clicks deep and never named. Veterans navigate by place names, not by 'More'.

recommendations.change: Change the default workspace ground from #132b25 to the desk composition: a sage ground with a pale plane and an ivory sheet. Generalise `surface` into a register the view declares ('desk' vs 'legacy-forest'), and migrate views one by one. Some views paint light text straight onto the ground: the Analytics heading and the Reviews '← Back' link (baselines). A blanket flip would break their contrast.
recommendations.why: This is the single change that moves every remaining screen out of the rejected 'dark body with cards' look. Doing it per view keeps AA intact.

recommendations.change: Keep one persistent shell across staff routes. Make DashboardLayout a parent layout route with <Outlet/> in router.tsx instead of each page wrapping it. Cache the venue name (per venueId, in a small store or query cache), so the header never flickers 'Dashboard' → 'Your venue' → 'Opening venue…'. On failure, show 'Venue name unavailable', with the retry in the account menu.
recommendations.why: The header should feel like the building's frame: still, and never re-announcing itself on each move.

recommendations.change: Sentence-case every label ('Pending reviews', 'Executive analytics', 'Client search', 'Reference loadouts', 'Venue settings', 'Sign out'), and make the nav label and page heading the same words.
recommendations.why: Small inconsistencies read as unfinished to a detail-minded veteran.

recommendations.change: After a view change, move focus to the new view's h1 (tabIndex -1), and set main's aria-label to the view name (for example 'Enquiries'), not 'Dashboard workspace'.
recommendations.why: This fixes the focus loss when the More menu hides the focused item, and gives screen-reader users their place.

recommendations.change: Add a shell keyboard layer that follows the desk's idiom, with a legend in the desk's key-cap style under '?': g e Enquiries, g d Diary, g p Plan, / client search, ? shortcuts. Suppress it inside inputs and the planner canvas.
recommendations.why: This is keyboard-first operation for high-frequency switching, the Superhuman lesson recorded in the desk README, applied across the product.

recommendations.change: Put a search field in the header (as in the selected reference) that finds clients, enquiries and bookings by name, email or date, and opens results beside the list rather than replacing it.
recommendations.why: Salesforce and Cvent veterans expect one box that finds any record. Today it takes three steps (More → Client Search → type).

recommendations.change: Make the wordmark link role-aware: use getDefaultRoute(role, platformRole) from role-routing.ts instead of the fixed /dashboard.
recommendations.why: A hallkeeper clicking the logo should land on Today, not a sales desk.

recommendations.change: Build out the account menu: default landing view, notification preferences, keyboard shortcuts, help and contact, a venue switcher for multi-venue users, and Sign out last.
recommendations.why: Eight-hour users need to tune their tool, and every Salesforce and Cvent user expects these.

recommendations.change: Replace the header's hard-coded values with the desk tokens: paper, ink, a single rule colour and a hover wash with visible contrast. Remove the !important overrides at DashboardLayout.css:84-91 once NotificationCenter is restyled.
recommendations.why: This ends the drift between shell and desk.

evidence: DashboardLayout.tsx:199-229 top nav, More popover with Notifications inside
DashboardLayout.tsx:151-167 venue name 'Dashboard' → 'Your venue' → fetch; errors swallowed

Baselines: desktop-executive-analytics-success (executive nav = only 'More'), desktop-reviews-action-error and desktop-loadout-caption-error (dark forest ground under ivory header), mobile-event-day-acknowledgement-error ('Your venue' in header)
desk-overview.webp and desk-phone.webp: 'More' underlined while on Enquiries
questionsForBlake: Should Enquiries, the desk you judged best, be a named item in the top bar, perhaps taking the slot the reference image gives 'Messages'? Today a test deliberately keeps it under More.
Which top-level items does each role see first? For example sales staff: Enquiries, Diary, Plan; hallkeepers: Today, Diary, Rooms; executives: Analytics.
Do you want the header search field from the reference image, and should it search clients, enquiries and bookings together?
Should every staff screen (Pipeline, Reviews, Analytics, Settings, Admin) adopt the desk composition of sage ground, ivory sheet and forest decision panel, or should any keep a different register?

surfaces.name: Notifications (NotificationCenter inside the More menu)
surfaces.audience: Venue staff, venue admin, hallkeeper, executive and platform admin
surfaces.dailyUse: It should be glanced at all day, but it is hidden. It is reachable only by opening More, and the count is fetched once each time the layout mounts.
surfaces.currentLook: This is a dark cockpit widget inside an ivory menu. The trigger is inline-styled in pale cyan on dark (NotificationCenter.tsx:17-29), which the shell forcibly re-skins to ivory with `!important` (DashboardLayout.css:84-88). The panel keeps a near-black gradient with a gold border and a 42% black shadow (NotificationCenter.tsx:44-57), so it drops a black box inside the ivory More popover. Cards are dark translucent, with the severity as a raw uppercase word in salmon, gold or teal (lines 72-76, 176-178), a Georgia h2 (line 146) and icon-only actions (ExternalLink, CheckCheck).
slogFactors: It takes two clicks to see anything: More, then '3 unread notifications'. Nothing in the visible header shows that anything is waiting (DashboardLayout.tsx:226).
A black panel inside an ivory popover inside an ivory header is the most jarring register clash in the shell (NotificationCenter.tsx:44-57 vs DashboardLayout.css:64).
The trigger repeats the count twice: '3 unread notifications' plus a gold '3' badge (lines 137-139).
Severity is shown as the raw enum ('URGENT', 'ATTENTION'), not plain venue language (line 177).
An ExternalLink icon is used for in-app navigation (line 191), which suggests a new tab that never opens.
workflowGaps: markNotificationRead has no catch (lines 104-118). A failed mark-read clears the busy state silently, with nothing shown and an unhandled rejection.
There is no 'Mark all read', no history of read items and no grouping by enquiry or event.
It never refreshes on its own: one fetch on mount (lines 91-93) and a manual refresh icon. An urgent change can sit unseen all day.
Inferred from code: the panel's `open` state survives closing More, so reopening More can show the panel already expanded.
aria-haspopup='dialog' is declared, but the panel is a plain <section> (lines 134, 143).
strengths: The notifications are real data with an optional deep link (actionPath), and they use the shared Activity indicator for loading and busy states.
Its states are explicit: loading, error, empty and ready (lines 8-11, 153-161).

recommendations.change: Move notifications out of More into a dedicated header control beside the account: an outlined bell, the same style as the avatar ring, with a quiet copper numeral when unread items exist. No pulsing and no red. Open an ivory popover in the desk register: serif heading, rows led by what they concern (client name or event date), a named tone chip in plain words ('Needs a decision', 'For information'), a row click that navigates, and a small 'Mark read'.
recommendations.why: Calm technology informs without demanding attention, but it has to be visible. Today it is neither visible nor calm.

recommendations.change: Add 'Mark all read', show and announce a mark-read failure inline, replace ExternalLink with an in-app arrow, and refresh on window focus plus a gentle interval (for example every 2 minutes, paused when the tab is hidden).
recommendations.why: Honest closure and no stale urgency.

recommendations.change: Group notifications by record (enquiry, event, handoff) and end with a sealed 'Nothing waiting on you', the same closure pattern as the desk's 'All caught up'.
recommendations.why: A visible end state is what makes clearing a queue satisfying.

evidence: NotificationCenter.tsx:17-29 cyan trigger; 44-57 dark panel; 72-76 salmon/gold/teal tones; 104-118 no catch; 146 Georgia; 176-178 raw severity; 191 ExternalLink
DashboardLayout.css:84-91 !important re-skin of the trigger and panel position
DashboardLayout.test.tsx:84-85 test opens More to find 'No unread notifications'
questionsForBlake: Is a small copper count on a bell in the header acceptable, or does it break the 'no badges shouting' rule? The alternative is a dot with the count only inside the popover.
Which events should notify staff at all? For example a new enquiry, a client edit to a layout, a supplier acknowledgement or a date conflict.

surfaces.name: DashboardPage view routing, role-denied state and the arrival/loading chain
surfaces.audience: Venue staff, hallkeeper, executive and platform admin; suppliers who land on /dashboard
surfaces.dailyUse: On every view switch. The denied state is rare but memorable, and the loading chain appears on every sign-in and every cold route load.
surfaces.currentLook: The role-denied view (DashboardPage.tsx:88-111) is a near-black .vv-state-panel with a gold kicker 'ROLE RESTRICTED'. It has a 42 px bold Georgia headline, 'That dashboard surface is not available for this role', and a full-width gold button, all floating on the dark forest ground under the ivory header (desktop-admin-subroute-denied baseline). The route-level denial in ProtectedRoute.tsx:36-56 is a full-screen dark panel with no action. Its committed baseline, desktop-supplier-denied, still shows older copy and a disabled-looking 'Access not granted' pill. The loading chain has four registers. Inferred from source composition: the dark boot (#171715, index.html:174-203), then the RouteArrival Suspense fallback (a dark brown radial with 'Workspace' in Georgia up to 108 px, 'Opening…', and a 'Back to venue' link; RouteArrival.tsx:36, RouteArrival.css:64-92), then the dark 'Checking access…' panel (ProtectedRoute.tsx:21-29), then the ivory shell.
slogFactors: The denial is written for developers: 'The requested view "admin" is held back because it can change commercial, deployment, or admin records' (DashboardPage.tsx:103). It exposes the raw URL key and a blanket reason that is not true of every view.
A dark cockpit panel with a gold button on the forest ground is a third palette under the ivory header.
The supplier denial is a dead end. It shows 'Access needed / Ask your venue admin to grant access.' with no sign-out, no link to a supplier's own pages and no home (ProtectedRoute.tsx:36-44).
Arriving flashes dark, then brown, then dark, then ivory, with a huge 'Workspace' headline that does not name where you are going (RouteArrival.tsx:36).

The browser tab never names the staff view. A cold load reads the public 'Trades Hall of Glasgow — weddings and events' (index.html:16). After signing in through the SPA, LoginPage's 'Sign in - Venviewer' persists (LoginPage.tsx:21-23), because DashboardPage and DiaryBoardPage never set document.title (grep).
workflowGaps: The client profile is not in the URL. Opening a profile from Client Search (DashboardPage.tsx:229-233), or jumping from a profile to an enquiry (lines 169-178), changes only React state. Inferred from code: reload loses the place, and browser Back leaves the dashboard instead of returning to the search results.
For a denied view the header keeps the previous view's underline, because `view` is unchanged while the denied panel shows (lines 121, 144-146, 190-197).
The denied view offers only 'Open enquiries' or 'Open analytics'. It does not say who can grant access or offer to request it.

The committed baseline desktop-supplier-denied no longer matches ProtectedRoute's current copy: the test asserts 'Access needed' (e2e/dashboard-state-visual-performance.spec.ts:725-727). The visual record is stale.
strengths: The access rules are explicit and unit-testable (dashboardViewFromSearchValue, canOpenDashboardView and initialDashboardViewForRole, DashboardPage.tsx:60-86), and they mirror the nav rules.
Views are deep-linkable with ?view=, and switching pushes history (lines 158-160).
The return context from profile to enquiry and back is deliberately kept (lines 22-40, 167-187).
Unsaved inventory edits hold navigation until the router accepts it (lines 149-157).

recommendations.change: Redraw the role-denied state in the desk register: an ivory sheet on the sage ground with a Newsreader headline in plain words ('Admin is for Venviewer platform administrators'). surfaces.name: Toast system (stores/toast-store.ts and components/shared/ToastContainer.tsx)
surfaces.audience: Venue staff, venue admin and platform admin using dashboard views
surfaces.dailyUse: Often. There are 69 addToast calls across 10 dashboard files (AdminPanel 18, ReviewsView 12, LoadoutDetail 11, CommercialPipelineView 11, and others). Most are 'Failed to …' errors.
surfaces.currentLook: Toasts are generic library cards fixed at the top right (ToastContainer.tsx:73). They use Tailwind default washes with a 3 px left border in blue #3b82f6, green #22c55e or red #ef4444 (lines 54-59), 13 px Inter, 8 px radius, and a light grey × (#999, line 91). They auto-dismiss after 4000 ms whatever their type (toast-store.ts:31-34). The Diary has its own, better toast: a forest #2c513d capsule at the bottom centre with an Undo button (diary-board.css:183-184, DiaryBoardPage.tsx:813-817).
slogFactors: The toast covers the account control. Baselines desktop-reviews-action-error and desktop-loadout-caption-error show it sitting over the user's name and avatar.
Library colours (Tailwind blue, green and red) are exactly what the brief bans as 'generic library colours'.
The dismiss × measured about 2.6:1 on its wash, below 3:1. It is a 16 px glyph with 0 padding, well under a 24 px target, and it springs 6% on hover.

The copy is terse and blaming ('Failed to approve', 'Failed to reorder', 'Search failed') and says neither what did not happen nor what to do. The desk's own phrasing is better: '<name>'s status could not be changed' (EnquiriesView.tsx:429).
Errors appear twice. Reviews shows an inline 'Approval did not save. The layout has not been approved.' plus a toast 'Failed to approve' (baseline desktop-reviews-action-error).
workflowGaps: Errors vanish after 4 s, even while being read. There is no pause on hover or focus, and no way to recall them (WCAG 2.2.1 timing).
There is no action slot, so there is no Undo on deletes such as 'Photo removed', 'Loadout deleted', 'Venue deleted' or 'Space deleted', although the Diary proves the pattern.

Inferred from code: the live region is created only when the first toast arrives, because the container returns null when empty (ToastContainer.tsx:65). Screen readers often miss that first announcement. Error items nest role=alert inside role=status (line 81).
The container's aria-label 'Notifications' collides with the NotificationCenter's 'Notifications' region, which is a different thing.
The app has two toast systems (the shared store and the Diary's UndoToast) that look and behave differently.
strengths: The store is tiny and typed, and it clears timers on manual dismissal (toast-store.ts:21-46).
The Diary's UndoToast already expresses the right register and pattern to promote.

recommendations.change: Replace ToastContainer with a shared version of the Diary's UndoToast. Use a forest capsule at the bottom centre, clear of the header and the desk's decision panel, with cream text, an optional action ('Undo', 'Retry') and a ≥24 px AA dismiss. Keep one persistent polite live region always mounted, and give errors their own assertive region. Errors stay until dismissed. Successes last about 6 s and pause on hover or focus.
recommendations.why: One calm, on-palette confirmation voice with real recovery. It also stops covering the account control.

recommendations.change: Set toast policy: no toast when the change is already visible in place (the desk's calm-technology rule), and never both inline and toast for the same failure. Rewrite the messages to say what did not happen, what is kept and the next step ('Approval didn't save. The layout is still waiting for review.' with Retry).
recommendations.why: Fewer interruptions and honest consequences.

recommendations.change: Add Undo to reversible deletes (photo, loadout), and for venue and space deletion prefer archive with restore (see ConfirmModal).
recommendations.why: Undo is the lowest-effort safety net and removes the need for many confirm modals.

surfaces.name: Shared Activity component and first paint (Activity.tsx, Activity.css, index.html boot)
surfaces.audience: Everyone, on every loading or working state
surfaces.dailyUse: Constant but brief: venue name loading, saves, uploads, notifications and route arrival.
surfaces.currentLook: The indicator is a CSS-animated SVG particle field (56 particles, 28 when compact) folding from sphere to ring to helix over 6.4 s, in currentColor with copper #b98255 accents (Activity.tsx:5-57, Activity.css:22-39). Inline status is a polite live span; the panel variant is a pill capsule in Geist Mono (Activity.css:53-61). There is an optional 2 px measured progress bar. Reduced motion freezes the particles. The first-paint copy in index.html uses a dark #171715 page with system-ui text.
slogFactors: The first paint is dark and set in system-ui (Activity.css:3-11), then jumps to the ivory shell. It is the first impression of every working session.
The panel capsule's monospace font (Activity.css:54) adds a fourth family to staff screens.
It is placed under the venue name in the header on every shell mount ('Opening venue…', DashboardLayout.tsx:195), where it appears repeatedly because the shell remounts per route.
workflowGaps: No shared pattern exists for 'refreshing while showing content'. Views choose between blanking and showing a panel. The convention allows preserving content, but there is no component for it.
strengths: It is honest by design: it mounts only while work is active, allows no fake percentages, keeps status semantics and freezes under reduced motion (Activity.tsx:59-92, loading-and-working-motion.md).
The copper accent already matches the selected palette, and colour is inherited so it works on ivory and forest.
A convention test guards first paint and reduced motion (src/__tests__/activity-convention.test.ts:199-205).

recommendations.why: One typographic voice.

recommendations.change: Add a quiet 'refreshing' variant, a compact indicator beside the section heading while content stays visible, and use it for the stage counts, notifications and venue name.

evidence: Activity.css:3-11 dark boot; :53-61 mono capsule; :80-84 reduced motion

crossCutting: The Enquiries desk is the only surface that opts out of the global scale(1.06) spring (index.html:95-113, EnquiriesView.tsx:514). Every other staff view, and the shell header on the desk route, still springs. Fix this once at the source by making calm the default and the spring opt-in, rather than adding [data-calm-controls] view by view.

There is no shared ivory/forest/copper/sage token layer. house-tokens.css:22 leaves the ivory register 'deliberately absent'. I counted 18 surface-specific token prefixes (--enq, --diary, --hk, --event, --workspace, --onboarding and so on), 12 different ivory 'paper' hexes and 250 distinct hex colours across the dashboard and shared components. Promote the desk's --enq-* set to shared --desk-* tokens with an AA contrast test, and migrate every view to it.

Focus: the global cyan ring (#87e7f0, global.css:42-54) measured 1.22:1 on ivory. About 10 different outline treatments coexist in the dashboard and shared components (#365f4f header, desk ink and cream, inventory accent, #fff6e5 arrival, #9b653e, #2f614b, #eee1b4, cyan variants). One pair of tokens should replace them: ink on light, cream on forest.

Proposal: Newsreader for headings, numerals and the wordmark, and Inter for UI.

Buttons and radii: about 15 inline JS button-style constants and 16 CSS button classes in the dashboard, plus the global .vv-button; radii span 0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12 and 14 px, 50% and 999 px. The desk uses 3 px for controls and sheets and 999 px for chips. Adopt that scale and a shared Button with primary (cream on forest, forest on ivory), quiet and destructive variants.

Default workspace ground: DashboardLayout paints #132b25 dark forest under every view except Enquiries, Inventory and the Diary (DashboardLayout.css:92-99). Toasts: there are two systems. The shared one uses Tailwind colours, sits at the top right and covers the account control, and dismisses errors after 4 s. The Diary's is a forest capsule with Undo. Promote the Diary's pattern and apply the calm-technology rule (no toast when the change is visible in place).
Confirmation: the shared dark ConfirmModal (default red) conflicts with the desk's inline consequence confirmation. Extract the desk's version as the shared pattern.

Each page mounts its own DashboardLayout, so every cross-route move remounts the header, refetches the venue uncached, and flashes 'Your venue' and 'Opening venue…'. A parent layout route in router.tsx would fix this for every surface.

surfaces.name: Commercial pipeline (CommercialPipelineView)
surfaces.audience: venue staff (sales executives). Venue admins see the tab, but the API refuses them.
surfaces.currentLook: The old dark cockpit look. It sits on the forest #132b25 dashboard ground (DashboardLayout.css:92). Cards are near-black gradients with a cyan radial glow, 1px gold hairlines, an 8px radius and heavy 0 22px 70px shadows. Labels are gold #d7b56d, 12px bold. Everything is inline styles (CommercialPipelineView.tsx:54-107). The type is Inter only: a 20px bold 'Commercial pipeline' and a 22px/800 'Pipeline value' (371-378), with no serif and no light numerals. The layout is two fixed columns, the main area plus a 360px aside (367). Seven identical stage cards sit in a 3-column grid (439-479), so the stages wrap as New/Qualified/Proposal drafting, Proposal sent/Negotiation/Won, then Lost alone. Opportunity cards are <button>s, so each gets the global scale(1.06) and brightness(1.15) hover pop (index.html:95-113). The view has no motion of its own, no keyboard model beyond Tab and no media queries. There is no committed visual baseline for this view; everything here is judged from source.
surfaces.dailyUse: It is meant to be a sales executive's home for live deals: opened many times a day and potentially kept open all day beside the Enquiries desk. Today it is two clicks deep, under More > Pipeline.
slogFactors: Seven identical dark boxes in a 3-3-1 grid. Nothing flows left to right. Won and Lost get the same weight as live deals, and nothing says which deal needs attention first (439-479).

Every enquiry-created deal reads '£0.00'. The server always creates it with estimatedValueMinor 0 (api routes/crm.ts:133), and no control edits the value afterwards. The headline 'Pipeline value' therefore stays at £0.00 unless deals are added by hand.
A null guest count renders literally as 'Guest count pending guests' (CommercialPipelineView.tsx:472).
Cards lead with the title and money. The facts a booker decides on (event date, room) are not shown at all, although preferredDate is in the payload (api/crm.ts:28).
'Quick create from enquiry' asks for a raw UUID 'Enquiry ID' (385-396). The Enquiries desk never displays enquiry IDs, so no one can fill this field in.

Stage moves use a native <select> that lists all seven stages (514-523). Invalid jumps, such as New to Won, fail with 'Could not update the stage' and no reason. The server has the allowed moves (commercial-spine.ts:43-52). Inference, not browser-tested: on Chrome/Windows the arrow keys on a focused, closed select fire change, so a keyboard user can move a deal by accident.

'Today's follow-ups' lists every open task: the API filters on status 'open' only, never on date (api routes/crm.ts:196-203). Tasks added in the UI never get a due date (addFollowUpTask called without dueAt, 297). Rows show no deal name and cannot be opened or ticked from the list (485-494).
The activity list shows only the last 4 notes, with no time or author (599-603).
Every success raises a toast (215, 248, 339), and every failure raises both a toast and an inline alert. This is the opposite of the desk's calm feedback.
Hover swell on every card: the view does not opt into [data-calm-controls].
The fixed 360px aside plus the 3 × 180px minimum stage columns (367, 439) have no breakpoints. Inference: phone widths will scroll sideways, the bug the desk fixed at 390 px.
workflowGaps: 'Create proposal draft' tries to move the deal from New straight to Proposal drafting (346-349). The server refuses that move for staff (commercial-spine.ts:43-52; opportunities.ts:267-269). The failure is swallowed ('non-critical', 352), so the deal still reads New while a proposal exists. The unit test mocks this invalid move as a success (the fixture's stage is 'new'; __tests__/CommercialPipelineView.test.tsx:302-316).

Proposals appear in the detail as title · raw status text, not links (549-553). Sending or accepting a proposal never moves the deal's stage: the share-token route (api proposals.ts:711-800) and the approve route (1317-1380) never touch opportunities.
Won and Lost are a single silent select change. No reason is captured, although the server's next action for Lost says 'Record the reason' (opportunities.ts:61-62).

The detail shows no client name, contact, event date, room, source enquiry, diary hold or due date (506-615). The from-enquiry route creates a client account and a contact (crm.ts:95-116), but no web screen ever reads them.
'Pipeline value' adds up every deal, Won and Lost included (204-207), so it is not a pipeline figure.

Venue admins (role 'admin') are shown Pipeline (DashboardPage.tsx:56,70; DashboardLayout.tsx:55-66), but /crm/pipeline allows only role 'staff' or a platform admin (api crm.ts:35-38; opportunities.ts:36-44). For them it is a permanent 'Could not load the commercial pipeline'.
The list is capped at 200 deals, oldest-updated first (crm.ts:186-190). Inference: after a busy year the newest deals fall off the board.
strengths: Stale-response guards on the list and the detail (useLatestRequest, 162-202). A busy lock stops the automatic stage change and a manual stage change from interleaving (341-344).
Inline errors say what did not happen: 'The opportunity has not moved', 'It remains open until the server confirms it' (271, 322).
Money is parsed in exact pence. A bad amount gets a clear message instead of being turned into zero (235-238).
It uses the shared Activity component for loading and working states.
evidence: Measured contrast: muted text 7.70:1 and empty-stage text 5.65:1 on these dark cards pass. The problem here is style and hierarchy, not contrast.

recommendations.change: Make the desk's 'Create opportunity' open the new or existing deal in the pipeline via a deep link (?view=pipeline&opportunity=<id>), with the list kept beside it. Remove the UUID 'Enquiry ID' form. Stop toasting 'Existing opportunity opened' when nothing opens (EnquiriesView.tsx:466).

recommendations.change: Replace the all-stages <select> with buttons for the valid next moves only (from OPPORTUNITY_STAGE_TRANSITIONS), always in the same next-step slot. Won and Lost open an inline confirmation that captures a reason. Fix the proposal-draft advance: either step through New → Qualified → Proposal drafting, or allow the move on the server. Show a failure instead of swallowing it, and correct the unit-test fixture.
recommendations.why: States consequences honestly, removes silent failures and accidental keyboard moves, and keeps the next step in the same place.

recommendations.change: Align roles: either admit venue admins to the crm and opportunities APIs, or hide Pipeline from them, after Blake decides.
recommendations.why: Removes a guaranteed error screen for an entire role.

recommendations.change: Fix the 'Guest count pending guests' string. Lead every card with a date tile (reuse eventDateParts/eventLead from enquiry-desk-format.ts), then the client's name in serif, guests · room, value, and the age of the next action.

recommendations.change:
Rebuild in the desk composition, on tokens shared with EnquiriesDesk.css:
- **Ledger:** an ivory ledger of deals grouped by when the next action is due (Overdue, Today, This week, Later).
- **Counts:** a copper plane of live stages, each showing its count and value in light serif numerals and working as a filter. Closed stages are quieter.

recommendations.change:
Make follow-ups a real day list:

- **Summary:** one sentence such as '3 follow-ups due today; the oldest is 2 days overdue'.

recommendations.change: Make the estimated value editable, and fill it from the latest saved quote total. The headline shows open pipeline value and 'Won this month' separately.
recommendations.why: The money figures are currently untrue.

recommendations.change: Keep the deal in step with its proposal. When a proposal is sent, the deal moves to Proposal sent. When the client accepts, it moves to Negotiation or 'Accepted – contract to send', depending on Blake's contract decision. Record each move in the timeline.
recommendations.why: The board goes stale unless someone remembers to move it by hand.

recommendations.change: Adopt the desk's responsive behaviour: list and panel take turns below 1180px and go full-bleed below 760px.
recommendations.why: Removes the inferred sideways scroll and supports tablets on the floor.

recommendations.change: Show and create the Diary hold from the deal: first or second option, and the decision date from bookings.rank and decisionAt.
recommendations.why: A veteran's first question is whether the date is held and until when.

questionsForBlake: Stage names: keep Salesforce-style names (Qualified, Negotiation), or use venue language such as Enquiry, Viewing, Provisional hold, Proposal out, Contract out, Contracted, Deposit paid?
Should a date held in the Diary and a deal in the pipeline be one record the team sees in one place?
Should venue admins work the pipeline, or only the sales team?
Should the pipeline value be the raw total of live deals, or weighted by how likely each stage is to close?

surfaces.name: Proposals workspace (ProposalsView)
surfaces.currentLook: The same dark cockpit cards on forest (48-98). The left column holds 'New proposal' and the proposals list (447-533). The right column stacks up to five cards: detail, new version, latest quote, conversation and history (541-880). Type is Inter at 13-18px, with bold headings and no serif. Statuses appear as raw words ('changes requested', 'draft → sent'). Times read '18/06/2026, 10:00:00', seconds included, via toLocaleString('en-GB') (548, 808, 872). No committed baseline.
surfaces.dailyUse: Daily. Writing or revising a proposal is a focused 10 to 30 minute session several times a week per executive. Checking client responses happens several times a day.
slogFactors: Every new version starts blank. The composer is cleared when a proposal is selected (258-260) and after each save (395-397), and is never pre-filled from latestVersion. Answering 'changes requested' means retyping the whole message and every quote line.
The client's change request sits in the Conversation card, below the detail, composer and quote cards (775). The thing to read first is the furthest away.
List rows show only a title and a pill (510-531): no client, event date, total, age, or who is waiting on whom.
Status pills fail contrast (measured): white on #68d8d2 is 1.70:1 (sent), on #f2b35e 1.84:1 (changes requested), on #9ca3af 2.54:1 (expired) and on #059669 3.77:1 (accepted).
Quote lines are typed by hand, four inputs per line (688-731). The venue's pricing rules and estimatePrice exist (api/pricing.ts:66-78), but only AdminPanel uses them.
Safety caveats are repeated in the composer (591-593) and in the capacity result (657-661).
Why 'Generate client link' is disabled is explained only in a title tooltip (566), which touch and keyboard users never see.
The busy flag disables every list row while any save runs (516), and rows and buttons swell on hover.
The two fixed columns and the 4-column quote-line grid have no breakpoints (447, 689).
workflowGaps: 'Generate client link' actually sends the proposal. It marks it Sent, freezes the content (isProposalEditable, types proposal.ts:117) and mints a token (api proposals.ts:711-800). The button and its tooltip mention only a share link. Nothing is emailed, so staff must copy a raw URL, whose anchor opens in the same tab and takes them out of the dashboard (552-557).

The tokenised link lives only in component state (160, 422). After a reload the page falls back to /proposal/<shareCode> (430-432), the older link on which the client cannot comment (ProposalPage.tsx:183-184). Staff can send a weaker link without knowing.
Withdraw is one click with no confirmation (572-576). It makes the client's link return 404 (CLIENT_VISIBLE_STATUSES, api proposals.ts:972, 1030) and says so nowhere.

Proposals created here link no deal, enquiry or configuration (310). Pipeline-created proposals pass enquiryId but not configurationId, and the API does not derive it (proposals.ts:307-360). The to-scale layout snapshot needs configurationId (826-833), so a layout the client drew never reaches their proposal.

Client approvals and change requests notify staff only when the proposal's configuration is linked to an event (proposals.ts:155-156, 199-200). For proposals made in the dashboard nothing alerts the executive, who must poll this list.

The list API defaults to 20 rows, oldest-updated first (ListQuery 83-87, orderBy updatedAt 296-301). The web client drops the paging data (api/client.ts:158), so past 20 proposals the newest ones are invisible, with no paging.
When the client opens the link, the view time is recorded (lastViewedAt, proposals.ts:1242) but never shown. The same endpoint also records staff previews.
Once a proposal is Accepted, the only action is Archive (577-581). There is no next step toward contract, deposit or confirming the booking.
The Enquiries desk's AI 'Draft proposal copy' produces a read-only textarea (components/ai/AIDraftPanel.tsx:113) with no route into this composer.
strengths: The claim guard runs in the browser and explains unsupported certainty wording inline before anything is posted (287-293, 385-392).
Quote totals come from the server's exact money engine and are reused verbatim (349-373). Versions cannot be changed once saved.
Capacity guidance is worked out from the room's floor area and can be inserted in one click (617-673).
Each section has its own retryable load error, and stale responses are ignored for the list, history, versions and comments.
evidence: packages/web/src/components/dashboard/ProposalsView.tsx:430-432 (share URL falls back to the short code)
Measured: StatusPill sent 1.70:1, changes requested 1.84:1, expired 2.54:1, accepted 3.77:1

The page is a single 720px column of boxed sections: message, layout plan, quote table, room and layout summaries in two columns, packages, capacity guidance, actions, conversation, and a footer disclaimer. The planning summary is a fixed two-column grid (265) that gets cramped on phones.
The 'Request changes' border measures 1.63:1 against the page, a faint control edge.
workflowGaps: After Approve the buttons disappear (canRespond false, 180 and 311). The confirmation banner renders at the top of the page (203-208), and focus does not move. Inference from layout order: a client who scrolled down to approve sees the buttons vanish and nothing else.

surfaces.name: From enquiry to signed contract and deposit (the journey across screens)
surfaces.currentLook: The journey crosses four visual languages: the ivory and forest desk (Enquiries), the dark cockpit cards (Pipeline and Proposals), white stock cards (Client search and profile), and the dark graphite client page. The Diary is light ivory again. Pipeline, Proposals and Client Search sit inside the 'More' menu (DashboardLayout.tsx:38-51, 178), behind Plan, Diary and Hallkeeper. Notifications also live inside More (226).
surfaces.dailyUse: This is a sales executive's entire working day.
slogFactors: The style changes at every hand-off, so each step feels like a different product.
The sales tools are two clicks deep, and so are notifications.

Four separate vocabularies describe where a deal stands, and no screen joins them: the enquiry state (EnquiryStages), the deal stage (STAGE_LABELS), the proposal status (STATUS_COLORS) and the Diary hold (BOOKING_KINDS).
workflowGaps: Step 1, Enquiries desk. Approve… emails the client, and 'Create opportunity' is offered next (EnquiryPanel.tsx:290-299). Pressing it only raises a toast (EnquiriesView.tsx:461-472) and nothing opens. Pressing it again toasts 'Existing opportunity opened', and still nothing opens. Venue admins and hallkeepers get a 403 toast (api crm.ts:29-32).

Step 2, More > Pipeline. Find the new card, which reads '£0.00 · Guest count pending guests'. The value cannot be set. The stage moves through a select, and 'Create proposal draft' makes an empty draft while silently failing to advance the stage.
Step 3, More > Proposals. Find the draft in a 20-row list, oldest first. Compose from blank. 'Generate client link' sends it. Copy the raw URL into your own email.
Step 4, the client approves on the graphite page. Staff are most likely not notified, and the deal's stage does not change.

Step 5, contract and deposit, does not exist. There is no contract, e-signature, deposit, payment or invoice in the schema or the UI. T-459, 'Add contract, e-sign, payment, accounting, and invoice integration hooks', is not started (docs/state/tasks.md:249), and so is T-094, the Stripe integration (tasks.md:365).

The Diary supports prospect → hold → ink (types/src/booking.ts:39-99) and records which enquiry a hold came from (api db/schema.ts:3298-3301). It has no link to deals or proposals, so 'ink' (confirmed) is set by hand with no contract or deposit check.
The desk's AI proposal wording (EnquiryPanel.tsx:450-460) cannot be carried into a proposal.
So today, enquiry → opportunity → proposal → client acceptance works, with the gaps above. From acceptance to a signed contract and a paid deposit there are no steps in the product.
strengths: Each step has an honest state machine on the server: enquiry transitions, OPPORTUNITY_STAGE_TRANSITIONS, VALID_PROPOSAL_TRANSITIONS and VALID_BOOKING_TRANSITIONS.
Creating a deal from an enquiry is transactional and idempotent: it returns the existing deal instead of creating a duplicate (crm.ts:75-88, 95-160).
Client share tokens are stored as hashes and can expire or be revoked (proposals.ts:1024-1030).

recommendations.change: For sales roles, put the sales tools in the top navigation: Enquiries, Pipeline, Proposals, Clients, Diary, keeping Plan and Hallkeeper for the roles that use them. Show a visible notifications count.
recommendations.why: The tools used all day are hidden in a menu.

recommendations.change: Make every hand-off open the next thing with the list kept beside it: the desk opens the deal, the deal opens the proposal composer, and the proposal links back to its deal.
recommendations.why: Removes dead ends and lost context. This is the core of 'make everyone's life easier' for this cluster.
One visual family across the whole sales journey, without copy-pasting CSS.

recommendations.change: Show one deal path in every panel: Enquiry → Opportunity → Held → Proposal → Accepted → Contract signed → Deposit paid → Confirmed. Each step reflects the real state of the record that owns it. The current step is copper and completed steps are sage, with one consistent vocabulary.
recommendations.why: Visible progress and closure across the whole sale, which neither Salesforce nor Cvent shows at a glance.
Closes the sale inside the product, and is the core promise of 'everything Cvent offers and more'.

questionsForBlake: Is contract and deposit in scope now? If so, which e-signature provider (DocuSign, Adobe Sign or our own), and should deposits be taken in the product (for example Stripe payment links) or recorded from the venue's accounts (Xero or Sage)?
What confirms a booking at Trades Hall today: a signed contract, a deposit, or both? What deposit percentage and timing are normal?
Should approving an enquiry create the deal automatically, removing a click?
Which four or five destinations should a sales executive see in the top navigation?

crossCutting: The desk's tokens and parts are scoped to .enq-desk (packages/web/src/components/dashboard/enquiries/EnquiriesDesk.css:9-47). No other surface can reuse the ivory, copper, forest and sage palette, the chips, the path or the focus rings without copying them. Promote them to a shared desk layer first.

packages/web/index.html:95-113 applies the scale(1.06) hover pop plus brightness(1.15) to every button outside [data-calm-controls]. That covers pipeline cards, proposal rows, search result cards and the client's Approve button. The golden custom cursor (index.html:77-79) also applies to all of these routes.

The cyan focus ring #87e7f0 (packages/web/src/global.css:42-54) measures 1.22:1 on the desk's ivory #f2eddd by my calculation (the brief says about 1.4:1). Any surface moved to ivory needs the desk's ink and cream rings.

The whole app declares color-scheme: light dark with no body text colour (global.css:5-22), so any text without an explicit colour follows the operating system's light or dark setting. ClientSearchView and ClientProfile rely on it. Inference: some text becomes invisible (black on forest, or white on white).
Every non-desk dashboard view sits on forest #132b25 with 24px padding (DashboardLayout.css:92-93). Only the enquiries, diary and inventory surfaces have their own grounds.

Pipeline, Proposals, Client Search and Client Profile are pure inline styles. They cannot express pointer-gated hover, focus-visible, media queries or reduced-motion rules, so moving them to CSS is a prerequisite for desk parity.

The shared StatusBadge (packages/web/src/components/shared/StatusBadge.tsx:5-13) uses a stock UI-kit palette that fails AA: under review 2.86:1, approved 3.32:1, archived 2.34:1. ProposalsView's StatusPill fails too, down to 1.70:1.
Fonts: ProposalPage asks for 'Cormorant Garamond', which is loaded only in styles/fonts/quiz.css. None of the staff CRM views use Newsreader, the desk's serif, although site.css loads it everywhere.
A toast for every success (useToastStore in the pipeline, the desk's create-opportunity and search) contradicts the desk's calm-technology decision to have no toast per success.

Dates are formatted ad hoc: toLocaleDateString() with no locale, toLocaleString('en-GB') with seconds, and raw ISO strings. Promote the desk's enquiry-desk-format.ts helpers (eventDateParts, eventLead, relativeAge, venueDate) for app-wide use.

Role mismatch: the UI shows Pipeline to venue admins (DashboardPage.tsx:56,70; DashboardLayout.tsx:55-66), but the crm and opportunities APIs allow only role 'staff' or a platform admin (api routes/crm.ts:29-38; routes/opportunities.ts:36-44). Proposals and quotes do allow venue admins.

Paging: the proposals list silently shows only 20 rows, oldest-updated first (the web client drops the paging data). The pipeline is capped at 200, also oldest first. The desk's T-632 paging pattern should be reused.

There are no committed visual baselines for Pipeline, Proposals, Client Search or Client Profile. Only the client proposal page's comment-error state is captured, so Blake has not seen these views in any recorded form.
Client proposal decisions do not notify staff unless the proposal is linked to an event (api routes/proposals.ts:155-156, 199-200). That affects the notification centre and any future email.
Contract, e-signature, deposit and invoice do not exist anywhere (docs/state/tasks.md:249 T-459 and :365 T-094, both not started). The sales spine ends at 'proposal accepted' and 'opportunity won'.

surfaces.name: Pending reviews queue (ReviewsView list) and its entry points

surfaces.dailyUse: Inferred: approvers open it whenever a planner submits a layout, often from the 'Layout Awaiting Review' email. That could mean several times a week, with bursts before events. A visit is short triage (under a minute) before a detail review. It lives under 'More', so it is out of sight the rest of the time.
slogFactors: It is a wall of identical dark cards. None of the facts a booker decides on appear: no event date, room, planner or wait time. The only facts are guests and a US-format timestamp with seconds ('6/18/2026, 1:00:00 PM'), from toLocaleString() at ReviewsView.tsx:708.

Three different kinds of work are mixed without distinction. 'submitted' needs someone to start it, 'under_review' needs a decision, and 'changes_requested' waits on the planner. The API includes changes_requested in the pending set (api routes/configuration-reviews.ts:1031-1035). Its comment says 'a config the planner has revised needs re-review', but a revision re-enters as draft→submitted (types/configuration-review.ts:69), so these rows are someone else's move.
The page shows no sense of progress or closure. The '(n)' count is tiny grey text and nothing ticks down. The empty state is a dashed 'No pending reviews.' box rather than a settled 'All caught up'.
A manual Refresh button implies the list may be stale, and the list never refreshes itself.
Hovering a full-width card makes it swell 6% and brighten (index.html:102-106), the exact behaviour the desk removed.
The heading is set in Georgia, not the desk's Newsreader, and the page has no h1.
workflowGaps: The staff email's 'Open Review' button links to `${baseFeUrl}/dashboard/reviews/${config.id}` (api configuration-reviews.ts:474). The web router has no such route, so the catch-all sends staff to the public homepage (router.tsx:705-707). The email's call to action is a dead end.
A selected review is not addressable. selectedId is local state (ReviewsView.tsx:612), with no ?review= search parameter, so reloading or sharing loses the review.

Hallkeepers and planners can reach /dashboard (router.tsx:491-493). They see 'Pending Reviews' in More, because NAV_ITEMS has no staffOnly flag (DashboardLayout.tsx:41) and 'reviews' is missing from STAFF_ONLY_VIEWS (DashboardPage.tsx:56). The API then returns 403 (configuration-reviews.ts:1022-1027) and the view shows an error with a 'Retry reviews' button that can never succeed (ReviewsView.tsx:675-682).
The review queue sits behind 'More' with no count, so a waiting review is invisible from the Enquiries desk or the Diary.

Once a review is approved, rejected or withdrawn it disappears (handleStatusChange, ReviewsView.tsx:631-644). No UI can find a decided review again, and the approved→archived and rejected→archived transitions exist with no UI (archiveReview in api/configuration-reviews.ts:253 is never imported).
Opening a review replaces the list (lines 648-656). The desk fixed this for Enquiries: the reader loses their place, and no keyboard traversal exists.
strengths: The API sorts oldest submission first (configuration-reviews.ts:1054, 1074), which suits response-time triage.
Loading, error and retry states are honest and use the shared Activity components (ReviewsView.tsx:666-682).
Each card is a native button with a descriptive aria-label ('Open review for …', line 697).
The list and detail are role-scoped server-side, so venue tenancy is enforced.

recommendations.change: Rebuild the queue on the desk's shell. Reuse the .enq-* tokens and classes (or extract them into a shared desk stylesheet) and add data-calm-controls. Put it on an ivory sheet with an h1 in Newsreader. Add one summary sentence built from real counts, for example '2 layouts are waiting for a first look; the oldest was submitted 3 days ago. 1 is in review with Catherine.' Put the stage counts on the copper plane as filters: To start (submitted), In review (under_review), With planner (changes_requested). Lead each ledger row with an event-date tile, then the layout name in serif, then room · guests · planner, with a copper wait-time on rows that are waiting on the viewer.
recommendations.why: This matches the Enquiries desk Blake judged 'much cleaner … inviting' (EnquiriesDesk.css:9-64, 138-200, 257-326). It separates the viewer's work from the planner's and makes the distance to zero the navigation (the goal-gradient finding in docs/design/enquiries-desk-2026-09-24/README.md).

recommendations.change: Resolve the room name and Trades Hall room photo client-side with useVenueRooms, since the PendingReviewEntry already carries venueId and spaceId (api/configuration-reviews.ts:365-375). Extend GET /configurations/reviews/pending to return spaceName, planner name, the linked enquiry's preferredDate (the email context already joins it, configuration-reviews.ts:205-210), the latest snapshot version, and the reviewer's name from the most recent →under_review history row.
recommendations.why: Facts that decide come first: a veteran reads a layout request as 'which day, which room, how many, whose'. Today only guests is shown.

recommendations.change: Make the selection URL-addressable: /dashboard?view=reviews&review=<id> read from and written to useSearchParams. Change the email reviewUrl to that URL, or add a /dashboard/reviews/:configId redirect route.
recommendations.why: The 'Open Review' email button currently lands staff on the marketing homepage. The URL should also survive reload and sharing.

recommendations.change: Add staffOnly: true to the 'reviews' NAV_ITEMS entry and add 'reviews' to STAFF_ONLY_VIEWS, so hallkeepers and planners never see a view the API refuses.
recommendations.why: This removes a dead end with a permanent retry loop.

recommendations.change: Replace manual Refresh with a quiet re-read on focus and after each decision, and show a 'changed while open' notice as the desk does. Replace the dashed empty box with the desk's sealed 'All caught up' panel, which names what is with the planner.
recommendations.why: This gives visible progress and closure without chatter (the Amabile & Kramer and Weiser & Brown rows in the desk record).

recommendations.change: Add keyboard triage identical to the desk: ↑/↓ and j/k to move, Enter to open, Esc to close. Focus the panel heading on open and restore focus to the row on close.
recommendations.why: Every staff desk should share one learned grammar. Today opening a review unmounts the focused card, which drops focus to the body.

recommendations.change: Add a 'Decided' stage (the last 30 days of approved, rejected and withdrawn) with an Archive action for approved and rejected reviews. This needs a list endpoint.
recommendations.why: A booker checking 'what did we sign off yesterday?' has nowhere to look, and the archive transition has no UI.

api/src/routes/configuration-reviews.ts:474 (the reviewUrl) and web/src/router.tsx:705-707 (the catch-all Navigate to '/')
index.html:96-106 (hover pop without the data-calm-controls opt-out on this view)
questionsForBlake: Should layout reviews be their own desk, or a stage inside the Enquiries desk and event record? Many enquiries already show 'layout attached'.
What does the Trades Hall team call this step: 'layout sign-off', 'floor-plan approval', 'function sheet sign-off' or 'review'?
Should 'Layout reviews' move out of 'More' into the main navigation with a quiet count?
Should layouts that are 'with the planner' (changes requested) stay in the staff queue as their own stage, or leave it until the planner resubmits?

surfaces.name: Review detail (ReviewsView DetailView: header, facts, links, presence, timeline)
surfaces.currentLook: A cyan '← Back to pending reviews' text link sits above one full-width graphite panel (panelStyle, ReviewsView.tsx:81-89) with a heavy 70px shadow. The header is the name in 20px/700 sans, an uppercase status pill and a presence pill. Below it is a three-column grid of 13px grey facts, 'Guests: 120 | Submitted: … | Last updated: …', spread across about 1,390px (lines 457-466). Two outlined buttons, 'Open Layout' and 'Preview Sheet', open new tabs (lines 468-477). A small gold 'Actions' heading introduces a row of four or five buttons in four colour treatments (lines 479-540). A 'Timeline' follows, made of 11-12px rows of uppercase pills ('DRAFT → SUBMITTED') with US-format timestamps (lines 543-572).
surfaces.dailyUse: Inferred: a few minutes per layout, mostly spent in two other tabs (/plan and /hallkeeper) because the layout itself is not shown here.
slogFactors: The thing being approved is not on the page. The reviewer must open /plan/:id and /hallkeeper/:id in new tabs (lines 469-476) and hold the decision in their head across three tabs. The snapshot API (getLatestSnapshot and safeParseSnapshot) is already in the client, unused by this view. The snapshot carries the room and its dimensions, timing.eventStart and setupBy, guestCount, layoutStyle, totals.totalItems, diagramUrl, floorPlan and the planner's instructions (hallkeeper-v2.ts:181-240).

The facts are 13px grey labels spread edge to edge ('Guests: 120' far left, 'Last updated' far right in the baseline), which means a lot of eye travel and no hierarchy. There are no large light numerals and no date, room or version.

Four competing button colours sit in one row: a gold gradient, amber, salmon-red and outlined (lines 61-79). No single next step exists, and for the real 'submitted' state there is no primary at all (see the decisions surface).

The presence pill uses #1f4e9b text on a 13% cyan wash over graphite (lines 154-165). Computed from the source colours, that is 1.7:1, far under AA. The one collaboration feature is close to unreadable.

After every transition the whole Actions block is replaced by 'Loading review gates, transitions, and decision history...' while the context re-reads (lines 324-327, 482-486). The buttons vanish and the layout jumps, and the copy is jargon.
The timeline uses 11px dates in US format with seconds (line 553). The transitions read as pairs of uppercase pills rather than sentences ('Catherine started the review · 10:14').
A raw enum leaks into copy: 'No actions available for your role in state 'changes_requested'' (lines 534-538).
It uses the cyan (#68d8d2) and gold accent vocabulary of the rejected cockpit style.
workflowGaps: No 'what changed since the last version' view exists, although getSnapshotByVersion exists. On a resubmission after 'Request changes' the reviewer must re-inspect the whole layout.
The request-changes note from the previous round is buried in the timeline rather than shown as 'You asked for: …' beside the new version.

Presence only says who is viewing. It does not say who has claimed the review: under_review is described as claim-based (types/configuration-review.ts:24-25), and history already records changedByName.
The planner's identity and contact details are absent, so a booker cannot phone or email the planner from here.
There is no link from the review to the enquiry, client or event it belongs to, although the server already joins the enquiry for the email (configuration-reviews.ts:205-210).
strengths: Stale responses are guarded: contextRequest and actionOperation counters (lines 279-280, 296-322) prevent late responses overwriting a newer review.
Error copy is honest about what did not happen: 'Approval did not save. The layout has not been approved.' (line 367)
Live presence (use-review-viewers.ts) fails soft and leaves explicitly on unmount.
The timeline shows who acted and quotes notes.

recommendations.change: Present the detail as the desk's forest decision panel beside the queue. Open it with the Trades Hall room photograph (roomPhoto via useVenueRooms) fading into forest. Follow with the layout name in Newsreader, then three large light numerals: event date with weekday and lead time, guests, and room. Then the next step with a path Submitted → In review → Decision. Then the layout itself.
recommendations.why: This is the reference pattern: one focal point, facts that decide first, and the list never lost (EnquiriesDesk.css:380-523).

recommendations.change: Load the latest snapshot in the panel (getLatestSnapshot plus safeParseSnapshot, already exported). Show the floor-plan or diagram thumbnail, layout style, setup-by time, total items with the top five lines (for example '180 chairs · 18 round tables · 1 stage'), the planner's instructions and 'Version 3, submitted by <planner>'. Demote 'Open the layout' and 'Preview the hallkeeper sheet' to quiet secondary links.
recommendations.why: A reviewer should be able to decide without leaving the desk. This removes two tabs and the context-switching per review.

recommendations.change: Replace the presence pill with forest-ink text (cream on forest, at least 4.5:1). Pair it with a claim line derived from history: 'In review with Catherine since 10:14 · Alasdair is also looking'.
recommendations.why: This fixes a 1.7:1 contrast failure and turns presence into coordination, so two people do not review the same layout.

recommendations.change: Use venue-local British formatting from enquiry-desk-format.ts (venueMoment, venueDate, relativeAge) everywhere this view calls toLocaleString (lines 463, 465, 553, 708). Write the timeline as sentences with a dot rail, like .enq-timeline (EnquiriesDesk.css:627-634).
recommendations.why: Veterans read '18 Jun, 13:00' in venue time, not '6/18/2026, 1:00:00 PM'.

recommendations.change: Keep the actions area mounted while context re-reads. Show a quiet Activity status in place of the next step instead of unmounting it, and rename the loading copy to 'Checking what you can do next…'.
recommendations.why: This stops the layout jump after every decision.

recommendations.change: For resubmissions, show a 'Changed since version N' block: a diff of totals entries and guest count between the latest and previous snapshots, with the earlier change-request note quoted above it.
recommendations.why: This solves a problem other platforms ignore: re-checking an entire layout after a small revision.

recommendations.change: Show the planner's name and email and a link to the linked enquiry or client profile in the panel's contact section.
recommendations.why: This keeps context and lets the booker call or email the planner in one step.

evidence: desktop-reviews-action-error-chromium-linux.png: facts spread across the full width, 11px timeline, four button colours.
ReviewsView.tsx:137-179 (presence colours at 161-164). My script composited the source colours over #132b25 and computed 1.7:1; this is computed, not browser-measured.
api/configuration-reviews.ts:295-312 (getLatestSnapshot and getSnapshotByVersion, unused in ReviewsView); types/hallkeeper-v2.ts:120-127, 181-240
questionsForBlake: Which facts must be in view to sign off a layout? I propose date, room, guests, layout style, setup-by time, total chairs and tables, and the planner's notes. Is anything missing, such as dietary or AV requirements or fire capacity?
Should the review show the live 3D room, or is a floor-plan thumbnail with the room photograph enough for the decision?

surfaces.name: Review decisions: Start review, Approve, Request changes, Reject, Withdraw (with the NoteModal dialog)
surfaces.audience: venue staff / venue admin; the consequences reach the planner or client and every hallkeeper
surfaces.currentLook: Buttons: Start Review and Withdraw are outlined secondary, Approve is a gold gradient, Request Changes is amber and Reject is salmon-red (ReviewsView.tsx:61-79, 502-533). A 'Notify team' checkbox appears only for demo-eligible reviews, with an uppercase 'DEMO ONLY:' line (lines 507-513). Reject and Request Changes open a full-screen modal: 82% black with cyan and gold radial glows, a dark card with an 18px title, one sentence and a textarea (NoteModal, lines 197-265). Approve and Withdraw act on a single click. Success and failure both raise toasts as well as inline alerts.
surfaces.dailyUse: Inferred: each review ends in one decision and usually starts with Start review. The decision is the most consequential click on this surface.
slogFactors: Approve is a single click with no statement of consequence. The server then emails the planner (configApproved, configuration-reviews.ts:649-665) and every hallkeeper at the venue (hallkeeperNotified, lines 669-685). It also freezes the snapshot, pre-renders the PDF and emits an approval.recorded event for webhooks (lines 606-647). The staff email itself warns 'Approving will freeze the layout snapshot and notify the hallkeeper' (email-templates.tsx:460-462), but the UI never says it.

Withdraw is a single click and terminal. withdrawn has no outgoing transitions (types/configuration-review.ts:72), and the route sends no email (configuration-reviews.ts:834-870). Staff can silently end a planner's submission, and the planner is not told. It is styled exactly like Start Review and sits beside it.

For a real 'submitted' review a staff member can only move it to under_review or withdrawn (config-review.ts TRANSITIONS; types:67). The screen then shows two identical outlined buttons, Start Review and Withdraw, with no primary. The committed baseline, which shows Approve next to Start Review, comes from a mocked transition list (dashboard-state-visual-performance.spec.ts:408) and is not a real state.

The Request Changes dialog says only 'Your note is saved in review history' (line 590). The note is actually emailed to the planner (configChangesRequested with the note, configuration-reviews.ts:815-826). The consequence is hidden.
The difference between Reject and Request changes is never explained. Reject is not final either: the planner can start a new draft (types:70, rejected → draft).

A 409 conflict is reported as 'Approval did not save. The layout has not been approved.' (line 367), even when a colleague already approved it (INVALID_TRANSITION) or the planner changed it (SNAPSHOT_CONFLICT, 'The review changed. Refresh before approving.', configuration-reviews.ts:597). The message may be untrue, and the panel does not re-read.
The modal is heavy: a full-viewport dark overlay for a one-line note. The desk replaced this with an inline confirmation in the panel.

Messages are doubled: every success raises a toast ('Review started', 'Layout approved — team notifications requested') and every failure raises a toast plus an inline alert. In the baseline, 'Failed to approve' sits in the header over the account name while the same message appears inline.
The shouting uppercase 'DEMO ONLY:' label is set 13px with no hierarchy (line 511).
workflowGaps: Approval accepts an optional note that is included in the planner's email (ReviewNotificationBody, configuration-reviews.ts:84, and note: trimmedNote, line 663). The UI never offers it (handleApprove passes no note, lines 358-359).
After Start review, a second round-trip re-reads transitions before Approve appears, so the reviewer waits and clicks again.
After a decision the view jumps back to the list (setSelectedId(null), line 642). No next review is offered and no stamp or closure is shown.
No 'undo' or grace period exists for Approve, although approval emails are fire-and-forget after commit.
strengths: The reject and request-changes notes are required client-side and server-side (NoteModal canConfirm; RequiredNoteBody).
The Reject dialog does state that the note is emailed to the planner (line 578).
