In-flight guards and operation counters prevent double submission and late updates (lines 332-435).
The note dialog traps focus and focuses the textarea first (useFocusTrap), and Escape cancels.

recommendations.change: Make the next step a single cream primary in a fixed place, with the path Submitted → In review → Decision. For 'submitted' the primary is 'Start review', which happens at once with the line 'Only your team sees this. Nothing is sent to the planner.' (verified: start-review sends no email, configuration-reviews.ts:500-531). For 'under_review' the primary is 'Approve…', with 'Request changes…' and 'Reject…' as quiet secondaries.
recommendations.why: One next step, always in the same place, as in EnquiryPanel.tsx:268 and EnquiriesDesk.css:525-566.

recommendations.change: Turn Approve into an inline confirmation in the panel, following the pattern at EnquiryPanel.tsx:314-387. Name the planner's email and say 'and the 3 hallkeepers at Trades Hall'. State 'Version 3 becomes the hallkeeper's set-up sheet and is locked'. Add an optional note labelled 'Included in the email to <planner>'. Extend GET /available-transitions (or add a small endpoint) to return the planner's name and email and the hallkeeper count, using the existing loadReviewEmailContext.
recommendations.why: The desk states real consequences before consequential external actions. Approval currently emails several people and freezes the sheet without saying so.

recommendations.change: Put Withdraw behind an inline confirmation that says 'This ends the review for good. <planner> is not emailed and would need to submit again.' Offer an optional note. Alternatively, remove Withdraw from the staff surface and leave it to the planner (see the question).
recommendations.why: It is terminal, silent to the planner, and currently one click, styled like Start Review.

recommendations.change: Correct the Request changes copy: 'Emails <planner> your note, quoted, with a link to edit the layout. They can revise and submit again.' Add the Reject copy: 'Emails <planner> your note. This version will not be used; they can start a new draft from it.' Set both inline in the forest panel with the brick and amber left rules (.enq-confirm[data-tone]), not in a modal.
recommendations.why: This removes a hidden consequence and makes the two decisions distinct in plain words.

recommendations.change: Handle 409 honestly. On INVALID_TRANSITION or SNAPSHOT_CONFLICT, re-read history and transitions and say what happened, for example 'Catherine approved this at 10:14' or 'The planner changed the layout; version 4 is now waiting', as the desk does for 422 (docs/design/enquiries-desk-2026-09-24/README.md).
recommendations.why: Error copy must not claim something untrue, and the reviewer should see the current state without reloading.

recommendations.change: Replace success toasts with in-panel closure: a status-chip stamp (the 320 ms .enq-chip--stamped, removed under reduced motion), the stage count ticking down, and the panel offering the next waiting review. Keep one inline error and no duplicate toast.
recommendations.why: This gives visible progress without chatter and removes the toast that covers the account name.

recommendations.change: Rewrite the demo-only checkbox as a calm sentence: 'Send notifications — untick to approve for an internal demo without emailing the planner or hallkeepers.'
recommendations.why: Remove the shouting uppercase while keeping the consequence explicit.

evidence: ReviewsView.tsx:352-373 (Approve with no confirmation), 417-435 and 529-533 (Withdraw with no confirmation, same style as Start Review at 503), 587-597 (the request-changes description), 575-586 (the reject description), 507-513 (the demo label)
api/src/routes/configuration-reviews.ts:606-687 (approve side effects), 745 (reject email), 815 (request-changes email), 834-870 (withdraw, no email), 500-531 (start-review, no email)
packages/web/e2e/dashboard-state-visual-performance.spec.ts:408 (the mocked availableTransitions behind the four-button baseline)
questionsForBlake: Should venue staff be able to withdraw a planner's submission at all? If so, should the planner be emailed? Today it is terminal and silent.
Should Approve always confirm, naming who is emailed? I recommend yes, because it emails the planner and every hallkeeper. Or do you want it as instant as Start review, with an Undo window instead?
Should hallkeepers receive the approval email by default for every approved layout, or only for events in the next N days?

surfaces.name: Reference loadouts library (LoadoutsView: room selector and loadout grid)
surfaces.audience: hallkeepers and venue staff/admin, who can manage (canManageVenue); planners also see it but cannot create
surfaces.currentLook: The dark forest ground carries a row of plain room pills. The selected pill differs only by a slightly brighter gold wash and text colour (LoadoutsView.tsx:214-227). Below them sits a full-width graphite panel with an h3 'Reference Loadouts' in Georgia 22px/650 and a gold-gradient 'New Loadout' button (lines 229-236). Then comes a grid of 240px graphite cards showing only the name (15px/700) and 'N photos' in 12px grey (lines 270-285). The cards carry heavy 70px drop shadows (panelStyle, lines 24-30). The global 6% hover swell applies to every card and pill.
surfaces.dailyUse: Inferred: occasional. The library is maintained when a standard set-up is created or re-photographed, perhaps a few minutes per week per venue. Hallkeepers would consult it before a set-up if it were surfaced where they work (it is not; see the gaps).
slogFactors: It is a collection of photos shown without a single photo. The list API already returns coverFileKey (api/loadouts.ts:19; reference-loadouts.ts:63), but the cards ignore it and show text only.

Room selection is by colour only. The pills have no aria-pressed or aria-current, so the selected room is not announced (lines 216-225). No room photograph appears, although roomPhoto() exists for Trades Hall.

One thing has three names: 'Reference Loadouts' (line 231), 'setup packs' (line 255, 'Loading setup packs...') and 'reference setup pack' (LoadoutDetail.tsx:246). The ellipsis is typed inconsistently: '...' here, '…' elsewhere.
Headings skip levels: the page has an h3 with no h1 or h2.
The empty state 'Add rooms in Admin to create loadouts.' (lines 249-253) gives no link to Admin.
Graphite cards with heavy shadows and gold borders are the rejected cockpit look.
workflowGaps: The web app has no consumer of loadouts outside this editor. A grep for 'loadout' in pages and hallkeeper components finds only DashboardPage and the dashboard views. The stated purpose, 'Add setup photos for hallkeeper preparation' (LoadoutDetail.tsx:338), is never delivered to the hallkeeper sheet, planner or review.

Planners see 'New Loadout' and the whole form, but POST is refused. canManageVenue allows only admin, staff and hallkeeper (api utils/query.ts:14-21), and the nav shows the view to any role (DashboardLayout.tsx:48, 55-66).
Cards omit the description and last-updated date, so choosing between similar set-ups means opening each one.
strengths: The room list and loadout list have separate retry paths with honest copy (lines 240-264).
The selected room is kept when the room list reloads (lines 120-123).
Cards are native buttons with descriptive labels (line 277).

recommendations.change: Rebuild on the desk shell (ivory sheet, data-calm-controls). Use an h1 with the venue's own word for these (see the question), then the room selector as a row of room tiles with the Trades Hall photograph from roomPhoto(), the room name in serif and the count of set-ups. Mark it up as a tablist or with aria-pressed.
recommendations.why: Veterans think room-first. Real photography is the moment of scale, and it fixes a selection state carried by colour alone.

recommendations.change: Make the loadout tiles photo-first using coverFileKey: a 4:3 cover image, the name in Newsreader, the description's first line in italic, and '6 photos · updated 12 Sep' in ink-3. Stack two offset planes behind a tile with several photos to suggest a set rather than a card.
recommendations.why: The tangible illustration and overlapping planes of the selected inventory reference; the data is already returned and unused.

recommendations.change: Choose one noun and use it everywhere. Replace 'Loading room list...' and 'Loading setup packs...' with Activity copy in that vocabulary.
recommendations.why: Three names for one thing make a veteran doubt whether they are the same.

recommendations.change: Hide 'New' and the editing affordances for roles canManageVenue refuses (planner), or hide the view for planners entirely.
recommendations.why: This stops a form that can only fail.

recommendations.change: Close the loop by showing a room's reference set-ups where the work happens: the hallkeeper sheet for that room, the review panel ('Compare with Grand Hall · Ceremony') and the planner's starting points.
recommendations.why: Photos nobody downstream sees are effort without reward. This is a problem competitors leave unsolved.

evidence: A grep for loadout consumers returned only DashboardPage.tsx, LoadoutsView.tsx, LoadoutDetail.tsx, AdminPanel copy, and the api/spaces and clients types.
questionsForBlake: What does the Trades Hall team call these: 'reference loadouts', 'standard set-ups', 'room set-ups', 'set-up photos' or 'house layouts'?
Who owns them: the hallkeepers, sales, or both? Should they appear on the hallkeeper's sheet, in the planner as starting points, or in client proposals as 'how the room looks set for a ceremony'?
Should a set-up carry its furniture counts, linked to Inventory (for example '180 Chiavari chairs · 1 altar table'), as well as photos?

surfaces.name: New loadout dialog (the create modal in LoadoutsView)
surfaces.currentLook: A full-viewport overlay of 82% black with cyan and gold radial glows (lines 289-299). On it sits a 420px graphite panel with a 20px/700 'New Reference Loadout' title and gold 12px/800 labels 'Name *' and 'Description'. The inputs are dark with sample placeholders ('e.g. Masonic Lodge Setup', 'Full ceremonial layout with altar table...'). Cancel and a gold 'Create' button sit at the bottom right (lines 288-336).
surfaces.dailyUse: Rare. It is used only when a new standard set-up is defined.
slogFactors: A modal blackout for two fields. The desk principle is no modal for routine internal steps.
Enter does not submit because there is no <form> element (lines 314-333), so keyboard users must tab to Create.
'Name *' uses an asterisk convention with no required attribute or aria-required.
It uses the cockpit colour vocabulary: gold labels, cyan glow.
workflowGaps: After Create the dialog closes and the list re-reads. The new loadout, whose id createLoadout returns (api/loadouts.ts:61-63), is not opened, so adding photos, the whole point, takes another find-and-click (handleCreate, LoadoutsView.tsx:162-182).
Nothing records which room the set-up is being created for. The dialog does not name the selected room, so a hallkeeper can create 'Ceremony' under the wrong room without noticing.
strengths: The create action has busy, error and retry behaviour (lines 162-182, 309-313, 330-332).
It is labelled with htmlFor and aria-labelledby, and the focus trap is active only while open (line 102).

recommendations.change: Replace the modal with an inline creation row at the top of the room's set-ups: 'New set-up for Grand Hall', with name, an optional description and 'Create and add photos'. Wrap it in a <form> so Enter submits, and mark the name required.
recommendations.why: This names the context (the room), removes a modal and follows the one-action-per-routine-step principle.

recommendations.change: On success, open the new set-up's detail with the photo drop area focused.
recommendations.why: It removes a step at the moment the user most wants to continue.

questionsForBlake: Should creating a set-up start from photos (drop photos, then name it) rather than from a name?

surfaces.name: Loadout detail (LoadoutDetail: name, uploader, photo grid, captions, reorder, delete)
surfaces.currentLook: Four stacked full-width graphite panels. First comes a cyan '← Back to loadouts' link and the name panel (20px/700 sans title with a 12px cyan 'Edit name' link, lines 273-322). Then a panel containing a 120px dashed drop-zone with a 📷 emoji and 'Click or drag photos here' (FileUploader.tsx:120-127). Then a grid of 200px photo cards with 150px images. Without R2 these fall back to #f3f4f6 blocks with #999 filenames, and each card has an 11px row of 'Move Up · Move Down · Remove' text links (lines 342-440). Last is a panel holding only a salmon-red 'Delete Loadout' button (lines 443-450). In the baseline the grey blocks are the brightest objects on the page.
surfaces.dailyUse: Inferred: occasional editing sessions of a few minutes (uploading and captioning a set of photos after a set-up), plus quick look-ups if the page were linked from the hallkeeper workflow.
slogFactors: The caption editor overflows its card. The input is flex:1 without minWidth:0 (line 393), so 'Save' is clipped past the card edge. This is visible in desktop-loadout-caption-error-chromium-linux.png.

The photo fallback is a pale #f3f4f6 block with #999 text, 2.59:1 contrast computed (lines 374, 381). It glares against the dark page and is built by imperative DOM injection in onError (lines 368-378).

Controls are tiny: Move Up, Move Down and Remove are 11px text buttons with padding 0 (lines 419-436). Inferred: that makes targets of about 13-15px, under the 24px minimum of WCAG 2.2 2.5.8, and the disabled links render at 2.71:1.
The drop-zone is a 120px dashed box above the photos (FileUploader.tsx:28-33). It dominates the page for an occasional action, and its 'JPEG, PNG, WebP' hint computes to 4.38:1 at 11px, under AA.
A whole panel is spent on a destructive red 'Delete Loadout' as the page's last and heaviest element.
It is a stack of four identical panels, the 'walls of identical cards' pattern the brief rules out.
Success toasts ('Photo added', 'Photo removed', 'Loadout deleted') fire for routine steps.
Drag reordering has no visible handle or keyboard equivalent beyond the text links, and the comment says it 'swaps' when the code moves (lines 181-208).
workflowGaps: The room is never named on the detail page, so the user loses context about which room this set-up belongs to.
The description cannot be edited. updateLoadout accepts description (api/loadouts.ts:65), but the UI edits only the name (lines 100-114, 273-318).

Upload and link are two steps with mixed signals. FileUploader marks a file 'Done' in #22c55e once it reaches storage (FileUploader.tsx:143), then LoadoutDetail links it (lines 116-130). If linking fails, the user sees 'Done' beside an alert saying the file could not be linked.
Captions save only on Enter or a tiny Save link. Blur does nothing, so tabbing away silently abandons the edit.
The first photo is the cover (sort_order 1 in the list API, reference-loadouts.ts:63), but nothing says so.
The Delete copy says 'This cannot be undone.' (line 455), but the API soft-deletes by setting deletedAt (reference-loadouts.ts:204-232). An Undo is technically possible and not offered.
strengths: Every mutation is guarded by busyAction with honest inline errors (lines 100-179).
Reordering has a non-drag alternative with file-specific aria-labels (lines 420-434).
Removing a photo states that the file stays in storage (line 467).
Loading uses the shared ActivityStatus, and upload shows real progress (FileUploader.tsx:141).

recommendations.change: Recompose as one ivory sheet. A header gives the room and the set-up ('Grand Hall · Ceremony'), a description editable in place, and '6 photos · updated 12 Sep'. The photos form a generous grid (about 280px tiles, 4:3), with the first marked 'Cover' and order numbers shown. The whole grid is the drop target, with one quiet 'Add photos' button in the header.
recommendations.why: This matches the selected style's ivory sheet and tangible imagery. The photos become the page instead of one of four panels.

recommendations.change: Fix the caption editor. Add minWidth: 0 to the input, save on blur and Enter, cancel on Esc, and confirm quietly with a small 'Saved' in ink-3 instead of refreshing the whole loadout.
recommendations.why: The overflow is visible in the committed baseline, and blur-abandon loses work.

recommendations.change: Replace the #f3f4f6/#999 fallback and the DOM-injecting onError with a rendered state: a sheet-coloured tile with the filename in ink (at least 4.5:1) and a small 'Preview unavailable'.
recommendations.why: This fixes a 2.59:1 contrast failure and the glare on a dark page.

recommendations.change: Give each photo a 44px drag handle that also works from the keyboard (focus the handle and use ↑/↓, announced as 'Moved to position 2 of 6'). Move 'Remove' into a small per-photo menu. Drop the 11px text-link row.
recommendations.why: Target size, keyboard parity and a calmer tile.

recommendations.change: Show uploads as placeholder tiles in the grid with Activity progress. Mark a tile 'Added' only after addPhoto succeeds, and remove the 📷 emoji and the #22c55e 'Done'.
recommendations.why: This gives one honest status per photo and shows progress where the photo will live.

recommendations.change: Demote delete to a quiet text action at the foot of the sheet ('Remove this set-up'). Because the API soft-deletes, replace the confirmation with an Undo for a short window, which needs a restore endpoint, or keep the confirmation and use the brick token instead of #dc2626.
recommendations.why: This removes the heaviest red element from an everyday page and keeps consequences honest.

recommendations.change: Stop success toasts for photo add, remove, reorder and rename. The visible change is the confirmation. Keep inline errors only.
recommendations.why: Calm technology: no toast for every success.

evidence: desktop-loadout-caption-error-chromium-linux.png: the clipped Save, grey placeholder blocks, 11px link row and full-width Delete panel.
Computed contrast from the source colours: #999 on #f3f4f6 = 2.59:1; the dropzone hint rgba(246,241,232,.48) on its wash = 4.38:1; disabled links rgba(.34) = 2.71:1.
questionsForBlake: Does photo order matter to the hallkeeper, as a walk-through sequence? If not, the reorder controls can become a single 'Set as cover'.
Should hallkeepers be able to add a set-up photo from their phone at the end of a set-up, with a one-tap 'Add to Grand Hall · Ceremony'?

surfaces.name: Shared confirmation and upload components used here (ConfirmModal, FileUploader)
surfaces.audience: venue staff / hallkeepers (shared across the dashboard)
surfaces.currentLook: ConfirmModal is a full-viewport 82% black overlay with cyan and gold radial glows and a 400px dark card. It has a 16px/700 title, one 14px sentence, and a Cancel button beside a default #dc2626 (Tailwind red-600) confirm with white text. The busy label reads 'Working...'. FileUploader has a dashed gold drop-zone with a 📷 emoji, a 'Done' status in #22c55e (Tailwind green-500), and a cyan underlined 'Retry'.
surfaces.dailyUse: Whenever a loadout or photo is removed or uploaded. The same components are used by other dashboard surfaces (inferred from the shared location).
slogFactors: Generic library colours: the #dc2626 confirm and the #22c55e 'Done' are out of palette, and the brief explicitly rules out generic library colours.
The emoji icon is off-style and renders differently per platform.
'Working...' tells the user nothing about what is happening.
workflowGaps: ConfirmModal's message is a single string, so it cannot structure 'what changes / who is told / can it be undone'.
FileUploader's 'Done' is emitted before the owning view has finished linking the file.
strengths: The focus trap moves focus in, restores it to the opener, and ignores hidden or disabled nodes (use-focus-trap.ts). Cancel is the first focusable element, a safe default for destructive actions.
The busy, error and retry paths exist, and the progress percentage is real.

recommendations.change: Give ConfirmModal a desk variant that renders inline in the owning panel (the .enq-confirm pattern). It should take a question, a consequence sentence and a tone (brick, amber or sage) instead of a colour string, and name the action on the busy label ('Removing photo…').
recommendations.why: One confirmation grammar across the app, honest consequences, and no modal-on-page.

recommendations.change: Give FileUploader a compact mode (button plus parent-provided drop target) and an onLinked handshake, so 'Done' reflects the owner's success. Replace the emoji and library colours with desk tokens.
recommendations.why: This removes a false-success signal and off-palette colour.

crossCutting: The global cockpit button spring (scale(1.06) and brightness(1.15) on hover, scale(0.93) on press) applies to every button on these three surfaces, because only the Enquiries desk carries [data-calm-controls] (index.html:96-110; EnquiriesView.tsx:514). Full-width review cards and loadout tiles swell 6% under the pointer. Blake has decided to remove it everywhere (product-experience.md, 'Hover motion').
The golden SVG cursor applies to every non-homepage route, including these (index.html:77-78). It is a cockpit-era leftover out of keeping with the selected style.

The dashboard ground is the dark forest #132b25 for every view except Enquiries, Inventory and Diary (DashboardLayout.css:92-99). ReviewsView, LoadoutsView, LoadoutDetail, ConfirmModal and FileUploader each duplicate the same inline graphite panel, alert, gold-gradient and cyan-link style objects (e.g. ReviewsView.tsx:54-99, LoadoutsView.tsx:18-83, LoadoutDetail.tsx:24-64). Extract the .enq-* tokens (EnquiriesDesk.css:9-47) into a shared desk stylesheet with shared button, confirm, chip and timeline classes, so every staff surface moves together.

The global cyan focus ring (#87e7f0, global.css:42-54; house-tokens.css:79) passes on the current dark panels (12.5:1 computed) but computes to about 1.2:1 on ivory #f2eddd. Once these surfaces move to ivory they need the desk's ink-on-ivory and cream-on-forest rings (EnquiriesDesk.css:84-90).

Toasts are fixed at the top right (ToastContainer.tsx:26) and cover the header's account name in both committed baselines. These surfaces toast every success and duplicate every inline error. Adopt the desk rule: no toast for routine success, one inline error.

Dates use new Date(...).toLocaleString() (US format with seconds in the baseline). Move shared venue-local formatters (venueMoment, venueDate and relativeAge in enquiries/enquiry-desk-format.ts) to a shared module for all staff surfaces.
The serif is Georgia on these surfaces (ReviewsView.tsx:661; LoadoutsView.tsx:203, 231; LoadoutDetail.tsx:244), not the desk's Newsreader. None of the three views renders an h1.

Nav and role scoping drift: the dashboard nav shows 'Pending Reviews' and 'Reference Loadouts' to any role that reaches /dashboard (DashboardLayout.tsx:55-66), while the API allows reviews only for staff and admin and loadout management only for staff, admin and hallkeeper. Planners and hallkeepers hit 403 dead ends. A single role-capability map should drive both the nav and in-view affordances.

The staff email 'Open Review' link (/dashboard/reviews/:id, api configuration-reviews.ts:474) has no web route and falls through to the homepage (router.tsx:705-707). Audit every email template's CTA URL against router.tsx.

The committed visual baseline for reviews uses a mocked availableTransitions list that the real state machine cannot produce for 'submitted' (dashboard-state-visual-performance.spec.ts:408 versus types/configuration-review.ts:67). Future baselines should use real transition sets so visual review judges real states.

use-review-viewers.ts sends a heartbeat on every 5 s poll tick and again on a separate 10 s interval (lines 53-80), about 18 heartbeats a minute per open review. This is not a design issue, but worth tidying when the panel is rebuilt.

cluster: Analytics, venue settings, admin and onboarding

surfaces.name: Executive analytics
surfaces.audience: Venue admin, staff and hallkeepers (through More). For the web-only 'executive' role it is the whole app. Planners (a customer role) can open it, and so can platform admins.
surfaces.dailyUse: Inferred: a GM or director of sales glances at it for 5 to 10 minutes each morning or week and before meetings. For the executive role it is the only page, so they use it every session.
surfaces.currentLook: Near-black cards (rgba(9,14,16,0.94) with a gradient and a 70px shadow) on the #132b25 forest-black dashboard ground. Labels are 12px, weight 850, uppercase cyan #8ff8f2. Numbers are gold #f1c978 at 28px, weight 800. The h2 is bold Georgia, not the loaded Newsreader. The utilisation bar is cyan #68d8d2. The layout is a grid of 4 identical KPI cards, then 2 cards, then 2 more. There are no charts, no period and no motion beyond the global spring on Refresh. Every style is inline (ExecutiveAnalyticsView.tsx:11-35, 188-208). In the 1440x900 baseline the content ends near y=560 and the rest of the screen is an empty dark field.
slogFactors: It is a wall of identical cards with no hierarchy. The eye must read eight cyan uppercase labels to find what matters (ExecutiveAnalyticsView.tsx:102-180; desktop-executive-analytics-success baseline).
Money reads like machine output: 'GBP 4,750.00' instead of '£4,750' (types/src/revenue-analytics.ts:278-284).

Raw enums and code-style plurals appear on screen: 'Comfort status review_required; 2 review gate(s).' (ExecutiveAnalyticsView.tsx:160), '1 review bottlenecks' (line 141), and 'review gate(s)' generated by the API (services/revenue-analytics.ts:131).

The subtitle is the API's compliance literal, 'Commercial planning insight - review constraints preserved.', which is jargon with a hyphen standing in for a dash (ExecutiveAnalyticsView.tsx:96; types/src/revenue-analytics.ts:245).
There is no period, no 'as of' time and no comparison. generatedAt is fetched but never shown (types/src/revenue-analytics.ts:236; not rendered). Veterans read pace against the same time last year.
Every number is a dead end. 'Review bottlenecks 1' cannot be opened to see which proposal or room it means.
Only the first revenue scenario is shown and the others are silently hidden (ExecutiveAnalyticsView.tsx:89).
Cyan labels at weight 850 and gold numerals at weight 800 shout. Neither colour is in the selected palette.
The error state shows the raw server string ('t469 analytics unavailable' in the baseline; in production, 'Insufficient permissions' or 'Admin analytics requests must provide venueId').
The global scale(1.06) spring runs on Refresh and Retry (index.html:96-111).
workflowGaps: The labels misstate what the numbers measure. 'Room utilisation' is accepted quotes ÷ all quotes for that room (services/revenue-analytics.ts:88-90), not occupancy of dates or space. 'Pipeline value' is the sum of every non-deleted quote of any status for all time (routes/revenue-analytics.ts:331-332). 'Enquiry conversion' is accepted proposals ÷ all enquiries ever (services/revenue-analytics.ts:60-61). A veteran will read all three differently.

Inferred from source: a platform admin always gets an error. The view calls getVenueDashboardAnalytics() without a venueId (ExecutiveAnalyticsView.tsx:57), and the API returns 400 for platform admins who omit it (routes/revenue-analytics.ts:57-64).

Inferred from source: planners (customer role) see 'Executive Analytics' in More (DashboardLayout.tsx:55-66) but receive 403, because canManageVenue excludes them (api/src/utils/query.ts:14-21; routes/revenue-analytics.ts:73-75).

The 'executive' role is routed in the web app (DashboardPage.tsx:65-76; DashboardLayout.tsx:61) but does not exist in USER_ROLES (types/src/user.ts:19). The API gives it no analytics grant, so the executive-only experience exists only in mocked e2e tests.
In the executive baseline, their only destination is hidden under 'More' (DashboardLayout.tsx:178, 209-228).
There is no drill-through to Proposals, Enquiries, the Diary or rooms, and no export or print for a board pack.
strengths: Loading, error and retry are honest, use the shared ActivityIndicator and set aria-live and role=alert (ExecutiveAnalyticsView.tsx:70-86).
Money is computed in minor units, so there is no float drift (types/src/revenue-analytics.ts:278).
The empty states say how to populate each panel ('Link quotes or events to rooms to see utilisation.', line 128).
Its data is already venue-scoped, with server-side authorisation (routes/revenue-analytics.ts:51-81).

recommendations.change: Name each metric for what it measures and show its scope. Relabel 'Room utilisation' as 'Quotes accepted, by room' and 'Pipeline value' as 'Quoted value, all quotes' until real occupancy and open-pipeline metrics exist. Show 'As of 14:05, Thursday 24 September' from generatedAt.
recommendations.why: The current labels will be misread by veterans. That is an honest-consequence failure and it erodes trust in every number on the page.

recommendations.change: Format money as £4,750 (Intl en-GB currency, no pence on whole pounds). Humanise enum values (review_required becomes 'Needs review'). Fix the plurals. Replace the disclosure literal with a plain sentence.
recommendations.why: These remove the machine voice that makes the page feel unfinished.

recommendations.change: Match nav visibility to API authority. Hide Analytics from planner and client. For a platform admin, pass a venueId from a venue picker or hide the view. Then either add a real executive role (API plus USER_ROLES) or remove the web-only branch.
recommendations.why: This removes 403 and 400 dead ends and a persona that does not exist.

recommendations.change: Rebuild the page on the desk composition. The ivory sheet carries an h1 'Performance' in Newsreader and a one-sentence summary built from real counts, such as '£4,750 quoted across 7 proposals; 3 await the client's answer.' A copper plane holds 3 to 5 light Newsreader numerals (Quoted, Accepted, Awaiting answer, Conversion), and each numeral is a link to its filtered list. A forest side panel titled 'Needs you' lists the review bottlenecks and comfort warnings as rows showing room and event, with one primary next step, and ends in a sealed 'Nothing waiting'.
recommendations.why: Facts that decide come first, the next step always sits in the same place, and the wall of cards goes. This is the pattern Blake called 'not a slog'.

recommendations.change: Add a period switch (This month / Quarter / Year / Financial year) with the same period last year alongside it. Use a per-room bar in sage and copper and a 12-month on-the-books sparkline (dataviz palette, AA 3:1 for marks). Give period switching keyboard shortcuts ([ and ]).
recommendations.why: Veterans judge pace and trend, not cumulative all-time totals. A period switch is also what Salesforce and Cvent dashboards offer.

recommendations.change: Add a print/PDF 'board pack' of the current period.
recommendations.why: It removes a spreadsheet step executives take today (an inference from the tools Blake says the team uses).

questionsForBlake: Who reads this page? The GM, the owner, the director of sales, or the whole sales team? Should ordinary staff see money totals?

Which 3 to 5 numbers decide your week? For example: confirmed revenue on the books by month against last year, enquiry-to-confirmed conversion, response time to new enquiries, average spend per head, or room occupancy by date.
How should 'utilisation' be defined: days booked ÷ days available per room, or sellable hours?
When does Trades Hall's financial year start? Should figures be net or VAT-inclusive?
Should the 'executive' role become a real account type?
evidence: packages/api/src/routes/revenue-analytics.ts:57-75,331-336 (venueId required for platform admin; all-status quote sum)

surfaces.name: Venue settings
surfaces.audience: Venue admin, staff and hallkeeper can edit. A planner (customer role) can open it but cannot save. A platform admin sees 'No venue assigned'.
surfaces.dailyUse: Rare: at setup, then a few minutes a quarter. It is also a first-impression page when a venue joins.
surfaces.currentLook: Dark panels (#141b1c to #0b0d0d gradient plus a cyan radial glow) with gold borders and a 70px shadow (VenueSettings.css:7-17). The 30px h2 is Georgia at weight 650. Labels are 12px, weight 850, uppercase. Inputs are translucent on dark with a cyan focus border. The primary button is a gold gradient at weight 900. A cyan 'Saved' pill turns amber when dirty. On the right, a 'Public preview' card shows a 74px colour tile with initials or the logo, then Slug and 'Room records' counts. There are four fields in total.
slogFactors: The page is called Settings but holds four fields: name, address, a hex brand colour and a logo URL (VenueSettings.tsx:215-275). The venue-level decisions a booker actually lives with are not here.
The brand colour is a hex text box and the logo must be pasted as a URL (lines 241-273). Venue staff do not host logo files or think in hex.
'Slug' and 'Room records 2' are developer vocabulary, and the room count is not a link (lines 310-319).
Labels are Title Case ('Venue Name', 'Brand Colour', 'Save Changes'), while the rest of the app is moving to sentence case.
A green 'Saved' pill shows on first load, before anything has been done (lines 201-204).
An error appears twice, as a toast and inline (lines 147-151). Every success also gets a toast, against the desk's calm-technology rule.
Input focus uses outline:none, a faint cyan border and a 13% glow (VenueSettings.css:104-118), overriding the global ring. The indicator is weak, and it would vanish entirely on ivory.
The global spring hover applies to Save, Reset and Retry.
workflowGaps: The preview makes a false promise. brandColour is read nowhere outside this form, onboarding and the seed (a grep across api/src and web/src). For Trades Hall, the planner's name and crest are hard-coded (use-planner-venue-identity.ts:50-53), so edits here do not reach clients.

Inferred from source: a planner can open the page and edit the fields (DashboardPage.tsx:65-72 allows any role), then Save returns 403 'Insufficient permissions' (venues.ts:111-128; utils/query.ts:14-21).
A platform admin is told to 'Ask an admin to assign your account to a venue' (VenueSettings.tsx:167-176), a dead end for the most senior role.
Inferred from source: there is no unsaved-changes guard when switching views. Only inventory holds navigation (DashboardPage.tsx:148-161).
There is no 'last changed by / on' record.
strengths: Dirty tracking, Reset, and a Save button disabled until the form is valid (VenueSettings.tsx:95-115).
Inline validation messages with aria-invalid (lines 257-273).
The preview updates live, and the save state is announced through role=status and aria-live.
Load, error and retry use the shared Activity component.

recommendations.change: Remove the 'Public preview' framing and the brand colour field, or state exactly where each value appears ('Shown on proposals and in the planner header'). Only offer settings that actually change something a client sees.
recommendations.why: Intelligent design means naming real consequences. The current preview implies client-facing effects that do not exist.

recommendations.change: Show a read-only summary with 'Only venue administrators can change these' to roles the API refuses (planner). Give platform admins a venue picker instead of 'No venue assigned'.
recommendations.why: It removes an editable form that can only fail.

recommendations.change: Rebuild the page on the desk composition. An ivory sheet holds sections in a calm ledger: Identity; Rooms, linking to rooms with capacities; Commercial terms; Client communications. A forest panel beside it, 'What clients see', renders the real planner header, proposal cover and email header from these values.
recommendations.why: One focal point per screen, consequences visible before saving, and context kept.

recommendations.change: Replace the logo URL field with an upload that has a crop preview. Offer a small curated swatch set (if Blake wants venue colour at all) instead of a hex box.
recommendations.why: This removes a task staff cannot do unaided.

recommendations.change: Add an unsaved-changes guard on view change, and show 'Last changed by Elaine, 3 Sept' once audit data exists.
recommendations.why: It prevents silent loss and answers 'who changed our address?'

questionsForBlake: Which venue-wide settings does Trades Hall keep today in Salesforce, Cvent, sales-and-catering software or spreadsheets? For example: hold expiry days, deposit percentage, payment terms, VAT, terms and conditions, email signature, office hours.
Should client-facing pages (proposals, portal, planner chrome) carry the venue's own colour, or always the Venviewer selected style with only the venue's logo and photography?
Should editing the venue name here replace the hard-coded 'Trade's Hall of Glasgow' in the planner?
Should hallkeepers be allowed to change the venue name and address? The API currently allows it.

surfaces.name: Admin: venue registry, rooms and room-hire pricing
surfaces.audience: Platform admin (Venviewer staff) setting up venues. Inferred: venue admins would want the rooms and pricing half.
surfaces.dailyUse: Occasional: in bursts during venue onboarding, 10 to 30 minutes when drawing rooms and entering prices. Mistakes here flow into every quote.
surfaces.currentLook: Near-black panels with gold borders and heavy shadows. The kicker is cyan uppercase ('Platform admin'). Headings are Georgia. Primary buttons are a gold gradient with a glow, secondary buttons cyan, danger buttons a red wash (AdminPanel.css:7-16, 50-139). The registry is a grid of 150px-tall card-buttons showing name, address, '/slug' and 'OPEN VENUE' in cyan uppercase (AdminPanel.css:314-352). The detail view opens with 'Back to venues', then a header with the venue name and a red 'Delete Venue' at top right, then three metric tiles (spaces, pricing rules, 'public slug'), a Spaces record list with Edit and Delete, and a 'Room Hire Pricing' table. The form modals sit on an 82% black backdrop. The error-state baseline shows a 1334px-wide gold 'Retry' bar.
slogFactors: The first control beside the venue's name is the destructive 'Delete Venue' (AdminPanel.tsx:491-499), placed where the next step should be.
Rooms read as '12m x 20m x 7m' plus 'slug: grand-hall' (lines 543-544). A room's defining facts for a booker (capacities by layout style) do not exist in the Space model (types/src/space.ts:101-116).
Money shows as `£${toFixed(2)}` with no thousands separator, so £12500.00 (AdminPanel.tsx:39-42). The type column shows lowercase 'flat rate' (line 44), while the select shows 'Flat Rate'.
Buttons use Title Case throughout ('New Space', 'New Rule', 'Create Space', 'Save Changes').

The venue registry is a wall of identical big card-buttons. Each one swells under the global scale(1.06) spring with a brightness flash. The global selector's specificity (0,3,2) beats .admin-panel-button:hover's (0,3,0) (index.html:102-106; AdminPanel.css:82-88).
Loading and error states stretch the Retry button across the whole panel, because .admin-panel-state is a grid with no justify-items (AdminPanel.css:354-361; desktop-admin-registry-error baseline).
Raw server text is shown ('t469 venue registry failure' in the baseline).
The detail view replaces the registry, so context is lost ('Back to venues', lines 471-484).
workflowGaps: The delete confirmations are untrue. They say spaces, pricing rules, configurations and loadouts 'will be permanently removed' or 'removed' (AdminPanel.tsx:755, 770). The API only sets deletedAt on the one row (venues.ts:136-150; spaces.ts:250-273), and no restore exists. They also never say how many bookings, enquiries or layouts reference the room.
Deleting a pricing rule is one click, with no confirmation and no undo (AdminPanel.tsx:632-643). Room and venue deletes do ask for confirmation. The behaviour is inconsistent.

'Tiered' can be chosen, but tiers cannot be entered (AdminPanel.tsx:743-748). The calculator adds nothing when tiers is null (price-calculator.ts:153-166), yet the table shows '£500.00 · tiered · Active'. Every estimate would silently omit that hire charge.

The pricing model supports minimum hours, minimum guests, day-of-week and seasonal modifiers, and validity dates (types/src/pricing.ts:59-77). None are exposed, and rules cannot be edited, only deleted and re-created.

Inferred from DOM click semantics, not reproduced: the backdrop closes the modal on click (AdminPanel.tsx:63-74). Dragging a polygon vertex and releasing outside the dialog dispatches the click to the backdrop, which closes 'New Space' and discards the outline and name (setSpaceOutline([]) on lines 658-662). Esc also discards without asking.
There is no view of room setup completeness per venue (outline, height, prices, photos).

The committed baseline desktop-admin-create-venue-error-chromium-linux.png shows a retired sidebar layout ('VENUE COMMAND') and copy that is not in the current source, so it does not evidence the current UI.
strengths: Stale-request guards on venue and pricing loads (useLatestRequest, AdminPanel.tsx:246-291).
Mutations disable Back while pending (line 474).
Modals trap focus, and the entrance respects reduced motion (AdminPanel.css:384-404).
Every row button has a specific aria-label ('Delete space Grand Hall').
A slug preview and a minimum-three-points polygon guard.

recommendations.change: Make the delete copy honest now. Say 'Hidden from staff and clients. Venviewer support can restore it.' and list the affected counts (rooms, future bookings, open enquiries, layouts). Require typing the venue name to delete a venue. Move Delete Venue to a quiet 'Close this venue' section at the foot.
recommendations.why: It states the real consequences and takes the destructive action out of the primary position.

recommendations.change: Remove 'Tiered' from the type list until tiers can be edited, or build the tier editor. Format amounts as £12,500. Add undo (an 8 s inline 'Rule deleted · Undo') to pricing deletes. Allow rules to be edited.
recommendations.why: It stops silent under-quoting and one-click data loss.

recommendations.change: Stop closing the form modal on a backdrop click when it holds unsaved changes. Confirm before Esc discards a drawn outline.
recommendations.why: It prevents losing several minutes of room drawing.

recommendations.change: Rebuild the page on the desk pattern. Venues become ledger rows (serif name, address, room count, setup stage, last activity). The selected venue opens in a forest panel beside the list, with a setup path (Rooms outlined → Heights → Prices → Photos → Ready) and one next step. Rooms become rows showing their capacities and price. Use ivory tokens, calm controls and an ink focus ring.
recommendations.why: Context is kept, progress and closure become visible, and the card wall goes.

recommendations.change: Add room capacities by layout style (theatre, banquet, cabaret, reception, boardroom) as first-class room facts, including in the API and schema.
recommendations.why: It is the first fact a veteran asks about a room, and it is part of Cvent and venue sales-and-catering parity.

recommendations.change: Expose minimum hours, minimum guests, day-of-week and seasonal modifiers, and validity dates in a pricing editor that previews a sample quote ('Saturday, 120 guests, 6 hours → £4,200').
recommendations.why: It uses the model that already exists and lets admins see consequences before saving.

questionsForBlake: Should room capacities per layout style be first-class? Which styles does Trades Hall sell?
Who should manage rooms and prices: only Venviewer staff, or each venue's own admin?
Should deleted venues and rooms be restorable, and by whom?
How does Trades Hall price room hire today (day rates, sessions, minimum spend, seasonal)? That tells us which pricing controls to build first.

surfaces.name: Clients & access (onboarding)
surfaces.audience: Platform admin (Venviewer staff) onboarding venue clients and their people.
surfaces.dailyUse: Weekly or per new client: 15 to 30 minutes per onboarding, then short visits to fix access.
surfaces.currentLook: The closest in scope to the selected style. The shell is ivory (#f4f1e9) with paper panels (#fbf8ef). A forest hero band (#17382d) carries a 540px hairline circle and a decorative Building2 icon. There is a copper eyebrow (#8a5435), Georgia headings, numbered step circles, a sage contact block (#eef0e2) and a copper-bordered 'Share the account link' box. Status chips come in sage, amber, brick and slate, always with words. The focus ring is copper #9b653e (4.57:1 on paper). But the whole shell floats inside the dark #132b25 ground (DashboardLayout.css:92). Type is small: labels .79rem, notes .78rem, member meta .7rem, chips .65rem (OnboardingView.css:43, 54, 75, 77). The ivory values nearly match the desk's but are not the same (#fbf8ef/#17382d against #f2eddd/#264337).
slogFactors: The hero takes a large forest band to show only 'Clients & access' and an icon. It gives no facts, such as how many clients or who is waiting (OnboardingView.tsx:224). There is also a dead rule for a hero paragraph that does not exist (OnboardingView.css:14).
Clients are chosen from a <select> (OnboardingView.tsx:226), so you cannot see all clients' setup stage or waiting invitations at once.

Raw enum values appear in dropdowns: 'admin invite', 'pending review', 'not required', 'provider verified', 'manual invoice' (OnboardingSetupControls.tsx:7, 43, 46, 55, 59; tablet-onboarding baseline).

'Plan key' is free text pre-filled with 'managed_deployment' (OnboardingView.tsx:53, 115). Time zone is free text 'Europe/London' (line 103). 'Customer / Entitlement / Provider evidence reference' is developer vocabulary.
Chips at 10.4px and meta at 11.2px tire the eyes over a long session. They pass AA contrast (4.87 to 5.75:1 measured) but are too small.
Errors render at the bottom of the section, far from the button that caused them. In the baseline, the setup-review failure sits under the billing column (OnboardingSetupControls.tsx:68).
Setup review and billing are two separate Save buttons inside a disclosure.
Disabled primaries fade to 55% opacity with no reason given (OnboardingView.css:30). 'Grant venue access' in the baseline is an example.
The segmented toggle buttons pick up the global spring inside an overflow:hidden container.
workflowGaps: No invitation is sent. The admin copies a generic /register link and emails it by hand (OnboardingView.tsx:27-42, 127).
An expired invitation cannot be renewed in one click. It takes Manage access, then Save venue access, and the path is explained only in a note (line 192).
An active member cannot be removed or suspended. Only pending invitations can be cancelled (UI lines 185-186; API routes/onboarding.ts:295-337), so there is no offboarding when staff leave.
Cancelling an invitation is one click with no undo (line 185).
The audit events are loaded but never shown (types/src/onboarding.ts:403; no render in the view), so 'who granted this and when' is lost.
The setup stage is a dropdown, not a visible path from intake to ready (types/src/onboarding.ts:29-38), so progress and closure are invisible.
strengths: Plain consequence lines: 'No email will be sent. Existing venue records are preserved.' and 'Access starts after email verification.' (lines 110, 127).
Numbered steps with the billing options behind progressive disclosure (line 112).
Status chips are doubled with words and carry expiry dates in en-GB.
A confirmed creation stays visible even if the follow-up read fails (lines 217-222). Request-id guards prevent stale reads.
Counts use a serif numeral ('2 connected', '1 awaiting sign-in'), already in the desk idiom.
The copper focus ring passes 3:1 on paper.

recommendations.change: Humanise every enum label ('Admin invitation', 'Awaiting review', 'Not required'). Replace Plan key with a select of real plans and Time zone with a select. Place each error next to the Save that produced it. Raise chips and meta to at least 12.5px.
recommendations.why: Machine vocabulary and tiny type are the main slog on an otherwise near-conforming page.

recommendations.change: Rebuild the page on the desk pattern. A clients ledger shows each client as a row: serif venue name, organisation, setup path, connected and awaiting counts, and the oldest waiting invitation. The selected client opens in a forest panel beside the list with one next step ('Renew 2 expired invitations', 'Mark ready'). The stage becomes the desk's path (Intake → Venue → Admin → Staff → Billing → Ready), sealed with a restrained 'Ready' stamp. j/k move between clients.
recommendations.why: All clients stay in view and progress and closure become visible, the patterns Blake judged inviting.

recommendations.change: Add a one-click 'Renew invitation' on expired rows. Add 'Remove access' for active members, stating the honest consequence ('Elaine can no longer sign in to Trades Hall. Her past actions remain.'). Show the already-loaded audit history as a quiet timeline.
recommendations.why: It closes the offboarding and renewal gaps and keeps provenance visible.

recommendations.change: Seat the shell on the sage ground and use the shared ivory, forest and copper tokens and Newsreader, replacing the near-miss values.
recommendations.why: It makes this page read as the same family as the desk.

questionsForBlake: Should Venviewer send invitation emails itself, from a named sender, or keep link sharing by hand?
Should a venue's own administrator be able to invite and remove their staff, or only Venviewer staff?
Is removing a leaver's access needed before Trades Hall goes live?
Should billing and entitlement verification stay on this page, or move to a separate operator-only area?

surfaces.name: Room outline editor (PolygonEditor)
surfaces.audience: Platform admin, or a venue admin, drawing a room's floor outline inside the Admin 'New Space' and 'Edit Space' modals.
surfaces.dailyUse: Rare: 2 to 10 minutes per room at setup, or when geometry is corrected. A wrong outline feeds every layout and capacity.
surfaces.currentLook: A fixed 400×400px near-black SVG (#071112) with a dashed origin crosshair. The polygon has a cyan #68d8d2 stroke and a 14% cyan fill. Handles are cyan and turn gold while dragged. A 12px readout reads '4 vertices — bounding box 10.00m × 10.00m. Right-click a vertex to delete.' Two 12px buttons follow, 'Reset to rectangle' and 'Clear'. All styles are inline (PolygonEditor.tsx:202-342).
slogFactors: Outlines are clicked freehand with no grid, rulers, scale bar or snapping, so points land on arbitrary decimals (canvasToWorld, lines 70-77). Veterans know rooms as '30 m by 15 m' and would rather type the dimensions.
A click always appends to the end of the point list (lines 144-146). Adding a corner mid-shape therefore creates crossing edges, and nothing checks for self-intersection.
Deleting a point needs a right-click (lines 163-171), a hidden gesture with no touch equivalent. The Delete key works only mid-drag (lines 173-181).
'Clear' and 'Reset to rectangle' wipe the work at once, with no undo (lines 183-191).
Dark cyan drafting sits on a dark modal, entirely off the ivory, forest and copper style.
workflowGaps: It is not keyboard operable, despite role='application' and tabIndex=0: focus lands on the canvas but no key adds, selects or moves a point (lines 208-216). This fails WCAG 2.1.1.
Inferred: it handles mouse events only (onMouseDown/Move/Up), so on a tablet a touch drag will not move points.
The fixed 400px canvas (lines 19, 206-207) overflows phone widths inside the 96vw modal and ignores the available 740px on desktop.
No floor plan or reference image can be traced over.
strengths: The viewport freezes during a drag so the target does not drift, then refits on commit (lines 116-120).
A minimum-three-points guard and a live bounding-box readout.
Stable keys and test ids, with the reasoning written up in comments.

recommendations.change: Add keyboard and pointer support. Tab or arrows select a point, arrows nudge it 0.1 m (Shift for 1 m), Delete removes it and Insert splits the selected edge. Switch to pointer events with setPointerCapture. Add Ctrl+Z undo covering Clear and Reset.
recommendations.why: It fixes an accessibility failure and removes irreversible one-click loss.

recommendations.change: Start from dimensions. 'Width × Length' fields generate the rectangle, followed by an editable corners table (x, y in metres). Snap to 0.1 m with a visible metre grid and scale bar. Insert new points on the nearest edge, and refuse crossing edges with a plain message.
recommendations.why: It matches how veterans know their rooms and prevents invalid geometry.

recommendations.change: Restyle as an ivory drafting sheet: ink hairlines, copper handles, a sage fill and Newsreader dimension labels. Make the canvas responsive with viewBox.
recommendations.why: It brings the editor into the selected style and fits every declared device.

recommendations.change: Allow tracing over an uploaded floor plan, or over the reconstruction's existing plan.
recommendations.why: It removes guesswork and uses sourced venue data.

questionsForBlake: Do you have measured floor plans for Trades Hall's rooms that we should trace, or should outlines come from the reconstruction?
Is room drawing a Venviewer-only job, or should venue admins do it themselves?

surfaces.name: Reconstruction Foundry release review (FoundryReleaseDetail, FoundryActionDialog, FoundrySigningControls)
surfaces.audience: Platform operators who review and promote reconstruction releases. No venue professional uses it.
routes: None. No route or parent view mounts these components; only __tests__/FoundryActivity.test.tsx imports them.
surfaces.dailyUse: None today, because it is not mounted. If mounted, it would be used occasionally per release.
surfaces.currentLook: It has no styling. All the runtime-foundry__* class names have no stylesheet anywhere in packages/web (a grep of .css files finds nothing). Mounted today, it would render as default browser HTML: full 64-character SHA-256 digests, 'in-toto statement', 'DSSE payload', 'Ed25519', 'TransformArtifact', 'Scene Authority Map', and lowercase status chips such as 'machine qa failed'.
slogFactors: Full digests and object keys are printed in bulk (FoundryReleaseDetail.tsx:229-237, 210-217).
Raw status values run through humanize ('ready to publish', 'approved · public') at lines 147 and 182.
The operator reason needs 20 characters, but the rule is enforced only by a disabled button, with no counter or hint (FoundryActionDialog.tsx:88, 145).
workflowGaps: There is no mount point. The router comment still says 'the Runtime Foundry dashboard links to it' (router.tsx:571-572), but no such dashboard exists in this tree.
The dialog's textarea sits outside its <form> (FoundryActionDialog.tsx:117-133), so the structure is unusual. This is an observation only; submit still works through the button.
strengths: Each action has honest consequence copy, including what does not change (FoundryActionDialog.tsx:14-45).
Blockers are listed explicitly before the actions (FoundryReleaseDetail.tsx:93-135, 528-535).
Preview loading shows its counts, can be aborted and revokes its object URLs (lines 313-402). The tabs support arrow, Home and End keys (lines 491-515).

recommendations.change: Decide whether this tool ships. If it does, mount it behind platform-admin, give it the desk composition (a release ledger, and a forest decision panel with a Review → Publish → Promote path and one next step), shorten digests to 12 characters with a copy button, and add a character counter to the operator reason.
recommendations.why: An unstyled orphan cannot meet the standard. Its consequence copy and blocker logic are already good raw material.

questionsForBlake: Should the Foundry release review be a visible operator tool in this app, or stay off the product until reconstruction work resumes?
evidence: No CSS file defines runtime-foundry__* (grep across packages/web)

crossCutting: There is no shared token layer for the selected style. The desk's ivory, forest, copper and sage tokens are scoped to .enq-desk (EnquiriesDesk.css:9-47). house-tokens.css is the dark back-of-house set and says 'FOH (ivory register) tokens are deliberately absent' (house-tokens.css:22). Every in-scope surface hard-codes its own palette: inline styles in ExecutiveAnalyticsView and PolygonEditor, and separate values in VenueSettings.css, AdminPanel.css and OnboardingView.css (whose ivory and forest nearly match the desk's but not exactly). Recommendation: lift the --enq-* tokens into a shared FOH layer before rebuilding these surfaces.
Every non-desk dashboard view sits on the #132b25 forest-black ground (DashboardLayout.css:92). Only the inventory, diary and enquiries views have their own grounds.

The global springy hover, scale(1.06) plus brightness(1.15) with an overshoot curve, applies to every in-scope button (index.html:96-111). Its specificity (0,3,2) beats the components' own hover rules, for example AdminPanel.css:82-88. Only the desk opts out ([data-calm-controls], EnquiriesView.tsx:514). Blake has decided to remove it app-wide.

Focus: the global cyan ring (--vv-focus #87e7f0; global.css:42-53, house-tokens.css:79) measures 1.22:1 on #f2eddd and 1.34:1 on #fbf8ef (computed). Any surface moved to ivory must switch to the desk's ink ring (cream on forest). VenueSettings sets outline:none on its inputs (VenueSettings.css:104-118).

Serif: the in-scope surfaces hard-code Georgia (ExecutiveAnalyticsView.tsx:94, VenueSettings.css:30, AdminPanel.css:33, OnboardingView.css:8,13, DashboardLayout.css:21) even though Newsreader is already loaded app-wide (index.html:15).

Headings: analytics, settings and admin render only an h2, and the shell has no h1 (the venue name is a

, DashboardLayout.tsx:194). The desk and onboarding use an h1.

All four surfaces show raw ApiError messages to users ('Insufficient permissions', 'Admin analytics requests must provide venueId', or the fixture strings in the baselines). Each surface needs a plain-language message layer.

The web nav and API authority disagree. Planner, a customer role, sees Executive Analytics and Venue Settings in More (DashboardLayout.tsx:55-66), but the API refuses both (utils/query.ts:14-21). The 'executive' role exists only in web routing (DashboardPage.tsx:65-76) and not in USER_ROLES (types/src/user.ts:19).

The 'More' menu holds up to 10 destinations plus Notifications, with mixed Title Case and sentence case ('Executive Analytics', 'Venue Settings', 'Pending Reviews' against 'Clients & access'; DashboardLayout.tsx:38-53). For the executive role, their only page is hidden behind More.
The shared ConfirmModal is dark-themed (ConfirmModal.tsx:11-18) and is used for the Admin deletes. It needs the desk's inline-confirmation pattern that names consequences.
Success toasts fire for every save (VenueSettings.tsx:147; AdminPanel.tsx:302,329,386,401,426,444), against the desk's calm-technology rule of no toast for every success.

The committed baseline operational-state-visual-performance.spec.ts-snapshots/desktop-admin-create-venue-error-chromium-linux.png shows a retired sidebar shell ('VENUE COMMAND') and copy absent from the current source. It is stale evidence and should be regenerated when these surfaces change.

The access-denied panel (DashboardPage.tsx:88-111; global.css:72-82) is dark with a bold 40px serif and quotes the internal view key ('The requested view "admin"…'). It should become a calm ivory state that names the page in plain words and offers the one permitted next step.

surfaces.name: Diary frame: header, toolbar, legend, loading and live states
surfaces.audience: venue staff (sales executives, bookers), venue admin; hallkeeper reads
surfaces.dailyUse: This is the landing frame for every Diary visit. Inferred: bookers and sales executives keep it open all day and return to it many times an hour, including during calls to check availability. Hallkeepers check it several times a day.
surfaces.currentLook:
Described from the CSS and TSX only: there is no committed Diary baseline PNG in packages/web/e2e/*-snapshots, and the design-qa evidence is private. The page is a flat, full-bleed ivory sheet (#f6f5ed, padding 28/30px) inside the dashboard shell. It has no sage ground, no tilted sheet and no copper plane. The title 'The Diary' is Georgia 500 at 32 to 46px and stands alone, with no date line and no summary sentence. Below it, one wrapping row holds about 13 equal-weight 38px buttons, each #fffef8 with a 1px #d7dcce border that measures 1.28:1 against the page:
- Day / Week / 2W
- Earlier / Today / Later
- a 14px bold range title ('Week of Mon 7 Sep 2026')
- Overview / Timeline
- a 12px 'Show released & cancelled' checkbox
- Refresh and How the Diary works
- a pale-copper 'New booking' primary
- a read-only note and a 12px 'Live · n' pill

A five-item 11px legend follows. Active toggles fill forest #2f5947. Body text is Inter (from the shell) and headings are Georgia. The CSS holds about 190 hard-coded hex values; the --diary-* colour tokens (brass, wax, paper) are defined but never used. Motion comes from the global springy hover pop on every button, and the Diary adds no press feedback. Changing the range swaps the whole board for a loading panel, and each refetch inserts an inline 'Refreshing the Diary…' row above the board.
slogFactors: There is no opening statement of what matters. The desk says '4 new enquiries are waiting…'; the Diary shows only 'The Diary' and then a toolbar. A booker must scan the grid to learn how many dates are provisional, which decisions are due, or whether anything is double-booked.

About 13 equal-weight controls share one wrapping row (DiaryBoardPage.tsx:618-711). Rarely used items (Refresh, How the Diary works, Show released & cancelled) carry the same weight as the everyday ones (Earlier, Later, Week). The primary 'New booking' sits in the middle of the row and moves as the row wraps, so the next step has no fixed place.
The orienting fact, which week you are looking at, is a 14px bold inline span between buttons ('Week of Mon 7 Sep 2026', board-time.ts:175-179). It is not a large light numeral as on the desk.

There is no way to go to a date. Range navigation offers only Earlier, Today and Later (DiaryBoardPage.tsx:634-664); no date input exists (grep finds none), and the palette searches only the loaded range (board-palette.ts:5-8). Checking a date nine months out in Week view means about 39 clicks of 'Later', and each click replaces the board with a full loading panel.

Every range change blanks the board. useCalendar hides the previous data while the new range loads (useCalendar.ts:77-79, pinned by the test 'hides previous range/venue data while a new identity loads'), and the page then renders the panel loader instead of the grid (DiaryBoardPage.tsx:732-733). Rooms, photos and scroll position all disappear on each step.

Inferred: a failed background refresh also replaces a loaded board with the error notice. The catch sets status 'error' even when data exists (useCalendar.ts:60-64, 80), and the page checks status === 'error' before it checks the data (DiaryBoardPage.tsx:724).

Every refetch shifts the layout. 'Refreshing the Diary…' and 'Saving booking moves…' are inserted into the flex column above the board (DiaryBoardPage.tsx:721-722). Refetches also follow colleagues' live changes (useDiaryLive calls refetch), so the board jumps whenever someone else edits. The tray reloads open enquiries on every data change too (deps [venueId, data, enquiryRetry] at DiaryBoardPage.tsx:193), which shows a second Activity row in the tray.

The global springy hover applies here. index.html:96-111 scales every button to 1.06, brightens it by 1.15 and presses it to 0.93, because the Diary root (DiaryBoardPage.tsx:613) lacks [data-calm-controls]. That rule's !important transition also replaces the Diary's own 160ms colour transitions (diary-board.css:39, 85).

The vocabulary is jargon, and the same concept is named several ways. The legend reads 'Inked — confirmed', 'Pencil — ranked option', 'Prospect — never blocks' and 'Occupancy footprint' (board-copy.ts:62-68), and '2W' is an abbreviation (board-copy.ts:22). Elsewhere the page says 'Confirmed', 'Pencilled · option 2', '2nd option', 'Ladder position' and 'Ladder'. None of this is the provisional / first option / second option language a veteran uses.
Presence is hidden: colleagues' names appear only in a native title tooltip on the Live pill (DiaryBoardPage.tsx:700-710). 'Reconnecting…' is plain text rather than the shared Activity component.
The legend is 11px #647267 (4.63:1). It passes AA but is small for the only key to the colour code.
workflowGaps: There is no 'is this date free?' path. This is the most frequent question a venue booker is asked, and it needs a go-to-date field plus an availability answer per room.

The only keyboard shortcuts are t / d / w / f / m, Ctrl+K and Ctrl+Z (DiaryBoardPage.tsx:530-546). No key moves to the previous or next range, creates a new booking, switches Overview/Timeline or shows a legend, and nothing lists the shortcuts on screen. The desk keeps its keyboard legend in the panel.
Month is reachable only by the hidden 'm' key or the URL (DiaryBoardPage.tsx:59-62), and it renders a 3px-per-hour timeline, not a month availability view.

Inferred: the global key handler does not exclude <select> (DiaryBoardPage.tsx:520-529). Type-ahead in the drawer's Room or Commitment select ('d', 'w', 't') would switch the board's view or date behind the open drawer.
'New booking' always opens on the first room at the first day of the range, 17:00 to 23:00 (DiaryBoardPage.tsx:367-376; drawer-form.ts:134-148). The user then has to correct the room and the date.
strengths: The page uses light ivory with forest active states and real, sourced room photography, so it is already far from the rejected dark board.
Deep links carry ?view= and ?date= (DiaryBoardPage.tsx:221-227), and the memoised range avoids re-render churn (lines 98-104).
Live updates arrive over /ws/diary with presence, honest reconnection and idempotent commands (useDiaryLive.ts).
Reduced motion is honoured for the Diary's own transitions (diary-board.css:263-265).
Loading and working states use the shared ActivityStatus, as the convention requires.
Dates are venue-local and DST-aware, in en-GB formats (board-time.ts).

recommendations.change: Mark the .diary-page root with data-calm-controls, or better, remove the global pop app-wide as Blake decided on 26 September. Add the desk's feedback: 120ms colour-only hovers gated to fine pointers, scale(0.97) press on buttons and no transform on booking cards.
recommendations.why: Blake explicitly asked for the springy pop to be removed everywhere (product-experience.md:34). It also distorts the precise timeline (see the Timeline surface) and cancels the Diary's colour transitions.

recommendations.change: Add a 'Go to date' control, bound to the g key, that accepts '5 Jun 27' or a date picker. Answer inline, per room, beside the grid: 'Sat 5 June 2027 — Grand Hall: free · Saloon: 1st option Fraser, decides 12 Oct'.
recommendations.why: This removes dozens of clicks and loading panels from the most common booking question. It is the 'small problem nobody solves' that would win over Cvent users.

recommendations.change: Keep the board frame while a new range loads: keep the room rail and photos, draw the new axis, and show Activity inside the cells. Prefetch the adjacent ranges. On a failed background refresh keep the loaded board and show a quiet 'Couldn't refresh at 14:02 — showing the last loaded diary. Retry' instead of the full error notice.
recommendations.why: This keeps context and avoids a blank flash on every week step, while staying honest about what is shown.

recommendations.change: Move 'Refreshing' and 'Saving' into a fixed-size status slot in the header, next to the Live pill, and show them only after about 400ms. Stop re-reading open enquiries on every calendar refetch; refresh them on their own cadence or on enquiry events.
recommendations.why: This removes the layout jump that each colleague's live edit now causes. Calm technology informs without demanding attention (Weiser & Brown, as cited in the desk record).

recommendations.change:
Rebuild the header on the desk pattern:
- a small-caps date line ('Saturday 26 September · Week 39'), with the greeting only if Blake keeps it on the desk
- a large serif range with light numerals ('7 – 13 September')
- one factual sentence built from real counts: 'This week: 9 confirmed and 4 provisional bookings across 5 rooms. 2 provisional decisions are due by Friday; 1 date is double-booked.'
recommendations.why: Facts that decide come first, and the page stops opening on a toolbar.

recommendations.change: Add a copper plane of large light numerals that double as filters, as the desk's stage band does: Confirmed · 1st option · 2nd+ option · Prospects · Decisions due · Conflicts. The counts tick when a hold is confirmed or released.
recommendations.why: Visible progress and a goal to drive to zero ('Decisions due'), grounded in the goal-gradient and progress findings in the desk record. It also makes the holds workflow the page's own structure.

recommendations.change:
Cut the toolbar down to:
- ‹ Today › and Go to date
- one segmented control: Day · Week · Fortnight · Month
- one Overview / Timeline switch

Move Refresh (redundant while Live), Show released & cancelled and How the Diary works into a quiet 'View' menu or the ? key. Rename 2W to 'Fortnight'.
recommendations.why: Fewer equal-weight choices, and the primary action stops moving.

recommendations.change:
Add keys for frequent work:
- [ and ] (or Alt+← →) for the previous or next range
- g to go to a date
- n for a new booking in the focused cell
- o to toggle Overview / Timeline
- ? for the legend

Show the legend permanently in the side panel, as the desk does. Exclude <select> in the global handler.
recommendations.why: This covers keyboard triage for high-frequency work (product-experience.md:25) and prevents surprise view changes while typing in a select.

recommendations.change: Replace the design tokens: adopt a shared token set with the desk (sheet #f2eddd, forest #264337, copper, sage, ink scale, focus rules) and Newsreader for the serif. Delete the unused --diary-* colour tokens and the roughly 190 hard-coded hex values.
recommendations.why: The Diary and the desk are the two all-day tools and should read as one family. The Diary now uses different ivories, four different forests and Georgia.

surfaces.name: Week / Fortnight overview (room × day booking summary)
surfaces.audience: venue staff (bookers, sales executives), venue admin; hallkeeper reads
surfaces.dailyUse: This is the default presentation for Week and Fortnight (DiaryBoardPage.tsx:96, 108). Inferred: it is scanned dozens of times a day, for minutes at a time.
surfaces.currentLook:
A white (#fffefa) rounded panel with a soft shadow and an intro line, 'Week overview · Open a day for the timeline.', in 11px #6c796e. Below it is an internally scrolling grid (max-height calc(100dvh − 265px)):
- a sticky 172 to 188px room rail with a sourced room photo (65×82 or 72×84), a Georgia 16px room name, 'N reception' and 'N bookings' in 12px #4d604e
- seven equal day columns; each day header is a 12px bold 'Mon 7 Sep' button with an arrow that appears on hover and a 10px forest 'Today' chip

Bookings are 88px-minimum cards with a 13px bold two-line-clamped title, a 12px tabular time and an 11px state label at 85% opacity. Fill colour carries the state: pale sage for confirmed, pale butter for provisional, a dashed near-white for prospect, grey-green for a house block, pale blush for a blocking conflict, and grey for exited bookings. A 10px 'Conflict' or 'Review' flag and a 9px uppercase 'Continues' marker complete the card. Phases appear as dashed boxes with 8px uppercase labels. Client and guests appear only in the native title tooltip and the aria-label.
slogFactors: Confirmed and provisional are not distinguishable at a glance. The butter hold fill #f5e9bf and the sage ink fill #d9e4cf differ by 1.08:1 in luminance, and a blocking conflict fill #f9e1d8 against a hold is 1.03:1 (computed). The difference is hue only, both pale, so a week's firm dates versus its provisional ones do not pop out (Few's preattentive principle, as cited in the desk record). Inferred: this is worse for red-green colour-vision deficiency.

The deciding facts for a provisional hold are missing from the card. No card shows its decision date or time to decide, its owner, or its guest count; guests and client appear only in a native tooltip (BoardOverview.tsx:61-63, 70).
The rank is buried in an 11px, 85%-opacity text label, 'Pencilled · option 2' (board-overview.ts:38-46; diary-board.css:95), rather than a numeral you can see across the room.
Every card and every day header is its own Tab stop, with no arrow-key grid navigation. A busy fortnight needs dozens of Tabs to reach Sunday.

Exited cards (with 'Show released & cancelled' on) put the status at 2.91:1 and the text at 3.68:1, both below AA (#758071 on #f3f2ec at opacity .85, computed). The phase labels are 8px uppercase (diary-board.css:101).
The day header is one small bold string, with no date-tile numeral like the desk's calendar tiles.
The empty state for a week with no bookings is a 12px grey line in the side column ('No bookings in this range.', DiaryBoardPage.tsx:769-771, 4.16:1), not in the grid.
Hover swells cards 6% (global pop). They sit in 133 to 145px columns, so a swollen card overlaps its neighbours (inferred).
workflowGaps: There is no per-day summary ('3 on · 1 decision due'), so a sales executive cannot see which days have open options without reading every card.

The overview cannot take an enquiry drag. onBeginEnquiryDrag is disabled in the overview (DiaryBoardPage.tsx:766), and the overview is the default view, so the drag hint and the drop only work after switching to Timeline.
The day header opens Day view, which is a context switch. The booking card opens the overlaying drawer, which hides the right-hand columns (see the Booking drawer surface).
There is no create-from-cell: an empty room and day cell cannot start a provisional hold for that room and date.
strengths: Honest summary contract: card width never implies duration, times are exact, and DST offsets are labelled (board-overview.ts:26-36; design-qa.md:38).
Real room photography from Trades Hall's supplied set, and no substitute photo for unknown rooms (BoardOverview.tsx:41-49).
Titles are readable at 13px with two-line clamps, and the full accessible name holds every fact (BoardOverview.tsx:71).
Overnight bookings keep one stable focus anchor, with 'Continues' on later days (board-overview.ts:61-63).
The sticky rail and axis, the weekend tint and the 'Today' chip are calm and orienting.
The index is built once per entries array, so the overview stays fast (board-overview.ts:48-122).

recommendations.change:
Encode the commitment by luminance, not hue alone:
- confirmed: forest fill (#264337) with cream text
- provisional: an ivory card with a copper numeral badge ('1st', '2nd'), and a copper 'decides in 3 days' age when the decision is 7 days or fewer away
- prospect: a dashed hairline
- house block: slate hatching
- conflict: a brick left bar plus a 'Double-booked' label

Keep the named status text on every card.
recommendations.why: A booker reads 'how firm is this week' at a glance: ink is dark and pencil is light, which is the Diary's own metaphor made visible. Forest against butter measures about 8.9:1, against 1.08:1 now.

recommendations.change: On each card, show guests as a light numeral and, for holds, the owner's initials and the decision date. Replace the native title tooltip with a styled focus or hover preview (client, guests, owner, decision, notes).
recommendations.why: Date, guests, room, stage and money are the facts that decide (product-experience.md:16). Native tooltips are slow, unstyled and unreachable by keyboard.

recommendations.change: Make the day headers date tiles: a small-caps weekday, a large light numeral and the month, plus a one-line day summary ('3 on · 1 to decide').
recommendations.why: This matches the desk's calendar tiles and adds scan-level facts.

recommendations.change: Add grid keyboard navigation with a roving tabindex: arrows move between cards and cells, Enter opens, n creates a booking in the focused cell, Home and End jump to Monday or Sunday.
recommendations.why: It turns dozens of Tab stops into direct movement, as with the desk's ↑ ↓ / j k triage.

recommendations.change: Fix the sub-AA text: exited status and text to at least 4.5:1 without opacity; phase labels at least 11px.
recommendations.why: WCAG AA text on every surface (product-experience.md:27).

recommendations.change: Let an empty cell accept a click, n, or a dropped enquiry slip to start a provisional hold prefilled with that room and day.
recommendations.why: This removes the 'New booking → change room → change date' steps.

recommendations.change: Add a true month or season availability view (rooms × dates, coloured free / provisional / confirmed) for 12 to 18 months ahead, replacing the hidden 3px-per-hour 'm' timeline.
recommendations.why: Weddings and dinners are sold a year or more out. Veterans think in months, and Cvent users ask for this at-a-glance availability.

Computed contrast: hold fill against ink fill 1.08:1; blocking fill against hold fill 1.03:1; exited status 2.91:1; exited text 3.68:1.
BoardOverview.tsx:61-63 builds the detail (title, time, state, client, guests) used only as title and aria. :73-75 renders only title, time, state and the conflict flag.
board-overview.ts:38-46: state labels such as 'Pencilled · option 2'.
DiaryBoardPage.tsx:766: enquiry drag is disabled when showingOverview.
design-qa.md:28-34: client and guests were removed from the cards to control density, and the busy first row is about 323px.
questionsForBlake: Are you happy for confirmed bookings to become dark forest cards, so a firm week visibly 'fills in', with provisional holds as light ivory with a copper option numeral?
Should booking value (hire fee, minimum spend, deposit status) appear on the cards, and if so which figure matters most?
