surfaces.name: Day view and precise Timeline (room lanes, drag, gaps, now line)
surfaces.audience: venue staff and admin (moving bookings); hallkeeper (event-day reading)
surfaces.dailyUse: Inferred: sales staff use it several times a day to adjust times or rooms and check changeovers. Hallkeepers use it daily on event days.
surfaces.currentLook:
A bordered ivory scroll region with a sticky pale-sage axis: 12px bold day labels and 10px #74816d hour ticks in Day view. Each room lane has a sticky 196px rail with a 58×72 photo, a Georgia 17px room name and 10px #77816e lines for capacity, 'n inked', 'n pencilled' and utilisation %.

Blocks are absolutely positioned 68px cards at 96px per hour (Day) or 18px per hour (Week timeline). Each has a 12px bold nowrap title that shares one row with the countdown and a 10px rank chip, an 11px time, a 10px client line and an 8px phase bar. Changeover gaps are dimension lines with 9px labels. Orphan phases are 16px dashed strips with 9px text. The 'Now' line is a 1px sage rule with a 9px white-on-sage plaque. A blocking conflict tints the card blush with a 9px 'Conflict' stamp. The drag ghost is a 2px sage outline, or brick when the drop is blocked.
slogFactors:
Information that matters is set at 9 to 10px and below AA:
- hour ticks: 3.64:1 at 10px (diary-board.css:136)
- rail counts, capacity and utilisation: 3.87:1 at 10px (:144)
- changeover durations: 3.11:1 at 9px (:170-172)
- phase strips: 3.87:1 at 9px (:169)
- the Now plaque: 4.29:1 at 9px (:178)

design-qa.md:32 fixed only the overview rail, not this rail.

The setup, live and teardown labels never render. The segment text is written when a band is at least 46px wide (BoardGrid.tsx:270), but .diary-block-segment sets font-size: 0 (diary-board.css:165). The phase is therefore told by colour alone: setup against the bar background measures 1.27:1 and setup against live 2.39:1 (computed). That fails the non-text contrast bar, and the only text is a title tooltip.

Inferred: the title is squeezed. Title, countdown and rank chip share one nowrap flex row (BoardGrid.tsx:204-214; css:159-160). On a Week timeline, an evening hold is about 108px wide, and 'joint 1st option' leaves the title a few characters before the ellipsis.

The global hover pop scales positioned blocks by 1.06 (index.html:102-105). On a precise timeline that visibly misstates start, end and duration under the pointer, and the 0.93 press shrinks a block just as a drag begins (inferred from the rules).
The rail's 'n inked · n pencilled · 42%' is terse jargon at 10px. The percentage's meaning ('Booked share of this range') exists only in a tooltip (BoardGrid.tsx:366-376).
A 15-minute booking is 24px wide at 96px per hour, and nothing shows on the card below 42px (TITLE_MIN_WIDTH, BoardGrid.tsx:40). That is honest, but the card becomes a blank sliver.
workflowGaps: You cannot create a booking by clicking or dragging on empty lane time. Lanes have no create handler.
Moving a booking has no 'swap rooms' or 'move to another day' shortcut beyond dragging and arrow nudges. Nudges exist (Space, then arrows) but appear only in the aria-label and welcome copy.
The toast after a move says 'Moved {title}.' without the new room and time (board-copy.ts:217).
For hallkeepers: 'Doors in 2h 05m' appears only on ink blocks within 4 hours (BoardGrid.tsx:43, 447-452). Setup and teardown timing cannot be read because the segment labels are invisible.
strengths: The keyboard drag is excellent: Space lifts, arrows nudge in 15-minute steps (or 1 minute with Shift), Enter drops, Escape cancels. It is announced for screen readers (useBoardDrag.ts:199-252; board-drag.ts:248-257).
The ghost carries its validity reason inline ('Overlaps "X" — two inked bookings cannot share a room'), so drag states the consequence before you drop (board-drag.ts:99-104).
Moving an ink needs explicit confirmation, while pencils move in one action with undo. That is the desk's 'confirm only the consequential' rule.
Optimistic moves use compare-and-delete rollback, and race messages are honest (DiaryBoardPage.tsx:282-317).
Turnaround gaps are dimensioned as guidance, flagged 'tight' only where the server engine measures them (board-layout.ts:153-220).
Performance care: memoised lanes and blocks, and the ghost re-renders only the lanes it enters or leaves (BoardGrid.test.tsx).

recommendations.change: Exempt the timeline blocks from all hover and press transforms. The hover becomes a border or ink colour change, and the press no more than scale(0.995), as on the desk's rows.
recommendations.why: On a timeline, geometry is data. A 6% swell misreports duration.

recommendations.change: Bring every timeline label to at least 12px and at least 4.5:1 (ticks, rail counts, gap durations, phase strips, the Now plaque). Use desk ink tokens such as ink-3 #55655c on ivory.
recommendations.why: These labels are sub-AA today. Hallkeepers and bookers read times and changeovers from them all day.

recommendations.change: Make the phase bands readable. Remove font-size: 0 so the Setup / Live / Teardown labels render where they fit (at least 11px), and add pattern or luminance contrast (hatched setup and teardown, solid live) of at least 3:1.
recommendations.why: This fixes colour-only meaning and gives hallkeepers their run of show.

recommendations.change:
Restructure the block face:
- line 1: the full-width title
- line 2: time · guests
- a copper rank numeral badge top-right for holds
- a copper decision countdown when the decision is 7 days or fewer away

Drop the chip text 'joint 1st option' in favour of '1=' with an accessible label.
recommendations.why: The title stays readable at Week-timeline widths, and the rank reads as a numeral.

recommendations.change: Drag across empty lane time (or click, then n) to open a new provisional hold prefilled with the room, start and end.
recommendations.why: This removes three corrections from every manual booking.

recommendations.change: Rewrite the rail as plain facts: 'Grand Hall · 300 reception', then '2 confirmed · 1 provisional', then 'Booked 42% of this week'.
recommendations.why: Veterans' vocabulary, readable without tooltips.

surfaces.name: Side tray: Needs attention, Open enquiries and Conflicts rail
surfaces.audience: venue staff (sales executives, bookers), venue admin; hallkeeper sees it read-only
surfaces.dailyUse: It is visible every session. Inferred: it is the booker's hygiene list for chasing holds, several times a day.
surfaces.currentLook:
A 254px column of pale-sage panels (#f1f3e9).

'Needs attention' has a forest (#2f5845) title band with Georgia 23px cream text and a count pill. Below it are ivory item buttons (a 13px bold title and 11px reasons), then an 11px uppercase 'OPEN ENQUIRIES' subhead. Enquiry slips show a name and 'eventType · N guests' with a small forest 'Pencil in…' button (11px, 32px high), plus an 11px drag hint.

'Conflicts' is a pale apricot panel (#f6e8de) with Georgia 23px title and native <details> groups: Blocking is open, while Warning and 'Ladder' are collapsed. Uppercase 11px headings carry counts and 'Review'. There is also a collapsed 'What was checked' disclosure in 10px text and the disclaimer. Below 1200px both panels move under the 72dvh board, off-screen.
slogFactors: 'Needs attention' covers only the week on screen. trayItems = needsAction(entries, nowMs), and entries holds only the loaded range (DiaryBoardPage.tsx:280). A provisional hold six months out whose decision date passed yesterday never appears unless you navigate to its week.

The open-enquiry slips omit the requested date and room. The tray maps only id, name, eventType and estimatedGuests (DiaryBoardPage.tsx:754-759) and drops preferredDate and spaceId, which the convert path does use (:378-396). The first fact a booker needs to pencil a date is missing.

The ladder (who holds 1st and 2nd option on a date) exists only as 'info' conflicts labelled 'Ladder', collapsed by default inside the Conflicts panel (BoardPanels.tsx:40; board-copy.ts:237). The core of the provisional workflow is hidden in a disclosure.

Several texts fall below AA:
- the empty states 'No overdue next actions.' and 'No conflicts detected in this range.': 4.16:1 and 3.89:1
- 'What was checked': 3.89:1 at 10px
- the drag hint: 4.16:1

(diary-board.css:106, 114, 126; computed.)

Clicking an attention item only scrolls to and focuses the block (BoardPanels.tsx:131-133; DiaryBoardPage.tsx:554-559). A second action is needed to open it, and there is no inline 'Extend a week', 'Confirm' or 'Release', although the reason text says 'release, extend, or ink' (board-layout.ts:302).
There is no closure. A clean tray shows grey text, with no sealed 'Nothing to decide' like the desk's 'All caught up'.
'Pencil in…' is a small 11px button (diary-board.css:113), and the conflict heading is 11px uppercase copper-brown (4.16:1).
workflowGaps: There is no 'due soon' horizon. needsAction flags only overdue next actions, passed decision dates or unranked holds (board-layout.ts:276-316), so decisions due tomorrow are invisible until they are late.

Holds with no decision date are never flagged. needsAction tests decisionAt only when it is not null, and a prospect promoted with 'Make it a pencil' gets no hygiene fields (see the Booking drawer surface).
The API documents T-7 / T-3 / T-1 hold reminders as not built (packages/api/src/services/hold-hygiene.ts:11-15).
Hallkeepers see client enquiry names and sales hygiene items they cannot act on. The panel is not role-aware.
Clicking a conflict focuses only the first of its two entries (BoardPanels.tsx:53).
strengths: Hold hygiene is the wedge Salesforce and Cvent users wish for: each overdue next action or passed decision is stated in plain language with the action to take.
The conflict engine is honest: severities are graded, 'not_checked' is never shown as OK, and a 'What was checked' disclosure exists (BoardPanels.tsx:65-73).
The forest title band is a first nod to the selected style's decision surface.
Enquiry loading and error states are honest: previous rows are kept and a retry is offered (DiaryBoardPage.tsx:165-193; tests at DiaryBoardPage.test.tsx:271-328).
A slip can be dragged onto a lane to open a prefilled pencil-in form.

recommendations.change: Make 'Needs attention' venue-wide with a new API query (active holds with a decision or next action overdue or due within 7 days, any date). Group it as Overdue (copper) and Due this week, show each item with a date tile, room, option numeral, owner and decision date, and open the booking directly.
recommendations.why: The workflow is chasing provisional holds before they lapse. Today it depends on which week happens to be on screen.

recommendations.change: Show each enquiry slip with a date tile for the preferred date, then room · guests · event type. Rename the action 'Hold as provisional…' at the desk button size.
recommendations.why: The first fact that decides is missing today. The date is already on the Enquiry object.

recommendations.change: Raise the empty-state, drag-hint and checks text to at least 4.5:1 and at least 12px.
recommendations.why: WCAG AA.

recommendations.change: Promote the ladder to a first-class 'Contested dates' list: 'Sat 5 Jun · Grand Hall — 1st Henderson (decides 12 Oct) · 2nd Fraser'. Give the 1st option inline actions: Confirm, Extend, Release.
recommendations.why: This is the provisional / first option / second option workflow, and it should be visible rather than a collapsed 'info conflict'.

recommendations.change:
Turn the side column into the desk's forest decision panel:
- with nothing selected it proposes the next move ('Next up · decides tomorrow — Henderson wedding, 1st option, Grand Hall', with 'Open' as the single primary) and holds the keyboard legend and a sealed 'Nothing to decide' closure
- with a booking selected it hosts that booking (see the Booking drawer surface)
recommendations.why: One next step, always in the same place, with visible closure (product-experience.md:23-24).

recommendations.change: Make the side panel role-aware. Hallkeepers get 'Today and tomorrow': doors, setup start and guests, with no client enquiries.
recommendations.why: Every professional is designed for, without showing tools they cannot use.

evidence: DiaryBoardPage.tsx:280 computes trayItems from range-scoped entries. :754-759 builds TrayEnquiry without preferredDate or spaceId.
board-layout.ts:276-316: needsAction rules (overdue only, decisionAt null not flagged).
BoardPanels.tsx:40: details open only for blocking. :131-133: tray item click focuses only. :147-190: enquiry slip content.
hold-hygiene.ts:11-15: the reminder job is deliberately not built.
Computed contrast: panel-empty 4.16 and 3.89; check 3.89; drag hint 4.16; conflict heading 4.16.
questionsForBlake: How long does a provisional hold last at Trades Hall by default, and what happens when a 2nd option wants to confirm? For example, does the 1st option get 48 hours to confirm or release (a 'challenge')? Should the Diary run that challenge with a visible countdown?
Should decision reminders go only to the owning colleague in-app, or also by email?
Should hallkeepers see open client enquiries in the Diary at all?

surfaces.name: Booking drawer (create, booking details / edit, pencil in an enquiry, lifecycle, floor plan)
surfaces.dailyUse: Opened for every booking touch. Inferred: many times a day per booker.
surfaces.currentLook:
A fixed 430px panel on the right edge (#fcfcf5, a sage hairline border and a soft left shadow) that overlays the board and tray. It has a Georgia 27px title ('Booking details' / 'New booking' / 'Pencil in this enquiry') and a plain 'Close' button. In edit mode a pale-sage box shows the title (21px Georgia) and client and guests in 13px.

Then comes a full form of 40px inputs with 12px labels: Commitment, Room (disabled in edit), Title, Event type, Starts and Ends as datetime-local, and a 'Pencil hygiene' fieldset (Ladder position number, Joint first option, Decision date, Next action, Next action due, 'You will own this pencil.'). Notes appear only when creating. Save and Discard follow, then a 'Floor plan' box, then 'LIFECYCLE' with equal buttons (Ink it in copper; Release, Mark expired, Mark lost, Cancel the ink). Every success closes the drawer and raises a toast.
slogFactors: It is form-first, not facts-first. Opening a booking shows the title, client and guests, then a wall of 9 to 13 editable fields. The date, time, room, status ('1st option'), decision date and owner are never stated as facts (BookingDrawer.tsx:303-307 onwards). The desk opens with large numerals (date, guests, room) and one next step.

The next step sits at the bottom. The lifecycle buttons (Ink it / Release…) come after the form and the floor plan (BookingDrawer.tsx:515-534), so their position shifts with the booking kind and they are usually below the fold in a 430px panel.

Raw developer messages reach users. issuesToFieldErrors passes Zod messages through unchanged (drawer-form.ts:177-186), for example 'A hold requires decisionAt — pencils carry a decision date, an owner, and a dated next action (hold hygiene).' (booking.ts:146-151) and 'endsAt must be after startsAt — a booking occupies a real interval.' (booking.ts:174-179). A new hold starts with those fields empty (drawer-form.ts:134-148), so the first Save almost always shows them.

The owner note is false in edit mode. The hygiene fieldset always shows 'You will own this pencil.' (BookingDrawer.tsx:442), including when a colleague's hold is opened. The owner is never changed or shown by name.

Existing notes are invisible and cannot be edited after creation. The notes field renders only when mode.kind !== 'edit' (BookingDrawer.tsx:447-452), and the edit form resets notes to '' (drawer-form.ts:101).
Inferred: the drawer overlays the board. At 1440px wide it covers the whole tray and most of the Sunday column of the week overview, which is the busiest day for weddings.
The vocabulary ('Commitment', 'Ladder position', 'Pencil hygiene', 'Ink it', 'Cancel the ink') is not the veteran's own.
workflowGaps: There are no consequences and no confirmation on terminal lifecycle moves. runTransition fires on a single click (BookingDrawer.tsx:180-192). 'Cancel the ink' irreversibly cancels a confirmed booking: cancelled has no further transitions (booking.ts:87-98), and staff may do it (state-machines/booking.ts ink→cancelled). Dragging an ink needs confirmation, yet cancelling it does not.

A promotion goes unreported. Releasing or losing a hold resequences the ladder server-side and returns resequence.promotedToFirst 'so the caller can tell someone "this hold is now 1st option"' (routes/bookings.ts:236-240). The web client parses only BookingSchema and drops it (api/diary.ts:77-89), so the toast says only 'Release: {title}.'

There is no reason field. The transition API accepts a note (TransitionBookingSchema, booking.ts:237-240; api/diary.ts:80) but the drawer never offers one, so 'Mark lost' records no reason (and so no lost-business reporting).

Promotion from prospect to hold skips hold hygiene. transitionBookingCore writes only kind, status and rank (booking-mutations.ts:523-532), so the decision date, owner and next action required at creation (booking.ts:181-188) are never asked for.
Converting an enquiry always defaults to rank 1 (drawer-form.ts:124) even when another 1st option already holds that slot. The loaded ladder is not consulted.

The convert note is false for New enquiries. 'Pencil in {name}. The enquiry stays in review.' (board-copy.ts:97-98) appears for 'submitted' enquiries too (the tray loads both states, DiaryBoardPage.tsx:68). It also never says that nothing is sent to the client.
'Ink it' does not say what happens to other provisional holds on the same slot, or who should be told.
There is no link back to the source enquiry or client contact (the booking has enquiryId), and no value or deposit facts.
Hallkeepers cannot open an attached floor plan from a booking: the plan section requires canWriteDiary (BookingDrawer.tsx:471), a behaviour pinned by a test.
strengths: Validation uses the same Zod schemas the API parses, so the UI can never drift from the server's rules (drawer-form.ts:15-22).
A save in flight keeps the drawer open, and Escape waits (BookingDrawer.tsx:263-270).
The floor-plan corridor is honest about two-step failure: 'Plan created but not attached. Try again to attach it.' A retry finishes the job rather than orphaning a plan (BookingDrawer.tsx:200-246).
Remounting is keyed by a nonce, so retargeting never leaks the previous form (DiaryBoardPage.tsx:116-124).
Hold hygiene (decision date, owner, dated next action) is enforced at creation. That is a real advantage over Salesforce and Cvent.
The read-only role has disabled fields, no Save, and focus on Close.

recommendations.change:
Fix the false and raw copy:
- in edit mode, show the real owner (needs an owner name on the calendar entry) or hide the 'You will own this pencil' note
- map schema issues to plain British field messages ('Add a decision date', 'The end must be after the start')
- fix the convert note to 'Adds a provisional hold. The enquiry's status doesn't change and nothing is sent to the client.'
recommendations.why: Honest consequences, and no developer text in front of veterans.

recommendations.change: Confirm terminal and ladder-changing moves inline, as the desk's Approve… and Decline… do, stating the real consequences. For example: 'Cancel this confirmed booking? Sat 5 June 2027, Grand Hall becomes free. Fraser (2nd option) becomes 1st option. Nothing is sent to the client.' Add an optional reason note that is sent with the transition. Parse resequence.promotedToFirst and say who was promoted.
recommendations.why: Cancelling an ink is irreversible from the UI today, and the promotion the API computes is thrown away.

recommendations.change:
Restructure the drawer as facts, then next step, then details:

surfaces.name: Transient layers: ink-move confirmation, undo toast, Ctrl/Cmd-K palette, first-run welcome, enquiry drag chip
surfaces.audience: venue staff and admin; welcome also shown to hallkeepers
surfaces.dailyUse: Toasts appear after every save and move, many times a day. Ink confirmation appears occasionally. The palette is used occasionally by power users. The welcome appears once per device.
surfaces.currentLook:
Five layers, all described from source:
- Toast: a forest (#2c513d) cream-text bar at bottom centre with a pale 'Undo' button, auto-dismissed after 7 seconds.
- Ink confirmation: a bottom-centre ivory card with Georgia 23px 'Move this inked booking?', the body 'This changes the client's confirmed time or room.', a copper 'Move the ink' button (autofocused) and 'Keep it where it is'.
- Palette: a centred 660px ivory dialog on a forest scrim, with a search input and a list of sage result rows (10px uppercase kind in #7b8e6d, bold label, 11px detail).
- Welcome: a modal ivory card with Georgia 34px 'Using the Diary', a term/definition list and a copper 'Open Diary' button.
- Drag chip: a butter paper chip reading 'Pencil at 18:00'.
slogFactors: The ink confirmation names no specifics. It does not say from where to where (room, day, time) or whether the client is told (board-copy.ts:170-175).
A toast follows every success ('Saved X.', 'Added X to the diary.', 'Release: X.'), which the desk deliberately avoids. The timer does not pause on hover or focus.
The toast's Undo focus ring (#517963) sits on forest #2c513d at 1.81:1, below the 3:1 a focus indicator needs (diary-board.css:34, 183-184; computed).

The palette has no arrow-key selection: Enter always picks the first result (BoardPalette.tsx:69-72). Escape works only while the input is focused, so from a result button it does nothing (lines 64-68). Inferred: aria-modal is set but focus is not trapped. Booking results show 'Room · 18:00' with no date (board-palette.ts:55-58), and the palette searches only the loaded range.
The first-visit welcome is a modal that blocks the board before a veteran has seen it (WelcomePanel.tsx:43-50), and it stays re-openable from a permanent header button.
The palette kind label is 3.23:1 at 10px, and the detail 4.06:1 (computed).
workflowGaps: The e2e helpers still dismiss the welcome by 'Take me to the diary' (e2e/support/diary-live.ts:101; production-smoke.spec.ts:98), but the UI now says 'Open Diary' (board-copy.ts:212). Inferred: with the guarded isVisible check, the opt-in live and smoke runs would leave the modal open over the board.
Ctrl+Z undo keeps working after the toast disappears (DiaryBoardPage.tsx:530-533), but nothing tells users this.
Ink confirmation and toast are both bottom-centre at 24px. Inferred: they can overlap.
strengths: The ink-move confirmation is the right boundary: routine pencil moves are one action with Undo, and ink moves need a deliberate second step. It traps Tab and closes on Escape (BoardPanels.tsx:219-272).
The undo stack survives the toast, and failures and races are stated plainly ('That slot was just inked by someone else — the board has been refreshed.').
The palette's empty state is honest about its scope, and typing never re-renders the board (BoardPalette.tsx:14-20).
The welcome copy is short, factual and free of praise, and its dismissal survives storage failure (welcome.ts).
The drag chip announces the snapped time and cancels cleanly with Escape.

recommendations.change: Have the ink confirmation state the change and the absence of notification: 'Move Henderson wedding from Grand Hall, Sat 5 Jun 18:00–23:00 to Saloon, Sat 5 Jun 19:00–00:00? Nothing is sent to the client.' Put it inside the forest decision panel rather than a floating card.
recommendations.why: Honest consequences before acting (product-experience.md:17).

recommendations.change: Adopt the desk's focus rule: an ink ring on ivory and copper, a cream ring on forest (the toast, the forest panel and active toggles).
recommendations.why: The focus ring is invisible on forest today (1.81:1).

recommendations.change: Update the e2e welcome label, or better, locate the button by role within the dialog.

recommendations.change:

- Escape from anywhere in the dialog

diary-board.css:183-185 (toast and ink confirm both bottom:24px). Computed focus ring on toast: 1.81:1.

The side panels still show sales hygiene and client enquiry names without actions.
slogFactors: Booking details are presented as a disabled edit form, not a readable facts sheet (BookingDrawer.tsx:308, 317).
A 'Discard' button appears although there is nothing to discard (BookingDrawer.tsx:465-467), alongside a header 'Close'.

surfaces.name: Diary design QA record (design-qa.md)
surfaces.audience: platform team and Blake (the internal design gate for the Diary)
surfaces.dailyUse: It is referenced from product-experience.md:40 as the current scoped Diary QA.
surfaces.currentLook: A 56-line Markdown record: 'T603 Diary design QA — 7 September 2026, final result: passed'. slogFactors: Its scope is the week overview with the drawer closed. It says nothing on Day or Timeline contrast, the drawer, the tray or the transient layers, and each of those has sub-AA text today (see the other surfaces).
All visual evidence is private (D:/claude/…, design-qa.md:15), and no Playwright baseline exists for any Diary state, so reviewers of this branch cannot see the Diary at all.

It predates the desk. It measures against the 7 September references (Georgia, the ivory/forest workspace), not the 26 September standard: one next step, keyboard triage, calm motion, visible closure, honest consequences.
Its 'passed' headline can be misread as acceptance, although the body is careful to say it is not.
It lives at the repository root rather than beside the other design records in docs/design.

recommendations.change:
After the rebuild, move the record to docs/design/diary-2026-09/README.md in the desk record's format:

evidence: design-qa.md:3 ('final result: passed'), :15 (private evidence root), :22 (the drawer-closed week view only), :32 (overview-only contrast fix), :38 (Georgia), :52-56 (open items).
product-experience.md:38-40 links this record as the current scoped Diary QA.
questionsForBlake: Can the two private 7 September Diary references be recreated with synthetic data, so they can be committed as the visual target beside the desk?

crossCutting: Global hover pop: index.html:96-111 applies scale(1.06), brightness(1.15), a 0.93 press and an !important transition to every button and [role=button] outside the homepage. Only the Enquiries desk opts out (EnquiriesView.tsx:514). In the Diary it swells overview cards over their neighbours, misstates duration on the precise timeline, and overrides the Diary's own 160ms colour transitions. Blake decided on 26 September (product-experience.md:34) to remove it everywhere, so fix it at the source rather than adding data-calm-controls surface by surface.

Two separate token systems for the two all-day tools:
- The desk scopes its palette to .enq-desk: sheet #f2eddd, forest #264337, copper, sage and ink scales, Newsreader serif, Inter sans (EnquiriesDesk.css:9-47).
- diary-board.css hard-codes about 190 hex values, uses four different forests (#2f5947, #2f5845, #335b45, #2c513d) and Georgia, and defines --diary-* colour tokens (brass, wax, paper) it never uses.

A shared token module (surfaces, ink levels, state washes, focus rules, serif and sans) should serve both, then the hallkeeper tools, proposals and the portal.

Focus rings: the Diary's own ring (#517963, diary-board.css:34) passes on ivory (4.5 to 4.9:1) but fails on forest (1.81:1 on the toast). The global cyan ring (global.css:42-52) measures about 1.4:1 on ivory everywhere else. Adopt the desk rule app-wide: an ink ring on light surfaces and a cream ring on forest.

Raw Zod messages leak into the UI. The shared schemas in packages/types/src/booking.ts:146-151 and 174-179 embed camelCase field names ('A hold requires decisionAt…', 'endsAt must be after startsAt…'), and the Diary's issuesToFieldErrors shows them verbatim. Any surface built on these schemas needs a message map at the client boundary.

The desk and the Diary do not talk to each other:
- The desk's decision panel shows the requested date, guests and room, but not whether that room is free or who holds 1st or 2nd option, and it has no 'Hold as provisional' action (the enquiries components contain no reference to bookings or the Diary).
- The Diary's pencil-in neither advances nor annotates the enquiry.
- The two lists show the same open enquiries with different facts (the Diary omits the date).

This handoff between enquiry and provisional hold is the core of a veteran booker's day.

The API computes consequences the web client discards: transition responses carry resequence.promotedToFirst (routes/bookings.ts:236-240), but web api/diary.ts:77-89 parses only BookingSchema. Calendar entries carry ownerUserId but no owner name. The hold reminder job (T-7/T-3/T-1) is documented as unbuilt (services/hold-hygiene.ts:11-15). All three block honest-consequence and 'decisions due' designs.

Success toasts after every save, and Activity rows that shift the layout on background refresh, go against the desk's calm-technology rule. Adopt a shared rule: status in a reserved slot, toasts only for undoable actions, and state changes shown on the object itself.

Vocabulary: the internal Canon terms (pencil, ink, ladder, prospect, house block, occupancy footprint, hygiene) have reached the UI. Blake's framing and UK venue practice use provisional, first option, second option and confirmed. The vocabulary pass should be decided once and applied across the Diary, the desk, proposals and the hallkeeper tools.

E2E drift: e2e/support/diary-live.ts:101 and e2e/production-smoke.spec.ts:98 look for a welcome button labelled 'Take me to the diary', which the UI no longer has ('Open Diary'). No Diary visual baselines exist under packages/web/e2e/*-snapshots.

Verification limits: this review read the source and computed contrast. It did not render the Diary: there is no committed Diary baseline, and this was a read-only task with no servers. Claims marked 'inferred' (select type-ahead changing the view, the board replaced on refresh failure, the drawer covering the Sunday column, title squeeze, overlapping hover) should be confirmed in the browser during implementation.

surfaces.name: Inventory workspace: equipment sheet, featured item, catalogue, search and filter
surfaces.audience: venue admin (only role that can open it: InventoryPanel.tsx:132, DashboardLayout.tsx:205, DashboardPage.tsx:68)
surfaces.currentLook: The layout follows the selected reference. A sage ground (#819087, InventoryStyle.css:9) holds a 58/42 grid (:11). The ivory equipment sheet (#f0ebd9, tilted clip-path :15) shows a Georgia 'Inventory' h1 (:17) and an 'N items' toggle in the header. Below them sit a search field and a 'Filter' <details> popover with two <select>s (InventoryPanel.tsx:80-88). The featured item has a 260–360px illustration (InventoryStyle.css:30), a Georgia name, and Owned / Damaged / Other unavailable numerals at weight 450 (:38) with hairline dividers. Two 'secondary' items with small pictures follow. The full catalogue list is hidden until toggled (InventoryPanel.tsx:31,109). Text is Inter. Hovers are 150 ms background changes (:41-52). No keyboard shortcuts. Text contrast measured: ink 12.48:1, muted #4c6055 5.65:1, 11px figcaption #5c685a 4.91:1, all on #f0ebd9.
surfaces.dailyUse: Inferred: whoever keeps stock at the venue opens it daily to weekly, in long bursts during stocktakes and before large events. Not measured.
slogFactors: Every inventory button still gets the global springy hover: scale(1.06) and brightness(1.15) (index.html:96-110). Inventory never opts out with [data-calm-controls]; only EnquiriesView.tsx:514 does. That includes full-width 64px catalogue rows, image tiles and the full-width Save. Inferred: because the list has overflow-y:auto (InventoryStyle.css:48), a swelling row can also flash a horizontal scrollbar.
The catalogue is hidden by default behind a button labelled only with a count ('3 items' plus a list icon, InventoryPanel.tsx:77-79). Nothing says it opens a list.

The two 'secondary' items are just the first two filtered items other than the selected one (InventoryPanel.tsx:66). They are not the most urgent, so with 200 real items the screen still shows three arbitrary ones.
The default selection is the first item that has stock (InventoryPanel.tsx:38-39), not the one that is short or damaged.

Only three item names have illustrations (InventoryPicture.tsx:84-90). Every other item without a 3D preview gets a 260–360px blank box captioned 'Equipment photo not added' in 11px (InventoryPicture.tsx:113, InventoryStyle.css:29-30).

Headings use Georgia (InventoryStyle.css:17,32,44), although Newsreader loads app-wide (index.html:15) and the desk uses it. Numerals are weight 450, not the desk's light 300 (InventoryStyle.css:38 vs EnquiriesDesk.css:175). The two surfaces read as related but not identical.
The search field's border #c0c4b4 measures 1.49:1 on #f0ebd9 (InventoryStyle.css:20), well under the 3:1 a control boundary needs.

Cancel or Done on an unchanged editor still refetches the whole list (closeEditor → setRetry, InventoryPanel.tsx:65). A 'Refreshing stock…' line then appears above the featured item and pushes it down (:89).
The secondary tiles show only 'N owned' (InventoryPanel.tsx:106). Damage and shortage are invisible until you select the item.

'Correct stock', catalogue rows, 'Review decisions' and the event links all carry ArrowUpRight, an external-link glyph, although all of them act on the same page (8 uses: InventoryPanel.tsx, InventoryImpact.tsx).
workflowGaps: No keyboard triage: no ↑/↓ or j/k through items, no '/' for search, no Enter to open. The desk has these (EnquiryLedger.tsx:35, EnquiryPanel.tsx:76).

The filter summary never shows an active filter. With the list collapsed, a Damaged/Retired filter is invisible, and the featured item stays put even when the filter excludes it (InventoryPanel.tsx:45-54,84-88).
Storage filter options are built from distinct free-text storage strings (InventoryPanel.tsx:52-53). 'East store' and 'East Store' become two locations.
The selected item and period are not in the URL. A reload loses the place, and a colleague cannot be sent a link to 'the chairs'.
No summary of what needs attention. The desk opens with a sentence built from real counts; inventory opens with only 'Inventory' and a count.

Copy and test disagree. The component renders 'No matching items.' (InventoryPanel.tsx:111; unit test InventoryPanel.test.tsx:181), but the live Playwright spec expects 'No matching items. Try another name, category or storage location.' (e2e/venue-inventory-style-live.spec.ts:74). Inferred: the live spec fails when its fixture runs. Not run here.
strengths: It is the origin of the selected founder style: sage ground, tilted ivory sheet, copper plane, skewed forest frame, and a tangible furniture illustration drawn with mix-blend-mode: multiply.
Facts come first on the item: Owned / Damaged / Other unavailable as large numerals with hairline dividers.
Switching items with unsaved edits asks first (select → editor.requestClose, InventoryPanel.tsx:59-64). Typing in search never discards a draft (live spec lines 61-66).
Illustrations are marked 'Illustrative view' and never imply stock identity (InventoryPicture.tsx:83,107). They use responsive srcset ladders.
Working states use the shared ActivityStatus (InventoryPanel.tsx:72,89).
Layouts are set for 1190, 900 and 560px, with a 16px-safe phone layout (InventoryStyle.css:129-201).

surfaces.name: Reservation impact plane (period assessment)
surfaces.currentLook: A copper plane (#deb599) sits under the sheet, tilted by clip-path (InventoryStyle.css:56-57). It holds a 17px 'Reservation impact' heading, a 'Review decisions ↗' link, a 'Choose period' disclosure, and a caption: 'Selected period · 25 Sept 2026, 14:00 GMT+1 → … · Europe/London'. Below come Usable / Reserved / Remaining in large numerals, then '⚠ N needed' in brick (#842b1c, 4.77:1) or 'Approved demand covered', then a list of overlapping event names. Ink on copper measures 7.93:1, the 12px caption 4.87:1 and the focus ring 3.81:1.
surfaces.dailyUse: Inferred: glanced at every time an item is opened, and checked before each big event.
slogFactors: Each period change is a round-trip through a disclosure: two datetime-local fields and an 'Assess demand' button (InventoryWindowForm.tsx:196-201). Editing either field clears the assessment (InventoryDemand.tsx:168), and the plane says 'Choose a period to assess stock.' (InventoryImpact.tsx:23) until Assess is pressed.

Captions print full timestamps with a numeric UTC offset plus the IANA zone name twice (inventory-window.ts:87-90; InventoryImpact.tsx:20,26). That is system notation, not how a booker says 'next week'.

After every stock save the numbers vanish. The revision is part of refreshKey (InventoryPanel.tsx:73), which re-runs the assessment effect; that effect sets assessment to null (InventoryDemand.tsx:80), and the plane swaps its numerals for 'Checking reservations…' (InventoryImpact.tsx:22). The most satisfying moment, a shortage closing, is shown as a blank and a spinner.

Overlapping reservations list event names only (InventoryImpact.tsx:32-34). The reference shows each event's quantity (120, 70), and the data exists in assessment.sources[].demands (used in InventoryReservationReview.tsx:158).
The shortage reads '10 needed', not '10 chairs needed' (InventoryImpact.tsx:31).
The fragment link #inventory-decisions has no scroll-margin, and the dashboard header is sticky (DashboardLayout.css:5). Inferred: the 'Demand & decisions' heading lands under the header.
workflowGaps: No period presets (Next 7 days, This weekend, Next 30 days) and no way to assess for a chosen event's occupied window.
The default window starts at the next hour and runs 7 days (inventory-window.ts:64-67), but it is never named as 'Next 7 days'.
There is no way to see where in the period the low point falls. Segments are computed but only the minimum is shown.
strengths: All three quantities come from the same interval, so the arithmetic always holds (InventoryImpact.tsx:12-15).
The copper plane holds the numbers that matter, as in the reference, and a shortage is doubled with an icon and words, not colour alone.
It says so honestly when the assessment is stale or has coverage gaps (InventoryImpact.tsx:21,35).
The default assessment runs on mount, so the first paint already has an answer (InventoryDemand.tsx:54-56,75-89).

recommendations.change: While re-assessing, keep the previous numbers visible, dimmed, with an inline ActivityStatus, instead of nulling the assessment. When the new result lands, tick the numerals to their new values, e.g. Remaining −10 → +10. Disable the tick under reduced motion.
recommendations.why: It turns a correction into visible progress and closure (the desk's counts that tick down) instead of a flash of loading.

recommendations.change: Replace the 'Choose period' disclosure with segmented presets (Next 7 days · This weekend · Next 30 days · Custom…) that assess at once. Label the period in words, e.g. 'Next 7 days · Fri 25 Sep – Fri 2 Oct'. Show the time zone only when the browser's zone differs from the venue's.
recommendations.why: Removes the Assess round-trip and the offset notation. Custom keeps full control.

recommendations.change: Show each overlapping reservation's quantity and date ('Grand Hall dinner · Sat 3 Oct · 120'), and name the item in the shortage ('10 Chiavari chairs needed').
recommendations.why: These are the facts that decide which booking to adjust or hire for, and the reference shows them.

recommendations.change: Add scroll-margin-top at least as tall as the sticky header on #inventory-decisions. Use a down arrow, not ArrowUpRight, for in-page links.
recommendations.why: The anchor target stays visible, and the icon says what the link does.

recommendations.change: Add a thin remaining-stock strip across the period, built from the existing segments, with the low point marked in brick.
recommendations.why: Shows when the pinch happens at a glance, in the Diary's language of time.

evidence: Contrast measured: ink/copper 7.93, caption 4.87, shortage 4.77, focus 3.81
questionsForBlake: What default period suits Trades Hall: the next 7 days, the rest of this month, or 'until the next large event'?

surfaces.name: Stock correction pane (forest panel), history and leave/sign-out guards
surfaces.currentLook: A forest panel (#264337) with a skewed inner frame (InventoryStyle.css:72-73) spans both grid rows. It shows a Georgia 'Correct stock' / 'Record stock' heading with 'Chiavari chair · Unsaved correction' state text (InventoryEditor.tsx:151-152,164-167). Three quantity inputs use Inter 29px (InventoryStyle.css:82), then a free-text Storage location field, then Reason. Two disclosures follow, 'Stock details' and 'Recent adjustments', then a 'Review remedies' block. At the bottom are a 56px full-width cream 'Save stock correction' and a borderless Cancel. Measured contrast is high: ink 9.32:1, muted 7.47:1, cream focus 8.28:1, input border 3.25:1.
surfaces.dailyUse: Inferred: used in bursts, dozens of corrections in a row during a stocktake or after an event.
slogFactors: The quantity fields are plain type=text with no steppers and no arrow-key increments (InventoryEditor.tsx:31-36). The reference shows steppers.

The serviceable figure (owned − damaged − unavailable) is computed live (InventoryEditor.tsx:123) but hidden inside the 'Stock details' disclosure in inline mode (:206-208). The one derived fact that matters stays out of sight while typing.

History is nested three disclosures deep: Recent adjustments > each receipt > Audit identifiers (InventoryEditor.tsx:55; InventoryReceipt.tsx:125,135). Colleagues appear only as 'Venue administrator' (InventoryReceipt.tsx:122).
Every correction requires a free-typed reason (inventory-form.ts:41), with no quick presets.
The 'Review remedies' heading carries an ArrowUpRight icon but is not interactive (InventoryImpact.tsx:44).

After Done, the panel falls back to a near-empty rest state: 'Stock correction' plus an 'Open stock correction' button (InventoryPanel.tsx:122-123). That is a dead end where the desk proposes the next move.
Success is a green box plus a collapsed receipt (InventoryEditor.tsx:178-180). The before → after figures, which would give closure, are one click away.
The panel is not sticky (InventoryStyle.css:72), while the desk panel sticks at top:104px (EnquiriesDesk.css .enq-panel). Scrolling to decisions loses the correction.
Quantity numerals are Inter inline (InventoryStyle.css:82) but Georgia in the dialog presentation (InventoryPanel.css:62).
workflowGaps: No consequence line at Save in inline mode. The reference had 'Reservations remain unchanged until approved changes are made.' Today nobody is told what a save changes: future assessments, not reservations, and no one is emailed.
Storage location is free text (InventoryEditor.tsx:188-189), which fragments the storage filter.
No Ctrl/Cmd+Enter to save, and no 'save and next item' for stocktakes.
The remedy shortcut sits between the form and Save (InventoryEditor.tsx:211-212). Two workflows share one column, and the Save is pushed down.
strengths: A pending save is immutable and resumable, so a lost response never becomes two writes (InventoryEditor.tsx:66-67,125-149; inventory-pending.ts).
A revision conflict keeps the user's edits and rebases only untouched fields, then says so (InventoryEditor.tsx:193-202; inventory-form.ts:19-30).

Route changes, More-menu navigation and sign-out are all held behind a plain-language 'Leave this stock correction?' dialog that returns focus to the field (InventoryNavigationGuard.tsx:117-157). This is verified by the live spec.
The state is spelled out honestly: 'Save not confirmed', 'Retry this save', 'Close and check later' (InventoryEditor.tsx:151,213-215).
Receipts record before → after for every field (InventoryReceipt.tsx:130-134), a better closure pattern than anything the desk has.
One primary action in a fixed place at the bottom, in the reference's cream-on-forest.

recommendations.change: Add one consequence line above Save: 'Recorded with your reason. Reservations are unchanged; the impact for this period is recalculated. No one is notified.' After saving, stamp the header with 'Saved · Owned 200 → 201' using the desk's 320 ms stamp (removed under reduced motion), and keep the full receipt in history.
recommendations.why: States real consequences before acting and gives a calm, visible closure, matching the desk's stamp and path.

recommendations.change: Give quantity fields ↑/↓ for ±1 and Shift for ±10, plus visible − / + controls as in the reference. Show a live 'N serviceable' line in light numerals directly under the three fields, and move Status into a small segmented control beside it.
recommendations.why: Stocktake entry becomes fast and the deciding derived fact stays visible.

recommendations.change: Offer reason presets as chips (Stocktake · Damaged at event · Repaired · Purchased · Disposed) that fill an editable reason. Add Ctrl/Cmd+Enter to save and a 'Save and next' action.
recommendations.why: The audit trail stays mandatory without retyping the same sentence 40 times.

recommendations.change: Turn Storage location into a combobox (datalist) of existing locations that still accepts a new one.
recommendations.why: Prevents near-duplicate locations that split the filter (InventoryPanel.tsx:52-53).

recommendations.change: Replace the rest state with a 'next move' overview like the desk's EnquiryOverview: the most pressing item (short, damaged or unrecorded) with one cream CTA and a keyboard legend. Show a calm 'Nothing short this period' seal when there is nothing to do.
recommendations.why: Removes the dead end after Done and gives the goal a visible finish.

recommendations.change: Make the panel sticky, with a fixed frame and internal scroll (the desk's .enq-panel/.enq-panel__body).
recommendations.why: The correction stays beside whatever is being scanned.

recommendations.change: Flatten history into the desk's .enq-timeline, with the reason, time and before → after inline. Put identifiers in one 'Audit record' disclosure.
recommendations.why: Three nested disclosures hide the useful part.

recommendations.change: Drop the icon from the non-interactive 'Review remedies' heading, or make the heading the link. Use one numeral face for both inline and dialog quantity fields.
recommendations.why: Stops a false affordance and a typographic mismatch.

questionsForBlake: Is a written reason on every correction right for Trades Hall, and would preset reasons be welcome?
Should history name colleagues ('Recorded by Elaine MacGregor') rather than 'Venue administrator'?
What do Trades Hall staff call stock that is neither owned-usable nor damaged (on loan, in repair, held)? 'Other unavailable' is our word, not theirs.

surfaces.name: Demand & decisions section (reservations, stock against reservations, internal requests)
surfaces.currentLook: A full-width ivory block sits below the three planes (InventoryStyle.css:108), headed 'Demand & decisions' in 32px Georgia. It contains: a bordered coverage box repeating a long server paragraph, a 'Reservations and source layouts' list with a 'Review reservation' button per row, a 'Stock against approved reservations' grid of bordered cards (auto-fit, minmax 310px; InventoryPanel.css:113-114) each showing 'minimum remaining / maximum shortage' and a 'Demand by event and time' disclosure, and an 'Internal requests' list. All of it uses the generic InventoryPanel.css rules, not the selected style's planes.
surfaces.dailyUse: Inferred: weekly, and whenever an event's layout changes. It is where reservation approvals happen.
slogFactors: A wall of identical bordered cards, one per assessed item, unsorted by shortage (InventoryDemandEvidence.tsx:19-35). The brief bans exactly this.

The server's dense scope paragraph ('Counts cover verified placed catalogue objects only… Each room holds its item peak across its recorded footprint…', packages/api/src/services/inventory-reservations.ts:89) is printed in full (InventoryDemandEvidence.tsx:53), and again in each reservation review.

Developer vocabulary: 'source layouts', 'Source coverage checked', 'Retained attempt', 'This command identifier conflicts with a recorded action' (InventoryDemandEvidence.tsx:51-57; InventoryDemand.tsx:134,199-200).
Raw enum values reach users: remedy.status ('prepared', 'approved') and release.action print lower-case (InventoryDemandEvidence.tsx:73; InventoryReservationReview.tsx:100).

The same caveat appears in at least five places: 'does not add supply / resolve a shortage / confirm supply' (InventoryDemandEvidence.tsx:66,69; InventoryImpact.tsx:49; InventoryDemand.tsx:209; InventoryRemedyReview.tsx:55).
Repeated identical 'Review reservation' / 'Review request' buttons on every row (InventoryDemandEvidence.tsx:62-63,74-75).
workflowGaps: No counts or queue: nothing says how many reservations await approval or how many requests await sign-off, and no finish state exists.
It sits below the fold, reached by scrolling or by the 'Review decisions' anchor, and the forest panel does not follow.
Everything about reservation approval (an allocation decision) lives in a different visual system from the rest of the page.
strengths: Its honesty is exemplary: coverage gaps, unsupported history and stale sources are all surfaced, never hidden (InventoryDemandEvidence.tsx:38-41,50-56).
An unconfirmed earlier action is retained and offered back ('Check recorded result') before anything new can happen (InventoryDemand.tsx:174-178).
On a 409 it re-reads the facts and says 'Facts changed. Review a fresh assessment…' (InventoryDemand.tsx:137-139).

recommendations.change: Fold this section into the desk model. 'Reservations to approve' and 'Requests to approve' become counts on the copper attention band, their rows appear in the ledger, and each review opens in the forest panel. Where a per-item view is still needed, replace the card grid with a ledger sorted by shortage, then date, showing only items with demand by default.
recommendations.why: One place for the next step, visible progress to zero, and no wall of cards.

recommendations.change: Translate enums and jargon into venue language: 'Awaiting approval' / 'Approved' chips, 'Events using this stock' instead of 'Reservations and source layouts'. Keep command IDs, digests and snapshot IDs only under one 'Audit record' disclosure.
recommendations.why: Veterans should read their own vocabulary. The identifiers stay available for audit.

recommendations.change: Say the scope once per page, as one short line ('Counts come from verified room layouts; accessories are not included') with a 'What is counted' disclosure holding the server paragraph. State 'a request does not add stock' once, where the request is made.
recommendations.why: Keeps the honesty and removes repetitive grey caveats.

questionsForBlake: Should approving equipment reservations be its own queue (like New enquiries) that the stock-keeper works to zero, or should it happen automatically when a booking is confirmed?

surfaces.name: Review drawers: reservation review, prepare/approve internal request, pending and receipt states
surfaces.currentLook: A fixed right-hand modal drawer (650px) on a dimmed overlay (InventoryPanel.css:53-54,97; InventoryStyle.css:118). It is set in the forest editor material and slides in over 200 ms, with that animation removed under reduced motion. Content is stacked paragraphs, lists, disclosures and a row of buttons.
surfaces.dailyUse: Inferred: several times a week for reservation approvals and hire or inspection requests.
slogFactors: A modal drawer replaces the side-by-side context the desk keeps. The brief asks to open detail beside the list.

Reservation approval needs a mandatory reason, a confirmation checkbox ('I confirm these recorded times cover equipment setup through return.') and then Approve (InventoryReservationReview.tsx:173-180).

Disclosure-heavy: 'Frozen layouts and room phases' holds nested 'Source identifiers' with snapshot digests. There are also 'Currently approved allocation', 'Reservation decision history', 'Audit identifiers', 'Original command result' and 'Request record and audit identifiers', 15 <details> across the cluster (InventoryReservationReview.tsx:160-169; InventoryDemand.tsx:199,215; InventoryRemedyReview.tsx:79).
Receipts lead with 'Revision 2 · approved · <timestamp>' and UUIDs (InventoryReservationReview.tsx:100,105-108).

Inferred: the LeaveCorrectionDialog (InventoryNavigationGuard.tsx:138) and this drawer share .inventory-overlay at z-index 420. A navigation attempt with a dirty correction while a drawer is open could stack modal on modal.
workflowGaps: The approval's consequence is described abstractly ('Consequences across the full occupied window'). It does not say in one sentence what will be held, from when, until when.
After a receipt, 'Done' closes the drawer with no pointer to the next reservation waiting.
strengths: The consequences are stated plainly: 'Internal request only. No supplier contact, equipment confirmation or stock change.' (InventoryRemedyReview.tsx:30,55-56).
The request quantity is pre-filled with the maximum shortage (InventoryRemedyReview.tsx:13-14).
A title change moves focus to the heading, and Escape is blocked while busy (InventoryActionDialog.tsx:154-161).
Idempotent, retained pending actions validated with Zod before replay (inventory-action-pending.ts:136-166).
The reservation impact after approval is previewed before acting (InventoryReservationReview.tsx:170-172).

recommendations.change: Render reviews inside the sticky forest panel as inline confirmations, reusing the desk's .enq-confirm with a tone border, and remove the overlay drawer.
recommendations.why: Keeps list context and removes any chance of modal on modal.

recommendations.change: Lead each reservation review with one sentence of consequence, e.g. 'Holds 120 Chiavari chairs and 12 round tables in the Grand Hall from Sat 3 Oct 09:00 (setup) to Sun 4 Oct 01:00 (return). No one is notified.' Then one Approve action. Make the reason optional unless Blake wants it kept.
recommendations.why: Confirm only consequential external actions; an internal allocation should be one clear step with its real effect named.

recommendations.change: Receipts lead with a stamp and plain words ('Approved by you · 14:02'), then the demand lines. Revision numbers, UUIDs and digests go last, in one Audit record. After Done, offer the next waiting reservation.
recommendations.why: Gives closure and a next step rather than a system log.

questionsForBlake: When approving an equipment reservation, should Trades Hall staff still tick 'setup through return' and write a reason, or is one Approve with the times spelled out enough?
Should a hire request ever go to a supplier from Venviewer? Today it is internal only.

surfaces.name: Inventory loading, error, empty and access states
surfaces.audience: venue admin (non-admins reach it only by URL)
surfaces.currentLook: A flat ivory box (#efeada, padding 36px; InventoryStyle.css:10) on the sage ground, min-height 270px, with an h1 'Inventory', a Georgia h2 and a paragraph (InventoryPanel.css:50-52). Loading uses ActivityStatus 'Opening inventory'. Error has role=alert and a 'Try again' button.
surfaces.dailyUse: Seen at every page open while loading. Error and empty states are rare.
slogFactors: The loading and error states drop the three-plane composition entirely, so the page jumps from a small box to the full workspace (InventoryPanel.tsx:70-72).
The empty catalogue says 'Your catalogue is empty / Add catalogue items to record stock.' with no action or link (InventoryPanel.tsx:90-91): a dead end.
workflowGaps: Nowhere to import stock from a spreadsheet or paper list. Blake decided import paths must cover email, spreadsheets and paper.
strengths: Uses the shared Activity component, and errors are announced (InventoryPanel.tsx:70-72).
The access-denied copy is plain and explains why (InventoryPanel.tsx:132-133).

recommendations.change: Give the empty catalogue a next step: 'Import from a spreadsheet' and 'Add an item', or a link to where the catalogue is managed.
recommendations.why: Removes a dead end at the very first visit and starts the import-parity requirement.

recommendations.change: Render loading and error inside the sheet/panel composition: a skeleton sheet with ActivityStatus in the summary line, and the error as a desk-style .enq-notice--alert with Retry.
recommendations.why: No layout jump, and the page feels finished even while waiting.

questionsForBlake: Where does Trades Hall's equipment list live today (spreadsheet, stocktake sheets, Cvent)? That decides the first import path.

crossCutting: The two surfaces should converge into one system. Inventory and the desk come from the same reference but hold two drifting token sets: sheet #f0ebd9 vs #f2eddd, ink #102c25 vs #14302a, muted #4c6055 vs #42584e, Georgia vs Newsreader, numeral weight 450 vs 300, radius 4px vs 3px, button heights 46px vs 40/48px (InventoryStyle.css:3-8,17,38; InventoryPanel.css:22; EnquiriesDesk.css:9-47,173-176,338-346). Extract shared tokens (e.g. --vv-desk-*) and primitives: Sheet, CopperBand (counts as filters), ForestPanel (sticky, fixed skewed frame, internal scroll), FactRow (light numerals with hairlines), Chip with stamp, Notice, the Cta/Quiet/Button tiers, LedgerRow, KeyLegend and ConfirmInline. The inventory's before→after receipt, pending-command retention and navigation guard should be adopted by the desk and other surfaces.

The global springy hover (index.html:96-110) still applies to every inventory button. Only the Enquiries desk opts out (EnquiriesView.tsx:514). Blake decided on 26 September to remove it everywhere, so fix it at source rather than adding data-calm-controls surface by surface.

The global focus style (global.css:42-53) adds a cyan 6px halo box-shadow. Inventory overrides only outline and outline-offset (InventoryPanel.css:29; InventoryStyle.css:106-107), so the off-palette halo still shows on ivory, copper and forest. The desk zeroes box-shadow (EnquiriesDesk.css:84-89). The shared focus token should set outline, offset and box-shadow: none, with ink on light surfaces and cream on forest.

InventoryPanel.css still defines the obsolete dark palette (lines 1-16) and dead ledger/table rules: .inventory-ledger, .inventory-availability-note, .inventory-item-name, .inventory-row-action and .inventory-storage have 0 TSX uses. InventoryStyle.css overrides them only by import order (InventoryPanel.tsx:12-13). Merge them into one light stylesheet on shared tokens.
The ground colour differs by surface: DashboardLayout.css:94 paints inventory #7f9182 while the panel and desk use #819087 (InventoryStyle.css:9; DashboardLayout.css:98).

Fonts: Newsreader (site.css) loads app-wide from index.html:15, and Inter comes from cockpit.css via router.tsx:13-65. Inventory headings name Georgia directly, so they never use the Newsreader the desk uses. Weights 450 and 550 fall between the static faces loaded (200-700 in hundreds).
The sticky dashboard header (DashboardLayout.css:5) needs a shared scroll-margin-top for in-page anchors, and sticky panels need a shared top offset (the desk hard-codes 104px).
Icon semantics: ArrowUpRight, an external or new-context glyph, is used for in-page actions and for a non-interactive heading across inventory. Agree one icon vocabulary.

Visual regression: no inventory state is covered by any committed *-chromium-linux.png baseline under packages/web/e2e/*-snapshots. Add desktop, tablet and phone baselines for the inventory workspace, correction, shortage, empty and review states to the dashboard-state visual spec.
Copy drift between the component and its tests: the live spec expects the longer empty-result sentence (e2e/venue-inventory-style-live.spec.ts:74 vs InventoryPanel.tsx:111).

Audience reach: inventory is venue-admin only (DashboardLayout.tsx:62,205; DashboardPage.tsx:68). The Enquiries panel and the hallkeeper tools cannot say whether equipment is available for a date. Serving veterans may need a read-only availability fact where sales and event-day staff work.

Honest-consequence copy is strong but over-repeated in inventory. The shared system should give each consequence one canonical place (beside the action), as the desk does with .enq-next__hint and .enq-confirm__consequence.

surfaces.name: Hallkeeper event sheet (focused workspace, with its loading, error and denied states)
surfaces.audience: hallkeeper and porters on phones and tablets under time pressure; planners and staff reviewing on desktop
surfaces.dailyUse: Inference, not measured: opened on every event day and used continuously through setup, with dozens of check taps per hour on a phone or tablet held in one hand. Planners and staff open it briefly on desktop to review.
surfaces.currentLook: The page sits in its own framed ivory app (#fdfcf9) with its own top bar instead of the shared DashboardLayout (HallkeeperWorkspace.tsx:75-79). A 182px room rail with a Trades Hall room photo sits beside the main column. The heading is a 42px Georgia room name with the layout name beneath and a sage time card on the right. A strip of six pastel stage tabs (peach, honey, sage, blue, lilac) sits above a split of plan and working panel. Setup is a checklist paged five rows at a time, with a native category <select>, a search field and a 3px progress bar. Most labels are 8–12px Inter in a muted grey-green. The workspace CSS is minified onto one line (hallkeeper-workspace.css:2). The loading, error and denied states use a different stylesheet with Playfair Display headings (hallkeeper-sheet.css:20). There is no hover opt-out, so the global spring pop applies.
slogFactors: Operational text is set too small for a phone at arm's length. Item names are 12px, zone and notes 9px and quantities 11px (hallkeeper-workspace.css:2: .hkf-check-task strong 12px, small 9px, b 11px). At 640px and below, the time-card caption, footer and stage index drop to 8px (hallkeeper-workspace.css:17). The quantity, the number a porter acts on, is the smallest thing in the row.

The checklist is paged five rows at a time (HallkeeperWorkspace.tsx:57-58). The 43-row test manifest recorded in docs/design/hallkeeper-focus-2026-09-07/README.md needs nine pages. Each page turn is a 30px-high arrow (.hkf-pagination button min-height 30px, hallkeeper-workspace.css:2), below the 44px touch target used elsewhere.

Categories are chosen from a native <select> that carries no counts (HallkeeperWorkspace.tsx:104), so per-category progress is invisible. The old PhaseBlock showed done/total per phase (HallkeeperPage.tsx:505), but it now renders only in the print mirror (HallkeeperPage.tsx:463).

Contrast was measured. Muted #75796d on #fdfcf9 is 4.34:1 and is used for 9–12px text such as overlines, zones and footnotes. Footer #85897b is 3.49:1. The brand caption #8c8a7e is 3.44:1. The time-card caption is 4.04:1 and the facts link #64805a is 4.28:1. The unchecked checkbox border #b7bfae on #fffefa is 1.88:1, under the 3:1 non-text minimum, so the empty box barely shows. The progress fill #8aa277 on #efeee8 is 2.40:1.

Every checklist row is a <button> (HallkeeperWorkspace.tsx:107) and the sheet has no [data-calm-controls]. Under the global rule (packages/web/index.html:96-111), a row grows 6% and brightens on hover and shrinks to 0.93 on press. The hover is not gated to fine pointers. Inference: on touch devices a tapped row may stay in its hovered state.

The search field is 11px !important and the category select 13px (hallkeeper-workspace.css:2). Inference from known iOS Safari behaviour: it zooms the page on focus for inputs under 16px, so a porter's view jumps when they search.
Stage content is a fixed-height scroll box inside the scrolling page: height 390px, 360px above 861px and 340px on phones (hallkeeper-workspace.css:2, 17, 23).

The type changes between states: Playfair Display while loading or on error (hallkeeper-sheet.css:20), then Georgia once ready (hallkeeper-workspace.css:2). Neither is the desk's Newsreader, which index.html loads on every route through site.css.

The sheet version appears three times: the facts line 'Sheet vN' (HallkeeperWorkspace.tsx:89), the 'Sheet vN · approved by' note (line 92) and the status banner's own version (HallkeeperStatusBanner.tsx:44-60).
The raw IANA zone 'Europe/London' is printed under the time (HallkeeperWorkspace.tsx:90).
'Brief & contacts ↗' uses an external-link arrow, but it opens an in-page dialog (HallkeeperWorkspace.tsx:89, 126).
The working sheet links to a fictional demonstration: 'Workflow walkthrough ↗' in its footer (HallkeeperWorkspace.tsx:123) and in the error-state navigation (HallkeeperPage.tsx:477).
workflowGaps: The deadline that matters most to a hallkeeper is never shown. The payload carries timing.setupBy (packages/types/src/hallkeeper-v2.ts:120-127) and the PDF prints 'Setup by' (packages/api/src/services/hallkeeper-pdf-v2.ts:213), but grep finds no use of setupBy anywhere in packages/web/src. The time card shows only the event start.

The default indicative time is built as 18:00 UTC (hallkeeper-sheet-v2-data.ts:36, 429), although the comment at lines 28-29 says 18:00 local. Computed: a 15 June date renders as 19:00 start and 17:30 setup in Europe/London; a 15 December date renders as 18:00. The live sheet has not been checked.

Approval state is easy to miss. The status banner renders compact at 9px label and 10px detail inside the provenance row (HallkeeperStatusBanner.tsx:185-195; HallkeeperWorkspace.tsx:92). That includes 'Rejected: Do not prepare the room from this sheet'. The checklist beside it stays fully interactive and looks unchanged. The awaiting-approval label at 0.85 opacity measures 3.65:1.

Critical facts sit behind a tab or a dialog. The day-of contact phone, access notes, dietary counts and allergies, and door schedule appear only under the 'Prepare' stage (HallkeeperWorkspace.tsx:113) or in the Brief dialog (line 126). The default stage is 'setup' (line 44). Only critical accessibility callouts are promoted to the top (HallkeeperPage.tsx:443).

The approval time uses the device's locale and time zone (HallkeeperStatusBanner.tsx:51, toLocaleString(undefined…)). Phase deadline chips do the same (InstructionsBanner.tsx:199-202, toLocaleTimeString([]…)). Both can disagree with the venue clock and may show a 12-hour format.

'Keep in view' offers 'Review issues ↗', which opens /ops/events/:id (HallkeeperWorkspace.tsx:122). That page never lists issues; it shows only a count (EventDayOpsPage.tsx:223, 477). This is a dead end.

The room rail is hidden at 860px and below (hallkeeper-workspace.css:16), so on a portrait tablet or phone there is no way to switch to the event's other rooms. The rail is the only room switcher (HallkeeperWorkspace.tsx:84).
On phones the plan is ordered first (.hkf-plan order 0, hallkeeper-workspace.css:17), so the checklist sits below a plan up to 290px tall.
Finishing has no moment of closure. When every row is checked, only a 10px muted footnote changes: 'Every setup row is checked…' (HallkeeperWorkspace.tsx:111).

The second heading line is the layout name, data.config.name (HallkeeperWorkspace.tsx:89), although its class is hkf-event-name. Inference: the event name is available from the verified context graph when ?eventId is present.

The 403 state offers only 'Try Again' (HallkeeperPage.tsx:424, committed baseline mobile-hallkeeper-mobile-denied-chromium-linux.png). Retrying cannot fix a permission error. The 404 copy is 'Configuration not found.' (line 156).
There is no keyboard support beyond Tab and Space. The only key handler is Escape on the Brief dialog (HallkeeperWorkspace.tsx:126).
strengths: The offline behaviour is robust and honest. Optimistic checks are kept and queued in IndexedDB on a retriable failure and rolled back on a terminal rejection, and a pending count shows (HallkeeperPage.tsx:197-269). Reconnect reconciles against server truth (lines 287-363). Stale-response guards are in place (lines 150-168).
The plan and the checklist are linked both ways: tapping a footprint opens the exact category and page of its row (HallkeeperWorkspace.tsx:67-72; SavedFloorPlan.tsx:44-52).

The copy is honest about limits: 'Indicative event time', 'Checks record setup work. Approval and room release remain separate.' (HallkeeperWorkspace.tsx:90, 111), and 'Planned times do not confirm that an activity has started.' (line 115).
The print mirror keeps the full manifest, plan, instructions and approval provenance (HallkeeperPage.tsx:457-470).
The ivory and sage direction, the Trades Hall room photography in the rail and the pastel stage colours already lean toward the selected style.
Loading, saving, syncing and PDF preparation all use the shared ActivityStatus component (HallkeeperPage.tsx:410, 445-446; HallkeeperWorkspace.tsx:78).

recommendations.change: Mark the .hkf-app root and the hk-page state cards [data-calm-controls]. Give checklist rows the desk's press feedback, scale(0.98) on :active. Restrict colour hovers to @media (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine). Remove the transforms under reduced motion.
recommendations.why: The whole row currently swells 6% and brightens on hover and shrinks 7% on every tap. This is the springy look Blake asked to remove everywhere, on the most frequently tapped control in the product.

recommendations.change: Set a type floor. On phones, item names 16px, zone and notes 13px and nothing operational under 12px. Show quantities as the desk's large light serif numerals (Newsreader 300, about 26px, tabular). Make the search and select 16px.
recommendations.why: Porters read these rows standing and moving. Today the quantity, the fact they act on, is the smallest text at 11px, and sub-16px inputs zoom the page on iOS.

recommendations.change: Adopt the desk's colour tokens. Muted text becomes #55655c (measured 6.02:1 on #fdfcf9). The checkbox border becomes at least #8b927f (3.19:1), with a 24px box inside the full-row target. The progress fill becomes the sage dot #5d8963 (3.46:1). Focus becomes the desk's 2px ink ring.
recommendations.why: Several 9–12px labels fail AA (4.34, 4.04, 3.49 and 3.44:1). The unchecked box measures 1.88:1, so on a phone in daylight an empty box can pass for a checked one.

recommendations.change: Put 'Ready by' next to the start time in the time card, as the generated reference's 'Room ready by 17:15 / Doors at 18:00' does. Use timing.setupBy or the planner's phase deadline, and label it 'indicative' when it is the 90-minute default. In the API, build the default start as venue-local 18:00, not 18:00Z.
recommendations.why: This is the deadline the whole setup works to. It is in the payload and printed on the PDF but absent from the screen, and the default shows an hour late in summer.

recommendations.change: Replace the five-row pages and the category <select> with a copper count plane of setup categories, for example 'Furniture 12/20 · Dress 0/8 · Technical 3/3 · Final 0/5'. Each count is its filter, as on the desk. Inside a category, group rows by zone. A finished zone folds to one sealed line, 'Top table · 6 of 6 ✓'. One category is open at a time.
recommendations.why: It keeps the short, focused view Blake asked for when he rejected the long sheet, but removes page-turning. Progress becomes visible as counts ticking toward full, the desk's goal-gradient pattern.

recommendations.change: Promote approval state. Any state other than approved gets a full-width band at the top of the working panel, in words: brick 'Rejected — do not set this room from this sheet', amber 'Awaiting approval — preview only'. Approved becomes a quiet restrained stamp beside the heading ('Approved v4 · 18 Jun, 13:00', in venue time). Remove the other two version mentions.
recommendations.why: A rejected sheet currently looks almost identical to an approved one while every check stays live. That is a hidden consequence with real cost on the day.

recommendations.change: Add a 'Keep in view' band above the checklist on every stage. It holds critical access needs, allergies, the day-of contact as a one-tap tel: link, and the next deadline. The full brief stays in the side panel.
recommendations.why: 'Who do I call' and 'what must not go wrong' are currently one tab or one dialog away, while the default stage is Setup.

recommendations.change: Give setup a close. When a category completes, its count seals with the desk's 320ms chip stamp (none under reduced motion). When every row is done, a forest panel reads 'Setup checked · 43 of 43'. Its sub-line is 'Room release is a separate decision', and it offers one next step (Open event operations or Review handoff).
recommendations.why: Completion is currently a 10px grey footnote. Visible progress and closure is the desk pattern Blake judged inviting, and here it is done without praise copy.

recommendations.change: Phone layout. Add a 'Checklist | Plan' segmented switch at the top with the checklist as default. Remove the fixed-height inner scroll boxes. When the rail is hidden, move the room switcher into the header as a room chip with a menu.
recommendations.why: On a phone the plan pushes the checklist below the fold, there is a scroll box inside the scrolling page, and other rooms of the same event become unreachable.

recommendations.change: Unify the typography. Use Newsreader for the room name, headings and numerals in the loading, error and ready states. Delete the retired long-sheet rules in hallkeeper-sheet.css; a grep of .tsx files finds no use of .hk-sheet-shell, .hk-sheet-heading, .hk-summary-sticky, .hk-phase-strip, .hk-time-pair, .hk-workspace, .hk-plan-card, .hk-sheet-bottom or .hk-skip-link. Expand the minified workspace CSS into readable rules.
recommendations.why: The typeface currently changes between loading and ready. The dead rules and one-line CSS make every future polish pass slower and riskier.

recommendations.change: Rewrite the state copy. For 403: 'This sheet hasn't been shared with you', with 'Back to today's rooms' and a named ask; drop 'Try Again'. For 404: 'This setup sheet could not be found'. Use sentence case throughout.
recommendations.why: The only action offered on a permission error cannot succeed, and 'Configuration' is system vocabulary.

recommendations.change: Format every time in the venue's zone and 24-hour clock: the status banner, deadline chips and approval stamp. Show 'UK time' only when the device's zone differs from the venue's, and never the raw IANA string.
recommendations.why: Times from the device clock and times from the venue clock can disagree on the same screen.

recommendations.change: When a verified ?eventId is present, show the event name on the second heading line, with the layout name as a quieter detail.
recommendations.why: A hallkeeper thinks in 'Heritage Trust Dinner in the Grand Hall', not in layout names.

recommendations.change: Add keyboard support for desktop reviewers: j/k or arrow keys to move between rows, Space or x to toggle, / to search, 1–6 for stages, l to locate on the plan, and a legend shown in the empty panel as the desk does.
recommendations.why: It gives staff checking sheets in the office the same speed the desk gives bookers.

recommendations.change: Move 'Workflow walkthrough' out of the working sheet's footer and error navigation into a help menu.
recommendations.why: It is labelled a fictional demonstration and adds noise to a live tool.

questionsForBlake: You rejected the long hallkeeper sheet on 7 September. Was it the length, or the way it looked? Would one category open at a time, with zones that fold away when they are done (the desk's grouped ledger), be acceptable instead of pages of five?
Should hallkeepers be able to tick setup rows on a sheet that is awaiting approval or has been rejected? Or should those checks be locked until the venue approves?
Should allergies and the day-of contact always be in view for hallkeepers? Or should allergy detail stay with the caterer and the brief?
Would you like the sheet to open with the room photograph fading into forest, the way the desk panel does, as its one moment of scale? Or should the working sheet stay plainer?
