surfaces.name: Day Board (today's rooms)
surfaces.audience: hallkeepers, staff and admins, on phones, tablets and possibly an always-on wall tablet
surfaces.dailyUse: Inference, not measured: the hallkeeper's landing page, opened at the start of every shift and glanced at all day. The CSS header describes a wall-tablet use (day-board.css:2).
surfaces.currentLook: The stylesheet opens with a dark 'Ink & Gilt' board (day-board.css:1-275). A block at the end repaints it ivory (lines 288-314). The title is 36px Georgia 'The Day Board', with a subtitle of the date plus a hard-coded 'Europe/London'. A controls row holds a date input, a Today button, a room select, and 'Open Diary' and 'Workflow walkthrough' links styled identically to the filters. Each room has a lane (auto-fit, one column on phones) of white slot cards with a coloured left border. A card carries a time range, a countdown chip with a dot, the title, an uppercase state label, the booking kind and guests, and pastel two-column phase tiles. The chip dots pulse or breathe forever at 1.5–4 s cadences, and a colour legend sits at the foot.
slogFactors: The motion never stops. Every slot within 60 minutes of its first phase pulses (4 s, 3 s, 2 s), a slot in progress breathes (4 s), and an exception pulses every 1.5 s (day-board-state.ts:137-188, 263; day-board.css:244-267). On a board watched all day, something in peripheral vision is always moving. The desk rule is 'no pulsing'.

The legend does not match the cards. It labels the gilt chip 'Scheduled event' (DayBoardPage.tsx:172-175), but that chip is tone 'live', whose card label reads 'In booked window' (day-board-state.ts:144-148). The actual 'Scheduled' state uses the quiet tone. 'Starting soon' (amber-deep) is missing from the legend.

The turnaround warning is the least legible text on the board. The ivory override never recolours amber, so .dayboard-slot-warning stays #d99a2b on #fffdf7, measured 2.40:1 (day-board.css:182-186, 289).
Finished bookings drop to opacity 0.55 (day-board.css:138-140). Their meta text then measures 2.20:1 and their title 3.35:1.
Every empty room gets a full lane reading 'Nothing scheduled.' (DayBoardPage.tsx:154-156). On a phone, a hallkeeper scrolls past each idle room to reach the busy ones.
Navigation links and filters share one bordered-box style (day-board.css:294), so nothing in the row reads as the main control.
The header comment still describes a dark board where 'text is ALWAYS paper-on-ink' (day-board.css:1-16), which the override contradicts. Inference: a future edit could re-darken the board.
The subtitle hard-codes 'Europe/London' (DayBoardPage.tsx:117) rather than using the venue's time zone.
workflowGaps: There is no direct way to the setup sheet from a slot. The card links to /ops/events/:id (DayBoardPage.tsx:62), and only from there does 'Open current setup sheet' appear (HallkeeperEventLinks.tsx:20). The document used most is two taps away. Calendar entries carry eventId but no configuration id (packages/types/src/booking.ts around 399-419), so a direct link needs an API projection.
Slots show no setup progress (for example '12 of 43 checked') and no ready-by deadline, so the board cannot show which room is behind.
There are no previous or next day controls, only a native date input and 'Today' (DayBoardPage.tsx:128-129). Checking tomorrow means opening a date picker.
When the socket drops, the page says only 'Live updates disconnected' (line 124). It shows no last-updated time and offers no reconnect or refresh, although the data may be stale.
No summary sentence says what matters today. The desk's header sentence built from real counts has no equivalent here.
clientName is derived (day-board-state.ts:70) but never shown. This may be deliberate on a shared board.
strengths: The state machine is a pure, unit-tested derivation (day-board-state.ts). Red is reserved for real exceptions, and words carry every state, so the board works without colour and under reduced motion.
The phase-locked epoch keeps any motion in sync rather than noisy (DayBoardPage.tsx:30-35, 104).
It updates live over the diary socket, with a snapshot refetch (useDiaryLive), and rolls over at venue midnight (lines 91-95).
Controls are 44px (day-board.css:294), and loading and refreshing use ActivityStatus (lines 134-135).
The ivory lanes and pastel phase tiles already sit near the selected style.

recommendations.change: Remove the infinite pulses and breathing. Tone becomes static colour plus words. When a slot crosses into a new state, play one restrained 320ms stamp on its chip, removed under reduced motion.
recommendations.why: It is calm technology, and consistent with the desk. Urgency then comes from change and from words, not from a board that is always moving.

recommendations.change: Rebuild the legend from the real states: Upcoming, First phase due, Starting soon, In booked window, Changeover at risk, Finished. Colour the turnaround warning with the desk's amber ink #6f500f on wash #efe0b8 (5.66:1). Show finished slots with a slate chip and a faded border, but keep full-strength text.
recommendations.why: The legend currently mislabels a colour, and the most important warning measures 2.40:1.

recommendations.change: Delete the dead dark block and the stale comment, and move the board onto the desk's tokens and Newsreader: ivory sheet, sage ground, Newsreader title, and large light numerals for times.
recommendations.why: The board would join the family Blake judged inviting, and a future edit could no longer accidentally restore the rejected dark look.

recommendations.change: Give it a desk-style header: the venue date, then one sentence built from the counts (for example 'Three rooms in use today; the Grand Hall's first phase is at 14:00'). Below it, a copper count plane (Upcoming · Starting soon · In progress · Needs attention · Finished) whose counts are the filters.
recommendations.why: The facts that decide come first, the next move is in the same place every day, and progress is visible as counts tick down.

recommendations.change: Make 'Open setup sheet' each slot's primary action, and show its ready-by time and checked count. The event-operations link becomes secondary. This needs the approved configuration id and progress in the calendar or ops projection.
recommendations.why: It removes a hop from the most frequent journey and shows which room is behind at a glance.

recommendations.change: Add ← Today → day-stepping buttons, with the ←, → and t keys.
recommendations.why: Checking tomorrow's setup is a daily task and should not need a date picker.

recommendations.change: Collapse empty rooms into one quiet line: 'Also free today: Saloon, North Gallery, South Gallery.'
recommendations.why: On phones the busy rooms come first and there are no dead lanes to scroll past.

recommendations.change: Show honest connection status: 'Updated 14:02 · reconnecting…' and a Refresh action when the socket is down.
recommendations.why: A wall board that silently goes stale is a hidden consequence.

recommendations.change: If Blake wants it, add an optional wall-display mode: very large type, no controls, a now line, and nothing moving except state changes.
recommendations.why: The file's own header describes a wall-tablet use, which needs different density from a phone.

questionsForBlake: Is the Day Board mainly a wall display seen from across a room, or a list a hallkeeper works through on a phone? The two need different type sizes and density.
Should anything on the board still move? I propose nothing except a single stamp when a room's state changes.
Should client names appear on the Day Board, or stay off a shared screen for discretion?

surfaces.name: Event-day operations board (with the embedded Mission Control and the Working documents card)
surfaces.audience: hallkeepers, staff, admins and planners running a live event, mostly on phones and tablets
surfaces.dailyUse: Inference, not measured: open for hours on an event day, with repeated task updates, acknowledgements and issue logging on a phone.
surfaces.currentLook: This is the old dark cockpit. The page is a teal-black gradient (#111818) with cyan #8fd8d2 kickers and icon tiles and an amber #e8b85f primary button, at 800–950 font weights with uppercase 0.72rem labels (EventDayOpsPage.css:1-9, 31-38, 186-193). An ivory 'Working documents' card is dropped onto the dark page (HallkeeperEventLinks.css). A separate dark cyan glass 'Mission Control' panel follows, with a glowing top rule and a pulsing live dot (EventMissionControl.css:1-28, 216, 716). Then come eight identical stacked sections, each an icon tile plus h2: Required acknowledgements, Phase timeline, Setup progress, Task checklist, Issue report, What changed, Supplier arrivals and Escalation notes. The committed mobile baseline shows it under the ivory app header.
slogFactors: The palette, weight and mood are the opposite of the selected ivory, forest, copper and sage style: dark cyan and amber at 800–950 weights (EventDayOpsPage.css).
It is a wall of identical sections. Nine blocks carry equal weight, and nothing places the one thing that needs you in a consistent spot.

The tools are duplicated. There are two task lists: 'Task checklist' with Start, Done and Block (EventDayOpsPage.tsx:457-467), and Mission Control's 'Live execution', also with Start, Done and Block (EventMissionControl.tsx:225-246). There are two problem logs that write to different tables: 'Issue report' writes eventDayIssues (services/event-day-ops.ts:423) and 'Incident channel' writes eventMissionIncidents (services/event-mission-control.ts:690).

The vocabulary is science fiction rather than venue language: '4D Mission Control', 'Spatial command map', 'Live execution', 'Phase authority', 'Incident channel', 'Time machine', 'Live edge', 'timeline cursor' and 'active operators' (EventMissionControl.tsx:170, 222, 512-517, 534-542, 568, 583).
Every tap produces generic chatter such as 'Task status updated.' (EventDayOpsPage.tsx:241). It persists at the top of the page, away from the task (line 359).

Setup is summarised as a readiness percentage, '67% done' (lines 426-433). The hallkeeper design record says to avoid a readiness percentage and explain readiness by its blockers (docs/design/hallkeeper-2026-09-07/workflow.md, 'Screen family 1').
Task buttons never show the current state as pressed. State appears only as a small cyan uppercase label (lines 450, 186-193 CSS).
The lazy plural 'open issue(s).' (line 477) and the kicker 'Today's event', which appears whatever the event's date (line 345).
The global spring pop applies to every button, because the page has no calm-controls opt-out.
workflowGaps: Logged issues are never listed or resolvable here; the page shows only a count (EventDayOpsPage.tsx:223, 477). updateEventDayIssue exists in the web API client (src/api/event-day-ops.ts:43), but the page never calls it, so a problem cannot be closed. The hallkeeper sheet's 'Review issues ↗' lands here.

'Log issue' never states its consequence. The server records a change-feed item for the staff and hallkeeper roles, assigns nobody and notifies nobody (routes/event-day-ops.ts:153-175; services/event-day-ops.ts:423-435). Choosing 'Urgent' pages no one.
Block takes no reason, although the status input accepts a note (packages/types/src/event-day-ops.ts:147-150).
The phase timeline shows names and durations but no start times, although phases carry startsAt (EventDayOpsPage.tsx:411-417; packages/types/src/event-phase-graph.ts:124). It has no 'now' marker.
Supplier arrivals omit arrivalWindow (EventDayOpsPage.tsx:546-551; types event-day-ops.ts:115).
'What changed' shows only three counts (lines 522-535). The actual rows are on the handoff page.
Times use the device's time zone: formatTime, formatEventDate and formatChangeTime have no timeZone (lines 37-64).

Errors appear far from what failed. In baseline mobile-event-day-acknowledgement-error-chromium-linux.png, 'Change acknowledgement could not be saved.' sits above Mission Control, while the change card is below it.
The board's assignments and statusUpdates are never shown, so who is doing what is invisible (grep finds no use in EventDayOpsPage.tsx).

The Working documents card gives 'Day Board', 'Open current setup sheet' and 'Open version N handoff' equal weight (HallkeeperEventLinks.tsx:18-22). The hallkeeper's next document is not marked as primary.
strengths: Writes survive a bad connection. There is an offline queue with idempotency keys, a replay that drops terminal failures, and an honest '3 pending sync' label with a manual sync (EventDayOpsPage.tsx:66-77, 173-206, 224).
The acknowledgement flow is real and tied to the change feed (lines 225-230, 294-304).

Mission Control confirms consequential actions in plain terms: 'Phase, task, incident, and acknowledgement history will become read-only and remain replayable.' It also states its limits: 'Internal execution only. This does not approve the layout…' (EventMissionControl.tsx:490-491, 527-531).
Busy states use ActivityIndicator and ActivityStatus.

recommendations.change: Restyle the page on the desk's structure and tokens. The ivory sheet on sage holds the event facts first (weekday date, start and ready-by in venue time, room, guests). A copper count plane shows Needs acknowledgement · Blocked · In progress · To do · Done, and the counts are filters. A forest 'Now' panel on the right holds the single next action. Headings in Newsreader at 400–600 weights, with [data-calm-controls].
recommendations.why: This is the surface Blake named next after the Diary. Its current dark cockpit is the look the desk replaced.

recommendations.change: Offer one task list and one problem log. Keep the checklist and hand it to the live view when a mission starts, which it partly does already. Merge 'Issue report' and 'Incident channel' into a single 'Report a problem' flow backed by one store, or visibly route one into the other.
recommendations.why: Two forms that write to different tables leave staff unsure where a problem went, which is lost context during the most pressured hours.

recommendations.change: List open issues with owner, age and severity, add a 'Resolve' action using updateEventDayIssue, and show a sealed 'No open issues' state. On the form, state the real consequence: 'Recorded on this event for venue staff and hallkeepers. Nobody is notified.' Change that copy only when notification exists.
recommendations.why: It closes a dead end (the sheet's 'Review issues' link) and stops people assuming 'Urgent' reached someone.

recommendations.change: Block opens an inline 'What's stopping it?' note, sent as the existing note field, which says who will see it. The current status shows as the pressed button. Remove the success notices and place errors beside the affected card.
recommendations.why: Honest consequences, no chatter, and errors kept in context.

recommendations.change: Make the phase timeline a horizontal running order with venue-local start times and a now line, like the hallkeeper generated reference. Add arrival windows to supplier arrivals. Show all times in the venue's zone, and make the kicker read 'Today', 'Tomorrow' or the weekday date.
recommendations.why: On the day, the running order and times are the facts that decide.

recommendations.change: Rename Mission Control in venue language: 'Live running order', 'Tasks', 'Problems', 'History', 'Team on duty', 'Finish the event'.
recommendations.why: Veterans should recognise their own way of working. '4D Mission Control' and 'timeline cursor' read as a demo.

recommendations.change: Replace the readiness percentage with a blocker sentence ('2 tasks blocked: AV check waiting on access') and the Done/total count.
recommendations.why: The team's own hallkeeper research specifies that readiness is explained by its blockers.

recommendations.change: Show assignments (who is on each task) and the latest status updates in the Now panel.
recommendations.why: People coordinate by name on the day.

evidence: EventDayOpsPage.tsx:37-64 (device time zone), 223 and 477 (issue count only), 241 and 359 (notices), 345 (Today's event), 411-417 (no start times), 426-433 (percentage), 457-467 (task buttons), 546-551 (no arrival window)
routes/event-day-ops.ts:153-175 and services/event-day-ops.ts:423-435 (no assignee, no notification)
questionsForBlake: Which should stay as the one live tool on event day: the pre-mission checklist with 'Issue report', or Mission Control with its 'Incident channel'? Or should they merge into one?
When someone logs an 'Urgent' problem, who should be alerted and how (duty manager by text, by email, in-app)? Today nobody is notified.
Should 'Mission Control' keep its name, or use plain venue words such as 'Live running order'?
For evening service in a darkened hall, do you want a dim variant of the desk palette (forest-based), or ivory everywhere?

surfaces.name: Operations handoff pack
surfaces.audience: staff, hallkeepers and planners preparing and printing the issued operational pack
surfaces.dailyUse: Inference, not measured: opened a few times per event, the day before and on the morning, and often printed.
surfaces.currentLook: The page is near-black (#050708) with gold and cyan gradients and a 56px grid-paper overlay (OpsHandoffPage.css:1-33). A gold 'INTERNAL' kicker sits over a 650-weight sans heading, 'Ops handoff pack', up to 4.25rem, with a gold 'Print / export' button. Five equal metric tiles follow: Snapshot, Pick lines, Tasks, Supplier notes and Compiled. Then come dark bordered sections: a pick-list table with cyan uppercase headers, task lists, supplier notes, three diff columns, an AI draft panel, the BEO body as a monospace <pre>, and load-in and breakdown sequences. The committed desktop baseline shows exactly this under the ivory app header.
slogFactors: The page is off-style. Dark gold and cyan grid paper reads as a technical console, not an issued venue document.
The header leads with metadata (snapshot version, line counts, compile time) instead of the event, date, room and guests (lines 140-158).
The copy is jargon: 'Ops handoff pack', 'Pick lines', 'Snapshot v4', 'BEO internal handoff', 'Room flip'.
The BEO renders as a monospace wall of text (lines 314; CSS 342-351).
Five metric tiles of equal weight stack into five full-width boxes on phones (CSS 144-158, 409-417).
workflowGaps: There are no event facts or back links. The header lacks the event name, date and room, and nothing links back to the event board or setup sheet.
Empty supplier notes render an empty grid with no message (lines 239-247). Empty load-in and breakdown sequences render bare headings (317-340).
'Compiled' uses the device's time zone (formatDateTime, lines 16-26).

Inferred from CSS, not print-tested: printing leaves headings and text in #f7f0e4 or its 0.7 alpha on white. The print block sets colour only on .ops-handoff-section, while h1, h2, h3, strong and p carry their own light colours (CSS 55-62, 200-216, 414-440). Measured: #f7f0e4 on white is 1.13:1, so 'Print / export' would produce near-invisible headings.
The AI draft panel sits mid-document, before the BEO it drafts (lines 297-313).
strengths: The content is complete: pick list, setup, room-flip, breakdown and supplier tasks, supplier notes, itemised diffs with explicit empty states, and load-in and breakdown sequences.
The AI output is labelled 'Staff review required' and the AI panel is hidden in print.
The error state is honest and has Retry (committed baseline mobile-ops-handoff-unavailable-chromium-linux.png).

recommendations.change: Fix the print styles. Set ink colours on every text element in @media print, hide the DashboardLayout chrome, and verify with a real print preview.
recommendations.why: Inferred from the CSS, not print-tested: 'Print / export' would produce headings and text near-white on white paper, a broken promise on the one button in the header.

recommendations.change: Restyle the page as an issued ivory document in Newsreader. OpsHandoffPage.css:1-33 (dark and grid), 55-62 and 200-216 (light text colours), 342-351 (monospace), 414-440 (print block)

surfaces.name: Client event page and the planner's event schedule dock
surfaces.dailyUse: Inference, not measured: occasional, a few visits per event during planning, but it is the client's impression of the venue.
surfaces.currentLook: An ivory sheet (#f7f5ee) sits on a sage ground (#e9ede5) with a soft shadow. A 'YOUR EVENT' kicker sits over a Georgia event name up to 48px, with a line for venue and guest count. A pale sage 'Refresh schedule' button comes next. Then a numbered phase list with sage circles, 21px Georgia phase names and 12px meta with clock and pin icons. Saved layouts appear as sage tiles. This is the surface in scope closest to the desk.
slogFactors: A maintenance action sits in the reading line: 'Refresh schedule' comes between the heading and the schedule, styled with an inline margin (ClientEventPage.tsx:13).
The raw IANA string appears in client copy: 'All times are shown in Europe/London.' (ClientEventSchedule.tsx:22).
Two small labels fall just under AA: the kicker #647b65 on #f7f5ee is 4.22:1 at 11px, and the phase-number circle #5b745f on #e5ece1 is 4.24:1 at 11px (client-event-schedule.css:15, 21).
The serif is Georgia, not the desk's Newsreader.
The back link reads 'Venviewer home' and goes to the public homepage (ClientEventPage.tsx:10).
workflowGaps: The facts that decide are missing. The payload has event.startsAt, endsAt, eventType and status (packages/types/src/client-event-schedule.ts:14-23), but the heading shows only name, venue and guests (ClientEventSchedule.tsx:51-57). There is no date on the client's own event page.
There is no venue contact, no next step (for example 'confirm final numbers by…'), and no status for their layout review.
There is no room photograph for the room they booked, although the desk already has sourced Trades Hall room photography (enquiry-room-photo.ts per the desk record).

Proposals and contracts are not reachable from here. Blake's reach decision puts proposals, contracts and the client portal in the desk look (.claude/conventions/product-experience.md, 'Founder decisions on reach').
strengths: The disclosure is honest: 'Working plan · Times may change.' Empty states are kind and useful: 'Your venue team has not added the event schedule yet. You can continue planning your room.'
Times use the venue's zone with a 24-hour clock (ClientEventSchedule.tsx:9-18).
Sign-in keeps the return path, and every error has a retry (lines 36-49).
Its ivory-on-sage composition is already close to the selected style.

recommendations.change: Lead with the facts: a weekday date and lead time ('Saturday 5 June 2027 · in 8 months'), then event type, guests, and status in words. Set it in Newsreader with large light numerals, as the desk panel does.
recommendations.why: The client's first question is 'when', and the data is already in the payload.

recommendations.change: Remove the 'Refresh schedule' button, or demote it to a quiet link. Refresh when the window regains focus. Replace the IANA string with 'UK time', shown only when the device's zone differs. Lift the kicker and circles to at least 4.5:1.
recommendations.why: This removes chores from the reading line and fixes AA.

recommendations.change: Add a forest 'Your next step' panel with the one thing the client should do next (review the layout, confirm numbers) and the named venue contact.
recommendations.why: The desk pattern gives one clear next step in the same place, and the client should never wonder who to ask.

recommendations.change: For Trades Hall rooms, open the page with the booked room's supplied photograph fading into ivory.
recommendations.why: This is the moment of scale, from the client's secure position.

recommendations.change: Change the back link to the client's own home, their events list, rather than the marketing homepage.
recommendations.why: It keeps context for a signed-in client.

evidence: ClientEventSchedule.tsx:9-18 (venue-zone times), 22 (IANA disclosure), 51-57 (heading lacks date and status)
questionsForBlake: What should a client see on their own event page beyond the schedule? For example: their venue contact, final-numbers deadline, proposal and contract status, payments.
Where should a signed-in client's home be: a list of their events, or the planner?

surfaces.name: Room plans library
surfaces.audience: hallkeepers, staff and planners looking up a room's architectural plan
surfaces.dailyUse: Inference, not measured: occasional reference, a few times a week.
surfaces.currentLook: An ivory work area on #f4f1e9 with a 230px sage rail of six room buttons, each with a photo. The main pane shows a Georgia room heading, a Cleaned/Original switch, 'Download original', and the plan on paper, dark for transparent originals. It is calm and uncluttered.
slogFactors: Small labels fail AA. The eyebrow #7e8572 on #f4f1e9 is 3.39:1, the intro #78806f is 3.64:1, the rail caption #808774 is 3.46:1 and the room-heading overline #8c917f is 3.21:1 (hallkeeper-room-plans.css:3, 5, 10, 20).
The 88px room buttons take the global 6% hover swell (no calm-controls opt-out).
'Six room references' is hard-coded copy (HallkeeperRoomPlansPage.tsx:81), while the list itself comes from data.
workflowGaps: There is no link to today's events: a room does not show when it is in use today or open that event's setup sheet.
A reader cannot jump from a plan to the rooms' current layouts.
strengths: The page is calm and clear. Provenance is honest: 'Source dimensions are annotations, not a scale.' Image failure has a recovery link, and the venue is verified before references are shown (HallkeeperRoomPlansPage.tsx:32-50).
Room photography supports recognition.

recommendations.change: Add [data-calm-controls] and move to the desk's tokens: ink-3 for muted text (at least 4.5:1) and Newsreader headings.
recommendations.why: It fixes four AA failures and removes the hover swell.

recommendations.change: Under each room in the rail, show 'In use today 18:00 · open setup sheet' when the Day Board data has a booking for it.
recommendations.why: It connects reference to today's work, and saves steps.

surfaces.name: Hallkeeper walkthrough (fictional demonstration)
surfaces.dailyUse: Rare, for onboarding and demonstrations.
surfaces.currentLook: A sandboxed iframe holds a self-contained Segoe UI and Georgia ivory demo (hallkeeper-walkthrough.html:2). Around it is a Georgia 30px header, 'Hallkeeper walkthrough', with the note 'Fictional demonstration · resets when you leave.'
slogFactors: It uses a third type stack, Segoe UI and Arial (hallkeeper-walkthrough.html:2), and an iframe with a fixed minimum height of 780–850px (hallkeeper-walkthrough.css:9-10).
The working tools link to it: the sheet footer (HallkeeperWorkspace.tsx:123), the sheet error navigation (HallkeeperPage.tsx:477) and the Day Board controls (DayBoardPage.tsx:131).
workflowGaps: It is placed among daily work links, not in help or onboarding.
strengths: It is clearly labelled fictional and isolated in an opaque-origin sandbox with a strict CSP (HallkeeperWalkthroughPage.tsx:10-11).

recommendations.change: Move the walkthrough links into a help or onboarding menu. If it stays, align its type with Newsreader and Inter.
recommendations.why: It keeps the working tools free of demo links.

questionsForBlake: Is the fictional hallkeeper walkthrough still needed in the product? If so, should it live under Help rather than beside live work?

crossCutting: The global spring hover (packages/web/index.html:96-111: scale(1.06), brightness(1.15), 0.93 on press, not gated to fine pointers) hits every surface in this cluster. The only opt-out is EnquiriesView.tsx:514. Hallkeeper checklist rows are <button>s (HallkeeperWorkspace.tsx:107), so the most frequently tapped control swells. Blake has decided to remove it everywhere. Fix it at the source in index.html rather than surface by surface.
A golden cockpit arrow cursor is applied to every non-homepage route (index.html:77-79). It belongs to the retired cockpit look and clashes with the ivory, forest, copper and sage style.

Focus rings are fragmented. Global cyan measures about 1.4:1 (global.css:42-53). The in-scope surfaces each define their own: copper #986246 at 4.46:1 (hallkeeper-sheet.css:18), green #43694b (hallkeeper-workspace.css:2), gold #f2cf83 (EventDayOpsPage.css:308-317), #54795c (room plans) and copper #a9663e at 4.13:1 (client). One desk token pair is needed: ink on light, cream on forest.

There are five serif treatments. The desk uses Newsreader. The hallkeeper workspace, Day Board, room plans, walkthrough, client page and Working documents card use Georgia. The hallkeeper states use Playfair Display. Newsreader is already loaded on every route (index.html links /src/styles/fonts/site.css; asserted in src/__tests__/startup-guardrails.test.ts:52).

Palette tokens are per-surface and disconnected: --hk-*, hkf's --ink and --muted, --db-*, hard-coded event-day colours, --ops-* and --event-*. Promote the desk's --enq-* set (EnquiriesDesk.css:9-48) into a shared desk token layer, for example in src/styles/house-tokens.css, and have every staff and client surface consume it.

The shell is inconsistent. The hallkeeper sheet has its own top bar and drops the shared DashboardLayout navigation (HallkeeperWorkspace.tsx:75-79). The client event page has no shell. Day Board, room plans, event-day ops and handoff use DashboardLayout, but paint their own dark or ivory grounds inside it.

Time zones are inconsistent. Some places use venue time (the hallkeeper workspace, client schedule, Day Board helpers). Others use the device's zone or locale (HallkeeperStatusBanner.tsx:51, InstructionsBanner.tsx:199-202, EventDayOpsPage.tsx:37-64, OpsHandoffPage.tsx:16-26). Raw IANA strings are shown to people (HallkeeperWorkspace.tsx:90, DayBoardPage.tsx:117, ClientEventSchedule.tsx:22). A shared venue-time formatter is needed.

API timing default: resolveTiming builds the indicative start as 18:00Z (packages/api/src/services/hallkeeper-sheet-v2-data.ts:36, 429). Computed: it shows 19:00 start and 17:30 setup for summer dates in Europe/London, where 18:00 local was intended. This affects the sheet, the PDF and any consumer of timing.
Two problem stores for one event, eventDayIssues and eventMissionIncidents, have separate forms on one page, and neither notifies anyone. This is a product-level decision beyond styling.

Infinite status motion (Day Board pulses in day-board.css:244-267; Mission Control mission-pulse in EventMissionControl.css:216, 716) contradicts the desk's calm-technology rule. Adopt one shared 320ms 'stamp' on state change, removed under reduced motion.

Success chatter ('Task status updated.', 'Issue logged.', 'Change acknowledged.') and errors placed away from their cause recur across the ops surfaces. The desk's rule applies: the state change is the feedback, and errors sit beside the item.

The hallkeeper design record (docs/design/hallkeeper-2026-09-07/workflow.md) already specifies the target shape: a 'Needs attention' rail, readiness explained by blockers rather than a percentage, and 'Done / Blocked / Need help' at the point of work. generated-reference.png in that folder shows the 'Room ready by / Doors at' pairing and a now-line running order that the live surfaces lack.

surfaces.name: Desktop planner cockpit shell (layout, palette, type, motion)
surfaces.audience: clients planning events; venue staff preparing layouts
surfaces.dailyUse: Clients: a few sessions of 20 to 60 minutes per event. Staff: repeated layout sessions while preparing events, potentially hours a day.
surfaces.currentLook: Near-black smoked panels (ReferenceViewer.css:12 #11100e; :20 rgba(18,17,15,.91)) with brass/gold accents in at least five variants (#c9a84c, #c6a15b, #d0ad68, #dfb968, #e2bc70). Inter UI mostly at 9 to 12px, with Georgia, Playfair Display and Geist Mono in places; Newsreader (the desk serif) is not used. About a dozen separately positioned islands float over a full-bleed 3D stage: left dock, tool pill, the '...' button, right inspector, compact command deck, layer switch, bottom timeline, booking-time ribbon, resolve caption, 3D/2D switch, Send button, Event details button and review pill (ReferenceViewer.css:16-141, SubmitForReviewPanel.css:1-11). Each is placed with hard-coded offsets (bottom:134px, 352px, 390px) and :has() cascades. The lens rail has 11 icon-only buttons; labels are hidden (ReferenceViewer.css:36). The global springy hover (scale 1.06 plus spring transition) applies to every planner button, because nothing in the planner opts out with [data-calm-controls].
slogFactors: Type is tiny for eight-hour use. The editor, App.css, ChairCountDialog and BlueprintPage together hold 86 font-size declarations under 11px (7px ×7, 8px ×12, 9px ×18, 10px ×46), for example .reference-save-status 9px (ReferenceViewer.css:52), the room subtitle 9px (:49) and command-deck buttons 10px (:102). More than 30 distinct sizes are in use, including 11.8px, 12.5px and 16.5px.
There is no colour system. The planner chrome contains 287 distinct hex literals and 413 distinct rgba() literals, mostly inline style objects, so it cannot be themed or kept consistent.

Four visual languages meet in one flow: dark and brass (cockpit), paper and oxblood (2D blueprint, BlueprintPage.tsx:90-99), paper and wine (mobile, MobilePlannerTopBar.tsx:53-146), and generic library blue, green and red status pills (SubmitForReviewPanel.tsx:76-85).

The lens rail has 11 unlabelled icons: Design, Guests, Flow, Evidence, Lighting, Power, Rigging, AV, Ops, Costs and Share (cockpit-modes.ts:5-17; the label span is hidden at ReferenceViewer.css:36). Users must memorise Anchor = Rigging and Waypoints = Flow.

Active and inactive states differ only by hue. The rail's active #dfb968 against inactive #b3afa7 has a 1.17:1 luminance ratio, and the tool pill's #e2bc70 against #d3cec5 is 1.15:1 (ReferenceViewer.css:34,38,72-73). This is colour-only state.
Every button swells 6% on hover with an overshoot spring (index.html:96-111). The planner never sets [data-calm-controls], so the rail, pill and deck buttons all pop.

Text cannot be selected anywhere. `user-select:none` covers every descendant and even inputs and textareas (App.css:19-32), and ::selection is transparent (App.css:34-37, PlannerCockpit.css:50-53). A staff member cannot copy a dimension or a note. Inference, untested: iOS Safari may block caret placement in inputs with -webkit-user-select:none.

Chrome positions depend on magic numbers chained through `body:has(...)` (ReferenceViewer.css:121-141), for example `.reference-more-tools{left:calc(50% + 226px)}` (:76). Inference: overlap is likely at in-between widths.
strengths: The captured room is never letterboxed. The stage spans the whole grid and the chrome floats over it (PlannerCockpit.css:55-70).
Phase preview honestly locks editing and says so ('Editing is paused. Return to the saved plan to edit.', PlannerCockpit.tsx:77-86).
Working states use the shared ActivityIndicator (EditorPage.tsx:374,386; ReferenceRoomHeader.tsx:40,52).
A reduced-motion media query exists at shell level (PlannerCockpit.css:310-316; App.css:935-945).
Save robustness is carefully engineered: session capture, awaited flush, conflict reload (EditorBridge.tsx:326-356).
workflowGaps: The facts that decide a layout are not on screen while designing. Seats placed against expected guests and comfortable capacity live only in the Guests lens (GuestsLensPanel.tsx:127-167), which replaces the inspector. The capacity gauge (PlannerSpatialHud) is never rendered on /plan, because App renders it only when !compactDesktop && !mobileChrome (App.tsx:106-109) and PlannerCockpit always passes compactDesktop={!mobile} (PlannerCockpit.tsx:57).
The section-cut slider is unreachable for the same reason (App.tsx:113-117).

The first-visit coach is unreachable. OnboardingHint needs !compactDesktop and also !isNarrow && !isTouch (VerticalToolbox.tsx:1901-1907, render guard just after), so a first-time client gets no orientation.
Switching to 2D unmounts the whole cockpit and swaps to a different paper aesthetic with macOS window dots (EditorPage.tsx:500-504; BlueprintPage.tsx:872-880). This is a jarring change of context.
No keyboard legend exists in the planner. The digit viewpoint keys exist only in the unmounted BookmarkPanel (BookmarkPanel.tsx:65), so 1 to 9 do nothing on /plan (inferred from the imports).

recommendations.change: Opt the planner out of the global hover pop now: put [data-calm-controls] on .cockpit-shell and on the portalled dialog roots, or remove the global rule app-wide as Blake decided. Use 120ms colour hovers gated to fine pointers and scale(0.97) press only.
recommendations.why: Blake's 26 September decision: no springy hover anywhere. The desk already proves the pattern.

recommendations.change: Limit user-select:none to the canvas stage. Delete App.css:27-37 and PlannerCockpit.css:34-53 for chrome, inputs and textareas.
recommendations.why: Staff need to copy dimensions, notes and links. The current rule also hides selection highlight in fields.

recommendations.change: Add a persistent 'facts band' as a copper plane over the top-left of the stage: Guests 220 · Seats 200 · Tables 22 · Comfortable 240 (Standing/Banquet). Use large light Newsreader numerals that tick as furniture is placed, and make each fact open the relevant lens. Reuse GuestsLensPanel's model and referenceSceneSummary.
recommendations.why: This mirrors the desk's stage-count plane, which gives visible progress toward a goal (goal-gradient) and puts the deciding facts first. Today those facts sit in a 10px footer or behind a lens switch.

recommendations.change:
Re-compose into three stable zones:
- Left: an ivory sheet with the room identity (Newsreader) and the furniture list.
- Right: a forest decision panel with the inspector, and the one next step pinned to its bottom (Send to events team / Submit for approval / Create client link, depending on role and state).
- Centre: one tool bar.

Remove draggable FloatingWidgetFrame placement from core chrome.
recommendations.why: This follows the desk principle of one next step, always in the same place. It replaces about a dozen magic-offset islands.
Blake's reach decision includes the planner chrome. Brass cannot survive a background swap, so the accent must become copper or forest.

recommendations.change: Adopt a 4-step type scale with a 12px floor and 13 to 14px body text. Use Newsreader for room and panel headings, and light large numerals (tabular) for counts and measurements. Retire Playfair Display, Georgia and the uncapped fractional sizes.
recommendations.why: The 7 to 10px text at 38% alpha (house-text-3 measures 3.29:1 on the dock) tires the eyes over eight hours.

recommendations.change: Label the lens rail and split it into 'Plan' (Design, Guests, Share) and 'Production' (Flow, Evidence, Lighting, Power, Rigging, AV, Ops, Costs). Show Production to staff roles only. The active state becomes a forest fill with a cream label, not a hue shift.
recommendations.why: Clients should not face 11 unexplained engineering lenses. State must not rely on colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1 / 1.4.11).

recommendations.change: Add a '?' keyboard legend that lists the real bindings (F, D, M, G, Q/E/R, Delete, Ctrl+Z/Y, Esc), styled like the desk's keycap legend. Restore the 1 to 9 viewpoint keys, now only in the unmounted BookmarkPanel.
recommendations.why: Keyboard use is what makes high-frequency work fast for veterans, and the bindings exist but are invisible.

questionsForBlake: The planner sits over a live 3D room. Should its chrome be the forest decision surface (dark green) over the scene with ivory only for lists, or go fully ivory like the desk? Light chrome competes more with a dim captured room.
Should clients see the production lenses (Power, Rigging, AV, Evidence, Ops, Costs) at all, or only Design, Guests and Share?
Would you like the planner to open, like the desk, with the sourced room photograph as the arrival moment before the 3D room resolves?

surfaces.name: Tool controls (ToolPill, desktop 'More tools' grid, mobile dock)
surfaces.dailyUse: Constant during layout work: every move, rotation and save passes through these controls.
surfaces.currentLook: A dark pill top-centre with Select, Move, Rotate, Scale and Measure. Labels hide below 1280px (ToolPill.css:70-77) and the active state is gold text on transparent (ReferenceViewer.css:73). Beside it is a 32px icon-only '...' circle (VerticalToolbox.tsx:1958-1960) that opens a 3-column grid of 58px gold-gradient tiles with 8 to 9px uppercase captions at 42% white (VerticalToolbox.tsx:897-905): Select & Move, Furniture, Rotate, Save, Delete, Undo, Redo, Camera, Draw, Snap, Walls, Sheet and Account. Tooltips are 20px Playfair cards with blur and overshoot entry (VerticalToolbox.tsx:786-812, 928-1000). Mobile uses a light paper dock.
slogFactors: Two competing tool systems: the pill uses useToolStore and the More grid uses local `activeTool` state (VerticalToolbox.tsx:1445). There are two Selects and two Rotates with different behaviour.

The More grid's 'Rotate' and 'Delete' buttons do nothing to the selection. `handleToolClick` only sets local highlight state for them (VerticalToolbox.tsx:1561-1563, 1991, 1999), and nothing reads `activeTool === "delete"`. The tooltip still says 'Delete selected furniture and attached chairs' (inferred from source; untested in a browser).

False shortcut claims. The 'Select & Move' tooltip advertises V (VerticalToolbox.tsx:1983), but no KeyV handler exists (grep). ToolPill's comment says digits jump to bookmarks, but that handler lives only in the unmounted BookmarkPanel.
Core actions (Save, Undo, Delete, Draw, Camera) are hidden behind an unlabelled '...' on desktop.
Save's 'active' gold state means 'saved' (VerticalToolbox.tsx:2003), which conflates tool state with status.

'Sheet' opens /hallkeeper/:configId in a new tab (VerticalToolbox.tsx:1646-1650), but that route allows only admin, staff, hallkeeper and planner (router.tsx:471-476). Inferred: a guest or client gets a denial page.
Tooltips appear on mouse hover only (VerticalToolbox.tsx:870-873), so keyboard users never see the shortcut.
The motion is springy and blurred: tooltip scale 0.85→1.03 with blur(6px), pop-out scale 1.08, and toolbar hover translateY(-1px) (VerticalToolbox.tsx:700-715, 790-800).
strengths: The ToolPill value chip is a real instrument: a tabular readout (135°, ×1.25, 3.20 m) that scrubs in 1° or 1% steps, with one scrub making one undo entry (ToolPill.tsx:115-151).
The pill is permanent chrome that never animates open, and it gives press feedback at scale(0.97) (ToolPill.css:1-9, 55-57).
Undo aria-labels name the entry ('Undo Move 3 items', PlannerCommandDeck.tsx:115-133).
workflowGaps: The value chip is pointer-only: a div with no role, tabindex or keyboard stepping (ToolPill.tsx:175-185).

The same verbs appear in many places. Select appears 3 times (pill, deck, More), Undo and Redo 2 to 3 times, Add furniture 4 times (deck, outliner footer, empty inspector, More) and Delete 3 times (deck, More, inspector footer).
Grid Snap, Walls and Camera toggles give no visible confirmation outside the More grid once it closes.

recommendations.change: Make the More grid's Rotate act on the selection (15° steps as with R) and its Delete call removeItems on the selection with an Undo affordance, or remove both buttons. Add a regression test.
recommendations.why: A button that highlights and does nothing is the most frustrating failure a veteran can meet.

recommendations.change: Implement V or remove it from the tooltip. Fix the command-deck placement copy 'Rotate with R before release', because PlacementGhost handles Q/E only (PlacementGhost.tsx:340-345).
recommendations.why: Honest consequences start with honest shortcut claims.

recommendations.change:
Merge into one labelled tool bar:
- Select, Move, Rotate, Scale, Measure | Add furniture (F), Draw notes (D) | Undo, Redo.
- Always show the labels at 12 to 13px.
- The active tool gets a forest fill with a cream label.
- Move Snap, Walls, Camera views and Sheet into a labelled 'View' menu, and make Account part of the global header.
- Delete the duplicate verbs from the deck and the More grid.
recommendations.why: This gives one place per verb and one mental model, with the next step always in the same place.

recommendations.change: Show tooltips on keyboard focus as well as hover. Replace the blur and overshoot keyframes with a 120ms opacity fade under fine pointers, removed under reduced motion.
recommendations.why: Calm motion and keyboard parity.

recommendations.change: Make the value chip keyboard-operable (role=spinbutton with arrow keys ±1°/±1% and Shift ±15°), and show the Measure result as a large light numeral.
recommendations.why: Keyboard for frequent work, and numbers as a satisfying readout.

recommendations.change: Hide 'Sheet' for roles that cannot open /hallkeeper/:configId. For those who can, label it 'Open crew setup sheet (new tab)'.
recommendations.why: Do not offer a dead end or hide where a click leads.

questionsForBlake: Is Scale (resizing furniture) something clients should have? Venues usually own fixed sizes (5ft rounds, 6ft trestles), and scaling may produce layouts the venue cannot build.
Which planners do your veterans know (Social Tables, AllSeated, Prismm, Cvent's diagramming)? Should we adopt their shortcut conventions?

surfaces.name: Planner command deck (contextual 'what now' bar)
surfaces.dailyUse: Seen continuously. It changes with every selection or placement.
surfaces.currentLook: App.css:261-452 designs an 86px-tall glassy black and gold deck with a 22px Georgia title, 12px detail and a gold glow. On desktop the compact variant hides the title, detail and metric (ReferenceViewer.css:97-99), leaving a horizontally scrolling row of 10px text buttons (ReferenceViewer.css:100-103). The primary action is marked only by gold text on a 10% gold wash.
slogFactors: The only state-aware guidance in the planner is hidden on desktop: 'Right-drag to look. Escape to return.', 'Drag across the floor to paint a row or block.' and the count metric (PlannerCommandDeck.tsx:210-436 against ReferenceViewer.css:97-99).
Jargon for venue veterans: 'Laser' for floor drawing (PlannerCommandDeck.tsx:372), 'Showcase' for a fly-through (:391), 'Exit POV' (:290).
Seven equal-weight 10px buttons in one row, with no single clear next step.
strengths: The copy is state-driven, plain and short. It knows markup, placement, viewpoint, selection and empty states (PlannerCommandDeck.tsx:210-436).
'Auto-fill' is offered only on a blank floor, so it cannot overwrite work, and it sizes to the planned guest count (:401-421).
Undo and Redo aria-labels name the recorded entry.
workflowGaps: 'Clear' in drawing mode wipes every stroke with no confirmation and no undo. clearStrokes sets `strokes: []` and only logs (markup-store.ts:211-219).
Delete gives no closure or Undo prompt. The selection simply vanishes (PlannerCommandDeck.tsx:326-329).
Auto-fill states its consequence only in an aria-label. Sighted users are not told that it fills the whole room when no guest count is set (:411-413).

recommendations.change: Make the deck the single 'next step' bar. Show the one-sentence state (13 to 14px), one forest primary button and at most two quiet secondaries, and keep it on desktop. Move undo, redo and select to the tool bar.
recommendations.why: The desk's key pattern is one next step, always in the same place.

recommendations.change: After destructive or bulk actions, show a quiet closure line with Undo, for example '12 chairs removed · Undo' or '22 round tables placed for 220 guests · Undo'. Keep it in the deck, not as a toast storm.
recommendations.why: Visible progress and closure, and honest consequences. It removes the fear of experimenting.

recommendations.change: Give 'Clear' drawing an undo (push the cleared strokes to history) or an inline confirm naming the count ('Clear 14 strokes?').
recommendations.why: It currently loses work irrecoverably.

recommendations.change: Rename the labels: Laser → Draw notes, Showcase → Walk-through, Exit POV → Leave viewpoint. The Auto-fill label names its result: 'Lay out 22 rounds for 220'.
recommendations.why: Use veterans' vocabulary and state consequences before acting.

questionsForBlake: Should Auto-fill offer the common Trades Hall set-ups by name (Banquet rounds of 10, Theatre, Cabaret, Boardroom), as veterans think in named set-ups?

surfaces.name: Furniture catalogue panel
surfaces.dailyUse: Opened many times per layout. It is the main way to add anything.
surfaces.currentLook: A near-black slide-out 336px panel (VerticalToolbox.tsx:136-145) with a gold 'Event kit' kicker and a 28px Playfair 'Build the room' hero on every open (:2093-2102). Three workflow cards use 9px sub-labels at 48% white (:2105-2138), then search, a 3-column chip tablist with 9px uppercase labels (:209-227), and a permanent 'Chair brush' hint. Rows are 36px thumbnails with the name at 13px and the subtitle at 35% white. The panel slides in over 450ms with an 8px overshoot and blur (:649-653), and rows stagger at 40ms each (:2243).
slogFactors: The search focus is effectively invisible. `outline:none` is set inline, with a 0.06-alpha gold ring (:2153-2158) that measures about 1.07:1.
The stagger replays on every open. At 40ms per row, the 20th row appears about 0.8s after opening, every time.
The hero and hints repeat forever for daily users, pushing the actual furniture down.
Category headers are clickable divs with no role or keyboard access (:2205-2215), and asset rows respond to Enter only, not Space (:2256).
Hover drives rows sideways with translateX(6px) and the global pop (:692-698).
strengths: Drag-from-panel with a floating drag preview and a pointer threshold, plus click-to-place (:229, :1735+).
Supplied-model previews with a silhouette fallback.
Search filters live and counts per category update.
workflowGaps: No venue facts: no seats per table, no dimensions in the list, and no owned quantity. Nothing stops a client placing 40 rounds when the venue owns 24. The inventory reference image leads with owned and usable numbers.
No recents or favourites, so a staff member placing the same 5ft round a hundred times a week re-finds it each time.
F opens the panel, but focus does not move to search, so typing to filter is not keyboard-first.

recommendations.change: Fix contrast (subtitles and counts at least 4.5:1) and give search a visible ink or cream focus ring. Make category headers real buttons with aria-expanded, and make rows respond to Space as well as Enter.
recommendations.why: WCAG AA text and a visible focus ring.

recommendations.change: Remove the per-open stagger and the overshoot slide. Use one 160ms fade and slide with ease-out, none under reduced motion.
recommendations.why: Calm motion. The panel is opened hundreds of times a day.

recommendations.change: Replace the hero and permanent hints with a compact header showing Recents first. On F, focus search.
recommendations.why: Remove steps for daily users.

recommendations.change: Re-skin as an ivory sheet. Each row shows the tangible furniture illustration, a Newsreader name and a fact line in the desk's style: '5ft round · seats 10 · 1.52 m'. For staff, add 'Owned 24 · placed 18', and when placed exceeds usable stock, add a copper note linking to Inventory.
recommendations.why: This is the selected inventory style and solves a problem other planners ignore (layout versus stock).

questionsForBlake: Should clients see owned stock limits (for example 'up to 24 rounds'), or should only staff see stock, with clients warned softly?
Is the illustrated furniture from the inventory style acceptable in the catalogue, or should rows show the actual supplied model thumbnails?

surfaces.name: Chair count dialog (seats per table)
surfaces.audience: clients and staff placing dining tables
surfaces.dailyUse: It fires on every dining-table placement and every double-click to edit, so a 22-table banquet means 22 modals.
surfaces.currentLook: A full-screen 55% black overlay with a 24px-radius near-black card. It shows a gold uppercase 'ROUND TABLE' kicker, a Playfair 'Seating Arrangement' title and a 40px bold number stepper, then a gold gradient CTA 'Place 10 Chairs' with hover lift and scale 1.02, and grey 'Table Only' and 'Cancel' buttons. It enters with scale 0.88, translateY(24px) and blur(8px) (ChairCountDialog.tsx:59-127, 205-414).
slogFactors: A blocking modal every time a table is placed (PlacementGhost.tsx:209-221). The count resets to 10 or 2 each time (ChairCountDialog.tsx:133-140, 165-171), so a planner wanting 8 per table corrects every one.

Keyboard trap with a hidden consequence. A window keydown handler treats Enter on any focused button as confirm (ChairCountDialog.tsx:191) and preventDefaults the click. Enter on 'Cancel' or 'Table Only' therefore places the table with chairs (inferred from source; untested).
The −/+ buttons act on pointerdown only and their onClick calls preventDefault (:288, :342), so Space does nothing and Enter confirms the dialog.
Contrast: the range hint and Cancel in #555 on #101010 measure 2.55:1 (:355, :402). The count input sets `outline:none` (:321).
Title Case copy ('Seating Arrangement', 'Place 10 Chairs', 'Table Only') and a bouncy CTA.
strengths: The stepper is capped at what physically fits this table and scale, so there is no silent clamping (:152-163).
After confirming, it re-selects the same item so the next table can be placed at once (App.tsx:152-156).
It has a focus trap and closes on Escape.
workflowGaps: Cancel or a backdrop click discards the table placement entirely, because the ghost and selection were cleared before the dialog opened (PlacementGhost.tsx:217-219).
It does not show the consequence for the event, for example 'Seats 150 → 160 of 220 guests'.

recommendations.change: Fix the Enter handling now. Only confirm when focus is in the count input or on the confirm button, and make −/+ respond to click and keyboard. Add regression tests for Enter on Cancel and Table Only.
recommendations.why: Enter on Cancel places furniture: a consequence the user never chose.

recommendations.change: Replace the per-table modal with an inline 'Seats per table' stepper in the placement bar. Default it to the venue's standard and remember the last choice for the session. Place with one click, and edit a placed table's seats in the inspector.
recommendations.why: This removes 22 modals from a banquet. Modal-on-every-action is exactly the 'hard work' Blake forbids.

recommendations.change: Show the running consequence beside the stepper as a light numeral: 'Seats 160 of 220 guests'.
recommendations.why: Visible progress toward the goal.

recommendations.change: Until it is replaced, re-skin the dialog: forest card, cream Newsreader heading 'Seats at this table', sentence case, AA contrast, visible focus, and no blur or scale entry.
recommendations.why: The desk's palette and calm motion.

questionsForBlake: What is Trades Hall's default seats per round (10 at 5ft? 12 at 6ft?), and should the planner assume it without asking?

surfaces.name: Room header, Layers outliner, inspector and lens panels (side docks)
surfaces.audience: staff preparing layouts; clients checking their plan
surfaces.dailyUse: Always on screen on desktop.
surfaces.currentLook: Left dock (260px): the venue name uppercase at 10px, the room name at 9px in #a6a095, a 26×30 save icon, and save status at 9px (ReferenceViewer.css:40-52). Below that sits a 'Layers' tree listing every chair individually, and an 11px uppercase header. Right dock (248px): an 'Inspector' in CAD language (X (m), Z (m), Surface height, Scale %) with 10 to 11px labels (SelectedFurnitureInspector.tsx:79-86; ReferencePanels.css:38-45). Lens panels in the same 248px dock use a different, larger scale of 12.5 to 23px (LensPanel.css:55-331).
slogFactors: For a 200-seat banquet the Layers tree runs to 200+ rows: every chair is a row (SceneOutliner.tsx:33-44). 'Layers', 'Architecture' and 'Room capture' are software words.
The only whole-layout summary is a 10px footer, '22 tables · 200 chairs · 22 groups' (SceneOutliner.tsx:92; ReferencePanels.css:33).
The inspector leads with geometry (X/Z metres, surface height, scale %) rather than what a booker cares about: table number, seats and linen.
Save state is a 9px caption beside a 26px icon. Closure is barely perceptible.
Type scale jumps between docks: 9 to 11px in the outliner and inspector, then 16.5px metrics in a lens panel of the same width.
strengths: Remove states its count ('Remove 11 objects') and is undoable through history epochs (SelectedFurnitureInspector.tsx:147).
Number inputs validate with a clear message ('Use 25–400.') and revert on Escape (:17-37).
It warns honestly about approximate dimensions ('Approximate planning dimensions · confirm before final setup.', :58).
The venue logo falls back to an icon, and the home link resolves per role (Diary, event details, or home) (ReferenceRoomHeader.tsx:27-30).
workflowGaps: Switching lens replaces the inspector (CockpitRightDock.tsx:183-194), so checking seat balance loses the selection context.
Table numbering and naming are absent. Veterans and hallkeepers speak in 'Table 7', and the tree shows shortLabel only.

recommendations.why: Lead with the facts that decide, give visible closure, and use veterans' vocabulary.

recommendations.change: Inspector order becomes: What it is (name, seats, linen, place settings, note) → Position. Move the X/Z/rotation/scale fields into a 'Precise position' disclosure. Use a forest panel with cream text.
recommendations.why: This reduces cognitive load for clients and bookers, while staff keep precision one click away.

recommendations.change: Keep the facts band (see the shell) visible across lenses. Open lenses beside the inspector as a tab within the forest panel, rather than replacing it.
recommendations.why: Keep context: detail beside, not replacing.

recommendations.change: Unify panel type to the shared 4-step scale with a 12px minimum, and tabular light numerals for metrics.
recommendations.why: Consistency and legibility.

questionsForBlake: Should the planner number tables automatically (Table 1 to n, with the top table named) so the client, the booker and the hallkeeper sheet share one reference?

surfaces.name: Save, send, review and share flows
surfaces.audience: clients sending a layout; staff submitting or sharing with clients
surfaces.dailyUse: Clients: once or twice per event (the conversion moment). Staff: submit and share several times a day.
surfaces.currentLook: 'Send to Events Team' is a gold-gradient button stacked bottom-right. It opens a near-black modal with a blur-in (scale 0.92, blur 8px), a gold 'ALMOST THERE' kicker, a Playfair 'Send your layout' title and a dark form. The success screen has an animated gold check. The review status is a floating top-centre pill using generic library colours (blue 'Under Review', green 'Approved', red 'Rejected') in Title Case. The Share lens offers 'Create client share link'. The save error is a dark toast with a ⚠ glyph and gold 'Retry'.
slogFactors: The venue name is hard-coded. 'Trades Hall will reply to' (GuestEnquiryModal.tsx:254) and 'shared only with the Trades Hall events team' (:596) appear for any venue. This is a tenancy and trust bug.
Praise and encouragement copy ('Almost there', :362) and a showy blur and scale entry, both of which Blake calls belittling or noisy.
Contrast: 'No account needed.' at 40% white measures about 3.81:1 (:372). Placeholders sit at 25%.
Status pills use off-palette generic colours and harsh wording ('Rejected') (SubmitForReviewPanel.tsx:76-85).

The Share lens calls the result 'Client link — sent' (ShareLensPanel.tsx:208). The flow transitions the proposal to 'sent' and creates a token (:93-101), but inferred from proposals.ts:525-560 no email reaches the client. Staff may believe the client has it.
strengths: Sending flushes autosave first and never reports success over a stale layout (EditorBridge.tsx:326-356; send-layout-flow.ts:8-46).
Capacity guidance in the enquiry form uses the same basis as the planner (GuestEnquiryModal.tsx:134-147).
Review actions respect preview locks and say why a button is disabled ('Exit preview to submit').
The save-conflict toast gives revision numbers and a Reload action (EditorPage.tsx:578-580).
workflowGaps: If flushAutoSave fails, 'Send to Events Team' silently returns to idle with no message (SaveSendPanel.tsx:92-104).
'Submit for Approval' does not say who is notified or that the layout locks while under review. Withdraw does not say what happens.
Each 'Create another link' click creates a whole new proposal (createProposal inside run(), ShareLensPanel.tsx:92-96). That consequence is hidden and can clutter the pipeline.
The enquiry form asks for guest count and event type from scratch, although the planner knows plannedGuestCount and the seats placed.
The toast promises 'we'll try again'. Autosave only reschedules on the next edit (EditorBridge.tsx:287-310). This is an inference; no timed retry after failure was found.

recommendations.change: Replace the hard-coded 'Trades Hall' with the planner venue identity (usePlannerVenueIdentity).
recommendations.why: Tenancy and truthfulness: another venue's client must not be told Trades Hall will reply.

recommendations.change: Relabel the Share result honestly, for example 'Link ready. Not emailed; copy it into your message.'. Reuse the existing proposal for 'another link', or say 'Creates a new proposal' before acting.
recommendations.why: Say real consequences before acting.

recommendations.change: Put the one next step in the forest decision panel with its consequence line. Client: 'Send to the {venue} events team' then '{venue} receives this layout and your details'. Staff: 'Submit for approval' then 'Your events team is notified; the layout locks until they respond'. Surface flush failures inline with Retry.
recommendations.why: One next step, always in the same place, with honest consequences.

recommendations.change: Prefill the enquiry from what the planner knows (expected guests or seats placed, event type), and remove 'Almost there'. Re-skin to ivory and forest, with a sealed Newsreader 'Layout sent' stamp in place of the gold animated check.
recommendations.why: Remove steps, cut praise copy, and give dignified closure like the desk's stamp.

recommendations.change: Show review status in desk tones and words: copper 'With the events team', sage 'Approved', amber 'Changes asked for', slate 'Withdrawn'. Use sentence case.
recommendations.why: Tone doubled by a named chip, in the selected palette.

recommendations.change: Either add a real timed retry with visible state ('Retrying in 10 s') or change the toast copy to 'Your layout is safe here. Retry'.
recommendations.why: Do not promise behaviour that does not exist.

questionsForBlake: When a client sends a layout, should they receive a confirmation email with the layout link? Which address should the venue's reply come from?
Should 'Create client link' also email the client from Venviewer, naming the recipient before sending, or stay copy-and-paste?

surfaces.name: Event details (hallkeeper instructions) and object notes
surfaces.audience: staff and planners writing instructions for the hallkeeper
surfaces.dailyUse: Once or twice per event, with long-form typing: dietary needs, access, contacts, deadlines.
surfaces.currentLook: 'Event details' is a 10px gold-on-black fixed button (EditorPage.tsx:518-539; ReferenceViewer.css:137). It opens a 640px dark modal on a 60% black overlay. Field labels are 10px uppercase in TEXT_MUT #5c5955 (EventDetailsPanel.tsx:696) and inputs are #111. The footer reads 'Not saved yet' or 'Saved at' with toLocaleTimeString() (:598-599). Object notes use 9px gold kickers (ObjectNotePanel.tsx:107, 271).
slogFactors: Label contrast: #5c5955 on #1a1a1d measures 2.49:1 at 10px.
A backdrop click or × closes the modal and silently discards unsaved long-form text. There is no dirty guard (EventDetailsPanel.tsx:387, 411).
No focus trap or Escape handling in this modal (grep finds neither).
The time format is browser-locale (toLocaleTimeString() without en-GB).
Modal-over-scene hides the layout that the instructions describe.
strengths: The panel is hidden for unclaimed public previews, avoiding silent 401s (EditorPage.tsx:461-466).
Save is blocked until the GET resolves, so an early save cannot wipe instructions (EventDetailsPanel.tsx:63, 629-655).
Placeholders are real venue examples (fire exits, service entrance, dietary).
workflowGaps: There is no indication on the main planner that instructions exist or are incomplete, for example 'Day-of contact missing'.

recommendations.change: Add a dirty guard (inline 'Keep editing / Discard changes'), a focus trap, Escape handling and en-GB times.
recommendations.why: Preserve data, and keep keyboard use safe.

recommendations.change: Move the panel into the forest side panel as an 'Event' tab beside the layout, rather than a modal. Show completeness facts ('Contact ✓ · Access ✓ · 2 deadlines') on the tab.
recommendations.why: Keep context, and show visible progress and closure.

recommendations.change: Raise the labels to at least 12px at 4.5:1 or better, in cream on forest.
recommendations.why: WCAG AA.

surfaces.name: 2D Blueprint (editor 2D view and public /blueprint demo)
surfaces.audience: clients and staff wanting a flat plan; public visitors on /blueprint
surfaces.dailyUse: Occasional. It is used to check spacing and to print or share a flat plan.
surfaces.currentLook: A paper look: PAPER #f3ecdd, INK #1a1a1a and ACCENT_RED oxblood #8c1f1f (BlueprintPage.tsx:90-99). A fake macOS title bar has red, amber and green dots (:872-880). A left sidebar has pills and a stepper, a right inspector, and a status bar with a 'Send for quote →' CTA. JetBrains Mono is specified but not loaded (none found in index.html or the styles). Canvas tool buttons are glyphs (✛ ⟲ ⟳) with title attributes only (:1721-1728).
slogFactors: The public /blueprint demo shows 'Plan sent — our events team will respond within 24 hours.' but only marks the local draft saved (:294-298). This is placeholder success and an invented service promise.
The 'Room' control looks like a dropdown ('▾') but is static text (:915-921). The Wedding/Gala/Conference pills are local state that is never saved.
INK_FAINT #8c8579 on PAPER measures 3.11:1, and 2.89:1 on the sidebar (used for 11 to 12px labels).
A third palette (oxblood) and fake window chrome, unrelated to the selected style.
strengths: Drag moves grouped items together and writes to the shared editor store, so 2D and 3D stay consistent (:765-791).
The status chips give useful facts: seats placed, rounds, floor used and an egress draft (:2274-2290).
The demo has a keyboard help overlay (:412-470), a model the planner lacks.
workflowGaps: You cannot delete, rotate or add in 2D, yet the buttons suggest you can.
Switching 3D and 2D swaps the whole visual world and loses the docks.

recommendations.change: Remove the fake 'Plan sent' success from /blueprint now: route it to the real guest-enquiry flow or remove the CTA. Hide or disable (with a reason) every noop control in the editor 2D view until it is wired.
recommendations.why: No placeholder success or fake integrations, and no dead ends.

recommendations.change: Wire the 2D view to the same store actions: rotate, removeItems, zoom and pan state, and add-from-chip through the placement store.
recommendations.why: Parity makes 2D a real tool for bookers who think in floor plans.
One family across views, and AA text.

questionsForBlake: Is /blueprint (the standalone local demo with templates) still wanted as a public page, or should it redirect to /plan?

Should the 2D plan be the printable floor plan that goes into proposals and the hallkeeper sheet? If so, which drawing conventions do your veterans expect (table numbers, scale bar, north arrow, exits)?

surfaces.name: Room layout timeline dock and client schedule dock (bottom)
surfaces.audience: staff reviewing phase layouts; clients viewing their schedule
surfaces.dailyUse: Always visible, collapsed at 74px on desktop. It is expanded occasionally.
surfaces.currentLook: A dark dock, 292px when expanded, with brass accents. The title 'Room layouts' is 10px uppercase with the subtitle 'Frozen room outline + furniture are the saved plan · motion is a preview' (RoomLayoutTimelineDock.tsx:1335). Phase chips and filmstrip labels run 7 to 9px, many at house-text-3 38% alpha (CockpitBottom.css:111-862).
slogFactors: 7 to 8px text in at least 19 declarations (for example CockpitBottom.css:244, 251, 283, 526, 589, 706, 827, 862), with house-text-3 at about 3.29:1.
The permanent subtitle is engineering jargon.
For a public client with no event, the dock permanently says 'Your event schedule / No event linked to this layout' (ClientEventScheduleDock.tsx:38), 74px of dead chrome.
strengths: The playback controls declare aria-keyshortcuts ([ ] Space) (RoomLayoutTimelineDock.tsx:1500-1506).
Preview never mutates the saved plan, and it says so.
workflowGaps: The dock shifts every other island by hard-coded offsets when expanded (ReferenceViewer.css:121-141).

recommendations.change: Hide the client dock entirely when no event is linked. For staff, show the dock only when the event has phases.
recommendations.why: Remove chrome that carries nothing.

recommendations.change: Raise the minimum text to 12px, use Newsreader for phase names, replace the jargon subtitle with 'Preview of each phase. Your saved plan does not change.', and use desk status tones for frozen, draft and gap.
recommendations.why: Legibility and plain language.

surfaces.name: Planner loading and error states
surfaces.audience: clients and staff opening a plan
surfaces.dailyUse: At every open, for a few seconds.
surfaces.currentLook: A black gradient full screen with a dark gold-bordered card, a Georgia 28 to 42px heading and the shared ActivityIndicator (global.css:61-110; EditorPage.tsx:339-412).
slogFactors: The load error shows the raw store message, and its only action is 'Start a fresh planner draft' (EditorPage.tsx:394-411). A transient failure pushes the user away from the layout they asked for.
Georgia and black-and-gold instead of the selected style.
strengths: Honest progressive headings ('Opening the planner' becomes 'Opening the {room} planner' only once the room is resolved) (EditorPage.tsx:366-379).
Distinct, plain copy for not-found, forbidden, empty and network cases (:63-90).
workflowGaps: There is no 'Try again' for a saved-layout load failure, and nothing says the saved layout itself is not lost.

recommendations.change: Add a primary 'Try again' with the plain cause, and keep 'Start a new draft' as the secondary. Re-skin to the ivory sheet with a Newsreader heading, and show the room photograph if it is sourced.
recommendations.why: No dead ends, and a calm, beautiful arrival.

surfaces.name: Mobile planner chrome
surfaces.audience: clients on phones and tablets; staff on site
surfaces.dailyUse: Client browsing and quick edits. Staff walkthroughs on site.
surfaces.currentLook: A light paper top bar (rgba(248,242,230,.94)) with ink #241913 and a wine #7a1f2a Send button (MobilePlannerTopBar.tsx:53-146). A dock gives Select, Add, Draw, View and More, with contextual Rotate, Cancel, Done and Delete (VerticalToolbox.tsx:1325-1340). Its sheets are light paper.
slogFactors: A fourth accent colour (wine), outside the selected palette.
The non-embedded layer switch uses 3D jargon 'Mesh / Splat / Hybrid' (CanvasLayerControls.tsx:17-20, 147); desktop says Model / Capture / Combined (:94).
Inferred: the planner shell's user-select:none on inputs (App.css:27-32) may hamper caret placement and editing on iOS.
strengths: The contextual dock (idle, placing, selected) gives exactly the relevant actions with 44px targets.
The catalogue becomes a bottom sheet with a 44px close button and Escape handling, and returns focus to its opener (VerticalToolbox.tsx:1447-1456, 2085-2089).
workflowGaps: There is no facts summary (seats against guests) on mobile.

recommendations.change: Retone to the ivory, forest and copper tokens. Use the desktop wording (Model / Capture / Combined). Add a one-line facts strip ('200 seats · 220 guests').
recommendations.why: One family, and plain words.

surfaces.name: Unmounted legacy planner chrome (CatalogueDrawer, BookmarkPanel, WallTogglePanel UI, CockpitTopBar, PlannerSpatialHud, .planner-status-header CSS)
surfaces.dailyUse: Never shown.
surfaces.currentLook: CatalogueDrawer is a 'TFT-style bottom shop bar' (CatalogueDrawer.tsx:15-16) and is referenced only by itself. BookmarkPanel is referenced only by a store test. The WallTogglePanel UI in generic #333/#fff is not imported; only AutoWallSelector and InvalidateOnToggle are (PlannerScene.tsx:23). CockpitTopBar has no JSX usage. PlannerSpatialHud and SectionSlider never render on /plan (App.tsx:106-117). About 260 lines of `.planner-status-header` CSS (App.css:84-259, 864-921) exist only as avoid-selectors.
slogFactors: Dead chrome carries stale shortcut behaviour (the digits in BookmarkPanel) and conflicting palettes into every future re-skin.
Avoid-selector lists across seven components still reference `.planner-status-header` (for example SaveSendPanel.tsx:32, VerticalToolbox.tsx:1029).
strengths: PlannerSpatialHud contains useful ideas (capacity gauge, layout grade) worth re-homing in the facts band.
workflowGaps: The capacity and grade facts built for PlannerSpatialHud are not reachable anywhere on the planner.

recommendations.change: Delete CatalogueDrawer, the BookmarkPanel UI (moving its digit-key handler into a mounted hook), the WallTogglePanel UI, CockpitTopBar and the .planner-status-header CSS. Re-home the PlannerSpatialHud capacity model into the facts band.
recommendations.why: Less surface to re-skin and no stale claims. The re-skin cannot miss hidden variants.

crossCutting: Global hover pop: index.html:96-111 applies scale(1.06) and a spring to every button outside [data-calm-controls]. The planner (cockpit, portalled ChairCountDialog and GuestEnquiryModal) never opts out. Blake decided to remove it everywhere, so remove it at source rather than adding per-surface opt-outs.

Focus rings: the global cyan ring (#87e7f0, global.css:42-54; house-tokens.css:79) still reaches catalogue rows (role=button) and dialog inputs. The planner overrides it with brass on dark (ReferenceViewer.css:143) but with 'outline:none' on key inputs (ChairCountDialog.tsx:321, VerticalToolbox.tsx:2153). Adopt the desk's ink-on-ivory and cream-on-forest rings as shared tokens.

Desk tokens are scoped to .enq-desk (EnquiriesDesk.css:9-46). Lift them into a shared token file (ground, sheet, plane, forest, copper, sage, brick, amber, slate and their inks) before re-skinning the planner. The house-* tokens (house-tokens.css) are dark-theme only.
Brass and gold (#c9a84c) measure 1.95:1 on ivory #F2EDDD. Re-skinning cannot keep brass as a text or accent colour on light surfaces, so map accents to copper #94491f or forest.

Fonts: the planner uses Playfair Display, Georgia, Inter and Geist Mono, and specifies JetBrains Mono, which is not loaded. None is Newsreader, the desk's serif. Consolidate to Newsreader (headings, numerals) plus Inter (UI).

Inline style objects and module-load <style> injection (VerticalToolbox.tsx:645-812, ChairCountDialog.tsx:59-127, GuestEnquiryModal.tsx:25-77) hold 287 hex and 413 rgba literals across the planner chrome. They must become CSS classes on shared tokens before any theme is possible.

Motion: blur plus overshoot keyframes (panel slide, tooltip, dropdown, dialog entry) contradict the desk's press-only calm motion. The cockpit's `filter:none !important` (PlannerCockpit.css:42-48) already kills the blur inside the cockpit, but not in body-portalled dialogs.

Shared FloatingWidgetFrame: autoCompact={cameraInteractionActive} collapses widgets on every camera orbit (for example SaveSendPanel.tsx:128, VerticalToolbox.tsx:1064). Movable, minimisable widgets conflict with 'next step always in the same place'.
Hard-coded 'Trades Hall' copy in shared client flows (GuestEnquiryModal.tsx:254, 596) breaks tenancy; a venue-identity audit is needed across client-facing copy.

Visual baselines: no committed Playwright snapshot covers /plan or /blueprint (e2e/*-snapshots cover the dashboard, operational, public and twin pages only). Add desktop, tablet and phone planner baselines before and after the re-skin so Blake can compare.

cluster: Event architect, mission control and supplier portal

surfaces.name: Event Architect: brief and three-layout comparison
surfaces.audience: venue staff (sales executives, event planners); admins; hallkeepers can reach it (InternalEventRoute, DashboardLayout 'More' menu)
surfaces.dailyUse: Inferred: a few times a week per new booking or enquiry, 5 to 20 minutes per session. It is not a desk that is open all day, so every visit has to be self-explanatory.
surfaces.currentLook: This is a near-black sci-fi canvas under the ivory DashboardLayout header. Tokens are #07100f ground, mint #81d8c5, gold #e1b866 and rose #e69b8f (EventArchitectPage.css:1-23), with two radial glows and a 48px white grid overlay (13-35). The hero is at least 310px tall with a 6.2rem Georgia h1 at -0.055em tracking (45-52, 74-83). Georgia is not a loaded face, while Newsreader is loaded globally by index.html:15. There are uppercase mint 0.75rem, weight-800 kickers (54-67) and monospace ID chips (149-155). The brief is a 4-column grid of 12 inputs, then an accessibility fieldset and a prompt (157-259). Below it sit three tall candidate cards side by side (384-388). Each card stacks a plan SVG, 4 metrics, spacing facts, 5 witness paragraphs at 0.75rem, a guest-flow box with 4 more metrics and 2 paragraphs, repair hints and a full-width button (TSX 341-402). Motion is a hover lift on non-interactive cards (CSS 400-408) and a local press scale(0.97) that the global spring overrides.
slogFactors: The dark palette is off-style: #07100f with mint, gold and rose, a grid overlay and radial glows (EventArchitectPage.css:1-35). It sits directly under the ivory DashboardLayout header (DashboardLayout.css:15), so the page changes world halfway down the screen. Blake's reach decision puts every staff tool in the desk's look.
About 310px of hero sits before the first input: a 6.2rem headline 'Compare event layouts' plus a dense scope disclaimer (TSX 578-587, CSS 45-52).

Comparing the options means reading three tall columns side by side. The facts that decide are buried in 0.75rem witness sentences: seats against guests, whether it fits the room, the closest gap and the total against budget (TSX 155-189, CSS 601-608). No aligned row lets a booker compare Option 1, 2 and 3 on the same fact.
Tiny labels: dt at 0.68rem uppercase (CSS 503-509), witness status at 0.65rem (594-599), the flow hash in 0.65rem mono (653-659) and flow dt at 0.64rem (673-678).
The 'optional' labels and the accessibility note use --ea-faint (alpha 0.48). I measured 4.37:1 on the top of the brief panel gradient, under AA 4.5:1 (CSS 7, 178-182, 249-255).
