Engineering vocabulary is shown to sales staff: 'Replayable snapshot facts' (TSX 290), 'Conservative footprints', 'Exact minor units', 'Simulated flow sidecar' (746-751), 'Agents', 'Max density p/m²', 'Bottleneck %', 'Replay artifact <hash>' (324-330), 'Run 1a2b3c4d' (705).

Six separate disclaimers repeat the same caution: the scope note (585), the accessibility note (673), a per-card 'Ops handoff gate' repeated three times (335), the selection banner (713), the footer (741) and the method aside (746-751).
'Open review gates' always adds 1 (TSX 352). A clean option therefore never shows 0 and always reads as a problem.
Every card lifts 2px on hover although the card itself is not clickable (CSS 400-408), which is a false affordance.

Global cockpit spring: index.html:96-110 applies scale(1.06) and brightness(1.15) on hover, and scale(0.93) on press, to every button here. Its specificity is (0,3,2), which beats the local .event-architect-generate:active rule at (0,3,0). The !important transition also replaces the local 160ms ease. The full-width 'Use this layout' button swells 6% past its card.
workflowGaps: The run URL is not updated after generation. createEventArchitectRun resolves into setPersisted only, with no navigate to /event-architect/runs/:runId (TSX 523-530). A refresh therefore loses the comparison view, the link cannot be shared, and no endpoint lists earlier runs (api/src/routes/event-architect.ts:172-231 has no GET /runs).

Opening a saved run shows the wrong brief. The runId effect loads only the candidates (TSX 447-461), while the form keeps EMPTY_FORM defaults (80 guests, dinner) and the first room (419-445). The results never show the date, guests or room they were computed for. PersistedEventArchitectRunSchema has no brief field (types/src/event-architect.ts:244-252).

Choosing an option is final, and the page does not say so. The server rejects a second selection (services/event-architect.ts:434-436, 457-461). The UI's 'Use this layout' gives no warning. Afterwards the other two buttons simply go disabled with no explanation (TSX 393, 566).

The page does not start from the work that already exists. There is no enquiry or event parameter (only useParams runId, TSX 405), so the booker retypes date, guests, room and event type that already sit on the enquiry. Event type is free text (625), not the venue's list.

After 'Generate three options' the results render below the long form. Nothing moves focus or scrolls to them (TSX 689-744). The error path's 'Return to the brief' only resets state (699) and does not focus the form.
After selection, a 15-field ops review form is inserted above the three options (TSX 718-724). It pushes the comparison the user was just reading out of view.
The success banner says 'event binding are still required' (713) but links only to the planner. The page gives no path to attach the layout to the enquiry or booking.
strengths: Recovery messages are honest and keep the user's input: 'Your inputs are still here; try again.' (TSX 533) and 'No selection was changed; try again.' (557).
A retry reuses the idempotency key, so a double click is safe (TSX 508-517).
Missing pricing is shown as a review gate, not a pass (TSX 184; test src/__tests__/EventArchitectPage.test.tsx:356).
The '01 / Brief' and '02 / Compare' numbering gives the page a sense of progress (TSX 591, 704).
Top-down plans are drawn from the recorded room outline and real object footprints (TSX 238-285). This is tangible and could become the moment of scale.
Repair hints are plain, actionable verbs: 'Add space for 4 more guest seats.' (TSX 202-210).
Loading and working states use the shared Activity component (TSX 22, 596, 682, 691). Reduced motion is honoured for the card transition (CSS 1070-1075).

recommendations.change: Rebuild the page in the desk composition, with sage ground, an ivory sheet and a sticky forest decision panel. The ivory sheet holds the brief, then the comparison. The forest panel shows the brief's deciding facts as light large numerals (date with weekday and lead time, guests, room, budget) and the single next step in the same place at every stage: Generate three options, then Choose one, then Open in planner. Reuse the --enq-* token values, set headings in Newsreader (already global via site.css), and delete the grid overlay, the glows and the 310px hero. Mark the root [data-calm-controls]. .event-architect-page's overflow: hidden must go, because it would break position: sticky.
recommendations.why: Removes the dark sci-fi look Blake has moved away from and brings the page into the desk family (reach decision of 26 September). Keeping the facts and the next step in one place avoids hunting on a long page.

recommendations.change: Replace the three tall cards with a comparison ledger. Put the three plan thumbnails in a row on top. Beneath them, aligned rows name the fact and give each option's value with a named status chip: seats for N guests; fits the room (objects outside); closest gap against the threshold; planning total against budget; changes needed. Move the witness sentences, guest-flow metrics and spacing inputs into a per-option 'How this was checked' disclosure.
recommendations.why: A veteran decides by scanning one fact across three options. Today the facts are split across three 1,000px-plus columns in 0.75rem prose.

recommendations.change: Make the selection's consequence visible before the click. Label the button 'Use Balanced'. Under it, one line: 'Saves it as a draft layout in the planner. This comparison then closes; the other two stay here to look at. To compare again, generate new options.' After selection, the disabled buttons read 'Balanced chosen'.
recommendations.why: Selection is irreversible on the server (event-architect.ts:434-461), and today that is invisible.

recommendations.change: After a run is created, navigate (replace) to /event-architect/runs/:runId. Add a short 'Recent comparisons' list, which needs a GET /event-architect/runs endpoint scoped to the venue.
recommendations.why: Today a refresh loses the work and the result cannot be shared with a colleague.

recommendations.change: Return the brief in PersistedEventArchitectRun and use it. Hydrate the form when a run is opened, or collapse the form to a read-only brief summary with 'Start a new comparison'. Always print 'For 140 guests · Grand Hall · Sat 5 Jun 2027' above the options.
recommendations.why: Today a saved run shows 80-guest defaults above results computed for a different brief, which misleads the reader.

recommendations.change: Accept an enquiry or event ID and prefill date, guests, room and event type from the approved enquiry (the desk's 'Create opportunity' step is the natural entry). Offer event type as the venue's list.
recommendations.why: Removes retyping facts the booker already has, and ties the draft layout to the booking.

recommendations.change: Consolidate the six disclaimers into one scope line in the decision panel and one footer sentence. The footer must keep the exact test-asserted text 'not safety, occupancy, accessibility-route, or statutory determinations' (EventArchitectPage.test.tsx:395). Show the ops handoff gate once as a named step, and stop adding it to every option's 'Open review gates' count (TSX 352).
recommendations.why: Keeps the governance honesty while removing three repeated amber boxes and a count that never reaches zero.

recommendations.change: Manage focus. After generation, move focus to the 'Three layout options' heading and scroll it into view, honouring reduced motion. After an error, focus the first invalid field. Remove the hover lift on non-interactive cards. Use the desk's focus rings: ink on ivory, cream on forest.
recommendations.why: Gives keyboard and screen-reader users a clear path, and removes a false affordance.

recommendations.change: Replace plain-text IDs with meaningful labels. Drop 'Run 1a2b3c4d' and the user-name chip; show 'Created 14:05 by Elaine' in ink-3. Rename the method aside to plain venue language or move it into the disclosure.
recommendations.why: Veterans read venue vocabulary, not engine vocabulary.

questionsForBlake: Who is Event Architect for? It could be the sales executive answering an enquiry, opened from the enquiry with the facts filled in, or the events and operations team after a booking is confirmed. The answer decides where it lives in navigation.
Should choosing an option stay final for that comparison, or should staff be able to change their mind until the layout is used?
Would you like the photograph of the requested room at the top of the decision panel, as on the Enquiries desk?
The brief caps guests at 300 (TSX 483). Is that the right ceiling for Trades Hall's rooms, or should it come from each room's recorded capacity?
evidence: packages/web/src/pages/EventArchitectPage.tsx:447-461 vs 419-445 (saved run does not hydrate brief)
No committed baseline exists for this route under packages/web/e2e/*-snapshots

surfaces.name: Event Architect: Ops review evidence panel
surfaces.audience: venue staff, hallkeepers and administrators recording an operations approval; read-only for others
surfaces.dailyUse: Inferred: rare, once per chosen layout. It is a long form filled carefully once.
surfaces.currentLook: A dark gradient panel (EventArchitectPage.css:827-832) with a Georgia 3rem h2 and an uppercase status pill in mint, rose or gold (857-875). The summary box shows 'artifact <12 hex>' in gold code (877-890). There are 4 metadata cells at 0.65rem uppercase dt (909-918). The form is a 2-column decision row, then three fieldsets of four inputs each: source label, source reference, SHA-256 content digest and observed-at (TSX 192-202). Then come a required note, a mint 'Record review' button, and a 0.78rem immutability note placed after the button (TSX 205-206).
slogFactors: Fifteen inputs, including three hand-typed 64-character SHA-256 digests (TSX 198). No veteran hallkeeper can produce these without a separate tool.
Jargon: 'Ops compilation remains blocked', 'Ops evidence gate resolved' (167), 'artifact <hash>' (170), 'Awaiting reviewed evidence' (69).
The error message asks the user to 'Verify every SHA-256 digest, authority, and validity date' (145) without saying which field failed.
All labels are 0.69rem uppercase (EventArchitectPage.css:923).
workflowGaps: The decision defaults to 'approved' (TSX 57), so a reviewer who scrolls straight to the button approves by default.
The button always reads 'Record review' whatever the decision (205). The irreversible consequence ('Reviews cannot be changed or deleted') appears only after the button, in small text (206).
'Valid until' silently defaults to 7 days ahead (49), and the page does not say what happens when it lapses beyond 'expired approvals block Ops'.
The panel renders above the three options it concerns (EventArchitectPage.tsx:718-724), which breaks the reading order.
strengths: Revision envelope and idempotency: the review is bound to the exact request, snapshot, proof and guest-flow digests (TSX 123-138).
Honest read-only state for roles that cannot review (209).
The latest decision, reviewer authority and validity are shown once history exists (176-183).

recommendations.change: Replace hand-typed digests with 'Attach document' for each of the three evidence items. Compute the SHA-256 in the browser (crypto.subtle.digest), fill the label from the file name, set observed-at from the file's date, and allow editing. Show a tick per item and '2 of 3 attached' progress.
recommendations.why: Removes the hardest step and turns the form into visible progress towards closure.

recommendations.change: Start with no decision selected. Label the button with the consequence: 'Record approval (cannot be changed)' or 'Record rejection (cannot be changed)'. Put the immutability sentence and the validity date in plain words before the button: 'Valid until Thu 2 Oct, 14:00; after that the handoff is blocked again.'
recommendations.why: This is an honest consequence before an irreversible action, with no risky default.

recommendations.change: Move the panel. Either put it below the chosen option as the next step in the forest decision panel, or put it on the hallkeeper and handoff surfaces where operations reviewers work. Show it to sales staff only as a status line: 'Operations review: waiting'.
recommendations.why: Keeps the sales comparison clean and gives operations the task in their own place.

recommendations.change: Restyle on the forest decision surface: cream ink, Newsreader heading, 13px-plus labels, a restrained status stamp when a review is recorded, and a cream focus ring.
recommendations.why: Brings the panel into the desk family.

questionsForBlake: Who at Trades Hall signs off door positions, route models and operations? Should that sign-off happen on this page or in the hallkeeper tools?
Is attaching the source documents (PDF plans, sign-off emails) acceptable in place of typing digests? Where should those documents be kept?
evidence: packages/web/src/components/event-architect/EventArchitectOpsReviewPanel.tsx:192-206 (12 evidence inputs, button then immutability note)

surfaces.name: Mission Control (live event-day mission inside the event-day board)
surfaces.audience: hallkeepers, duty managers and venue operations staff on the event day
routes: event-day ops route that renders EventDayOpsPage (router.tsx:512)
surfaces.dailyUse: On event days, open continuously for hours: it polls every 5 seconds and heartbeats every 10 seconds (TSX 64-65). Inferred from the mobile baseline and hallkeeper routing: mostly phones and tablets on the floor, sometimes a duty manager's desk.
surfaces.currentLook: A dark teal glass shell with cyan #8fe5dc, gold #f2c66d and red #ff8f76, radial glow, an 18px radius and a cyan hairline (CSS 1-28). All type is Inter with no serif. There are 8 boxed sub-panels with a 14px radius, each led by an icon and heading (306-317). The stat strip has 1.05rem bold numerals (296-298). A horizontally scrolling phase rail uses 168px tiles (346-366). Also: a 220px SVG pin map, a presence list, a task card grid with three equal dark buttons per card (564-576), an incident form on a light input field, and a 'Time machine' range slider. Many labels are 0.61 to 0.68rem uppercase weight 950 (378-387, 399-403, 557-562). The live dot pulses indefinitely (215-218, 716). The mobile baseline shows a bright cyan full-width 'Start live mission' block as the brightest element on the page.
slogFactors: The palette is off-style: cyan-on-teal sci-fi glass (CSS 1-28) under the ivory app header. Blake prioritised the hallkeeper and event-day tools for the desk standard next.
The layout is a wall of eight boxed panels with the same border, radius and icon heading (CSS 306-344). Nothing establishes priority.
Tasks, the most frequent action on the day, come fourth. They follow the stat strip, phase rail, map and presence (TSX 534-564). On a phone the hallkeeper scrolls past four panels to tap 'Done'.
Tiny type for all-day use: 0.61rem phase and task kinds (CSS 378-387), 0.62rem timestamps (399-403, 508-511, 690-694), 0.64rem map coordinates (489-492), 0.65rem task status (539-543).

Invented or engineering vocabulary: '4D Mission Control' (TSX 512), 'Phase authority' (542), 'Spatial command map' (170), 'Live execution' (222), 'Time machine' (583), 'Live edge' (517), 'timeline cursor #N' as a headline stat (538), 'Replay through sequence N' (584), 'spatial ref(s)' (231).

Raw enums shown as labels: phase.status 'pending', 'active', 'completed' (546); task.kind with underscores replaced, such as 'room flip' (228); status 'in progress' (228); incident.status (579); presence 'role · view' such as 'hallkeeper · board' (559).
A live dot pulses every 1.8s for the whole event (CSS 215-218). Calm technology says status should not demand attention. It is only removed under reduced motion (766-770).
Every task card has three equally weighted buttons, Start, Done and Block (TSX 233-247, CSS 570-576). There is no primary action, and they sit adjacent on a phone.
Touch targets are 32 to 36px on phone-first controls: task buttons 36px (CSS 575), phase buttons 34px (406), 'Finish mission' 34px (184) and timeline Acknowledge 32px (697).

The global cockpit spring applies to every button. index.html:96-110 at (0,3,2) beats .mission-task-actions button:active:not(:disabled) at (0,3,1). Buttons swell 6% under the pointer and press to 0.93 with a brightness flash.
Notices never clear. Once set, 'Incident logged.' stays until the next action replaces it (TSX 262, 525).
workflowGaps: Acknowledgements dead end: blocked tasks and urgent incidents require acknowledgement (services/event-mission-control.ts:650, 705). The Acknowledge button exists only inside the last 10 timeline events (TSX 462, 588). Once 10 newer events arrive, the item can no longer be acknowledged, and the only trace is 'N event(s) require acknowledgement.' (589).
The Acknowledge button has no busy state, no catch and no error message (TSX 588). A failed or duplicate (409) acknowledgement fails silently.

Incidents can be logged but never resolved. updateEventMissionIncident exists (api/event-mission-control.ts:155) but is never imported (TSX 35-46). The 'open incidents' count can only climb, so there is no closure.

'Go live' is shown on every pending phase while one is already active (TSX 547). The API rejects a second active phase with a 409 (services 574; routes 182-186). The UI then says 'That phase changed on another device' (397-399), which is untrue; the real reason is to finish the current phase first.

Starting the mission removes the offline path. The event-day page queues task and issue writes offline (EventDayOpsPage.tsx:237-260, 270-285). Once a mission is live, that checklist is replaced by 'Managed in Mission Control' (EventDayOpsPage.tsx:454-456), and Mission Control's task and incident writes have no offline queue (TSX 420-457). Inferred: the thick-walled venue on the event day is where signal is weakest.

Two parallel systems show on one page while the mission is live. The event-day 'Issue report' (EventDayOpsPage.tsx:475-515) runs beside Mission Control's 'Incident channel' (TSX 567-580). 'Required acknowledgements' (EventDayOpsPage.tsx:375-405) runs beside the timeline's Acknowledge. Staff must guess which one the team watches.
Lists are cut off silently. Incidents show only the first 6 (TSX 579), the map legend the first 6 anchors (200) and the timeline the last 10 (462), with no 'show more'.

The start card does not say what starting does. It says only what it does not do ('does not approve the layout…', TSX 491). It should say that it freezes handoff vN as the baseline, moves the checklist here, and shows your presence to the team.
'Block' asks for no reason, yet it triggers a team-wide acknowledgement (services 650). 'Done' has no undo in the UI (TSX 233-247).
strengths: The inline 'Complete this live mission?' says the real consequence (history becomes read-only and stays replayable) with 'Keep live' beside it, not a modal (TSX 526-531).
Revision-checked, idempotent transitions, with a refresh when another device changed the task (TSX 420-437).
The heading 'Now · {phase}' leads with the decisive fact (TSX 504-506). 'X/Y tasks complete' is a real progress count (535).
The presence panel is honest: 'Online status does not confirm venue attendance.' (557).
Replay with 'Return to live' (587); timeline pages are merged and deduplicated (108-138).
The gold focus ring measures 10.3:1 on the shell (CSS 708-714). Loading uses ActivityStatus (TSX 474).

recommendations.change: Restyle Mission Control and its host event-day page together as one event-day desk. The ivory ledger holds tasks grouped under running-order phases. A copper plane holds the counts, which double as filters: Done x of y, In progress, Blocked, Open incidents. A forest 'Now' panel shows the current phase, its planned time, the next open task and one primary action, always in the same place. Use Newsreader headings, light large numerals, 13px minimum text and [data-calm-controls]. Replace the pulsing dot with a static 'Live' chip and 'updated 18:42:05'.
recommendations.why: Blake named the hallkeeper and event-day tools as the next surfaces for the desk standard. This gives priority, closure and calm across a whole event day.

recommendations.change: Put 'Waiting for your acknowledgement' in its own block at the top, listing every unacknowledged event with the reason (blocked task or urgent incident). Give each Acknowledge button a busy state, an error message and a 409 re-read. Count it down to a sealed 'Nothing waiting'.
recommendations.why: Fixes a real dead end for items older than the last 10 events and gives visible closure.

recommendations.change: Wire updateEventMissionIncident. Add a 'Resolve' action with an optional note, and show resolved incidents struck through under a 'Resolved' fold. The Open incidents count reaches zero with 'All clear'.
recommendations.why: Today the incident count can never fall, so there is no closure.

recommendations.change: Show 'Start' only on the next pending phase. Label it with the phase ('Start Service') and put 'Finish Arrivals first' beside the others. Map the 409 active-phase conflict to that message.
recommendations.why: Prevents a guaranteed failure and a misleading 'changed on another device' message.

recommendations.change: Choose one authority for tasks, issues and acknowledgements on the event day. Extend lib/event-day-offline-queue.ts to mission task transitions and incidents, or keep the offline-capable checklist writable while live. Show the queued state honestly: 'Saved on this phone, will send when signal returns'.
recommendations.why: Removes duplicate forms and keeps the day working when signal drops.

recommendations.change: Use plain venue vocabulary and label maps. 'Phase authority' becomes 'Running order'. 'Spatial command map' becomes 'Where in the room'. 'Live execution' becomes 'Tasks'. 'Time machine' becomes 'History', with the slider labelled by clock time ('As at 18:42'), not a sequence number. Remove 'timeline cursor' from the headline stats. Map the enums to labels: Room flip, In progress, Waived.
recommendations.why: Veterans read their own words, and raw engine terms tire and confuse.

recommendations.change: Give each task card one primary action per state: Start, then Done. Make 'Blocked…' secondary; it opens an inline reason field and says 'The team is asked to acknowledge this.' Offer 'Reopen' on done tasks. Use 44px touch targets on coarse pointers.
recommendations.why: Removes three-way ambiguity, prevents mis-taps and states the consequence.

recommendations.change: Rewrite the start card to say what starting does: 'Starts the live run from handoff v1 (compiled 14:05). The checklist moves here and your team sees who is on duty.' Make the button cream on forest, not the page's brightest cyan block.
recommendations.why: States the real consequence of a consequential internal action.

recommendations.change: Replace the silent slice(0,6) and slice(-10) with 'Show earlier (12)' controls.
recommendations.why: Keeps context without hiding records.

recommendations.change: Add keyboard triage for desk use, modelled on the desk: ↑/↓ or j/k to move, s to start, d for done, b for blocked, a to acknowledge, with the legend shown in the Now panel.
recommendations.why: High-frequency work for duty managers at a desk.

questionsForBlake: On the event day, should Mission Control replace the event-day board's checklist, issue form and acknowledgements completely, so there is one list? Or do the two serve different people?
Who holds Mission Control during an event: a hallkeeper on a phone on the floor, or a duty manager at a desk or tablet? This decides between a thumb-first and a keyboard-first design.
Should the name stay 'Mission Control' or '4D Mission Control', or use plain venue language such as 'Event day' or 'Live running order'?
Do you want any live indicator motion at all, or a still 'Live' mark with the time of the last update?

surfaces.name: Supplier portal (public tokenised supplier handoff)
surfaces.audience: supplier (external florist, AV, catering or logistics contact); the first impression of the venue for the supplier's team
surfaces.dailyUse: Opened once or twice per event, for a few minutes, often on a phone in a van. It is also printed or forwarded to crew (inferred).
surfaces.currentLook: Dark charcoal #15171c with a gold #c9a96a and teal #68d8d2 accent (CSS 1-19), and rounded bordered panels with a 12 to 14px radius and heavy shadows (34-40). Titles specify 'Cormorant Garamond', which is loaded only by the craft quiz (src/styles/fonts/quiz.css), so they fall back to Playfair Display (CSS 60, 172, 397), as the baseline shows. Uppercase gold 12px kickers sit on every panel (47-55). Change counts are teal 24px bold in bordered tiles (185-206). Items are bordered cards with pill metadata (213-267). The right column holds acknowledgement history and a response form with a gold button. The focus ring is the global cyan (no local rule). The baseline desktop-supplier-acknowledgement-error shows the result.
slogFactors: The palette is off-family: charcoal with gold and teal cards, not the ivory, forest and copper that Blake extended to 'everything clients receive' (CSS 1-19). The title font is an unintended fallback (Cormorant, then Playfair).
Every section is the same bordered, shadowed, rounded panel with an uppercase gold kicker (CSS 34-55): a wall of identical cards.

Internal references are shown to an outsider. Item pills show compiler paths such as 'snapshot.totals' and 'snapshot.instructions.accessNotes' (TSX 249; ops-compiler.ts:606, 618, 630, 643). The hero shows 'Snapshot abcdef123456' and 'Handoff v3' (TSX 167-180).
Item text points to documents the supplier cannot see: 'against the handoff pack', 'Use the pick list…', 'review the hallkeeper sheet' (ops-compiler.ts:604, 616, 628).
With no previous snapshot, the change strip still shows '0 Added / 0 Changed / 0 Removed line items' (TSX 220-233; routes 546-551). The zeros look like data.

Every generated item gets the kind 'requirement' (routes/supplier-coordination.ts:346). The 'Load-in' and 'Handoff' labels (TSX 27-32) never appear for real packs, so every item carries the same teal 'REQUIREMENT' tag.
The global cockpit spring applies to 'Acknowledge handoff' (index.html:96-110).
workflowGaps: The deciding facts are missing. SupplierSafePackView has no event name, event date, start time, room, venue address, loading entrance or quantities (types/src/supplier-coordination.ts:207-229). A supplier cannot tell from the page which day, which room or how much to bring.
The venue phone is dropped. contactPhone is in the view (routes 530-532) but never rendered (no reference in SupplierPortalPage.tsx). The email is plain text, not a mailto link (TSX 200).

The response is a dead drop. POST /supplier-share/:token/acknowledge writes a row and updates the pack status but sends no email or notification (routes/supplier-coordination.ts:596-638). No staff web UI reads acknowledgements. 'Send clarification request' implies someone is told, but nobody is.

There is no way to raise a later question. After acknowledging, statusAllowsAcknowledgement hides the form (TSX 52-54, 288) and shows 'Response closed · No response requested.' (367-370). The API would still accept a clarification (routes 473-487 reject only draft, revoked and expired).
One message covers every failure. Network errors and expired links both show 'This supplier link is not available… may have expired' (TSX 142-151) with no retry and no venue contact.
There is no print, save-as-PDF or add-to-calendar for the arrival window, although these are the usual supplier actions (inferred).

A supplier who signs in lands on a denied screen, 'This workspace is not available to your role' (baseline desktop-supplier-denied; DashboardLayout.tsx:60 hides all navigation for suppliers). No home lists their packs. I could not find this copy in current src, so the baseline may be stale.
strengths: Only supplier-safe data is shown, enforced by a server-side supplier-safe view. The test asserts that no internal IDs appear (SupplierPortalPage.test.tsx:121).
The choice between acknowledging and asking for clarification is clear. A note is required for clarification (TSX 99-103), and the button label follows the choice (360).
An honest error keeps the user's input (TSX 124; baseline shows the name and email kept).
The response history lists who, when and the note (TSX 275-285).
Readable 14px body copy. Measured contrast: muted #b7b0a4 is 7.5:1 and the button is 8.0:1 on its panels.

recommendations.change: Lead with the facts a supplier decides on, set as light large numerals on an ivory sheet: a date tile (weekday, day, month), arrival window, room and venue with address and loading entrance, then 'What to bring' with quantities. This needs event date, time, room, venue address and item quantities added to SupplierSafePackView and the compiler. It also needs the supplier item text rewritten so it does not cite internal documents.
recommendations.why: A supplier's questions are which day, when, where and how many. None of these are answered today.

recommendations.change: Make the response honest and closed. Before sending, say: 'Sent to Venue Operations (ops@…). Nothing else changes.' Add the API email or notification to the pack contact, and a staff list of responses. After acknowledging, show a restrained sealed stamp, 'Confirmed by Jordan · Mon 15 Jun, 10:00', and keep a quiet 'Something changed? Ask the venue team' that posts a clarification.
recommendations.why: Today the promised message reaches nobody, and a supplier who acknowledged cannot raise a later issue.

recommendations.change: Remove internal references from the supplier's view. Drop the sourceRef pills and replace the hash grid with 'Version 3 · issued Mon 15 Jun'. Keep the snapshot prefix only as a small 'Reference abcdef12' footer for support calls. This means updating the assertion at SupplierPortalPage.test.tsx:118 with care.
recommendations.why: 'snapshot.totals' reads as a system fault to an outsider.

recommendations.change: Show the venue contact as tap-to-call and mailto links in the response panel.
recommendations.why: The phone number is already in the data, and calling is the fastest route on the day.

recommendations.change: Restyle in the client-facing family: sage ground, an ivory sheet for scope, a forest response panel with one cream primary action, Newsreader headings, ink and cream focus rings, and [data-calm-controls]. Remove the Cormorant declaration.
recommendations.why: Blake's reach decision covers everything clients receive. This page is the venue's face to its suppliers.

recommendations.change: When there is no previous snapshot, replace the 0/0/0 strip with 'First version sent to you'. Show counts only when a real comparison exists.
recommendations.why: Zeros that are not data mislead the reader.

recommendations.change: Split the error state. For a 404 or expired link: 'This link has expired' with the venue name if known. For a network error: 'Couldn't load, try again', with a retry that uses Activity.
recommendations.why: Gives an honest recovery instead of a guessed cause.

recommendations.change: Add a print stylesheet, 'Save as PDF' and an .ics 'Add arrival to calendar'.
recommendations.why: This is how suppliers actually pass the brief to crew. It is a small, often-ignored problem.

When a supplier confirms or asks a question, who should be told and how? For example, an email to the contact on the pack, plus a list on the hallkeeper page.
Which facts must suppliers always see (date, room, address, loading entrance, parking, quantities, contact phone)? Is anything off-limits (client name, guest count, budget)?

surfaces.name: Supplier share flow: staff side (create pack, issue link, track response)
surfaces.audience: venue staff (events coordinator, hallkeeper) sending packs to suppliers
routes: No web route. API only: POST /supplier-coordination/packs, GET /supplier-coordination/packs/:id, POST /supplier-coordination/packs/:id/share-token
surfaces.dailyUse: It would be per event, per supplier: a few times a week during busy season (inferred).
surfaces.currentLook: There is no UI. The web client exposes only getSupplierShare and acknowledgeSupplierShare (web/src/api/supplier-coordination.ts). Nothing in web/src calls /supplier-coordination/packs or /share-token (grep). OpsHandoffPage shows only a 'Supplier notes' count and list (OpsHandoffPage.tsx:156, 236-249). EventDayOpsPage shows 'Supplier arrivals' with category, title and statusLabel (EventDayOpsPage.tsx:538-555).
slogFactors: Staff cannot issue the link that the public portal depends on without a developer or a direct API call. The supplier journey starts with a missing step.
workflowGaps: No UI to choose supplier instructions, set contact and expiry, or create the pack.
No UI to generate or copy the share link, or to email it. The API returns shareUrl only to the caller (routes 463-469).
No view of whether a supplier has opened the link (lastViewedAt is stored, routes 588-590), acknowledged it, or asked for clarification.
No revoke or reissue control, although the pack status supports revoked and expired.
The hallkeeper's 'Supplier arrivals' block does not show acknowledgement status (EventDayOpsPage.tsx:546-552), so on the day nobody can see which suppliers confirmed.
strengths: The API is sound. It checks tenancy (canManageVenue), requires a compiled handoff, blocks cross-supplier packs, hashes tokens and handles expiry and revocation (routes 251-470).

recommendations.change: Add 'Send to suppliers' on the ops handoff surface as a desk-style ledger, one row per supplier. Each row shows the items included, contact, status chip (Not sent, Sent, Opened, Confirmed, Question asked), sent and opened times, and one next step in the same place: Send, then Copy link or Email, then Read question. Before sending, state the consequence: 'Emails Petal & Stem (jordan@…) a private link to 2 items. They can confirm or ask a question; links expire Fri 19 Jun.'
recommendations.why: Completes the flow that the public portal depends on, with visible progress towards 'All suppliers confirmed'.

recommendations.change: Show supplier confirmation status on the hallkeeper's 'Supplier arrivals' and on the Mission Control running order.
recommendations.why: On the day, 'has the florist confirmed?' should be answered where the hallkeeper already looks.

questionsForBlake: Who sends supplier packs at Trades Hall today (events coordinator, hallkeeper or sales), and do they send them from their own email or should Venviewer send them?
Should a supplier's clarification question land in the same inbox-style desk as enquiries, or on the hallkeeper tools?
evidence: grep: no web/src caller of /supplier-coordination/packs or /share-token

crossCutting: Global cockpit spring (index.html:96-110): scale(1.06) and brightness(1.15) on hover, and scale(0.93) on press, with an !important 150ms overshoot transition. It applies to every button in all three surfaces, because only the Enquiries desk opts out through [data-calm-controls]. Its specificity (0,3,2) beats the surfaces' own press rules (Event Architect .event-architect-generate:active:not(:disabled) at (0,3,0); Mission Control at (0,3,1)), so their calm scale(0.97) never shows. Blake has already decided to remove the spring everywhere, and doing it at source fixes all of these at once.

Focus ring: global --vv-focus #87e7f0 (house-tokens.css:79, global.css:42-54) measures 1.41:1 on ivory. The supplier portal relies on it today. Every surface moved onto ivory needs the desk's ink/cream rings, so fixing the global token beats per-surface overrides.

Tokens: each surface defines its own palette (--ea-*, --mission-*, --supplier-*). Promote the desk's --enq-* values (EnquiriesDesk.css:9-46) to app-level tokens so Event Architect, Mission Control, the event-day page and the supplier portal share one ivory/forest/copper/sage set with measured AA pairs.

Type: Event Architect uses Georgia (not loaded), the supplier portal uses Cormorant Garamond (loaded only by quiz.css, so it falls back to Playfair), and Mission Control uses Inter only. Newsreader is already global via index.html:15 (site.css). Inferred: the Event Architect route is not wrapped in cockpitImport (router.tsx:162-164), so Inter may not be requested on direct entry.

Raw enums and IDs are rendered as user text: status.replace(/_/g,' ') in Mission Control (EventMissionControl.tsx:228, 546, 579); 'Run 1a2b3c4d' and 'Replay artifact <hash>' (EventArchitectPage.tsx:324, 705); 'Snapshot abcdef123456' (SupplierPortalPage.tsx:178); 'snapshot.totals' (ops-compiler.ts:606). A shared label map, plus a rule that hashes appear only in quiet reference footers, would fix this family.

Disclaimer stacking: governance caveats are repeated as boxes on each surface (6 in Event Architect; 'Internal execution only…' and 'Online status does not confirm…' in Mission Control; 'planning handoff… subject to venue-team confirmation' in the supplier portal). Pattern: one scope line placed at the decision, with the exact test-asserted sentences kept.

Mission Control's restyle cannot be separate from EventDayOpsPage (dark #111818, EventDayOpsPage.css:1-9) and the hallkeeper tools. It also has to resolve their duplicated task, issue and acknowledgement controls and the offline queue (lib/event-day-offline-queue.ts).
Micro-type: many 0.61 to 0.69rem uppercase labels across Event Architect and Mission Control. For eight-hour use, set a 12px floor for labels and 13px for data text.

surfaces.name: Front door (the / route, RoomsHomePage)
surfaces.audience: public: prospective clients and venue buyers (and, through its header links, venue staff)
surfaces.currentLook: An ivory masthead (#f4efe4) with a forest (#203c31) nav sits over a warm-black page (--ink #14100c) with sandstone text and one brass accent. Type is Fraunces 300 for display, Newsreader for body, Geist for UI and Geist Mono for measurements. A full-bleed Grand Hall photograph carries an ink wash and 'Plan Grand Hall' as the cream primary action. Below it is a horizontal scroll rail titled 'More rooms' of 16:9 cards, then a footer. Motion is limited to a 620 ms opacity resolve on load and a poster filter that goes from soft to sharp on hover; reduced motion is honoured. Production is different: gaussianSplatsAvailable() is import.meta.env.DEV (splat-access.ts:4-6), so every room is 'closed'. Every card then renders as a non-link div with the caption 'Work in progress' (RoomsHomePage.tsx:65,101-112). Each poster stays permanently at saturate(0.82) brightness(0.74) blur(0.4px) (RoomsHomePage.css:242-268). The hero shows 'Gaussian splats · Work in progress' and 'Try the virtual tour · Work in progress' (RoomsHomePage.tsx:171-174).
surfaces.dailyUse: It is the first page every visitor and every staff member sees, a few seconds per visit. Staff use the header as their way into Dashboard, Diary and Hallkeeper.
slogFactors: In production the only content below the hero is a rail of real supplied photographs, deliberately dimmed and blurred (RoomsHomePage.css:246, 266-268). Each is captioned 'Work in progress' and none can be clicked. The page reads as unfinished and slightly out of focus, the opposite of the desk's 'real, sourced venue photography as the moment of scale'.
'Work in progress' appears on up to 9 elements, and 'Gaussian splats' is engineering jargon that means nothing to a wedding client (RoomsHomePage.tsx:65,173-174,200).

No fact that decides is shown. Guest capacities per layout exist in lib/trades-hall-venue-truth.ts:31-46 and are used on /fresh, but the front door shows only a metres footprint, and in production only when a room is walkable, which is never (RoomsHomePage.tsx:96,168).
The header mixes the client path ('Plan an event') with staff tools ('Dashboard', 'Diary', 'Hallkeeper') and 'Log in' (RoomsHomePage.tsx:141-147). A client does not know what 'Hallkeeper' is.

The brand lead is 'Venviewer' with 'Trades Hall of Glasgow' as a sub-line (RoomsHomePage.tsx:137-140), while index.html's title, description and social card say 'Trades Hall of Glasgow — weddings and events'. The page is unsure whose it is.

Inference from specificity, not browser-verified: the golden 'cockpit' arrow cursor and golden scrollbar in index.html apply here (index.html:77-79,139-168). The guard only exempts pages that mount .fr-root, and this page does not. The rail's own hairline scrollbar (.rooms__track, RoomsHomePage.css:220-221, specificity 0,1,0) loses to body:not(:has(.fr-root)) * (0,1,1). The stale comment at index.html:73-76 still says 'the landing page mounts .fr-root'.
workflowGaps: There is no enquiry action above the fold. The only 'Enquire' link is in the footer and jumps to a different homepage design at /fresh#enquire (RoomsHomePage.tsx:201). The primary action instead drops a client into the planner (/plan?space=grand-hall).
There is no phone number, email or address anywhere on the page. /fresh has them (FreshPage.tsx footer).
There are no Privacy, Terms or Accessibility links. /fresh has them (fresh-copy.ts FRESH_LEGAL_LINKS), and LegalPage.tsx's own notes say the privacy notice must be easy to find.
Closed cards look like the open ones apart from a caption. Nothing says what a client can do instead, such as look at photographs, see capacities or ask about the room.
strengths: The ivory and forest masthead is already close to the desk's family (RoomsHomePage.css:24-63).
It has a true hierarchy: the Grand Hall leads full-bleed and the other rooms follow.
The house motion rule of 'resolve, don't arrive' is calm, uses no scale pops and honours reduced motion (RoomsHomePage.css:314-324).
Posters use responsive ladders and the hero is preloaded (index.html:18-31), so the first paint is fast.

The honesty in lib/room-card-copy.ts is good: dimensions are withheld when a scan is not confident. The footnote 'Scan dimensions are estimates. Confirm measurements with the venue.' is exactly the tone veterans trust.

recommendations.change: While splats are on hold, show the rail's supplied photographs at full clarity. Drop the brightness(0.74) and blur filter for closed cards, and make every card open that room's dossier (photo, capacities by layout, 'Ask about this room'). Express the splat hold once, as one quiet line, instead of on every card.
recommendations.why: Real photography is the page's moment of scale. Dimmed and blurred stills behind nine 'Work in progress' captions tell clients the product is broken.

recommendations.change: Under each room name, show the venue-published capacities from TRADES_HALL_ROOM_CAPACITIES as light large numerals in the desk's style, for example '180 dinner · 250 reception'. Keep metres as a secondary detail.
recommendations.why: A booker and a client decide on 'how many, which room'. Metres alone do not answer that.

recommendations.change: Make 'Ask about a date' the one primary action, always in the same place: the hero and a sticky header button. It should open the /fresh enquiry composer in place or scroll to an embedded one. Demote 'Plan Grand Hall' to secondary.
recommendations.why: The desk's HBR finding: response within an hour multiplies qualification. The front door should feed the Enquiries desk directly, not push visitors into a tool first.

recommendations.change: Replace the staff links in the public header with one discreet 'Staff sign in' link. Staff reach the Dashboard, Diary and Hallkeeper after sign-in through /app, whose role-aware redirect already exists.
recommendations.why: It removes confusing vocabulary for clients and keeps the page about the venue.

recommendations.change: Add the contact block (telephone, email, address, map) and the legal links to the footer, reusing /fresh's footer component.
recommendations.why: There is currently no way to ring the hall from the front door, and no privacy notice link.

recommendations.change: Mount the calm-controls opt-out on this page, or better, delete the global cockpit cursor, scrollbar and springy hover from index.html (Blake decided 26 Sep to remove the springy hover pop everywhere). Fix the stale comment at index.html:73-76.
recommendations.why: A golden arrow cursor and golden scrollbar on an ivory and forest page is off-family.

Do you want the staff links (Dashboard, Diary, Hallkeeper) to stay on the public homepage for your team's convenience, or move behind 'Staff sign in'?
On 19 September you asked for 'Work in progress' labels while splats are held. Is one calm line for the whole 3D feature enough, or must each room carry the label?

surfaces.name: Editorial homepage /fresh (also /editor, the URL on Trades Hall's flyers): hero, rooms, dossier, rates, enquiry composer
surfaces.audience: public: prospective clients such as couples, event organisers and corporate bookers
surfaces.currentLook: Light-first sandstone paper (#ede7db) with a paper-grain tile, brown-black ink, bottle green (#1f4a38) as the action colour and ochre for rules. Fraunces variable handles display, with the word 'lit' breathing on its axes on an infinite 3.4 s loop (fresh.css:336-352). Newsreader is the body face and Geist the UI face. An aerial hero is clipped by a drawn fanlight arch over the real dome. Room articles alternate sides, and a native <dialog> dossier draws each layout to count. Wedding rates sit in two columns. An enquiry composer answers the fit question, previews the exact email, and offers Send, mailto, Copy and a phone number. The palette follows the system theme, with a manual Auto/Light/Dark control. Press feedback is scale(0.96-0.97), hovers are gated to fine pointers, reduced motion is honoured, and focus is a green 2px ring (8.1:1).
surfaces.dailyUse: Clients visit once or a few times and spend minutes, reading and composing an enquiry. The venue's printed flyers point here through /editor.
slogFactors: The kinetic word 'lit' is ochre #b7862f on paper #ede7db, which measures 2.64:1. That fails even the 3:1 large-text minimum (fresh.css:336-340). It also animates forever, which is the only non-calm motion on an otherwise calm page.

A whole section, 'The 3D room', exists only to say it is unavailable ('Work in progress… currently unavailable', 'access is paused'). A hero action and two dossier links also say 'Work in progress' (FreshPage.tsx:789-846; fresh-copy.ts:34,45,58-59,239-244).

The sticky desktop header runs to two rows: brand, a theme switcher, the CTA, then a second row of five pills including the staff links 'Dashboard', 'Diary' and 'Hallkeeper' (FreshPage.tsx:635-666; fresh.css:118-190). That is a lot of chrome for a client.
The '(optional)' hints on labels are ink-2 at opacity 0.7 on paper, which measures 3.23:1 at 12px (fresh.css:1346-1351, 802-810). This fails AA.

Inference: global.css's cyan focus box-shadow (rgba 107,217,232 at 0.16, 6px) still sits under the green outline, because .fr-root :focus-visible resets only the outline (fresh.css:90-94 vs global.css:42-54).
workflowGaps: 'Ask about this room' in the dossier closes the dialog and jumps to #enquire (RoomDossier.tsx:153). The composer has no room field (FreshPage.tsx:321-330), so the room the client just chose is lost and has to be retyped into the message.

After 'Enquiry sent' the client gets nothing in their inbox. public-enquiries.ts sends email only to venue hallkeepers or the fallback address (line 243), so the email they previewed is never delivered to them. There is also no expected reply time.
The dossier link '3D room · Work in progress' (RoomDossier.tsx:164-168) sends the client to a section that only says the feature is unavailable. That is a dead end.
The same flyer audience lands on /fresh, while typed-URL visitors land on RoomsHomePage. The same venue has two different front doors.
strengths: The enquiry composer is excellent. It answers 'which room fits' from published figures, shows the exact email before sending, keeps the mailto, copy and phone fallbacks visible if the POST fails, and gives a plain GDPR note (FreshPage.tsx:317-599). That is honest consequences and closure in practice.
The room dossier's capacity pills redraw the plan to count, with provenance shown (RoomDossier.tsx:97-150). This is the 'facts that decide' idea, made beautiful.
Motion manners already match the desk: press-down only, hover gated to fine pointers, reduced motion removes all transforms (fresh.css:1291-1311).
Real, sourced June 2026 photography is used, one photograph each, never repeated (fresh-copy.ts:124-175).
The copy is plain, British and free of praise ('Enquiry sent. The events team will reply by email.').

recommendations.change: Recolour 'lit' to a darker ochre that holds at least 3:1 on paper (about #8a5e1a or darker, to be measured), or keep the ochre and put it on a darker plate. Slow the breath to a single settle on load, or keep the loop only under an explicit 'no-preference' with a longer, subtler range.
recommendations.why: It fails AA-large today, and infinite motion on the hero contradicts calm technology.

recommendations.change: Carry the room into the composer. 'Ask about this room' should preselect the room: add a room field to the composer and to submitGuestEnquiry (the desk already shows the room). Show 'Grand Hall · 180 dinner' in the answer.
recommendations.why: It keeps context, removes a retyping step, and gives the booker the room fact the desk leads with.

recommendations.change: Collapse the '3D room' section and the WIP dossier links into one quiet line near the photography ('A walk-through of each room is being prepared'), or hide them until the hold lifts, subject to Blake's answer.
recommendations.why: A section that exists to apologise makes the page look unfinished.

recommendations.change: Send the client a copy of their enquiry: an acknowledgement email with the composed text, the venue's phone number and the expected reply time. Say on screen 'A copy is on its way to you@…'.
recommendations.why: Closure and trust: veterans expect a receipt, and so do Cvent users.

recommendations.change: Fix the '(optional)' hint contrast by dropping opacity 0.7 and using ink-2 (6.26:1). Neutralise the leaking global focus box-shadow.
recommendations.why: WCAG AA text and a clean single focus ring.

recommendations.change: Slim the sticky header to one row: arms and name, 'Ask about a date', and a small 'Staff sign in'. Move the theme preference to the footer.
recommendations.why: The header's prime pixels belong to the venue and the one next step.

recommendations.change: Decide one canonical public homepage. Merge /fresh's composer, dossier, rates and contact into '/', and point /editor at it.
recommendations.why: One front door, one enquiry path, one place to maintain quality.

questionsForBlake: Which is the canonical public homepage: RoomsHomePage at '/' or /fresh (which the flyers reach through /editor)? May the other be merged into it?
What reply time can Trades Hall promise ('within one working day'?), and should the client receive a copy of their enquiry by email?
Should the public pages keep the Auto/Light/Dark theme control, or be light-only like the desk?

surfaces.name: The Rite (the previous homepage, /landing)
surfaces.currentLook: A near-black ground (#030707) with candle golds (#d7a64b) and italic Newsreader. It is staged as a three-act scroll: a threshold line ('There is a hall in Glasgow that has been lit for 235 years.'), a cursor-following light, a flame canvas, a synthesised room-tone audio toggle and a 'wick' reading-progress bar. The nav is hidden until Act II. The page swaps the favicon to a flame and changes the tab title when the tab is away. The committed baselines show a black screen with one italic line and 'ENTER ↓'.
surfaces.dailyUse: Rare; only stale bookmarks, and it is covered by the acquisition visual and audit specs.
slogFactors: The first viewport is pure black with one sentence. A client has to scroll through 'darkness' before navigation appears (RiteNav.tsx:12-16; rite.css:144-166).
Its dark and gold cockpit palette is the look Blake rejected for the Diary. It belongs to neither the desk family nor /fresh.
The primary action 'Begin with the room' / 'Open the planner' sends clients into a tool, not an enquiry (rite-copy.ts:224-233).
workflowGaps: The navigation is deliberately delayed, which costs a step to reach anything useful.
The public audit and visual specs still test this retired page (public-acquisition-visual-performance.spec.ts:129-150), not the live front door's production state.
strengths: It is careful about accessibility: the nav stays in the DOM and is focusable, audio is off by default and never autoplays (useRoomTone.ts:11-13), and reduced motion gets a static version.
The copy has real editorial voice.

recommendations.change: Retire /landing: redirect it to the canonical homepage and move its acquisition baselines and audit entry to '/' in its production (splats-held) state.
recommendations.why: It keeps a rejected, dark, delayed-navigation experience off the public domain and makes the visual baselines test what clients actually see.

questionsForBlake: May the Rite (/landing), the spotlight (/welcome) and the Living Hall (/living-hall) be retired and redirected to the one canonical homepage, keeping their source in history?

surfaces.name: Spotlight hero (/welcome)
surfaces.audience: public (links shared during the first review round)
surfaces.currentLook: One dark viewport (#030707) showing two photographs of the Grand Hall: an empty dark hall, with the dressed evening revealed through a cursor-following radial mask. The headline is Newsreader italic plus roman ('See your evening before it happens.'), with a gold pill nav and a gold focus shadow.
surfaces.dailyUse: Rare; old shared links only.
slogFactors: The page asks the visitor to 'Move the light to reveal the room' before they can see the room clearly. The effort is put before the reward.
Its dark and gold palette is outside both the desk family and /fresh.

Inference from CSS specificity: its attempt to stop the springy pop, .vv-spotlight button:hover:not(:disabled) at (0,3,1), loses to index.html's global rule at (0,3,2). The mobile menu button still scales 1.06 and brightens (spotlight.css:32-38; index.html:102-106).
workflowGaps: The nav link 'Weddings' goes to /rooms/grand-hall, which no route matches. The catch-all silently redirects to '/' (spotlight-copy.ts:58; router.tsx:706-708).
'The rooms' goes to /#rooms, but RoomsHomePage has no element with id 'rooms', so it lands at the top of the page (spotlight-copy.ts:57).
strengths: The menu is keyboard-safe: Escape returns focus to the button.
Interactive borders are chosen to hold 3:1 on black (spotlight.css:17-19).

recommendations.change: Retire /welcome by redirecting it to the canonical homepage. If it stays, fix the two dead nav links and neutralise the global springy hover.
recommendations.why: Dead links and a reveal-to-see hero cost clients effort for nothing.

questionsForBlake: (See the Rite: may /welcome be retired?)

surfaces.name: Living Hall and the splat 'Work in progress' hold page
surfaces.currentLook: In production /living-hall renders SplatsWorkInProgressPage through withSplatAccess (router.tsx:358-360). That page is light ivory (#f3f0e8) with forest ink (#193a30), Georgia for headings and Inter for text. Its eyebrow reads 'Gaussian splat viewer' over a large 'Work in progress', and its 'Try the tour' button is itself captioned 'Work in progress'. The Living Hall document, reachable only in development, is obsidian (#050807) with ivory ink, drafting-gold rules and a cyan accent.
surfaces.dailyUse: Rare. Only people who follow an old poster or room link land here.
slogFactors: The eyebrow 'Gaussian splat viewer' is jargon, and 'Work in progress' is said three times on one card (SplatsWorkInProgressPage.tsx:16-24).
It uses Georgia and Inter rather than the loaded Newsreader, Fraunces and Geist, so it is close to the family but not of it.
workflowGaps: A visitor who scanned a room poster lands on a page about the renderer, not about the room they wanted. There is no room photo, capacity or enquiry action.
strengths: The hold page is already ivory and forest, has a clear way back, and its focus ring is copper #9b6243 (4.37:1).

surfaces.name: Pricing (/pricing)
surfaces.audience: venue buyers: owners, general managers and sales directors evaluating Venviewer
surfaces.currentLook: Near-black (#0a0806) with a gold (#c9a84c) and oxblood (#7a1f2a) accent. Headings are Playfair Display and body text Inter, all as inline styles, with keyframes injected into <head> at module load. A single 'Venviewer Pro' card carries a 'MOST POPULAR' badge, a 4 s infinite glow pulse and an 18 s infinite drifting background glow (PricingPage.tsx:265,369). A gold Monthly/Annual toggle sits above it. Further down are add-on cards and scan-service cards that lift 4px on hover, an oxblood 'Founder bundle' card, a competitor price table, an FAQ and a gold gradient final CTA. Focus is a cyan ring (#87e7f0). The committed baselines confirm the black and gold look.
surfaces.dailyUse: A buyer reads it once or twice for a few minutes, and it is often shared internally.
slogFactors: It is the old cockpit look Blake has moved away from. Its dark, gold, Playfair, glowing and drifting treatment shares nothing with the desk the buyer would actually use, so the product and its price page look like two companies.
'MOST POPULAR' sits on the only tier (PricingPage.tsx:399). That is invented social proof, and veterans notice it.
The scan-tier labels are GOLD_DIM #8a6e1e on #15110d, 3.87:1 at 13px, which fails AA (PricingPage.tsx:569).
Hover lifts and infinite pulses are the opposite of calm motion (PricingPage.tsx:37-61, 265, 369).
workflowGaps: 'How it works' goes to /#how-it-works, and no such anchor exists anywhere (PricingPage.tsx:290).

'Start your 14-day free trial', '14 days free · No credit card' and 'Book a scan →' all go to /register?tier=…&cycle=… or ?bundle=founder (PricingPage.tsx:237,463,620,639,779). No code reads tier, cycle or bundle; grep finds them only in PricingPage.tsx. The Register page then says 'Use the email address your venue invited.' (RegisterPage.tsx:40-42). Inferred from WorkspaceAccessGate.tsx: an uninvited account ends at 'Venue access pending — Ask your Venviewer contact…'. The promised trial and scan booking are dead ends.

The FAQ promises behaviour not found in the web source: pro-rata add-ons 'from your dashboard', 'Annual plans refund the unused portion', 'your layouts are archived'. It also claims an 'Embed on your own website (one-line widget)' feature. An embed-configs API exists (api index.ts:422), but no customer-facing flow was found.
The competitor table quotes US-dollar prices for Cvent, Prismm and Matterport with no source or date (PricingPage.tsx:665-668).

It sells 'Planner + 3D walkthrough + enquiry pipeline' (PricingPage.tsx:702). It does not mention the enquiries desk, diary and holds, proposals or hallkeeper tools that would move a Salesforce or Cvent veteran.
The footer links to /privacy and /terms, which are the Trades House's documents as data controller for its own site (LegalPage.tsx:68-76,551), not Venviewer's terms for venue customers.
strengths: The arithmetic is consistent: £47.99 × 12 = £575.88, the '17%' saving holds, and the founder saving of £575 holds.
The copy is short and plain, focus is visible (if off-palette), and reduced motion is covered by global.css.

recommendations.change: Until self-serve billing and onboarding exist, change every CTA to an honest next step, such as 'Book a walkthrough with us' (a contact form or calendar link to the Venviewer team). State what happens next: 'We reply within a working day; nothing is charged.' Remove the trial, no-card and refund claims, or implement them first.
recommendations.why: Honest consequences. Today the page promises a trial that ends at 'Venue access pending'.

recommendations.change: Rebuild Pricing in the platform family: an ivory sheet, the forest decision panel for the plan, a copper plane for the one number that matters (the monthly price as a light large numeral) and sage ground, set in Newsreader and Inter. Remove the glow, drift, hover lifts, 'MOST POPULAR' and the cyan focus ring.
recommendations.why: Buyers should see the product's calm and luxury on the page that sells it, the same family as the desk.

recommendations.change: Replace the feature list with the veteran's day. Set enquiries (with the desk capture), diary and holds, proposals, hallkeeper sheets and imports from Salesforce, Cvent, S&C software and spreadsheets against what each tool does today. Source and date every competitor figure, or remove it.
recommendations.why: Blake's ambition is to replace Salesforce and Cvent, but the page sells a planner widget.

recommendations.change: Fix or remove 'How it works', and add Venviewer's own terms and privacy notice for venue customers.
recommendations.why: It removes a dead link and gives buyers legal documents that cover them.

questionsForBlake: Are £47.99/£57.99, the add-ons, the scan tiers, the founder bundle and the 14-day no-card trial approved prices and offers? Should Pricing stay public before self-serve billing exists?
Should Pricing sell the whole desk as a Salesforce/Cvent/S&C replacement, rather than 'Planner + 3D walkthrough'?
Do you have sourced, dated competitor prices, or should the comparison table go?
Is there a Venviewer legal entity and terms of service for venue customers to link from Pricing and Register?

surfaces.name: Trades House 'Which Craft is yours?' quiz

crossCutting: index.html:73-168 still applies the cockpit layer to every page that is not /fresh. That means a gold arrow cursor, a gold scrollbar, and on buttons a scale(1.06) + brightness(1.15) overshoot spring. The guard is body:not(:has(.fr-root)), and only FreshPage mounts .fr-root, so '/' (RoomsHomePage), Pricing, Legal, Login/Register, OAuth, the quiz, the leaflet, /demo and /welcome all get it. Local opt-outs lose on specificity: spotlight.css:33-38 is (0,3,1) against the global (0,3,2), and the quiz's translateY hover also loses. The comment at index.html:73-76 is stale, since the homepage moved to RoomsHomePage. Blake decided on 26 Sep to remove the springy pop everywhere, so the fix is to delete the cursor, scrollbar and spring rules at source.

global.css:42-54 draws a 3px cyan outline plus a 6px cyan glow. Pages that restyle focus override only the outline (fresh.css:90-94, LegalPage.css:77-81, AuthPage.css:166, RoomsHomePage.css:63), so the cyan glow still stacks under their rings. Pricing uses cyan explicitly (#87e7f0, PricingPage.tsx:74-87). The family needs one focus token: ink on ivory/copper and cream on forest, as on the desk.

At least eight type systems are in use across public surfaces: the desk uses Newsreader + Inter; / uses Fraunces + Newsreader + Geist + Geist Mono; /fresh and Legal use Fraunces + Newsreader + Geist; Pricing uses Playfair Display + Inter; auth and OAuth use Georgia + Inter; /demo uses Georgia + Segoe UI/Arial; the WIP page uses Georgia + Inter; the quiz uses Cinzel + Cormorant + EB Garamond. The editorial voice and the desk need one agreed pair each (for example Fraunces/Newsreader for public display, Newsreader/Inter for the product).

There is no shared public header or footer. Each page hand-rolls its nav with different links, which produces dead links: Pricing 'How it works' goes to /#how-it-works (no such anchor); Spotlight 'Weddings' goes to /rooms/grand-hall (no route); Spotlight 'The rooms' goes to /#rooms (no id on '/'). Staff links (Dashboard, Diary, Hallkeeper) sit on client-facing headers, and contact and legal links are missing on '/'.

The domain has two brands. index.html's title, social card and JSON-LD say 'Trades Hall of Glasgow'. The '/' masthead leads with 'Venviewer'. Pricing, Register and OAuth sell or authenticate 'Venviewer', while the legal documents are the Trades House's.

Honest claims: Pricing and /onboard promise a 14-day no-card trial, scan booking, refunds and pro-rata add-ons. Register ignores tier, cycle and bundle and asks for an invited email; the only references are in PricingPage.tsx.
Client closure after an enquiry is incomplete: POST /public/enquiries emails only venue staff (public-enquiries.ts:202-243). The client receives no copy and no reply-time promise.

Five competing homepage designs are reachable: '/' (RoomsHomePage), /fresh and /editor (FreshPage), /welcome (Spotlight), /landing (Rite) and /living-hall. The committed public baselines capture /landing and /pricing, not the production front door.

Accessibility coverage: e2e/accessibility-route-audit.spec.ts:378-398 audits only /, /landing and /pricing among public pages. Its focus check (support/accessibility-audit.ts:316-326) verifies that an outline exists, not its contrast, which is why the 1.4:1 cyan ring passes. /fresh, /login, /register, the legal pages, /quiz, /demo, /welcome and /oauth-consent are not audited.

Inference: html and body keep background var(--vv-ink), a dark tone from house tokens (global.css:10-21), under the ivory pages, so overscroll or rubber-banding on the ivory and paper pages would flash dark. Not browser-verified.

The 'Work in progress' framing (T-628, Blake 19 Sep) repeats on the /, /fresh, dossier, tour and hold pages. It needs one calm, consistent pattern rather than per-element labels, pending Blake's answer.

cluster: Twin, tour, room showcase and captures (TwinPage + src/twin shell/tags/tour/enquiry overlay, RoomShowcasePage, RoomsHomePage, RoomWalkPage, RoomCapturesPage, TradesHallAssetStatusPage). Read-only review. I read the source and CSS, the API route behind the public enquiry, the founder holds (docs/sessions/2026-09-19.md, T-628) and the committed twin and asset-rooms baselines. No server was started, so I have no live browser evidence of the enquiry modal or of the real room photography behind the HUD: the twin baselines render the canvas black. Contrast figures come from a WCAG luminance calculation on the CSS values.

surfaces.name: Twin walkthrough chrome (/tour and /venues/:venueSlug/twin: TwinPage states, TwinViewer HUD, room dossier, Rooms panel, quick actions, controls rail, coach hint)
surfaces.audience: public (prospective clients), plus sales executives who share or present it; inferred from the '/tour … sayable on the phone' route comment at router.tsx:634-640
surfaces.currentLook:
The palette is the Rite's 'black hall, parchment ink, flame gold' (twin.css:4-7, 16-24: --black #030707, --ink #fbf2df, --gold #d7a64b), not the selected ivory, forest, copper and sage. The HUD is made of hairline-gold pills on rgba(7,16,15,.78) blurred glass. Its type:
- Newsreader serif for room names only (room-dossier.css:154-155, 21px).
- Geist Mono for the viewpoint label (twin.css:258, 11px; 10px on phones at :934).
- Uppercase tracked labels at 0.72rem, 11.5px (twin.css:345, 396, 442; quick-actions.css:56-58; room-selector.css:80-82), falling to 0.62rem, 9.9px, on phones (twin.css:948, 955, 988).
- Dossier stat labels at 9.5px mono uppercase (room-dossier.css:251), a 'You are here' mark at 0.58rem (room-selector.css:305), and the disclosure at 10.5px (twin.css:746).

In walk mode on desktop, 11 chrome pieces occupy all four corners (desktop-walk baseline): the WIP strip, the 'Trades Hall Glasgow · Viewpoint 29' pill, the dossier card, WALK/DOLLHOUSE/PLAN, SURFACE ↑, ENQUIRE, share, fullscreen, SEE THE PLAN, the disclosure and ROOMS. The first visit adds a coach pill.

Motion is carefully built and honours reduced motion: a first-light iris, the dossier rising in (keyed per room), the Rooms sheet, and a vignette 'breath'. The focus ring is a gold halo that overrides global cyan (twin.css:56-64).
surfaces.dailyUse: Clients: a few minutes per visit, on phone and desktop. Sales executives: possibly several times a day while sharing links or presenting on calls (inference; the frequency is unknown).
slogFactors: Eleven competing chrome pieces sit over the room photograph in walk mode (desktop-walk baseline). No zone is quiet, so the room, which is the moment of the sublime, is framed by clutter.

Most labels are 9.5–11.5 px, uppercase, tracked and often monospace (twin.css:345/396/442/570/625/713/746/775; room-dossier.css:165,251; room-selector.css:305). That is tiring to read and reads as a technical HUD, not a luxury brochure. At phone widths the mode labels drop to about 9.9 px (twin.css:948).

Inactive mode labels are #b9aa8b on the 78% glass chip. Over a near-white window in a panorama this computes to about 4.3:1 for 11.5 px text, below AA. This is an inference: the backdrop blur softens it, but the baselines have no photographs to confirm either way.

Every button still gets the global springy hover (scale 1.06, brightness 1.15, overshoot curve; index.html:95-113). The twin does not opt out with [data-calm-controls], and the global selector's (0,3,2) specificity beats the twin's own :hover/:active rules (twin.css:421-423; room-selector.css:97). Rows in the Rooms panel therefore swell under the pointer, as desk rows did before T-633.

'Trades Hall Glasgow · Viewpoint 29' is scanner vocabulary. It also persists in dollhouse and plan mode, where it means nothing (desktop-plan baseline). On desktop the venue name appears twice, in the pill and again as TRADES HALL GLASGOW under the room name.
'SURFACE ↑' (twin-copy.ts:81) is an engineering word for 'go to the overview'.
The 'SEE THE PLAN' chip (TwinViewer.tsx:1910-1921) does exactly what the PLAN segment does. TwinViewer's own header (TwinViewer.tsx:139-143) says 'Two controls doing one job is its own defect'.

The dossier auto-expands to a 340 px card on every room arrival. In landscape on a phone it covers about 40% of the stage, and on a portrait phone about a third (landscape-walk and mobile-walk baselines).

The coach hint reads 'Click to move · drag to look · WASD to walk' on touch devices too (twin-copy.ts:85). It shows once ever (TwinCoachHint.tsx:38-43), and there is no way to recall a controls legend afterwards.
The 'Panorama tour · Work in progress' strip is gold 600-weight text on its own band (twin.css:78-90). It shouts rather than qualifies. It is required by Blake's T-628 hold, but its styling is not.
workflowGaps: The room-specific action exists but is not wired. RoomDossier renders 'Enquire about the {room}' only when onCompose is passed (RoomDossier.tsx:175-177, 593), and TwinViewer passes none (TwinViewer.tsx:1898). A visitor standing in the Saloon can only use the generic venue-wide Enquire.
There is no path from the tour to the planner. compose-link.ts, 'the door between the showroom and the workshop', has no importer outside tests.

The failure state 'The twin is being prepared. Walk the photographs meanwhile.' (twin-copy.ts:26-27) offers no link to any photographs and no phone number, only 'Try again' (TwinPage.tsx:85-91). It is a dead end.
Share falls silent when it fails: the 'failed' outcome shows nothing (TwinViewerControls.tsx:85-87).
A viewer on a sales call cannot see availability or the formats beyond reception and dinner. The questions a booker asks first, 'is my date free?' and 'theatre or cabaret?', go unanswered.
Several twin components are built but not mounted, including the guided tour, room notes, ViewpointPlan and the minimap. See the separate surface.
strengths: The room truth is honest. A room is named only at hand-validated viewpoints, and published figures come with their provenance ('Capacity figures confirmed by the Trades Hall team, 2026-07-09 — a planning guide…'). That matches the 'facts that decide' principle.

The Rooms panel uses relational storey names ('On this level', 'One level up'). Each row carries the facts (250 standing · 180 seated · 21 × 10 m), and the Usher glides the real corridor route instead of teleporting.
'Copy link to this walkthrough' shares the exact view (the ?look= builder), which is a real small problem solved for sales executives.

Accessibility craft is serious: live-region arrival announcements, a radiogroup mode switch with arrow keys, forced-colours fallbacks (twin.css:1013-1057), and reduced-motion counterparts for every animation (twin.css:1061-1087).
The walk stops fighting the hand: pointer or keyboard input ends Usher rides, and keyboard walking is disabled while the user is typing (TravelControls.tsx:53-62).

recommendations.change: Stop the springy hover on the twin now. Remove the global pop per Blake's 26 September decision, or at minimum mark .vv-twin with data-calm-controls. Keep colour-only hovers gated to fine pointers and a 0.97 press.
recommendations.why: The global (0,3,2) rule overrides the twin's own restrained :hover and :active, so every pill, row and the Enquire button swells 6% and brightens 15%.

recommendations.change:
Cut the HUD to three stable zones:
- Top-left: identity, meaning the room name in serif when validated, otherwise the venue. Drop 'Viewpoint N', or keep it only in the screen-reader announcement.
- Top-right: one view switch, with 'Surface' folded into it as 'Overview'.
- Bottom-right: one primary, 'Enquire about the {room}' (or 'Enquire' between rooms), always in the same place, with share, fullscreen and Rooms as one quiet tool cluster beside it.
Delete the duplicate 'See the plan' chip.
recommendations.why: This gives one next step in the same place. It removes the eleven-piece clutter and the duplicate control that the code itself calls a defect (TwinViewer.tsx:139-143).

recommendations.change: Wire RoomDossier's onCompose (TwinViewer.tsx:1898) so it opens the enquiry with the room preselected. This depends on the enquiry-flow API change.
recommendations.why: The visitor has just fallen for a room. The booker's first fact is the room, and the current flow discards it.

recommendations.change: Give the twin states an exit. On preparing or error, link to the room photographs and the rooms page, and show the events team's phone and email, while keeping 'Try again'.
recommendations.why: 'Walk the photographs meanwhile' with no link is a dead end for a client who arrived from a printed /tour address.

recommendations.change:
Restyle the chrome in the selected family, adapted to night glass:

- One copper-cream primary for Enquire.

recommendations.why: This matches the desk's editorial serif and light numerals and cuts eye strain. It also gives a family resemblance without losing the dark room-at-night mood (pending Blake's answer on reach).

recommendations.change: Open the dossier collapsed by default as a single line ('Grand Hall · 250 standing · 180 seated'), expanding on tap. It should auto-expand only the first time per session, and never in landscape on a phone.
recommendations.why: The auto-expanded card covers 33–40% of a phone's stage on every room change (mobile and landscape baselines), hiding the room people came to see.

recommendations.change: Use input-aware coach copy ('Tap to move · drag to look' on coarse pointers) and add a persistent '?' key legend in the tool cluster, like the desk's keyboard legend.
recommendations.why: The current hint is wrong on phones and disappears for good after 8 s.

recommendations.change: Report failed shares ('Copy failed — link selected' with the URL shown).
recommendations.why: Honest consequence: a sales executive thinks the link was copied when it wasn't.

questionsForBlake: The tour is client-facing but also a marketing surface. Should its chrome take the ivory, forest and copper desk look ('everything clients … work in'), or keep a dark 'hall at night' voice tuned to the same family, as the homepage does?
When the 'Panorama tour · Work in progress' qualification is required, may it become a quieter permanent label in the chrome rather than a full-width gold band?
Should the tour show live date availability or tentative holds to prospects ('Saturday 5 June 2027 is free')? It would beat Cvent and Salesforce, but it exposes the diary.
Which capacity formats may the public see: only reception and dinner (today), or also theatre, cabaret and boardroom?
Do sales executives present the tour on calls or at show-rounds? If so, do you want a presenter mode (larger labels, no fine print, a room-by-room 'next')?
