surfaces.name: Public enquiry from the twin (TwinEnquiryModal, the vv-twin-enq-* overlay, and how its lead lands on the staff desk)
surfaces.audience: client (prospect) submitting; venue staff and sales executives receiving it on the Enquiries desk
surfaces.currentLook:
A centred 460 px dark glass modal: a gradient from #0b1413 to #07100f, 18 px radius, blurred, with a 380 ms rise that is removed under reduced motion. Its type and colour:
- A 10 px mono gold eyebrow, 'HOST YOUR EVENT HERE'.
- A 22 px sans 600 title and a 13 px sub.
- 11 px labels and 13 px inputs with rgba(255,255,255,.04) fills and 28%-gold hairlines (twin.css:622-657).
- A full-width gold pill submit.
- An 11 px trust line.

Fields run in this order: Email *, Name and Phone, Event date and Guests, Event type (select with slug values), and 'Anything else?'. Success shows a '✓' in a gold ring, 'Enquiry sent', the email address, and 'Back to the walkthrough'.
surfaces.dailyUse: Clients: once per enquiry, often on a phone. Staff: every lead it creates is read on the desk, all day.
slogFactors: The inputs use 13 px text (twin.css:635), so iOS Safari zooms the whole page when an input is focused. That is standard browser behaviour for inputs under 16 px (inferred, not device-tested). The visitor then has to pinch back out of a 3D view.

Field boundaries measure 1.77:1 against the panel, so the input edges are near-invisible. Focus changes the border to only 1.87:1 against its resting state, with a 12% glow (twin.css:639, 651-654). Keyboard users can hardly see where they are.
Placeholders at 32% alpha measure 2.42:1, yet 'Approx.' and '+44 …' carry instruction (twin.css:647-649; TwinEnquiryModal.tsx:252, 285).

The copy 'Almost — just needs a valid email address' (TwinEnquiryModal.tsx:219) is the mild cheerleading Blake calls belittling. After a submit, the same problem shows twice, as a top alert and as a field hint.

Errors surface raw server text (TwinEnquiryModal.tsx:109), such as 'Validation failed' (public-enquiries.ts:57) or 'Venue not found', with no alternative contact. The textarea has no maxLength against the 2000-character limit (types/src/enquiry.ts:65), and guests have no max against 10000.
The field order starts with email. The facts a booker decides on (date, guests, room) sit mid-form, and the room is not asked at all.
workflowGaps: Room context is lost, and a false room is written. The modal sends only venueSlug (TwinEnquiryModal.tsx:93-104). The API then anchors every venueSlug enquiry to the flagship space, the lowest sortOrder, which is Grand Hall in the seed (public-enquiries.ts:101-137; seed.ts sort 0). The desk therefore shows 'Grand Hall', and a Grand Hall photograph in its panel, for a visitor who was standing in the Saloon or chose no room. spaces_id is NOT NULL (schema.ts:671).

The provenance is polluted. The API prepends 'Sent from the venue's virtual walkthrough (the twin).' to the message (public-enquiries.ts:17, 143-148). The desk ledger quotes the message's first text as the italic line (enquiry-desk-format.ts:65-68; EnquiryLedger.tsx:129), so every twin lead's quote reads the same sentence instead of the client's words.

The provenance is also mislabelled. fromTwin is true for every venueSlug call (public-enquiries.ts:136), and the homepage composer on /fresh uses that path (FreshPage.tsx:375-384). Website enquiries are therefore stamped as coming from the twin.

Vocabulary drifts. Event types post as slugs ('corporate', 'private', 'concert', 'other'; TwinEnquiryModal.tsx:301-307), and the desk prints eventType raw (EnquiryLedger.tsx:50). A veteran sees 'corporate · 80 guests' beside 'Annual dinner'.
The draft is lost. Clicking the overlay or pressing Escape unmounts the modal (TwinViewerControls.tsx:103-110; TwinEnquiryModal.tsx:118-125, 168), discarding everything typed.

There is no closure beyond 'will be in touch'. The client gets no summary of what they sent, no reference, no expected reply time and no acknowledgement email: the API emails only hallkeepers or a fallback address (public-enquiries.ts:195-250). There is also no next step such as 'plan a layout for this room'.
No e2e test or visual baseline covers this modal. Only unit tests exist (src/twin/__tests__/TwinEnquiryModal.test.tsx), so its real rendering is unverified.
strengths: It is a real, database-persisted lead to the venue's hallkeepers with a fallback recipient, not a mailto. The code carefully guards the asset-versus-database slug trap (types/src/enquiry.ts:141-160).
The modal is focus-trapped and restores focus to the opener (use-focus-trap.ts:122-127). Keyboard walking is disabled while typing in inputs.
The trust line is plain and factual, and the success state names the address the team will reply to.

recommendations.change: Carry the room. Add an optional room slug to GuestEnquirySchema, validate that it belongs to the resolved venue, and anchor to that space. When it is absent, keep the flagship anchor for the NOT NULL column but record 'room not chosen', which the desk should show instead of the flagship's name and photograph. Preselect the room from the dossier (RoomDossier onCompose), editable in the form.
recommendations.why: This is the honest consequence the principle asks for. Today the desk states a room the client never chose, which is the most basic fact a booker decides on.

recommendations.change: Record the source as data, not message text. Add a source field (tour, website or planner) set by the caller. Stop prepending TWIN_SOURCE_NOTE and stop setting fromTwin for every venueSlug call. On the desk, show the source as a quiet chip.
recommendations.why: The ledger quote shows the client's own words, and website leads stop being mislabelled as tour leads.

recommendations.change:
Make the inputs legible and touch-safe:
- 16 px input text on coarse pointers.
- Field borders at 3:1 or better against the panel.
- An unmistakable focus ring (cream on forest, as the desk panel uses).
- Placeholders carry examples only, and hints move into labels ('Guests (approximate)').
recommendations.why: Prevents iOS zoom, meets WCAG 1.4.11 and gives a visible focus ring. Currently the boundary is 1.77:1, the focus change 1.87:1 and placeholders 2.42:1.

recommendations.change: Keep the draft. Hold the field state in TwinViewerControls (or sessionStorage) so reopening restores it. Treat an overlay click on a filled form as 'minimise', not 'discard'.
recommendations.why: A mis-tap on a phone currently erases the whole enquiry.

recommendations.change:
Make failures plain and field-specific:
- Map 400 and 404 to plain field-level messages.
- Show the events team's phone and email on any failure, as FreshEnquiry keeps its mailto (FreshPage.tsx:363-366).
- Add maxLength 2000 with a quiet counter, guests max 10000, and date min today.
- Replace 'Almost — …' with one factual line at the field.
recommendations.why: Honest consequences with a working fallback, and no praise copy.

recommendations.change: Reorder to the booker's decision order: date, guests, occasion and room (prefilled), then name, email, phone and message. Use 'Email (required)' instead of an asterisk. Send human occasion labels from a shared enum that the desk, /fresh and the planner also use.
recommendations.why: The facts that decide come first, in the desk's own vocabulary.

recommendations.change:
Close the loop:
- The success state echoes a sealed summary card (date · guests · room · occasion) and says what happens next and when.
- A client acknowledgement email is sent with the same summary.
- Next steps offered: 'Continue walking' and 'Plan a layout for the {room}'.
recommendations.why: Visible closure for the client, and fewer 'did you get my enquiry?' calls for staff.

recommendations.change: Restyle the modal as the desk's forest decision panel: a cream serif title, one cream primary and ivory-on-forest fields. Add an e2e test that submits it and a visual baseline at 390, 820 and 1440 px.
recommendations.why: Clients' first working surface would then match what staff see, and the flow gets browser evidence.

questionsForBlake: Should every public enquiry send the client an automatic acknowledgement email, and what reply time may it promise (for example 'within one working day')?
If a visitor enquires from between rooms, should the form require a room, offer 'not sure yet', or leave the room to the team?
Is Email-only the right minimum, or should date and guest numbers be required too? More fields mean fewer leads but better ones.
Should the tour, /fresh and the planner share one enquiry form? Today there are three with different fields, vocabularies and failure behaviour.

surfaces.name: Guided tour and room notes (src/twin/tour, src/twin/tags; built but not mounted)
surfaces.audience: public clients (the guided tour); clients, hallkeepers and suppliers (room notes on power, AV, access and service), by design intent
surfaces.currentLook:
This is judged from source only, because nothing imports TourControls or TagLayer outside tests.
- Look: the same Rite dark-and-gold glass, with 9.5 px labels (tour.css:152, 181; tags.css:223) and 19–20 px serif captions.
- Tour: transport controls ('Play the tour', 'Next stop') and captions per room. It pauses on the first touch ('Paused — the view is yours.').
- Room notes: pins typed Power, AV, Access, Service and Feature, with an 'Example' badge and disclosure (tag-copy.ts:54-64).
surfaces.dailyUse: None today, because they are unmounted.
slogFactors: 9.5 px uppercase labels carry the same fatigue as the live HUD.
Mounting either one as a third or fourth floating layer over an already crowded HUD would add clutter unless the HUD is consolidated first.
workflowGaps: The room notes ship 'Example' content (tag-copy.ts:54-64). They must not become visible as venue fact, and the venue has no authoring path in this cluster.
A guided tour is the single press most visitors would make, per TourControls.tsx's own header, but it is not offered.
strengths: 'The moment the visitor touches the view, the tour pauses … and it says so' is exactly the clear-agency rule the brief asks for.
Room notes are the small unsolved problem Cvent does not handle: power, AV and access facts in place. They also refuse to draw a pin away from its true anchor.

recommendations.change: After the HUD consolidation, mount the guided tour as the single 'Play the tour' affordance that the first frame offers. Restyle it in the chosen family with captions at 13 px or larger.
recommendations.why: It gives the one-press path for visitors who never drive.

recommendations.change: Keep room notes unmounted until venue-authored notes exist. When they do, give hallkeepers a simple authoring surface in the desk style.
recommendations.why: This avoids showing example content as fact and serves the event-day vocabulary.

questionsForBlake: Do you want the guided 'Play the tour' offered to prospects? If so, which rooms, in which order, and with whose words?
Should room notes (power, AV, access, service) be public, or only for staff, suppliers and booked clients?
evidence: /home/user/omnitwin/packages/web/src/twin/tour/TourControls.tsx and /home/user/omnitwin/packages/web/src/twin/tags/TagLayer.tsx: imported only by their __tests__ (grep of src)

surfaces.name: Front door (RoomsHomePage at /)
surfaces.audience: public (clients and prospects); signed-in staff also pass through it, because the nav offers Dashboard, Diary and Hallkeeper
surfaces.currentLook:
There are two palettes on one page.
- Masthead: ivory #f4efe4 with forest #203c31 text and a forest 'Plan an event' pill, which is the desk family (RoomsHomePage.css:20-60).
- Body: warm black #14100c with stone #f2ecdf, brass #d8a64c and hairlines (:7-17).

Typography is Fraunces 300 for the hero room name (:109-116), Geist UI, and Geist Mono for the 'measured line' (:118-127). A Grand Hall hero photograph sits under an ink wash, followed by a horizontally scrolling rail of 16:9 posters. The posters rest dimmed and blurred (filter saturate(.82) brightness(.74) blur(.4px), :246) and sharpen only on hover or focus (:252). The page fades in once in 620 ms, with reduced motion honoured.
surfaces.dailyUse: Clients: seconds to minutes per visit. Staff: whenever they land on '/' (inferred from the staff links in its nav).
slogFactors: Posters rest blurred and darkened until hover (RoomsHomePage.css:246-253). On touch devices there is no hover, so the photographs, which should be the moment of scale, stay soft and dim.

Engineering states are shown to clients: 'Not yet walkable · alignment in review', 'Dimensions under review', 'Capture preview' (room-card-copy.ts:57-62; RoomsHomePage.tsx:74), 'Gaussian splats · Work in progress' (:173), and scan footprints like '10.1 × 19.9 × 7.4 m' instead of capacities.
Staff tools (Dashboard, Diary, Hallkeeper) sit in the public primary nav beside 'Plan an event' and 'Log in' (RoomsHomePage.tsx:141-147).
The golden cockpit arrow cursor and gold scrollbar apply here, because this page does not mount .fr-root (index.html:77-79, 165-168).
workflowGaps: In production the splat hold (splat-access.ts:4-6; T-628) closes /room/:slug. The hero's 'Walk the room' and every walkable card still link to /room/:slug (RoomsHomePage.tsx:104, 172), so they land on the WIP page: a door that opens onto a wall.
Enquire exists only as a small footer link to a different page, /fresh#enquire (RoomsHomePage.tsx:201), and carries no room.
The hero offers up to three actions of competing weight ('Plan Grand Hall', 'Walk the room', 'Try the virtual tour · Work in progress'; :170-174).
strengths: The masthead already uses the selected ivory and forest. The Grand Hall hero is sourced photography, and it is preloaded for first paint (index.html:17-30).
Honest measurement discipline: dimensions show only where the scan and the walk box agree.

recommendations.change: While the splat hold is on, point validated rooms' cards and 'Walk the room' at /tour at that room's validated viewpoint (twin-rooms.ts), and point the others to photographs and an enquiry. Stop linking to /room/:slug.
recommendations.why: It removes the dead ends the hold creates without breaking the hold.

recommendations.change: Show posters at full clarity at rest. Keep any dim-to-lit treatment only under (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine).
recommendations.why: Phone visitors currently never see a sharp photograph.

recommendations.change: Replace the staff links in the public nav with one discreet 'Sign in' (staff land on /app).
recommendations.why: Clients should not face staff tools, and staff already have the desk nav.

recommendations.change: Lead each card with the deciding facts from trades-hall-venue-truth: reception and dinner capacity, as large light numerals, and the published dimensions. Move alignment states and scan footprints to the internal captures page.
recommendations.why: Facts that decide come first, in the booker's vocabulary. Scan jargon makes the product look unfinished.

recommendations.change: Add one persistent 'Enquire' in the masthead, always in the same place. It should open the shared enquiry form in place, with the room preselected when launched from a card.
recommendations.why: This gives one next step always in the same place and keeps context.

questionsForBlake: Is RoomsHomePage the public homepage going forward, or is /fresh? The 26 September decision gives 'the public homepage' its own editorial voice, but two front doors exist.
Should staff links (Dashboard, Diary, Hallkeeper) appear anywhere on public pages?
While the splat hold is on, may the room posters open the panorama tour at that room?

surfaces.name: Room walk (RoomWalkPage at /room/:roomSlug; dev only under the splat hold)
surfaces.audience: public (clients arriving from a front-door poster)
surfaces.currentLook: The room fills the frame, with warm-black gradient bars top and bottom. The top bar holds '← Rooms', the Fraunces room name, a Geist Mono measured line, and a nav with a stone 'Plan this room' button plus Dashboard, Hallkeeper and Log in. A mono progress pill reads 'Streaming the room' and then 'Sharpening the room — 42%' through the shared ActivityStatus, and a 0.72 rem footnote sits at the bottom.
surfaces.dailyUse: Occasional client visits. Production visitors see the WIP page instead.
slogFactors: Staff links (Dashboard, Hallkeeper, Log in) sit in a client's room view (RoomWalkPage.tsx:131-138).
Stone text sits over a gradient that fades to 0 over live imagery (RoomWalkPage.css:21-30). Legibility near the bar's lower edge is not guaranteed over bright ceilings (inferred).
There is no hint of how to move (WASD, arrows or drag are supported per interior-camera-input.ts:16-18).

'N parts of this room did not load.' offers no retry (RoomWalkPage.tsx:160-162).

Rooms whose walk box cannot hold a visitor stay closed rather than placing them through a wall.

recommendations.change: Put 'Enquire about the {room}' as the primary action, with 'Plan this room' secondary, and remove the Dashboard and Hallkeeper links.
recommendations.why: One next step for a client, and no staff tools in public.

recommendations.change: Add the twin's first-run movement hint (touch-aware), plus a Retry for failed parts.
recommendations.why: Clear agency, and a recovery path instead of a dead statement.

recommendations.change: The closed-room page should offer that room's photographs, or the tour at its validated viewpoint, and an enquiry.
recommendations.why: This removes a dead end.

surfaces.name: Splat-hold page (SplatsWorkInProgressPage), the production face of /room/:slug, the room showcase and /captures
surfaces.audience: public (anyone who follows a room poster or a room link in production)
surfaces.currentLook: This is the closest page in the cluster to the selected palette: an ivory #f3f0e8 ground, forest #193a30 ink and primary, a copper-brown focus ring (#9b6243), and Georgia 400 headings over an Inter body. It shows the eyebrow 'Gaussian splat viewer', the heading 'Work in progress', and a 'Try the tour ↗' forest button.
surfaces.dailyUse: Every production visit to a room link.
slogFactors: Jargon for clients: 'Gaussian splat viewer', 'Gaussian splat viewing is currently unavailable' (SplatsWorkInProgressPage.tsx:17-19).
'Work in progress' appears three times on one card (h1, tour paragraph, status).
Georgia and Inter are used instead of Newsreader, which is already loaded.
workflowGaps: The page does not know which room the visitor asked for. It cannot name the room or open the tour there, and it offers no enquiry.
strengths: The palette, focus ring and single forest primary already follow the selected style. It honours Blake's T-628 hold.

recommendations.change: Read the requested room from the route. Say, in plain words, that the 3D room walk is being refined (keeping 'Work in progress' once, per the hold). Offer the tour at that room's validated viewpoint, its photographs, and 'Enquire about the {room}'.
recommendations.why: It turns a wall into a useful door while keeping the required qualification.

recommendations.change: Switch headings to Newsreader and use the shared ivory, forest and copper tokens.
recommendations.why: Family consistency.

surfaces.name: Room showcase (RoomShowcasePage at /venues/:venueSlug/rooms/:roomSlug; closed in production by the splat hold)
surfaces.currentLook:
This is a generic dark SaaS page: a #101317 gradient ground, 8 px radius cards, translucent white panels with an 18 px blur, and one gold #d7b56d accent.
- Type: the h1 has no font-family, so it falls back to Inter from :root at up to 6 rem (RoomShowcasePage.css:36-43; global.css:7). Buttons and labels run at weights 800–850 (:70, :310, :348).
- Hero: 'Request layout' (gold), 'Enquire about this room' and 'View planning options' sit beside a photograph or runtime canvas, labelled 'Runtime visual available' or 'Visual preview'.
- Rail: an 8-column horizontal wall of 364 px cards.
- Lower panels: guidance, event-type chips and highlights.
surfaces.dailyUse: None in production (closed). In dev, occasional.
slogFactors: A wall of eight identical cards, each repeating compliance copy ('Client-safe preview. Human review required before final room details.', 'Enquiry-only room selection. No public runtime package is exposed.'; trades-hall-room-showcase.ts:227, 244).
Internal vocabulary shown to clients: 'Runtime visual available', 'Review state: Planning estimates. Venue review required before use.', 'Visual status' (RoomShowcasePage.tsx:98, 323-333).
Heavy 800-weight sans everywhere. There is no editorial serif and no light numerals.
The global spring pop applies to the event-type buttons. Cards lift and zoom their images on hover (:246-248, 286-289).
workflowGaps: 'Enquire about this room' links to /fresh#enquire (trades-hall-room-showcase.ts:69), which is another page with no room carried.
'Request layout' promises a request but links to /plan?space=…&intent=request-layout. Nothing in src reads 'intent', so it behaves exactly like 'View planning options'.

The event-type chips only record analytics and toggle a class (RoomShowcasePage.tsx:241-251, 339-352). They are dead controls that do not carry into the enquiry. role='list' also wraps buttons with no listitems.
Capacities are absent: guestGuidance is prose with no numbers (trades-hall-room-showcase.ts:61), although confirmed figures exist in trades-hall-venue-truth and the twin shows them.
strengths: All public copy passes through safePublicCopy. Analytics events are meaningful (room_viewed, enquiry_clicked).
Sourced room photographs, with image-position control per room.

recommendations.change: Offer one primary, 'Enquire about the {room}', opening the shared enquiry form with the room and any chosen occasion preselected. Make 'Plan a layout' secondary, and remove 'Request layout' unless the planner implements the intent.
recommendations.why: One next step. The consequence each button promises is the one that happens.

recommendations.change: Lead with the confirmed facts: reception, dinner and dimensions in Newsreader light numerals, with the provenance line. Delete 'Runtime visual', 'Review state' and 'Visual status', and remove the compliance copy from the cards.
recommendations.why: Facts that decide come first. Internal jargon makes clients doubt the venue.

recommendations.change: Make the event-type chips set the occasion carried into the enquiry, or remove them. Fix the list semantics.
recommendations.why: No dead controls.

recommendations.change: Restyle in the chosen family (editorial serif at 400–500, ivory or forest), and replace the 8-card horizontal wall with a compact room switcher.
recommendations.why: Not a slog to the eyes, and no wall of identical cards.

questionsForBlake: Should the showcase return once the hold lifts, or should its content fold into the tour's Rooms panel and the front-door cards?
evidence: grep: no reader of 'request-layout' or 'intent' in packages/web/src outside the showcase profile

The claim pill is amber on brown.
surfaces.dailyUse: Rare. Used by internal reviewers during capture work.
slogFactors: The global spring pop swells the room rail buttons on hover (index.html:95-113; RoomCapturesPage.tsx:195-215).
Lowercase badges and raw technical metadata, with the note text at #767d87 (4.62:1, passes AA but is faint).

recommendations.change: Opt the console into calm controls and add ↑/↓ and j/k room stepping with a small key legend.

surfaces.name: Trades Hall asset registry (TradesHallAssetStatusPage at /dev/assets/rooms)
surfaces.currentLook:
A near-black #0a0d0f console sits inside the ivory desk header and a forest frame (the success baseline).
- Heading: bold Georgia at 58 px in pale gold ('Trades Hall runtime rooms'; CSS:31-33).
- Accents: cyan #71d3df (CSS:22, 152).
- Rooms: each is a card with eight bordered dl cells of 11–13 px text, mixing enum strings, IDs and amber warnings.
surfaces.dailyUse: Occasional platform-admin checks.
slogFactors: A wall of identical dense cells: 8 per room and up to 15 lines in 'Capture control' (TradesHallAssetStatusPage.tsx:62-196). Status enums have their underscores removed ('captured / needs processing'), and IDs are inline ('Record 10000000-0000-4000-8000-…').
Off-palette cyan and bold Georgia inside the desk frame. The two halves read as two products.
The error baseline shows the raw 't469 asset registry failure' (:234).
The role-denied baseline is a dark card, 'Access needed', with no link back and no named admin.
workflowGaps: There is no 'what to do next' ordering across rooms: nextAction is buried per card (:199-208).
Access denied is a dead end.
strengths: The Retry is a real reload. Unsafe public wording is actively detected (:28-46, 259-264).

recommendations.change:
Rebuild as a desk:
- An ivory ledger of rooms (name, one status chip, next action) grouped by what needs doing.
- A forest detail panel for the evidence chain, with IDs behind a disclosure.
- Use Newsreader, drop the cyan, and use the shared tokens.
recommendations.why: Facts that decide come first, then progress toward 'all rooms registered', with no walls of identical cards.

recommendations.change: Replace raw error text with a plain sentence and keep the last known data. On access denied, offer a way back and name who grants access.
recommendations.why: No dead ends, and honest failure.

crossCutting: The global springy hover (scale 1.06, brightness 1.15, overshoot curve; index.html:95-113) hits every button in the twin, the room showcase, the captures console and the asset registry. The twin's own restrained :hover and :active rules lose to the global (0,3,2) selector. Blake has decided to remove it everywhere (product-experience.md, 26 September).
Cockpit gold arrow cursor and gold scrollbar (index.html:77-79, 165-168) apply to every page without .fr-root, including the public front door at '/' (RoomsHomePage) and the tour.

The global cyan focus ring (global.css:42-54, --vv-focus #87e7f0) measures 1.22:1 on the desk's ivory #f2eddd by my calculation. On the dark showcase and asset pages it is visible but off-palette. The twin overrides it with a gold halo, but the twin's enquiry inputs fall back to a 1.87:1 focus change.

No shared tokens exist for the selected style. The desk's ivory, forest, copper and sage live only as --enq-* in EnquiriesDesk.css:10-46, and house-tokens.css:22 says the ivory register is absent. This cluster uses five different golds: twin #d7a64b, rooms #d8a64c, showcase #d7b56d, captures #d8ad4a, asset #f0c86b. Promote the desk palette to shared tokens before restyling these surfaces.

Font sprawl in this cluster: Newsreader and Geist Mono (twin), Fraunces and Geist (front door and walk), Inter by default (showcase h1), Georgia (asset registry and the hold page), and system-ui (captures).

Public enquiries have three forms with different fields, event-type vocabularies and failure behaviour: TwinEnquiryModal, FreshEnquiry (FreshPage.tsx:320-420) and the planner's GuestEnquiryModal. The showcase and the front door send people to /fresh#enquire without the room.

API (packages/api/src/routes/public-enquiries.ts:101-148): every venueSlug enquiry is anchored to the flagship space, which is Grand Hall in the seed. Each one is also stamped 'Sent from the venue's virtual walkthrough (the twin).' at the head of the message, including /fresh enquiries. On the desk this shows a room the client never chose, the Grand Hall photograph, and the same italic quote on every such lead (enquiry-desk-format.ts:65-68). No acknowledgement email goes to the client.
Event-type slugs ('corporate', 'private', 'other') are stored raw and printed raw by the desk ledger (EnquiryLedger.tsx:50). Public forms need a shared, human-labelled occasion enum.
Staff links (Dashboard, Diary, Hallkeeper, Log in) appear on public pages (RoomsHomePage.tsx:141-147; RoomWalkPage.tsx:131-138).

The founder's splat hold (splat-access.ts:4-6; docs/sessions/2026-09-19.md) closes /room, the showcase and /captures in production. The public pages that link to them should stop offering doors that open onto the WIP page.

surfaces.name: Consequential and destructive actions (confirmations, lifecycle changes, deletes)
surfaces.audience: venue staff / venue admin / sales executives / client (proposal approval) / platform admin
surfaces.dailyUse: Several times an hour for sales staff (status changes, approvals); weekly for admins (deletes); once per event for clients (approving a proposal).
surfaces.currentLook: At least seven confirmation grammars. (1) The shared ConfirmModal is a near-black overlay (rgba(0,0,0,0.82) with cyan and gold radial glows) holding a 400 px dark card. It has a red #dc2626 confirm button, Title Case titles ('Delete Venue', 'Remove Photo') and a 'Working...' busy label (ConfirmModal.tsx:9-31, 109). (2) Reviews NoteModal is a separate copy of the same dark overlay (ReviewsView.tsx:197-257). (3) The Diary's InkConfirm is an alertdialog in Diary styling (BoardPanels.tsx:219-259). (4) The Enquiries desk uses an inline consequence panel on forest (EnquiryPanel.tsx:323-387). (5-7) Inventory and Foundry each have their own action dialogs and navigation guard. No window.confirm, alert or prompt exists anywhere (grep: 0).
slogFactors: Friction is inverted, so the safest actions are the most tedious and the terminal ones have no brake. Removing a photo, which the modal itself says keeps the file ('The file will not be deleted from storage', LoadoutDetail.tsx:465-468), takes a full-screen modal. Cancelling a confirmed booking fires on one click. 'Cancel the ink', 'Release', 'Mark lost' and 'Mark expired' render as equal buttons calling runTransition directly (BookingDrawer.tsx:180-192, 519-526), and each of those states is terminal with no transitions out (packages/types/src/booking.ts:94-97).
The Diary asks 'Move this inked booking?' before a drag (board-copy.ts:170-174), but cancelling the same inked booking gets no question. Veterans will learn not to trust the pattern.

Consequences are revealed only after the act. Reviews 'Approve' is one click (ReviewsView.tsx:515) and emails the planner, staff and hallkeepers (configuration-reviews.ts:146-161). The only statement of that is the success toast 'Layout approved — team notifications requested' (ReviewsView.tsx:361-363).

Proposal 'Withdraw' and 'Archive' are one click (ProposalsView.tsx:572-581) and terminal (packages/types/src/proposal.ts:104-105). They silently turn the client's share link into a 404 (api/src/routes/proposals.ts:964-975), and staff are never told the client's link stops working.
Deleting a pricing rule is one click, with no confirmation and no undo (AdminPanel.tsx:632-643). A pricing rule affects every future quote.
Reviews 'Withdraw' is one click and terminal (ReviewsView.tsx:530; configuration-review.ts:72).
The space-delete modal does not name the space or count what will go: 'Delete this space? Associated configurations and loadouts will be removed.' (AdminPanel.tsx:768-771).
On ivory or forest surfaces a near-black modal suddenly dims the whole app. This is the 'modal-on-modal' feel the brief warns against.
The client's 'Approve proposal' is one tap, and nothing beside it says what approving commits them to (ProposalPage.tsx:314-321).
strengths: The Enquiries desk's inline confirmation is the right model. It names the record and names the email address that will receive the message. It says whether a note is quoted to the client. It moves focus to the question and keeps the list in view (EnquiryPanel.tsx:323-368).
The Diary has a real undo for moves ('Moved X. Undo', BoardPanels.tsx:195-212; board-copy.ts:216-222). This is the calm alternative to a confirmation.
ConfirmModal and NoteModal use useFocusTrap, which puts first focus on Cancel when there is no note field and returns focus to the opener on close (lib/use-focus-trap.ts:77-129).
The Reviews reject and request-changes modals state the consequence: 'This note is emailed to the planner and saved in review history.' (ReviewsView.tsx:594-597).
workflowGaps: Undoing a mistaken 'Cancel the ink' is impossible because the state is terminal. Staff would have to re-create the booking by hand and may lose its history (inferred from booking.ts:96).

After 'Generate client link' there is no copy button. Staff must select a raw URL (ProposalsView.tsx:555) and send it from their own email. Nothing in the UI says the client is not emailed; the proposals route has no sendEmail (grep of api routes).
Destructive lifecycle buttons sit in the same row as 'Ink it' (BookingDrawer.tsx:515-531), so a mis-tap on a tablet is plausible.
evidence: packages/types/src/booking.ts:87-98 (released, expired, cancelled and lost have no outgoing transitions)
packages/api/src/routes/proposals.ts:964-975 (withdrawn or archived returns 404 to the client)

recommendations.change: Extract the desk's inline confirmation into a shared ConsequenceConfirm component. It appears in place of the button that opened it. It holds: a question naming the record; one consequence sentence saying who is emailed, what stops working and whether it can be undone; a verb-and-object confirm button ('Cancel the booking', 'Withdraw and close the client link'); and Cancel. Focus moves to the question and Esc closes it. Use it for Reviews (replacing NoteModal), for ConfirmModal uses in AdminPanel and LoadoutDetail, and in the Diary drawer. Style it on the workspace tokens (forest on ivory surfaces).
recommendations.why: One grammar that veterans learn once. It is honest before the act, keeps its context and has no black overlay. The desk's version is already the pattern Blake called inviting.

recommendations.change: Put a ConsequenceConfirm on every terminal one-click action. Diary: 'Cancel the ink', 'Release', 'Mark lost' and 'Mark expired' (e.g. 'Cancelling frees the Grand Hall on Sat 5 June. The client is not emailed. This cannot be undone.'). Proposals: 'Withdraw' and 'Archive' ('The client's link will stop working.'). Reviews: 'Withdraw'. Admin: deleting a pricing rule.
recommendations.why: These actions are irreversible under the current state machines, yet they get less friction than removing a photo.

recommendations.change: Make Reviews 'Approve' name its recipients before sending, as the desk does ('Approving emails Jane Smith (planner), 2 staff and 3 hallkeepers'). Keep it to one extra click on the same panel.
recommendations.why: The consequence is currently only in the success toast, after the emails have gone.

recommendations.change: Next to the client's 'Approve proposal' button, add one plain sentence on what approval means and what happens next, followed by an inline 'Approve this proposal?' step.
recommendations.why: It is the client's commitment moment. Nothing on screen says whether it holds the date or starts a contract.

recommendations.change: In BookingDrawer, show the constructive step as the single primary action ('Ink it'). Group Release, Cancel and Mark lost under a quiet 'Close this booking…' disclosure below it.
recommendations.why: It follows the desk principle of one next step in the same place, and keeps destructive options away from the thumb.

recommendations.change: Where the API can reverse an action (photo removal, caption edits, reorder), drop the modal and use a shared Undo notice built from the Diary's UndoToast.
recommendations.why: An undo removes a step and a doubt, and calm technology prefers it to a confirmation for reversible work.

recommendations.change: Next to 'Generate client link', add 'Copy link' and a line saying that the client is not emailed automatically.
recommendations.why: It removes a manual select-and-copy and states the real consequence.

questionsForBlake: Should cancelling or releasing a booking ever email the client? Today nothing is sent (the bookings route has no email). Should staff be offered a drafted email at that moment?
When a client presses 'Approve proposal', is that a commercial commitment (date held, deposit due, contract)? The wording before the tap depends on it.
For irreversible internal actions, do you prefer an inline 'are you sure' step, or a short undo window with no question? (Undo would need API support for cancelled or released bookings.)
When a proposal is withdrawn, should the client be told by email, and should their link show 'withdrawn by the venue' rather than 'isn't available'?

surfaces.name: Toasts and transient notices
surfaces.audience: venue staff / venue admin / platform admin (dashboard); the Diary, the planner and the Blueprint editor each have their own
surfaces.dailyUse: Every save and every failure on dashboard views, dozens of times a day for staff.
surfaces.currentLook: The ToastContainer is fixed at top 16 px, right 16 px, z-index 500. It uses Tailwind wash colours (#f0fdf4, #fef2f2, #eff6ff) with 3 px green, red or blue left borders, 13 px Inter and a 4-second auto-dismiss for every type, errors included. The dismiss × is #999, about 2.6:1 on the washes (ToastContainer.tsx:7-50; toast-store.ts:31-34). There are 94 addToast calls in 10 files: 20 success, 48 error. Three more toast implementations exist: Diary UndoToast (BoardPanels.tsx:201), SaveErrorToast (EditorPage.tsx:558) and Blueprint Toast (BlueprintPage.tsx:2309).
slogFactors: The error toast covers the account name in the header. The committed baseline desktop-reviews-action-error shows 'Failed to approve' sitting over 'Staff F…'.
Errors vanish after 4 seconds (toast-store.ts:31-34), before a busy person looks up. The timeout is the same for success and failure.

Failures are reported twice. 8 of the 10 toast-using files also render an inline role=alert for the same failure. For example, Reviews shows the toast 'Failed to approve' and the inline 'Approval did not save…' (ReviewsView.tsx:367-368; baseline). The desk itself does this: toast 'Failed to load enquiries' (EnquiriesView.tsx:203) plus inline 'Enquiries could not be loaded.' (EnquiriesView.tsx:551).
Messages have no subject and no next step: 'Failed to reorder' (LoadoutDetail.tsx:203,231), 'Failed to load loadout', 'Search failed'.

Success toasts fire for changes the screen already shows ('Photo added', 'Space updated', 'Venue settings saved'). Weiser and Brown's calm technology, which the desk follows, says not to toast every success.
Generic library green, red and blue unrelated to the ivory, forest and copper style.
Live regions are nested: a role=status aria-live container holds role=alert children (ToastContainer.tsx:21-34). The activity convention warns against nested announcements.
strengths: The Diary's UndoToast carries the right idea: a factual past-tense line ('Moved X.') with an Undo, and honest failure copy ('That move could not be saved — the board has been restored.', board-copy.ts:216-222).
removeToast clears pending timers (toast-store.ts:38-46).
workflowGaps: Validation errors go to a toast in the far corner instead of beside the field: 'Height must be a positive number' (AdminPanel.tsx:318), 'Name and positive height required' (375), 'Amount must be a non-negative number' (415), and FileUploader size and type errors (FileUploader.tsx:46,52).
An error toast offers no retry, so the person must find the control again.
evidence: packages/web/e2e/dashboard-state-visual-performance.spec.ts-snapshots/desktop-loadout-caption-error-chromium-linux.png (toast plus inline banner for one failure)

recommendations.change: Replace the ToastContainer with one shared Notice in the workspace palette: ivory card, forest ink, a copper rule for failures, Newsreader for the subject. Place it bottom-left above the content, never over the header. Failures persist until dismissed or resolved, carry a Retry, and say what is unchanged ('The caption wasn't saved. The photo is unchanged.').
recommendations.why: Calm, legible and in the selected style. People who look away do not lose errors.

recommendations.change: Remove the toast wherever an inline alert already reports the same failure, including the desk and Reviews. Keep success notices only when the change happens off-screen.
recommendations.why: It halves the noise and follows the desk's own 'no toast for every success' rule.

recommendations.change: Move validation messages out of toasts to the field they concern (AdminPanel space height, pricing amount, FileUploader size and type).
recommendations.why: An error far from its cause is frustrating and easy to miss.

recommendations.change: Merge UndoToast, SaveErrorToast and the Blueprint Toast into the shared Notice: one polite status region, with assertive only for failures and never nested.
recommendations.why: It gives one vocabulary and one position across the Diary, the planner and the dashboard.

questionsForBlake: When staff finish a routine save, should there be no notice at all (the screen simply shows the change), or a very quiet line near the control?

surfaces.name: Error, access-denied and crash states
surfaces.audience: all: venue staff, hallkeeper, supplier, client, platform admin
surfaces.dailyUse: Rare per person, but it is the moment trust is won or lost. A hallkeeper on a bad connection may hit it several times on an event day.
surfaces.currentLook: The shared .vv-state-panel is a dark gold-bordered card. Its heading is Georgia or Times New Roman at weight 600 and its kicker is a gold 850-weight uppercase label (global.css:72-110). Baselines show the Times fallback heading on dark forest. The error boundary is off-palette: grey #f5f5f0 page, #333 text and a navy #1a1a2e 'Reload Page' button (error-boundary.tsx:66-90). The hallkeeper error card is lighter, with Playfair. The client proposal error is cream on graphite.
slogFactors: Raw technical text reaches people. error.message is rendered at 39 call sites across 23 files (grep 'instanceof Error ? x.message'). ApiError falls back to 'Request failed (HTTP 500).' (client.ts:94) and to 'Server returned an unexpected response shape for GET /…' (client.ts:163-166). Hallkeeper shows 'Failed to load (500)' and 'Configuration not found.' (HallkeeperPage.tsx:155-157). The error boundary prints the JavaScript exception message (error-boundary.tsx:61-63). Committed baselines show server text verbatim ('t469 venue registry failure', 't469 caption save failure').

Dead ends. ProtectedRoute shows 'Access needed / Ask your venue admin to grant access.' with no action, no sign-out and no route to what the person can use (ProtectedRoute.tsx:37-43). The committed supplier-denied baseline is older, and its 'Access not granted' pill looks like a button but is not one.
The hallkeeper 403 page offers 'Try Again' (HallkeeperPage.tsx:424), which cannot fix a permission problem. Its branch is chosen by string-matching 'permission' (HallkeeperPage.tsx:415).
The client proposal error says 'contact the venue team' but gives no name, email or phone. It shows the same page for a network failure as for a withdrawn proposal (ProposalPage.tsx:97-99, 158-174).
DashboardAccessDenied exposes internals: 'The requested view "admin" is held back…', 'That dashboard surface' (DashboardPage.tsx:98-110).

Catch-alls that blame the person: 'Check the details and try again' fires for any failure, including server errors (CommercialPipelineView.tsx:255; ProposalsView.tsx:316; SupplierPortalPage.tsx:124; ReviewsView.tsx:344 'Check your role and retry').
The ops handoff error says 'compile it again from an approved snapshot' (baseline mobile-ops-handoff-unavailable), which is jargon for an ops coordinator.
strengths: Retry is nearly universal (about 60 retry or try-again controls), usually named for the thing ('Retry pipeline', 'Retry analytics').

Many failure lines are honest about what did not change. 'Approval did not save. The layout has not been approved.' (ReviewsView.tsx:367). 'Rejection did not save. The planner has not been notified.' (ReviewsView.tsx:387). Diary: 'That change could not be saved — nothing was altered.' (board-copy.ts:101).
The client comment error keeps the typed text and suggests contacting the venue (baseline desktop-proposal-share-comment-error).
ApiError never coerces an object body into visible text (client.ts:86-99).
workflowGaps: No denied state leads anywhere useful. A supplier who opens /dashboard is not pointed to their supplier handoff, and a hallkeeper is not pointed to 'Today's rooms'.
The error boundary always reloads the page and never says whether unsaved work survived.
evidence: packages/web/e2e/dashboard-state-visual-performance.spec.ts-snapshots/desktop-supplier-denied-chromium-linux.png (stale: the current source renders 'Access needed', per e2e spec line 726)

recommendations.change: Add describeFailure(error, {action, subject}) at the API boundary. It maps ApiError code and status to one plain sentence in venue language and says what is unchanged ('The layout wasn't approved. Nothing was sent. Try again.'), with a separate network variant ('Can't reach Venviewer. Your changes are still here.'). Render only its output, never error.message or HTTP codes, and send the detail to observability.
recommendations.why: This removes jargon at the 39 sites in one place and ends the blame-leaning catch-alls.

recommendations.change: Rebuild .vv-state-panel, the error boundary and the hallkeeper, proposal and handoff error pages on workspace tokens: ivory sheet, Newsreader heading, ink primary button, a quiet sage ground. Every one gets a way back ('Back to Enquiries' or 'Back to today's rooms') as well as Retry.
recommendations.why: Replaces the Times fallback, the grey-and-navy boundary and the dark cards. A failure should still feel finished and calm.

recommendations.change: Make every denied state name who can grant access (the venue admin's name or email when known) and offer what the person can do: suppliers go to their handoffs, hallkeepers to Today's rooms, and every denied state offers 'Use another account'. Remove 'Try Again' from 403 pages and branch on status, not string matching.
recommendations.why: No dead ends, and no action that cannot work.

recommendations.change: On the client proposal page, show the venue's name and events-team contact. Distinguish a connection failure (with Retry) from a proposal that is withdrawn or expired.
recommendations.why: The client is currently told to contact someone with no means to do so.

questionsForBlake: When access is denied, may we show the venue admin's name and email to the person who was refused (for example a supplier)?

surfaces.name: Empty states and closure
surfaces.audience: venue staff / sales executives / venue admin
surfaces.dailyUse: Every time a queue empties. For a good team that is daily, and it is the moment that should feel like closure.
surfaces.currentLook: About 22 'No … yet/found' strings. Outside the desk they are plain grey text in a dark card. Examples: 'No opportunities yet / Create one from an enquiry.' (CommercialPipelineView.tsx:430-436), 'No pending reviews.' (ReviewsView.tsx around line 689), 'No reference loadouts yet.' (LoadoutsView.tsx:267), 'No results found for “x”' in #999 (ClientSearchView.tsx:79), 'No venues found.' (AdminPanel.tsx:852). The desk has per-stage empty words (EnquiriesView.tsx:105-112) and a sealed 'All caught up'.
slogFactors: The Pipeline empty state tells people to 'Create one from an enquiry' but gives no link or button to do it.
An empty queue in Reviews and in Pipeline tasks feels like nothing rather than done. Only the desk marks closure.
'No venues found.' implies a failed search when the list is simply empty.
Client search with no results offers nothing: no alternative search and no 'add this person as a lead'.
strengths: The desk's stage-aware empty words and sealed 'All caught up' set the standard (desk-all-caught-up.webp).
Pipeline stage columns show the next action when empty (STAGE_NEXT, CommercialPipelineView.tsx:447-448).
The Diary copy is plain and factual ('No bookings in this range.', 'No overdue next actions.').
workflowGaps: No empty state carries the next step as a control, so every one is a dead end for a new user.

recommendations.change: Build a shared EmptyState with two variants. Nothing yet: the plain fact plus one next-step button in the position the primary action normally holds ('Open approved enquiries' for Pipeline). Caught up: the desk's restrained seal and one factual line ('Nothing waiting for a decision') for queues (Reviews, Needs attention, Pipeline tasks).
recommendations.why: Every empty screen leads somewhere, and emptying a queue feels complete without praise copy.

recommendations.change: When client search finds nothing, show 'Search enquiries by date or room instead' and 'Add as a new lead' as quiet actions.
recommendations.why: Solves the small problem a booker actually has at that moment.

questionsForBlake: Should the sealed 'All caught up' treatment appear on every queue (Reviews, Pipeline tasks, Diary 'Needs attention'), or stay special to Enquiries?

surfaces.name: Loading and route-transition states
surfaces.dailyUse: On every navigation between staff tools, many times a day.
surfaces.currentLook: The shared Activity component is imported in 90 files, and there are no ad-hoc spinners or skeletons (grep). But every transition surface is dark. The first-paint boot is #171715 (Activity.css:3-10; index.html:174). html and body sit on --vv-ink, a near-black (global.css:10-20). Every lazy route falls back to RouteArrival, a full-screen dark brown gradient headed 'Workspace · Opening…' with a 'Back to venue ↗' footer (RouteArrival.tsx:32-50; RouteArrival.css:11-19; router.tsx:186-192). ProtectedRoute's 'Checking access…' uses the dark .vv-route-state (ProtectedRoute.tsx:20-27; global.css:61-70).
slogFactors: (Inferred, not measured.) Moving between light surfaces, such as Enquiries (sage and ivory) to the Diary (ivory), can pass through one or two full-screen dark interstitials. That is a hard brightness swing for someone doing it all day.
RouteArrival's copy is written for the public planner ('Workspace', 'Back to venue') and is shown to staff.
11 labels use a three-dot '...' instead of '…', including ConfirmModal's generic 'Working...' (ConfirmModal.tsx:109), 'Loading pipeline...', 'Searching...', 'Loading profile...' and 'Creating...'.
strengths: The activity convention is followed: honest labels, the busy state sits on the control that owns it, and reduced motion is respected (EnquiriesView.tsx:585 'Loading more…'; ReviewsView.tsx:478 'Recording the review decision…').
The desk keeps content visible while it refreshes.

recommendations.change: Give staff routes a light RouteArrival and access-check variant (sage ground, ivory plane, the same particle Activity in forest, the destination's name: 'Opening the Diary…'). Make the html and body background follow the surface family.
recommendations.why: Removes the dark flash between light tools and keeps the sense of one continuous desk.

recommendations.change: Replace the 11 three-dot labels with '…' and specific verbs ('Deleting the venue…' rather than 'Working...').
recommendations.why: Precise, finished copy. The convention asks for the actual operation label.

surfaces.name: Forms and validation
surfaces.audience: venue staff / venue admin / supplier / client (planner and enquiry forms)
surfaces.dailyUse: Constant for sales staff: notes, tasks, opportunities and proposal versions.
surfaces.currentLook: There are 149 inputs and 32 textareas but only 16 form elements app-wide. aria-invalid appears 12 times in 5 files, aria-describedby 9 times, and aria-errormessage never. There are 17 native date or time inputs in 9 files. Styling varies by surface: dark translucent inputs (Pipeline, Proposals, Reviews), a white input with a #e5e7eb border (ClientSearchView.tsx:61-69), and an off-white admin form in the Onboarding baseline.
slogFactors: Enter does nothing on the most frequent inputs. Pipeline 'Add' opportunity, 'Add' task and notes, Proposals create and compose, and the supplier response all have no form element and no key handler (CommercialPipelineView.tsx, ProposalsView.tsx and SupplierPortalPage.tsx each have 0 onKeyDown or Enter).
Pipeline 'Quick create from enquiry' asks staff to type an 'Enquiry ID', a UUID (CommercialPipelineView.tsx:384-397). No veteran knows that.
The client search input has no label, only placeholder text (ClientSearchView.tsx:61-69).

Disabled buttons don't say why. The reject and request-changes confirm is disabled at opacity 0.5 until a note is typed, with no text reason (ReviewsView.tsx:201, 253-257). The Proposals send reason is only in a hover title tooltip (ProposalsView.tsx:566), which is invisible on touch and to keyboard users.
Validation speaks maths and web jargon: 'Amount must be a non-negative number' (AdminPanel.tsx:415) and 'Use a six-digit hex colour' (VenueSettings.tsx:260).

EventDetailsPanel is aria-modal, but a click on the backdrop calls onClose and discards unsaved edits. It has no Esc handling and no focus trap (EventDetailsPanel.tsx:376-387). Its state is local and reloaded on open, so edits are lost (inferred from EventDetailsPanel.tsx:65-80).
Only Inventory guards unsaved changes (InventoryNavigationGuard). VenueSettings shows 'Unsaved changes' (VenueSettings.tsx:201-203) but lets the nav discard them.
(Inferred.) Native date inputs display in the browser's locale, so a US-locale browser shows mm/dd/yyyy on BookingDrawer, EventDetailsPanel and the enquiry forms.
strengths: VenueSettings has field-level validation with aria-invalid and a live 'Unsaved changes / Saved' status (VenueSettings.tsx:201-273).
The desk's decline note field says exactly where the note goes ('shown in the email as “Note from the events team”').
The Inventory navigation guard is a working model for unsaved-work protection.
workflowGaps: There are two parallel public enquiry forms (GuestEnquiryModal and TwinEnquiryModal) with separate validation and error handling. GuestEnquiryModal.tsx:174 renders err.message.
Adding a pipeline task takes only a title. The due date is shown ('No due date', CommercialPipelineView.tsx:113-118) but cannot be set in that row.
evidence: packages/web/e2e/operational-state-visual-performance.spec.ts-snapshots/tablet-onboarding-project-gate-error-chromium-linux.png (raw enum selects, error far from its button)

recommendations.change: Wrap every create, compose and respond area in a form so Enter submits (Cmd/Ctrl+Enter for textareas). Add a shared Field component: visible label, hint, error linked with aria-describedby and aria-invalid, all in workspace tokens.
recommendations.why: The fastest route to keyboard-speed data entry for all-day users, and consistent accessible errors.

recommendations.change: Replace Pipeline's 'Enquiry ID' box with an enquiry picker (type a client name or date), or remove it in favour of the desk's 'Create opportunity' on approved enquiries.
recommendations.why: Asking for a UUID is the opposite of making life easier.

recommendations.change: Show why a button is disabled in visible text beside it ('Add a note to send the rejection', 'Save a version first'). Never rely on a title tooltip.
recommendations.why: Removes guesswork on touch and keyboard.

recommendations.change: Generalise InventoryNavigationGuard into a useUnsavedChanges guard. Apply it to VenueSettings, the proposal composer, EventDetailsPanel and the desk's open decline note. In EventDetailsPanel add useFocusTrap and Esc, and stop the backdrop discarding edits.
recommendations.why: Protects people's work and matches 'every action must preserve data'.

recommendations.change: Rewrite validation in venue language ('Enter a price of £0 or more', a colour picker instead of hex).
recommendations.why: Veterans are not developers.

recommendations.change: Use one date field component that shows the chosen date in British form (e.g. 'Sat 5 June 2027') beside or instead of the native control.
recommendations.why: A predictable date format regardless of the laptop's locale.

questionsForBlake: Would the team type quick notes and tasks with Enter to save, or is a visible Save button always preferred?

surfaces.name: Keyboard support and focus management
surfaces.audience: venue staff / sales executives (heavy keyboard users) / anyone using a keyboard or screen reader
surfaces.dailyUse: Continuous for power users. It is what separates a Superhuman-grade tool from a CRM.
surfaces.currentLook: The global focus ring is 3 px cyan #87e7f0 with a cyan glow (global.css:42-54; house-tokens.css:79). Computed contrast: 1.22:1 on the desk ivory #f2eddd and 1.43:1 on white, against 3:1 needed. Only the desk overrides it, with an ink or cream ring (EnquiriesDesk.css:84-90). useFocusTrap is robust: Tab cycling, disclosure-aware and returns focus (use-focus-trap.ts:66-130); 13 files use it. Keyboard shortcuts exist only in the desk (↑ ↓ j k Enter Esc with a kbd legend), the Diary (t d w f m and a Ctrl+K palette, DiaryBoardPage.tsx:535-546) and Blueprint.
slogFactors: On every light surface except the desk, keyboard focus is effectively invisible: 1.22:1 on ivory.
The Reviews, Pipeline, Proposals, Client search and Loadouts lists have no keyboard triage. Each item is a Tab stop and a click.

In list-to-detail views other than the desk ('← Back to pending reviews', ReviewsView.tsx:447; ClientProfile '← Back', ClientProfile.tsx:85), detail replaces the list and the Back button unmounts. With no .focus() call in those files, focus falls to the document and the reader loses their place (inferred).

10 role=dialog elements have no focus trap. Some are intentionally non-modal, but EventDetailsPanel (EventDetailsPanel.tsx:377-379) and the Blueprint shortcut help (BlueprintPage.tsx:414) declare aria-modal without trapping.
The Diary's shortcut legend lives in its own help panel and the desk's in its overview. No shared '?' convention exists.
strengths: The desk moves focus to the panel heading on open and back to the originating row on close (EnquiriesView.tsx:328-339, 409) and shows its keys (desk-overview.webp).
The Diary has a real command palette (Ctrl+K) and view keys.
useFocusTrap handles edge cases such as closed details elements and hidden nodes, and restores focus.
evidence: Contrast computed with the WCAG formula: #87e7f0 on #f2eddd = 1.22; on #ffffff = 1.43; on #132b25 = 10.51

recommendations.change: Replace --vv-focus with context tokens: a 2 px ink #14302a ring on ivory, copper and sage, and a cream ring on forest and dark surfaces. Apply them globally so the desk's override becomes the default.
recommendations.why: WCAG 2.4.7 and 1.4.11 on every light surface. It is a one-line fix with app-wide reach.

recommendations.change: Extract the desk's list triage into a shared useListTriage hook plus a kbd legend component (↑ ↓ / j k to move, Enter to open, Esc to close, focus follows the reader). Adopt it in Reviews, Pipeline stage columns, Proposals, Client search results and Loadouts.
recommendations.why: Veterans doing repetitive triage get the fast, satisfying loop Blake liked on the desk.

recommendations.change: On every list-to-detail swap, focus the detail heading on open and the originating row on Back. Prefer the desk's side-by-side layout at 1180 px and wider.
recommendations.why: Keeps the reader's place, as the desk does.

recommendations.change: Make '/' focus the surface's search and '?' open a shared shortcut sheet on every staff surface.
recommendations.why: Predictable keyboard grammar across the platform.

questionsForBlake: How keyboard-heavy is the Trades Hall team? Should j/k triage come to every list, or only the high-volume ones (Enquiries, Reviews, Pipeline)?

surfaces.name: Dates, times and numbers
surfaces.audience: all; especially clients and hallkeepers, for whom a wrong date or time format is a real risk
surfaces.dailyUse: Every screen, constantly.
surfaces.currentLook: Mostly British: 16 Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-GB') calls, and toLocaleString('en-GB') everywhere for numbers, with GBP used consistently (16 uses). But 9 calls pass no locale and follow the device: ReviewsView.tsx:463, 465, 553, 708; ClientProfile.tsx:103, 116; ClientSearchView.tsx:124; EventDetailsPanel.tsx:599; HallkeeperStatusBanner.tsx:51; InstructionsBanner.tsx:202. The committed Reviews baseline renders 'Submitted: 6/18/2026, 1:00:00 PM'. Bare toLocaleString('en-GB') on timestamps gives numeric strings with seconds ('18/06/2026, 13:00:00') in ProposalsView.tsx:548, 808, 872 and EventArchitectOpsReviewPanel.tsx:180-181. There are 14 separate date and time helpers in 10 files. Only some pass the venue time zone: the Diary's VENUE_TIME_ZONE (board-time.ts:15), and Foundry, which hard-codes Europe/London. EventDayOpsPage.tsx:48-53 and CommercialPipelineView.tsx:113-118 use the device time zone.
slogFactors: US-format dates with seconds and AM/PM appear in the Reviews detail and timeline (baseline desktop-reviews-action-error), which contradicts 'venue-local and British'.

(Inferred from locale behaviour.) Hallkeeper instructions can show a 12-hour clock on some devices (InstructionsBanner.tsx:202 uses the [] locale) while the rest of the hallkeeper flow uses 24-hour time.
Numeric timestamps with seconds make people parse where they should read.
ClientProfile renders preferredDate as a raw string (ClientProfile.tsx:133), and 'Since:' becomes 'Invalid Date' when both createdAt values are missing (ClientProfile.tsx:103).
Event-day times follow the device time zone, not the venue's. A travelling manager or a UTC-configured tablet would see shifted times (inferred).
strengths: The desk's enquiry-desk-format.ts already has venue-zone helpers (venueDate, venueMoment, relativeAge, eventLead, receivedGroup, lines 187-290) that produce 'Saturday, in 8 months' and weekday calendar tiles.
Currency formatting is consistently GBP.

recommendations.change: Promote the desk's venue-time helpers into lib/venue-time.ts (all taking the venue's IANA zone) and replace the 14 local helpers and the 9 locale-less calls. House style: 'Sat 5 Jun 2027', '14:30', relative age for recent items, absolute date on the same line for anything older than a week, and no seconds.
recommendations.why: One British, venue-local voice for time across every tool and document.

recommendations.change: Add an ESLint no-restricted-syntax rule banning toLocaleString, toLocaleDateString and toLocaleTimeString and new Intl.DateTimeFormat outside lib/venue-time.ts.
recommendations.why: Stops the drift coming back.

questionsForBlake: In client-facing documents (proposals, confirmations), should times read '14:30' or '2.30pm'? Staff tools would stay on the 24-hour clock.
Should every time follow the venue's time zone even when a staff member is travelling? (Recommended: yes.)

surfaces.name: Copy voice and vocabulary
surfaces.dailyUse: Everything people read.
surfaces.currentLook: There is no praise or cheerleading copy anywhere (grep for 'Great job', 'Awesome', 'Congrat' and similar: 0) and no exclamation marks in UI strings. The Diary speaks the trade's language (pencil, ink, house block). Elsewhere the vocabulary drifts, raw enum values leak through, and casing and legal hedging vary.
slogFactors: The same enquiry state has two names. 'rejected' is 'Declined' on the desk (enquiry-desk-format.ts:29) but 'rejected' in StatusBadge (StatusBadge.tsx:10, used in ClientProfile.tsx:131), and 'submitted' is 'New' on the desk but 'submitted' in StatusBadge.

17 sites render raw enum values with replace(/_/g, ' '): 'under review', 'changes requested', and in the Onboarding selects 'admin invite', 'pending review' and 'not required' (baseline tablet-onboarding-project-gate-error).

Internal text appears on screen: "No actions available for your role in state 'under_review'." (ReviewsView.tsx:536), 'DEMO ONLY: uncheck to approve internally…' (ReviewsView.tsx:511), 'That dashboard surface…' (DashboardPage.tsx:101), 'Enquiry ID', 'Slug: trades-hall-annex', 'configs', 'objects' (ClientSearchView.tsx:88; ClientProfile.tsx:116), 'compile it again from an approved snapshot', 'Current planning delta'.

Casing is mixed. Title Case in the nav ('Pending Reviews', 'Executive Analytics', 'Reference Loadouts', 'Venue Settings', 'Sign Out', DashboardLayout.tsx:38-51,74) and on buttons ('Delete Loadout', 'Start Review', 'Request Changes', 'Open Layout', 'Preview Sheet', 'Reload Page', 'Try Again'). The desk uses sentence case.

Heavy legal hedging: about 43 'planning estimate' or 'human review required' strings. A client proposal carries three, including 'Human review required before final operational reliance.' and a footer paragraph (baseline desktop-proposal-share-comment-error).
Reviews shows statuses as uppercase chips ('SUBMITTED', 'DRAFT') while the desk uses sentence-case chips with a dot.
strengths: There is no belittling encouragement anywhere; the tone is plain and factual.
Many sentences state real consequences ('Only your team sees this stage. Nothing is sent to the client.', EnquiryPanel.tsx:268).
The Diary copy module (board-copy.ts) centralises the Diary's words in venue vocabulary. It is a good pattern to extend.

recommendations.change: Create one shared vocabulary module (status labels, tones and nouns for enquiries, reviews, proposals, bookings and opportunities) and a StatusChip that uses it in place of StatusBadge and the ad-hoc badges. Delete the 17 replace(/_/g, ' ') renderings.
recommendations.why: A client's enquiry must have one name everywhere, and no enum should reach the screen.

recommendations.change: Use sentence case for every nav item, heading and button across the app.
recommendations.why: It matches the desk and reads calmer and more finished.

recommendations.change: Replace the hedging with one plain qualifier shown once per document or surface (e.g. 'Numbers are planning estimates; the events team confirms them.'), and drop 'operational reliance', 'certify' and 'compliance determination' from client and supplier views.
recommendations.why: Honest without making the product feel defensive or like hard work.

recommendations.change: Draft a glossary with Blake that renames internal terms (Loadouts, Configurations, Snapshot, Handoff pack, Runtime package, Slug, Planning delta), then apply it.
recommendations.why: Veterans should recognise their own words.

questionsForBlake: What does the Trades Hall team call these: 'Reference Loadouts' (standard setups?), 'Pending Reviews' (layout sign-off?), 'Pipeline' and 'Opportunities', 'Handoff pack' (function sheet?), 'Configuration' (layout or floor plan?)
Which planning and safety disclaimers are legally required, and may they appear once per document rather than on each panel?
Diary terms: keep 'pencil' and 'ink', or would 'provisional' and 'confirmed' read better to clients who see them?

surfaces.name: Global interaction chrome (hover motion, cursor, scrollbar, tokens)
surfaces.audience: all staff, clients and suppliers on non-homepage routes
surfaces.dailyUse: Every pointer movement and every click, all day.
surfaces.currentLook: Every button except those in the desk, which opts out with [data-calm-controls], swells to scale(1.06) with brightness(1.15) on hover and presses to scale(0.93) through an overshoot spring (index.html:95-112). A gold SVG arrow cursor with a dark stroke replaces the system cursor everywhere, including the ivory desk and client pages (index.html:77-79). The scrollbar is a gold gradient on a near-black track, and Firefox gets it on every element through a '*' rule (index.html:139-168). House tokens, the declared single colour source, are dark-only (house-tokens.css:27-49). The selected style's palette exists three times under different names: --enq-* (EnquiriesDesk.css:9-46), --workspace-* (DashboardLayout.css:2-3) and the Diary's own.
slogFactors: Every list and card button swells under the pointer, which Blake has already asked to remove.
A gold cursor over ivory is a brand gimmick on a work tool. The dark-track gold scrollbar looks like the old cockpit on a light desk.

Without shared light tokens, each rebuilt surface re-picks its ivory. Grep finds dozens of near-identical ivory and cream hex values (#fff7e8 62 times, #f4efe6 23 times, #f2ecdf, #f6f1e8, #f7f3e6 and others), and small drifts read as unpolished.
strengths: Reduced motion is honoured at the source: the spring is gated on no-preference, with killswitches in global.css:182-200.
The desk's calm motion (press-only, 120 ms colour hovers on fine pointers only) is a ready replacement (EnquiriesDesk.css:660-673).

recommendations.change: Delete the global spring and brightness hover in index.html (Blake decided this on 26 September). Adopt the desk's grammar app-wide: 120 ms colour hover on fine pointers, scale(0.97) press, and none under reduced motion. Then remove [data-calm-controls].
recommendations.why: It is a founder decision, and it removes a constant low-level jitter.

recommendations.change: Add a workspace token layer to house-tokens.css (ivory sheet, sage ground, forest panel, copper plane, ink scale, tone washes and dots, focus ink and cream, Newsreader and Inter) promoted from --enq-*. Point the desk, the Diary, the header, and all shared state components (Notice, ConsequenceConfirm, EmptyState, StatusChip, state panels) at it.
recommendations.why: One polished palette everywhere, not near-miss copies.

recommendations.change: Return the system cursor on staff and client work surfaces, and use a thin sage scrollbar on light surfaces (pending Blake's answer).
recommendations.why: Quiet, native and legible for all-day use.

questionsForBlake: The gold arrow cursor on every page: keep it as a signature, or return to the normal cursor on work tools?
The gold scrollbar: keep it on dark 3D surfaces only, or remove it everywhere?

surfaces.name: Notification centre
surfaces.dailyUse: It should be glanced at many times a day. At present it is effectively never seen.
surfaces.currentLook: The notification feed lives inside the 'More' disclosure (DashboardLayout.tsx:226), so no count shows in the closed nav. Opened, it is a dark gradient panel (NotificationCenter.tsx:44-49) inside an ivory popover, with a Georgia heading, a severity word in 900-weight uppercase in coral, gold or cyan (NotificationCenter.tsx:73-75, 170), and icon-only 'view' and 'mark read' buttons. No timestamps are shown.
slogFactors: The unread count is hidden behind 'More', so staff must open a menu to learn whether anything needs them.
A dark panel nests inside an ivory popover, mixing two palettes in one glance.
Notifications carry no time, so 'urgent' has no age.
markRead has no catch (NotificationCenter.tsx:104-117). A failure is silent and leaves an unhandled rejection; only .finally clears the busy state.
The feed loads once on mount, with manual refresh only (NotificationCenter.tsx:84-93). No polling or push was found in the component, so new items do not appear until reload (inferred).
There is no 'Mark all read'.
strengths: Loading, error and empty states are all modelled (NotificationCenter.tsx:96-101), and it uses the Activity indicator.

recommendations.change: Show a quiet count on the top nav (a copper dot and a numeral beside the account or a bell). Restyle the panel on workspace tokens, grouped Today / Yesterday / Earlier with venue-time stamps, add 'Mark all read', handle markRead failures inline, and refresh on focus or by polling.
recommendations.why: Visible, calm awareness of what needs you: the desk's 'facts that decide first' applied to alerts.

questionsForBlake: Which events deserve a notification at all (new enquiry, client comment, proposal approved, supplier acknowledgement, booking conflict)? The rest could stay silent.

crossCutting: There are no shared light workspace tokens. house-tokens.css is dark-only (house-tokens.css:27-49), so the selected ivory, forest, copper and sage palette is re-declared as --enq-* (EnquiriesDesk.css:9-46), --workspace-* (DashboardLayout.css:2-3) and the Diary's own, with many near-identical ivory hex values across the CSS and TSX. Every shared state component (ConfirmModal, ToastContainer, StatusBadge, .vv-state-panel, error boundary, NotificationCenter, RouteArrival) is still dark-cockpit or Tailwind-generic.
The global springy hover and brightness in index.html:95-112 affects every button outside the desk. Blake has decided to remove it; the desk's press-only grammar is the replacement.
The cyan focus ring (#87e7f0, global.css:42-54; house-tokens.css:79) measures 1.22:1 on ivory #f2eddd and 1.43:1 on white. Only the desk overrides it.
The gold arrow cursor (index.html:77-79) and the gold, dark-track scrollbar (index.html:139-168) apply on every non-homepage route, including ivory work surfaces and client pages.

Every transition surface is dark: the first-paint boot (Activity.css:3-10), the html/body background (global.css:10-20), the lazy-route fallback RouteArrival (router.tsx:186-192) and ProtectedRoute's 'Checking access…'. Light surfaces are entered through dark interstitials (inferred; not measured).

Serif drift in state components: .vv-state-panel and NotificationCenter use Georgia or Times New Roman (global.css:93-101; NotificationCenter.tsx:143). ProposalPage asks for Cormorant Garamond (ProposalPage.tsx:27), which is only loaded by the quiz stylesheet (styles/fonts/quiz.css), so client proposals likely fall back to Playfair or Georgia (inferred). The desk uses Newsreader.

There are seven or more confirmation grammars and four toast implementations. Friction is inverted: modals guard reversible deletes, while terminal booking, proposal and review transitions fire on one click (booking.ts:94-97, proposal.ts:104-105, configuration-review.ts:72).

error.message is rendered at 39 call sites, and the ApiError fallbacks expose HTTP codes and endpoint paths (api/client.ts:94, 163-166). A describeFailure boundary would fix every cluster's error copy at once.

Date formatting is fragmented: 14 local helpers, 9 locale-less calls (US format visible in a committed baseline) and inconsistent venue time-zone use. The desk's enquiry-desk-format.ts helpers should become lib/venue-time.ts for every surface.
Status vocabulary drifts ('Declined' on the desk versus 'rejected' in StatusBadge for the same enquiry state), and 17 raw enum renderings via replace(/_/g, ' ').

The primary sales surfaces (Enquiries, Pipeline, Proposals, Pending Reviews, Client Search) and the notification feed all sit behind 'More' in the top nav (DashboardLayout.tsx:209-227), which the navigation cluster should weigh.

Some committed visual baselines are stale relative to the source. desktop-supplier-denied shows copy that ProtectedRoute.tsx no longer renders, and desktop-admin-create-venue-error shows the retired sidebar shell. The regression suite does not currently protect the rebuilt look.

Only the desk moves focus between list and detail and offers keyboard triage. A shared useListTriage hook and legend would carry the desk's game-feel to Reviews, Pipeline, Proposals and Client search.

cluster: Live screenshot sweep: every renderable staff, client-facing and public route at 1440x900, plus 390x844 phone captures (mocked API, seeded users, dev server on 127.0.0.1:5301, since stopped)
crossCutting: FOUR STAFF GROUNDS, ONE APPROVED. packages/web/src/components/dashboard/DashboardLayout.css:92 gives every dashboard view a dark forest main (#132b25) by default. Only enquiries (:98 sage #819087), inventory (:94 #7f9182) and diary (:96 ivory #f6f4eb) override it. Pipeline, Reviews, Analytics, Proposals, Search, Loadouts, Settings, Admin, Event-day ops, Ops handoff and Event Architect all render near-black gradient cards on dark forest. That is the 'stack of identical cards on dark green' the desk record (docs/design/enquiries-desk-2026-09-24/README.md 'What was wrong') describes Blake rejecting. Evidence: shots pipeline.png, reviews.png, analytics.png, proposals.png, settings.png, admin.png, ops-event.png.

SERIF FRAGMENTATION (computed styles, probe.mjs and probe3.mjs):
- Only the Enquiries h1 uses Newsreader.
- Georgia stacks: the Diary, Day Board, Reviews, Analytics, Settings, Onboarding and Event Architect headings, plus the header VENVIEWER wordmark.
- Proposal-share and supplier-share h1s ask for 'Cormorant Garamond' but only Playfair Display is loaded on those routes (document.fonts), so they render in Playfair.
- Other routes: Pricing uses Playfair Display; the homepage uses Fraunces with Geist and Geist Mono; the quiz uses Cinzel and Cormorant; the Trades House leaflet uses Georgia and requests fonts.googleapis.com.
- Inference: Georgia is probably not installed in this Linux container, so a fallback serif was captured. Office PCs and Macs will show real Georgia, so the same screen looks different from one device to another.

THREE FOCUS-RING COLOURS.
- The dark dashboards use the global cyan rgb(135,231,240): 10.5:1 on #132b25, so fine on dark (shots/focus-reviews.png). The brief records it at about 1.4:1 on ivory. The search input on the dark ground shows a heavy cyan halo on a white field (search-typed.png).
- Onboarding uses copper rgb(155,101,62) at 2 px: 4.30:1 on ivory (focus-onboarding.png).
- The Diary uses green rgb(81,121,99) at 3 px (diary-focus-ring.png).
One token-driven ring per ground (ink on ivory and copper, cream on forest, as the desk does) would unify them.

DATES AND TIMES ARE NOT VENUE-LOCAL OR BRITISH:
- ReviewsView.tsx:463, 465, 553 and 708 use a bare toLocaleString(), which renders '9/26/2026, 8:12:00 AM' in an en-US browser.
- ClientSearchView.tsx:124 uses toLocaleDateString(), which gives '9/24/2026'.
- CommercialPipelineView.tsx:117 uses en-GB but no timeZone. A 10:00 BST follow-up showed as '09:00' in a UTC browser.
- Native date inputs show mm/dd/yyyy in an en-US browser: the Day Board shows 09/26/2026 and Event Architect shows mm/dd/yyyy. Inference: a UK browser would show dd/mm/yyyy, but the page does not control this.
The desk formats dates in the venue's zone and British style ('Fri 2 Oct 2026').

GENERIC LIBRARY COLOURS AND CYAN:

SALES WORK IS BURIED UNDER 'MORE'. The header shows Plan, Diary, Hallkeeper (and Inventory for admins).
